# A Note For Yourself

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/A_Note_For_Yourself

**A Note For Yourself** is an event that can appear in Act 1, Act 2, and Act 3. You found a card left by someone, along with a mysterious note that is supposedly written by yourself.

## Options
- **[Take and Give]** Receive a card that you had stored previously, and store a card in your deck in return. 
    - The first time the player encounters this event in their save file, it will have Iron Wave stored.
- **[Ignore]** Nothing happens.

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| *You spot a loose brick within a pillar that catches your eye.* |
| *You find a folded note and a card inside. It reads* "The Heart awaits." *This is your handwriting.* |
| Leave |
| *"What is going on?"* |

## Notes

- This event can store a card between runs, and allows the player to obtain a card from a different character.
    - This event can be used to store cards from other classes for amazing synergies. A great example of this is Juggernaut + After Image, which is a powerful synergy rarely available otherwise.
- If you store an upgraded card, it remains upgraded when found on another run.
- On Ascension 14 or lower, the player must have beaten that Ascension level on the chosen character in order to encounter this event.
- This event cannot be encountered on Ascension level 15 or higher,
- Outside of Ascension Mode, the event can be encountered regardless of whether the player has won before.
- If a card such as Ritual Dagger or Genetic Algorithm is stored, its damage or Block is reverted to the initial value.
    - However, Searing Blow retains its upgrade level.
    - With the *extremely* rare exception being when this event is encountered multiple times within a single run. The stored card is not reverted to its initial value in that case.  

- Interestingly, the player can encounter this event in Custom Mode and store otherwise unobtainable cards such as Pride in the event. 
- One could store a highly-upgraded Searing Blow this way.
- Since storing a card removes it from your deck, you cannot store a card that is Bottled.
- Curses obtained from this event will not be blocked by Omamori.
- A card obtained from this event is not duplicated when using the Hoarder modifier.

# A Thousand Cuts

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/A_Thousand_Cuts

# Achievements

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Achievements

**Achievements **are granted throughout the game for various merits of small and large scale. They do not unlock anything, but do count towards a Save File's completion percent.

| Image | Name | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | Shrug It Off | *Win a battle with 1 HP remaining.* |
|  | Purity | *Have 3 or fewer cards in hand, draw, and discard pile combined.* |
|  | Come At Me | *Win a combat without playing an Attack.* |
|  | The Pact | *Exhaust 20 cards in a single combat.* |
|  | Adrenaline | *Have 9 Energy in a single turn of combat.* |
|  | Powerful | *Have 10 or more buffs during combat.* |
|  | Jaxxed | *Have 50 or more Strength during combat.* |
|  | Impervious | *Have 99 or more Block during combat.* |
|  | Barricaded | *Have 999 Block during combat.* |
|  | Catalyst | *Apply 99 or more Poison on a single enemy.* |
|  | Plague | *Defeat 3 enemies with Poison in a single combat.* |

|  | Infinity | *Play 25 cards in a single turn.* |
|  | Focused | *Have 25 or more Focus during combat.* |
|  | Neon | *Channel 9 Plasma in a single turn.* |
|  | You Are Nothing | *Defeat a boss on turn 1.* |
|  | Minimalist | *Beat the game with a 5 card deck or smaller.* |
|  | Ooh Donut! | *Finish Donu with a *Feed*.* |
|  | Perfect | *Defeat a boss without taking any damage.* |
|  | Who Needs Relics? | *Beat the game with a single Relic.* |
|  | Speed Climber | *Beat the game in under 20 minutes.* |
|  | Common Sense | *Beat the game with a deck containing no uncommons or rares.* |
|  | My Lucky Day | *Win a Daily Climb*. |

|  | The Champion | *Defeated The Champ*. |
|  | The Crow | *Defeated the Awakened One.* |
|  | The Shapes | *Defeated Donu and Deca.* |
|  | The Time Eater | *Defeated the Time Eater.* |
|  | Ruby | *Beat the game with the Ironclad.* |
|  | Emerald | *Beat the game with the Silent.* |
|  | Sapphire | *Beat the game with the Defect.* |

|  | Eternal One | *Obtain all other Achievements.* |

## Notes
- You can still get the **Perfect** achievement if you lose HP from your own cards during a boss combat.
- You can still obtain the **Minimalist** achievement if your deck becomes 5 cards after Act 3.

## Tips
- **Adrenaline** can be easy to get using cards that generate Energy, such as Adrenaline, TURBO, Collect, Deva Form, or by using Ice Cream, which conserves Energy between turns. 
- **The Pact** can be earned in combats where the enemies applies many Statuses, such as the fight with the Sentries, or use any combo of Corruption with Dead Branch and/or Dark Embrace.
- To earn the **Purity** achievement, you either need a constant source of Exhausting, or a minimalist deck with some Exhaust cards. 
    - Facing the Bronze Automaton in Act 2 may also help, as the Bronze Orbs will temporarily remove two cards from your deck.
- The **Impervious** and **Barricaded** achievements can be earned with any source of Block and a way to conserve it between turns, such as Barricade. Entrench makes these achievements much easier and less tedious.
- Peace Pipe makes the **Minimalist** challenge easier, as you are given many more card removal opportunities with it.
- Killing the boss on turn 1 for the **You Are Nothing** achievement requires a large amount of damage to be done in a single turn. Consider using a highly upgraded Searing Blow, boosters like Offering/Adrenaline/Potions, or an "infinite" deck.
    - Killing the Awakened One's first phase in one turn counts for getting the achievement.
- The **Come At Me** achievement is easily earned with Thorns, Poison, or by playing The Defect and letting Orbs chip away.
    - Taking Neow's Lament on The Defect, combined with Orbs is an easy way to get this achievement
- The **Catalyst** achievement, as its name implies, is simplified with the use of Catalyst.
- The **Transient** is more or less a hard version of "*You are nothing*". Any build that scales quickly, e.g. via the use of Catalyst, Limit Break, rapid Mantra generation for a consistent Divinity or infinite one-turn killer combo, may beat it.
- **Neon** is best earned through the use of Meteor Strike and a way to play it multiple times in one turn, such as Echo Form and/or Hologram.
- Both **Focused** and **Powerful** are best earned with Creative AI as a continuous source of powers.
    - **Focused** can also be earned through the use of Consume, but will require many orb slots. Best coupled with Inserter.
- An "infinite" deck containing cards such as Flash of Steel, Dropkick or Heel Hook will make many achievements simple. An infinite can also be built with cards such as Tactician or an Unceasing Top but a deck like this may take longer to kill enemies.

## Acid Slime (L)

### Move
| Name | Intent | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Corrosive Spit |  | Deals 11 damage, shuffles 2 Slimed into the discard pile. |
| Deals 12 damage, shuffles 2 Slimed into the discard pile. |  |  |
| Lick |  | Inflicts 2 Weak. |
| Tackle |  | Deals 16 damage. |
| Deals 18 damage. |  |  |
| Split |  | Dies and spawns 2 Acid Slimes (M)  with current HP. |

### Pattern
Has a 30% / 40% chance of using Corrosive Spit, 40% / 30% chance of using Tackle and 30% chance of using Lick in every turn.

Cannot use Tackle / Lick twice in a row and cannot use other moves three in a row.

Once its HP reaches 50% or lower, Acid Slime (L)'s current intent will be interrupted and it will Split into two Acid Slime (M)s, each with the Acid Slime (L)'s current HP.

## Acid Slime (M)

### Move
| Name | Intent | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Corrosive Spit |  | Deal 7 damage, shuffles 1 Slimed into the discard pile. |
| Deal 8 damage, shuffles 1 Slimed into the discard pile. |  |  |
| Lick |  | Inflicts 1 Weak. |
| Tackle |  | Deal 10 damage. |
| Deal 12 damage. |  |  |

### Pattern
Below 17, its pattern is identical to Acid Slime (L), although Acid Slime (M) cannot Split.

On 17+, has a 40% chance of using Corrosive Spit, 40% chance of using Tackle and 20% chance of using Lick in every turn, though Lick cannot be used twice in a row and other moves cannot be used three times in a row.

## Acid Slime (S)

### Move
| Name | Intent | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lick |  | Inflict 1 Weak. |
| Tackle |  | Deals 3 damage. |
| Deals 4 damage. |  |  |

### Pattern
On turn 1, it has 50% chance of using either Lick or Tackle. If it is 17+, always starts with Lick.

It then alternates between the two moves.

# Acrobatics

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Acrobatics

**Infobox:**
- Name: Acrobatics
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/d/db/Acrobatics.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016211209
- Class: Silent
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Common
- Cost: 1
- Effect: Draw 3 cards.; Discard 1 card.
- [Acrobatics+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: Draw 4 cards.; Discard 1 card.

## Tips

- Acrobatics costs 1 energy to draw 3 cards and discard 1 card, thus yielding a net gain of 2 cards (not considering the cost of drawing acrobatics in the first place). Although on the surface it may seem to be no better than a card like Backflip, it synergizes very well with cards whose effects trigger upon being discarded (e.g. Tactician, Reflex), or who have additional effects if other cards have been discarded (e.g. Sneaky Strike, Eviscerate). It also allows you discard Curses, Statuses, or cards that aren't useful on a given turn.
    - The upgrade for Acrobatics is relatively powerful, as it provides a net gain of 3 cards instead of 2. In addition to the obvious benefits of additional card draw, this also means that you have more options for cards to discard.
- In general, drawing 3 cards sounds very meritable, but this is usually only true in the later part of the game. Early on, when you only have 3 Energy, it is rarely reasonable to spend 1 energy purely to draw cards, since you still need energy to play the cards that you draw.
    - Reusable cards that provide energy can help improve the effectiveness of Acrobatics early on. For instance, Concentrate (especially when both it and Acrobatics are upgraded) becomes more viable when you have the additional cards drawn by Acrobatics.

# Act 1

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Act_1

**Act 1** or **the Exordium** is the first of the three default acts of Slay the Spire.

## Overview
Act 1 is the introductory act of the game. The player always starts with a conversation with Neow before starting their journey. 

Most enemies do not have complex moves and are usually straightforward in nature. This act also teaches the player about basic Buffs and Debuffs that are widespread among the enemies.  

Enemies are usually comprised of one moderately strong monster, a group of weak monsters, or a pair of moderately strong monsters. 

Most events exclusive to this act don't have heavy penalties, and usually cost player their HP, whether directly through a choice or through an avoidable fight.

Card rewards in this act have a 0% chance to appear upgraded. The only way to have an  upgraded card in card rewards is by obtaining Molten Egg, Toxic Egg, or Frozen Egg.

This act spans from floor 1 to floor 17.

- Floor 1 is always a Monster battle.
- Floor 9 is always a Treasure Room.
- Floor 15 is always a Rest Site.
- Floor 16 and 17 are Boss battle and Boss Chest, respectively.

# Act 2

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Act_2

**Act 2** or **the City** is the second of the three default acts of Slay the Spire.

## Overview
Act 2 starts after the player defeats Act 1 boss. They are also healed to full health at the start of the act, or 75% of their missing HP on Ascension 5 and beyond.

Enemies in this act become drastically more difficult than those of Act 1. Monsters in this act either have some gimmick that makes disposing of them much more difficult, or can severely cripple the player. Most monsters also boast high damage output and high health.

Another common component for Act 2's monsters is their multi-hit attacks, and their preference to appear in groups. The player has to come prepared with not only strong Area-of Effect cards, but also ways to reduce and repel those pesky attacks as well. 

Enemies are usually comprised of one strong monster, a group of moderately strong monsters, or a pair of one strong monsters and one moderately strong monster.

Events exclusive to this act  arguably have the widest range of risk-versus-reward. Some are straightforward improvements to the player with little to no penalty. Others have great rewards while having a huge risk, such as losing a large amount of maximum health, or a battle against powerful foes. There is also a number of events that are affected by Relics the player has.

Card rewards in this act have a 25% chance to appear upgraded, reduced to 12.5% on Ascension 12 and beyond. 

This act spans floor 18 to floor 34.

- Floor 18 is always a Monsters battle.
- Floor 26 is always a Treasure Room.
- Floor 32 is always a Rest Site.
- Floor 33 and 34 are Boss battle and Boss Chest, respectively.

# Act 3

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Act_3

**Act 3** or **the Beyond** is the third of the three default acts of Slay the Spire.

## Overview
Act 3 starts after the player defeats the Act 2 boss. They are also healed to full health at the start of the act, or 75% of their missing HP on Ascension 5 and beyond.

This act is infamous for enemies that are notoriously difficult to deal with, with some boasting an amount of health that is comparable to that of a Boss. Even the weakest enemies in this act are very much a nuisance that requires careful plan of attack.

Due to the diverse nature of enemies and their difficulty, this is the act that will test the player's deck thoroughly for its ability to survive every kind of situation.

Enemies are usually comprised of one very strong monster, a group of strong monsters, or a group of moderately strong monsters.

Events exclusive to this act usually have great impact on the player while having huge risk tied to them. There are only a few exclusive events that do not cost the player something. Like in Act 2, there are a number of events that are affected by Relics the player has.

Card rewards in this act has 50% chance to appear upgraded, reduced to 25% on Ascension 12 and beyond. 

This act spans from floor 35 to floor 51.

- Floor 35 is always a Monsters battle.
- Floor 43 is always a Treasure Room.
- Floor 49 is always a Rest Site.
- Floor 50 is always a Boss battle.
- Floor 51 is the player facing an unknown entity.
    - If the player has the Ruby, Emerald, and Sapphire keys they will advance to floor 52 and Act 4.
    - Otherwise, the game will end in a *"Victory?"* screen.

# Act 4

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Act_4

**Act 4** or **The Ending** is the fourth and final act of Slay the Spire. 

## Overview
Act 4 is a bonus Act that can only be accessed through repeated gameplay — it is not accessible until the player has beaten the game with every character minus the Watcher. Unlike every other Act, Act 4 is unique in that it forces the player down a single path, which will always be the following rooms in order:

- A rest site
- A merchant encounter
- An Elite encounter against the Spire Shield and Spire Spear
- A final boss fight against the Corrupt Heart

The simple, predictable nature of Act 4 means that the player can build a deck around defeating the Corrupt Heart early in the game, as the only true source of randomness in Act 4 is what the merchant will sell. 

Despite its predictability, Act 4 is easily the toughest Act for unprepared players; it contains a resting site placed against the player's favor, a notoriously difficult Elite encounter, one merchant, and what is arguably the strongest boss in the entire game.

This Act spans from floor 52 to floor 55 (floor 53 to floor 56 on Ascension 20), which is the final floor of a non-Endless game:

- Floor 52 (floor 53 on Ascension 20) is always a rest site.
- Floor 53 (floor 54 on Ascension 20) is always a merchant.
- Floor 54 (floor 55 on Ascension 20) is always an Elite encounter against the Spire Shield and Spire Spear.
- Floor 55 (floor 56 on Ascension 20) is always a boss battle against the Corrupt Heart.

No events occur in Act 4. As such, unless the player has specific relics such as Peace Pipe or Shovel, their options are limited to the rest site and the merchant's offerings.

## How to access
To access Act 4, the player must first beat the game (defeat the Act 3 boss) at least once with the Ironclad, the Silent, and the Defect. Once this is done, the player will be able to start collecting the required keys; an unfilled triangle will appear to the left of the player's name to indicate that they are able to collect the keys.

Note that beating the game with the Watcher is not required to access Act 4.

### Keys
To unlock Act 4, three Keys must be collected throughout the course of a game: the Ruby Key, the Emerald Key, and the Sapphire Key.

#### Ruby Key
The Ruby Key is obtained by using the recall option at a rest site. Once the Ruby Key is obtained, the recall option will not be available until the next run.

#### Emerald Key
The Emerald Key is obtained by defeating a buffed Elite. A special Elite encounter is marked with flames on the spire map and will only appear once per Act. Defeating a special Elite will reward the player with the normal Elite payout plus the Emerald Key. 

The special Elite encounter will not appear again once the player has obtained the Emerald Key for the rest of the run.

#### Sapphire Key
The Sapphire Key can be obtained through any non-boss chest. The Sapphire Key is linked to the Relic that normally appears in the chest — the player may only take either the Relic or the Sapphire Key. Once the Sapphire Key is taken, it will no longer appear for the rest of the run.

### Entering Act 4
Once all three keys have been collected, the player must defeat the Act 3 boss to advance to Act 4. 

If the player does not have all three keys, Act 4 will be inaccessible and the player's run will be forced to end, resulting in the normal Victory? screen.

## Monsters

### Debuts
None. Act 4 has no monster encounters.

- Name: After Image

- Description: Whenever you play a card, gain X Block
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: Intensity

**After Image** is a Rare Power for the Silent.  Whenever the player plays another card, they gain 1 Block immediately afterwards.  When Upgraded, After Image becomes Innate.

## Mechanics

- Dexterity does *not* affect the Block gained from After Image, as the Block is generated by a buff and not the card itself.
- The After Image buff is stackable, so playing multiple copies of After Image will provide even more Block per card. Since After Image+ only costs 1 Energy and is Innate, playing more than 1 copy on the first turn is easily done.

## Tips

- After Image is helpful for countering the Corrupt Heart's Beat of Death status, which inflicts 1 damage immediately after the player plays a card. 
- This card is an excellent addition to any Shiv-based deck, as every individual Shiv grants 1 Block. 
- Playing many cards in a turn (e.g. with Shivs) is liable to generate excess Block, so Blur can be used to carry it over to the next turn.

# Akabeko

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Akabeko

**Infobox:**
- Name: Akabeko
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/4/4c/Akabeko.png/revision/latest?cb=20200203145854
- Description: Your first attack each combat deals 8 additional damage.
- Flavor: "Muuu~"
- Rarity: Common
- Class: Any

The Akabeko is a common relic that makes the first attack played each combat deal an additional 8 damage.
## Strategy
Akabeko is essentially a hefty 1-attack Strength boost. This relic benefits multihit cards, such as Pummel and Ragnarok, as the additional damage is applied to each attack done by the card.

## Synergy
 
- Bag of Marbles: If your first attack played is on turn 1, it will benefit from the Vulnerable given by Bag of Marbles.
- Bag of Preparation, Ring of the Snake, and Ring of the Serpent: The additional card draw means it is more likely for an attack that greatly benefits from Akabeko to be drawn on turn 1.
- Bottled Flame: Bottling a multihit attack such as Riddle with Holes allows a guaranteed powerful turn 1 attack.
- Wreath of Flame can stack its effect with Akabeko, allowing for stronger multi-hit attacks.
- Dramatic Entrance is innate, costs 0, and gains another 8 damage applied to all enemies.
- Wrath and Divinity Stances: The additional damage given by Akabeko is doubled / tripled by these Stances.
- Gambling Chip and Gambler's Brew: Allows the player to mulligan cards that do not benefit from Akabeko.
- Reaper: The additional damage from Akabeko counts towards the healing given by Reaper.
- Louses are much more likely to be killed instead of Curling Up after being attacked.

 
- Ordinary attacks such as Flash of Steel may not be played if the player decides to wait for a stronger card like Riddle with Holes.

 
- Innate Non-attack cards, Bottled Tornado, Bottled Lightning: Innate cards take up 1 of your 5 default draws, therefore making it harder to draw an attack that benefits from Akabeko. 
- Nemesis: Can completely negate Akabeko's effect with its Intangible.
- Being Weakened can reduce Akabeko's effect.

## Trivia
- An Akabeko is a traditional toy from the Aizu region of Japan. 
    - Aizu legend claims that the toy is based on a real cow that was used to build the Enzō-ji Temple of Yanaizu in the 9th century.

# All for One

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/All_for_One

**Infobox:**
- Name: All for One
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/0/09/AllforOne.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016203018
- Class: Defect
- Type: Attack
- Rarity: Rare
- Cost: 2
- Effect: Deal 10 damage.; Put all cost 0 cards from your discard pile into your hand.
- [All for One+]
- Cost+: 2
- Effect+: Deal 14 damage.; Put all cost 0 cards from your discard pile into your hand.

CardAutobox**All For One** is an Attack card for The Defect and the flagship card of its 0-cost archetype. As a Rare card, All For One can usually be obtained only as a boss reward and at a considerable price from The Merchant.

## Strategy
- All For One is a powerhouse in any deck with a significant number of 0-cost cards. Its ability to recover up to ten free cards enables The Defect to unleash a brutal beatdown while developing future plays. Its 10 base damage is merely a bonus.

- Avoid Velvet Choker at all costs, since it shuts down the 0-cost deck.

- All For One's strength hinges on the number of 0-cost cards in the deck, and how aggressively the player can draw them. When building around All For One, prioritize zero-cost Attacks like Beam Cell, Go for the Eyes and especially Streamline, FTL, and Claw. Pack as much card draw as possible to put them in the discard pile and All For One in the hand.

- After acquiring All For One, keep 150 Gold available to purchase Panache from The Merchant. All For One turns often involve 10 plays or more, which Panache translates into impressive area of effect damage.

- Be aware that All For One doesn't reliably help The Defect defend itself, as Steam Barrier decreases in effectiveness with every play, and the only infinitely replayable Block-granting 0-cost card, Force Field, is a poor fit in the deck. High-Block Skills, especially Auto-Shields, can stretch the single remaining Energy into a solid defense. Energy-granting Boss Relics like Cursed Key allow the player to mix more Block into big All For One turns.

- Consider adding Recycle and Hologram to a deck with All For One. While normally weak, these cards do a great job at stabilizing the deck. Recycle is especially useful for clearing unused Attacks from the hand to make room for more discarded cards.
    - In addition, Hologram can, with luck, make Snecko fights trivial. If both Hologram and All for One are randomly drawn as 0 cost, it can create an infinite loop of any 0-cost damage card -> All For One -> Hologram to recall All For One.

- While Scrape is normally a key part of a 0-cost deck, it can discard All For One. Check the decklist often to avoid an embarrassing misplay.

- All For One checks the cost that appears on the card. Cards decreased to 0 cost by Confused will be recovered, but cards increased above 0 cost will not. Note that a card retains its cost when discarded, and Confused randomizes the cost when the card is drawn.

- The player's hand can hold a maximum of 10 cards. If the player can't hold every 0-cost card in the discard pile, the recovered cards are selected in the order they are displayed in the discard pile. Note that playing a card immediately removes it from the hand, so All For One itself doesn't count towards the hand limit.

- All For One's power is entirely determined by the cards it will recover. If the player draws All For One too early, or the 0-cost cards are too weak, it's often better not to play it and hope for better luck next shuffle.

- Be very careful not to draw too many cards and shuffle the discard pile. Use extreme caution when fighting Time Eater, as his effect will likely interrupt the turn before all 0-cost cards are played.

- The downsides of TURBO and Steam Barrier are multiplied by replaying them. Instead of reflexively playing everything after playing All For One, estimate how many turns remain in the battle, and whether these cards will end the battle before their Status drawbacks overwhelm you.
- Rebound can save All For One for a better turn if there are few or no 0-costs to play from playing it.

# All-Out Attack

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/All-Out_Attack

**Infobox:**
- Name: All-Out Attack
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/6/68/All-OutAttack.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016211210
- Class: Silent
- Type: Attack
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Cost: 1
- Effect: Deal 10 damage to ALL enemies.; Discard 1 card at random.
- [All-Out Attack+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: Deal 14 damage to ALL enemies.; Discard 1 card at random.

All-Out Attack is an Uncommon Card for the Silent which deals damage to all enemies once, then discards a random card in your hand. If after playing All-Out Attack your hand is empty, no cards will be discarded.

## Strategy
All-Out Attack is a strong source of upfront AoE (Area-of-Effect) damage. It has higher burst of damage than Dagger Spray, upgraded or otherwise. It scales with Strength worse than the latter, given that All-Out Attack hits only once. However, due to the same reason, it is less punishing to use against enemies with Thorns.

With its discard being random in nature, it is highly preferable to use all the other high-impact cards before using this card as a sort of 'closer' card to make it less likely that it will discard a card that you actually wanted to play.

### Synergies
 
- Tactician and Reflex grant benefits when discarded, although you need to plan your use of card carefully to have All-Out Attack more likely to discard said cards.
- Tough Bandages and Tingsha have a synergy with discarding, granting free Block and damage respectively.
- This card is stronger in Act 1, where enemies have low health.
    - It can still perform moderately well in Act 2, being a cheap burst of AoE damage.

 
- Less risky to use against Spiker than Dagger Spray, especially if there are more than one. However, the Silent has an access to much better indirect damage in a form of Poison.

 

## Trivia
- The card's artwork, a cloud with fists popping out suggesting rapid beatings, is a reference to the move of the same name from the *Persona* series.

# Amplify

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Amplify

**Infobox:**
- Name: Amplify
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/6/6d/Amplify.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016203031
- Class: Defect
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Rare
- Cost: 1
- Effect: This turn, your next Power card is played twice.
- [Amplify+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: This turn, your next 2 Power cards are played twice.
- Name: Amplify
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/2/2d/Icon_Amplify.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202161409
- Description: Your next X Power cards are played twice.
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: Counter

CardAutobox

**Amplify** is a Skill card for the Defect. It plays the next Power card this turn a second time, for no Energy. As a Rare card, it can be obtained after defeating a Boss. It is Defect's version of Burst and Double Tap.

Upon Upgrade, it will trigger for the 2nd Power card played in the same turn.

The second play is NOT added to your draw or discard pile.

The scaling buff from Amplify (and also from Burst and Double Tap) is the number of cards that will be played twice, not the number of times the card will be played. This means playing multiple Amplifies will add to the number of cards that will be played twice that turn, not make the next card play 3 or more times.

## Interactions

- The second play will not cost any Energy, but it will trigger any other consequences of playing the card. For example, an Amplied Biased Cognition  will cause you to lose focus twice as fast.
- The second play of a card that costs X energy will use the same value of X as the first.
- The second play acts as a separate card. This has interactions including, but not limited to:
    - Ink Bottle, Pocketwatch: Both plays count towards playing Power for their counters. 
    - Velvet Choker: Both plays count towards the amount of cards played for the turn.
    - Time Eater's Time Warp power: Both plays increase the counter as usual. If the second power is the 13th action on his counter, it will NOT occur, unlike Velvet Choker.

- The second play happens after the Power is sent to the draw, discard or Exhaust piles.

# Anchor

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Anchor

**Infobox:**
- Name: Anchor
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/c/c0/Anchor.png/revision/latest?cb=20190923232659
- Description: Start each combat with 10 Block.
- Flavor: Holding this miniature trinket, you feel heavier and more stable.
- Rarity: Common
- Class: Any

**Anchor** is a common relic that provides 10 Block at the start of each combat.
## Strategy
This relic's ability makes your turn 1 easier, as you do not need to spend as much Energy on defense. This means you could either attack right away, or, more effectively, play Power cards on your first turn safely. Because of this, decks that rely on (likely Innate) Powers find this relic very useful.

## Synergy
 
- Bag of Preparation or Ring of the Snake: The additional 2 cards in your starting hand may be played safely.
- Body Slam: Does 10 additional damage.
- Bottled Flame and Bottled Tornado: You may play the bottled Attack or Power safely without worrying much about taking damage.
- Calipers, Barricade, Blur: The initial 10 Block may now carry into other turns.
- Runic Pyramid, Well-Laid Plans, Equilibrium: Block cards drawn on turn 1 may be Retained for later turns, therefore not making them useless when coupled with Anchor.

 
- Bottled Lightning: Allows to play the bottled Skill safely, but the Skill may also be a Block card.
- Boot Sequence: Mostly becomes redundant with this relic and takes one space on your first draw. However, together they can be useful against hard-hitters such as Taskmaster mob.

 
- Orichalcum: Will not work on first turn if any of the initial 10 Block remains at the end of your turn.

# Ancient Tea Set

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Ancient_Tea_Set

**Infobox:**
- Name: Ancient Tea Set
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/e/e6/AncientTeaSet.png/revision/latest?cb=20200203145924
- Description: Whenever you enter a Rest Site, start the next combat with 2 extra Energy.
- Flavor: The key to a refreshing night's rest.
- Rarity: Common
- Class: Any

The Ancient Tea Set is a common relic that provides 2 Energy at the start of the first combat encountered after entering a Rest Site.

This relic does not spawn beyond floor 48, excluding Endless mode.

## Strategy
This relic's ability allows the player to play more cards on turn 1 after entering a Rest Site, which means it is more likely for a combat to end much faster than it normally would. This gives the player an incentive to route towards Rest Sites. Since boss combats are always preceded with a Rest Site, this relic guarantees 2 additional Energy at the start of boss combats (barring some exceptions, see the Secret Portal event and the Ascension 20 modifier).

It is important to note that entering ? rooms or Treasure Rooms does not mean that the effect of the relic is wasted, as the Energy gain only triggers when entering a combat.

## Synergy
 
- X Energy Cost Cards (Whirlwind, Skewer, Tempest, etc.): The additional Energy makes playing these cards on turn 1 much more viable.
- Innate Powers (Infinite Blades+, Hello World+, etc.): The additional Energy allows these cards to be played without devoting your first turn to them. 
- Card Draw (Acrobatics, Shrug It Off, Battle Trance, etc.): The additional Energy gained from Ancient Tea Set allows you to use cards that draw more cards, while still having enough Energy to use the cards drawn.
- Bag of Preparation or Ring of the Snake: The extra card draw in addition to the 2 Energy provided by Ancient Tea Set allows you to have a much more powerful first turn.
- Ice Cream: Allows you to conserve the additional Energy gained from Ancient Tea Set between turns, giving the effect a much wider impact.

# Ancient Writing

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Ancient_Writing

**Ancient Writing** is an event found exclusively in Act 2. You discover a wall covered in the writing of Ancients.

## Options

- **[Elegance]** Remove a card from your deck.

- **[Simplicity]** Upgrade all Strikes and Defends.

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| *Scaling the city, you notice a wall covered in the writing of Ancients. As you try to wrap your head around what the puzzling symbols and glyphs could mean, the writing begins to glow.* |
| *Suddenly, the message becomes clear...* |
| Elegance |
| *The answer was elegance.* |
| *Of course.* |
| Simplicity |
| *The truth is always simple.* |

## Strategy
- **[Simplicity]** is more commonly the stronger choice. Upgraded Strikes and Defends are vastly improved from their base form, and can help you get through Act 2 more easily, taking on more Elites. 
    - This choice is more powerful with Strike Dummy. It increases Strike+ damage to an amount comparable to a moderately powerful attack card.
    - This choice is less powerful if you have already removed a good amount of Strikes and Defends.
    - This choice also help eliminates Strikes and Defends from being upgraded by Whetstone, War Paint, Warped Tongs, Lesson Learned, and Designer In-Spire.
- **[Elegance]** will help you thin your deck, or if you have a particularly nasty Curse you wish to remove such as Pain, Regret, or Normality
    - This choice is more powerful if your deck can already easily get through Act 2, or if you are aiming for a deck with an Infinite Combo

## Trivia
- This event internal name is "Back to Basics".

# Art of War

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Art_of_War

**Infobox:**
- Name: Art of War
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/b/bb/ArtofWar.png/revision/latest?cb=20190923232721
- Description: If you do not play any Attacks during your turn, gain an extra Energy next turn.
- Flavor: This ancient manuscript contains wisdom from a past age.
- Rarity: Common
- Class: Any

The Art of War is a Common Relic that provides an additional Energy next turn if you do not play any attack cards in your current turn.

## Strategy
This relic benefits during turns where you need to use all Energy to block fully in order to negate a large amount of damage. This relic is also useful during turn 1 on characters like the Defect and the Silent, as a good number of decks for the aforementioned characters include a turn 1 where only powers or skills are played.

## Synergy
 
- Pocketwatch: On turns where Pocketwatch activates, there is a good chance you did not play any attacks. This allows you to benefit more from the additional energy next turn, as you will have more cards to work with due to Pocketwatch.
- Snecko Eye: On turns where Art of War activates, the additional energy will allow you to play more cards if Snecko Eye randomizes cards into mostly high costs.
- Letter Opener: Allows you to deal damage without playing attack.
- The Bomb: The Bomb is a skill which deals damage, meaning you can deal damage without losing the benefit of Art of War.
- Pressure Points does damage without being an attack.
- Poison can be applied with skills, which is damage without being an attack.

 
- All attack cards: Prevents Art of War from triggering.
- Double Tap: Playing this skill would be a waste of Energy unless you played an attack, therefore preventing Art of War from triggering.
- Ornamental Fan, Nunchaku, Kunai, Shuriken: These relics reliance on attacking clashes directly with Art of War.

## Trivia

The relic references the Art of War, an ancient manuscript on military tactics written by Sun Tzu.

# Artifact

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Artifact

**Infobox:**
- Name: Artifact
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/a/a8/Artifact.png/revision/latest?cb=20190105133017
- Description: Negates X Debuffs.
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: Counter

Artifact is a buff that will negate the next Debuff on that unit.

Each stack of Artifact can block 1 *application* of a Debuff. For example:

- Bouncing Flask will remove 1 Artifact *with each bounce*.
- Envenom will remove 1 Artifact *with each unblocked Attack damage*.
- Shockwave and Crippling Cloud will remove up to 2 Artifacts from each enemy, since they inflict 2 Debuffs.

Effects that apply multiple Debuffs will do so in the order listed on the card. For instance, if an enemy has 1 Artifact and is hit by Shockwave, the card will apply Weak then apply Vulnerable as per its description, and the enemy will lose 1 Artifact to negate Weak and only has Vulnerable inflicted on it.

An Artifact charge is consumed with any application of debuff, even when applying an existing debuff that does not stack. (Notably, if the player has **Confused** from Snecko Eye and an active Artifact, an Artifact charge will be consumed when Snecko applies **Confused** to the player using its Perplexing Glare, even though the **Confused** debuff does not stack.)

## Enemy Interactions
- Note that all cards that inflict ongoing effects on enemies work via their own special Debuff, even if it's not specifically identified on the card; these will still be negated by Artifact. For instance, the ongoing effects of Corpse Explosion or Choke can be negated by Artifact.
- Enemy attacks which immediately add a card, whether Status or Curse, to your deck, such as the Slime Boss' Goop Spray, the Taskmaster's Scouring Whip, or Writhing Mass' Implant, are depicted as inflicting negative effects and might give the impression that it can be negated by an Artifact. However, an active Artifact will not prevent the addition of the cards.

## Player Interactions
- Flex's Strength loss at the end of turn is handled as a Debuff that can be negated by Artifact, making the Strength gain permanent. The same applies to Flex Potion and Mutagenic Strength’s end of turn Strength loss, and Speed Potion’s end of turn Dexterity loss. The Artifact can block either the debuff that causes the stat loss at the end of the turn, or the actual loss when it occurs, depending on when the Artifact was gained. 
- Wraith Form and Biased Cognition's Debuffs can be negated by Artifact before you play the mentioned cards. If you gain Artifact after being inflicted by the Debuffs, it will negate 1 tick of their respective effects.
- No Draw from Bullet Time or Battle Trance can be negated, allowing the player to keep on drawing cards.
- The downsides of Panic Button, Hyperbeam, Berserk, and Fasting can be negated, allowing them to be played safely.
- Blasphemy's effect is considered a *buff*, preventing Artifact from blocking it.

## Sources

### Cards

#### Defect Cards
- Core Surge - 1 Artifact.

#### Neutral Cards
- Panacea - 1 (2) Artifact.

### Relics
- Clockwork Souvenir - Start each combat with 1 Artifact.

### Potions
- Ancient Potion - 1 (2) Artifact.

### Enemy
- Sentry - Start each combat with 1 Artifact.
- Spheric Guardian - Start each combat with 3 Artifact.
- Bronze Automaton - Start each combat with 3 Artifact.
- Donu and Deca - Start each combat with 2 (3) Artifact.
- Spire Shield and Spire Spear - Start each combat with 1 (2) Artifact.
- Corrupt Heart - Gains 2 Artifact the first time it uses its Buff move.

- Class: Neutral
- Type: Curse
- Rarity: Special
- Cost: Unplayable

'''Ascender's Bane''' is a Curse that you receive in your starting deck at Ascension levels 10 and higher. 

In combat, it works in the same way as Clumsy; being both Unplayable and Ethereal, it will Exhaust itself at the end of your turn.

Similarly to Necronomicurse, Ascender's Bane cannot be removed in any way; however, it can be exhausted during combat. Omamori will only negate the copy of Ascender's Bane if it is duplicated. Neow cannot remove Ascender's Bane at the start of the game, nor can the Wheel of Change remove it.

# Ascension

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Ascension

is a game mode that adds new challenge modifiers to runs for added difficulty.

In order to unlock 1 for one character, you need to beat all three acts with that character. 

Winning a run in each  will unlock the next  for that character only.

Losing a run will NOT reset any progress or decrease your  number. Losing a run in Act 4 will still unlock the next .

You may play any  level you have unlocked.

All  levels can be played in Custom Mode, but completing them there will not count for your progress in the game.

The negative effects from each  level are cumulative. For example: If you are on3, the disadvantages of 1 and 2 will be in effect as well.

Each  level grants 5% additional score, up to 100% at 20 for the following score bonuses:
- Floors Climbed
- Enemies Killed
- Elites Killed
- Bosses Slain
- Champion
- Perfect
- Beyond Perfect
- Overkill
- C-c-c-combo

Category:Modes
## Modifiers
1 - Elites spawn more often.
- There will be approximately 60% more Elites spawned in a map.

2 - Normal enemies are deadlier.
- Normal enemies deal more damage with their attacks.

3 - Elites are deadlier.
- Elites deal more damage with their attacks.

4 - Bosses are deadlier.
- Bosses deal more damage with their attacks.

5 - Heal less after Boss battles.
- Heal for 75% of missing health instead of 100%.

6 - Start each run damaged. 
- Lose 10% health at the start of each run.

7 - Normal enemies are tougher.
- Normal enemies have more HP. Some gain higher Block. They are overall harder to take down.

8 - Elites are tougher.
- Elites have more HP.

9 - Bosses are tougher.
- Bosses have more HP. Some gain higher Block. They are overall harder to take down.

10 - Start each run cursed.
- Obtain 1 Ascender's Bane at the start of each run.
11 - Start each run with 1 less potion slot.

12 - Upgraded cards appear less often.
- Upgraded cards are 50% less likely to appear in Act 2 (12.5%, down from 25%) and Act 3 (25%, down from 50%).

13 - Poor bosses.
- Bosses drop 25% less gold

14 - Lower max HP.
- -5 for Ironclad, -4 for Silent, Defect, and Watcher

15 - Unfavorable events.
- Many events have less positive outcomes and more severe consequences. For example: More HP loss. Less gold or card as rewards. Guaranteed Curse.

16 - Shops are more costly. 
- Everything costs 10% more.

17 - Normal enemies have more challenging movesets and abilities.

18 - Elites have more challenging movesets and abilities.

19 - Bosses have more challenging movesets and abilities.

20 - Double boss.
- Fight 2 bosses at the end of Act 3
    - After you defeat the first boss that can be seen from the map, you will immediately enter a battle with a different Act 3 boss.

# Augmenter

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Augmenter

**Augmenter** is an event found exclusively in Act 2. You encounter a shady man who wants to do an experiment on you, for science.

## Options

- **[Test J.A.X]**  Obtain a J.A.X.

- **[Become Test Subject]** Choose and Transform 2 cards in your deck.

- **[Ingest Mutagens]** Obtain a Mutagenic Strength.

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| *A man with an eyepatch and a devilish grin strides up to you.* |
| **Shady Man:** ''"Hey there, stranger. Interested in advancing science? I can make you stronger than any training or blessing. You're gonna need it if you're one of those heroes with a death wish."* |
| **Shady Man:** *"Whad'ya say?"* |
| Test J.A.X |
| **Shady Man:** *"Excellent."* |
| *The man hands over a dangerous looking syringe filled with a glowing liquid before skulking off into a shadowy alleyway.* |
| Become Test Subject |
| **Shady Man:** *"Superb."* |
| *The man injects you with three unknown substances and pulls out a notepad. As you begin to feel light-headed, he starts to frantically write down notes.* |
| *Losing track of time completely, by the time you regain your senses, the shady character has disappeared.* |
| Ingest Mutagens |
| **Shady Man:** *"Marvelous."* |
| *You quaff the mysterious substance. Immediately, you are invigorated and feel your muscle fibers'' twitch. |

## Strategy
- If your deck is about losing HP with cards (particularly Ironclad's Rupture deck) or if you are not afraid to pay your HP for more damage (for instance, if your deck can generate a lot of Block to prevent incoming damage, or if you have a steady source of Intangible), consider choosing **[Test J.A.X]** to obtain J.A.X., since it is a fairly powerful source of Strength that can be used repeatedly.
- Mutagenic Strength from **[Ingest Mutagens]** gives you a heavy buff at the start of combat. Consider choosing this option if:
    - You can reliably draw multi-hit attack, or multiple cheap attacks, on the first turn.
    - You have a powerful Innate or Bottled Attack card.
    - You have a Bag of Marbles to apply Vulnerable at the start of the combat.
    - You have a reliable way to obtain Artifact or to remove debuffs on the first turn, to negate Strength Down and retain bonus Strength.
      - Relic such as Clockwork Souvenir and Orange Pellets can help you with this feat.
- If you rely on setting up on the first turn without much attacking, consider avoiding **[Ingest Mutagens]** as Mutagenic Strength would become fairly useless.
- Transforming cards is best when you have Strikes or other bad cards you would like to remove.
    - Keep in mind that transforming a Curse will result in another Curse.

## Trivia
- This event was named "J.A.X. Dealer", and has the internal name of "Drug Dealer". However, its name was changed to "Augmenter" as its effect expanded beyond giving J.A.X., and probably to distance itself from the negative connotation (and possibly censorship) of the word "Dealer".

# Awakened One

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Awakened_One

**Infobox:**
- Name: Awakened One
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/c/c3/Awakened-one-zzz-pretty.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20180110053847
- HP: 300 (Both Phases 1 and 2); 320 (Ascension 9+, both Phases 1 and 2)
- In Party With: 2 Cultists
- Debut Act: Act 3
- Powers: 10 Regen + 1 Curiosity; 2 Strength (Ascension 4+); 15 Regen + 2 Curiosity (Ascension 19+)
- Name: Curiosity
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/e/ec/Icon_Curiosity.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202161844
- Description: Whenever you play a Power card, gains X Strength.
- Type: Buff

-The **Awakened One** is one of the three bosses encountered at the end of Act 3.

## Pattern
### Phase 1 (Unawakened)
Always begins with Slash. Has a 25% chance of using Soul Strike and a 75% chance of using Slash every turn. Slash cannot be used three times in a row and Soul Strike cannot be used twice in a row.

Once its HP reaches 0, it loses Curiosity and the intent instantly changes to Rebirth, then enters Phase 2. Strength buffs from Curiosity are carried over into Phase 2.

| Name | Intent | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Slash |  | Deal 20 damage. |
| Soul Strike |  | Deal 6 x 4 damage. |
| Rebirth |  | Removes all debuffs, interrupts previous intents. |

### Phase 2 (Awakened)
Always starts with Dark Echo. Has a 50% chance of using Tackle and a 50% chance of using Sludge. Cannot use Tackle three times in a row and cannot use Sludge three times in a row.

Defeating the Awakened One in Phase 2 will cause the remaining Cultists to flee.
| Name | Intent | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dark Echo |  | Deal 40 damage. |
| Sludge |  | Deal 18 damage and shuffle 1 Void into the draw pile. |
| Tackle |  | Deal 10 x 3 damage. |
## Tips
The Awakened One is designed to counter decks that utilize Power cards and decks that are designed to deal massive amounts of damage in one turn due to its Curiosity and Rebirth buffs. If your deck heavily relies on these strategies in Act 3, the fight may be more difficult than normal.

Kill the Cultists as soon as possible as they gain Strength each turn after the first. The Awakened One itself is straightforward to handle: match your defense to the specific attack and use the rest of your energy to deal damage. Once you lower it to 0 HP, it will become invulnerable until its next turn while removing debuffs like weakened and vulnerable. Use that turn to ramp up your defense and possibly play power cards that were saved, since The Awakened One will immediately use its Dark Echo attack. Surviving Phase 2 is mostly a matter of surviving Dark Echo -- especially the first one, which could catch unsuspecting characters off-guard. Save any exhaust cards that will help speed up this phase (e.g. Terror).

Watch out for Phase 1's Curiosity ability. Whenever you play a Power, the Awakened One will gain 1 Strength (2 in Ascension 19+). This is especially dangerous with the Soul Strike attack, which will use the Strength bonus four times. Even if you have a Power build, you might want to avoid using them during this phase. Curiosity goes away in Phase 2, so you might want to spam your Powers when the Awakened One enters its invulnerable state between the phases, or as soon as Phase 2 begins.

Use temporary Strength debuffs (like Piercing Wail) right before killing his first form. The debuff will permanently lower Strength in Phase 2, but not below 0.

## Trivia
- The Awakened One is the deity that both the Cultists and the Chosen worship. 
- Matryoshka and Eternal Feather reference this boss in their flavor text.
- It is known that the Awakened One is the crow god Mazaleth according to the Bird-Faced Urn's flavor text.
- There is a Ritual Dagger stuck in the Awakened One's chest.
- The Awakened One may be the end result of a ritual involving a lucky Chosen, as a way to manifest the deity they worship. Evidence to support this theory includes the humanoid hands and body shape of the Awakened One, the name "Chosen", and the blue feathers that appear to be growing out of the body of the Chosen (in contrast to the Cultists, who appear to be only wearing clothes that mimic feathers). There is also the Ritual Dagger, which was used by worshippers of the deity in The Nest event, signaling that the body that houses the Awakened One was stabbed on purpose as part of a cult ritual.
- If you kill the main Awakened One boss without killing the two cultists (both forms, over two turns), the cultists will run away, with the speech bubble "Grr...". Coincidentally (?), this is the same speech bubble the Awakened One uses when they transform.
- Although the two Cultists in party with the Awakened One will run away when the Awakened One dies, they are not Minions and cards with the Fatal keyword will trigger when they are killed. This can be relevant if the Awakened One is the first Boss fought in Act 3 on Ascension 20, or if the player will continue to Act 4. Killing the first phase of the Awakened One will not trigger any Fatal effects, but will trigger on death effects such as Sunder.

# Backstab

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Backstab

**Infobox:**
- Name: Backstab
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/7/7a/Backstab.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016211210
- Class: Silent
- Type: Attack
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Cost: 0
- Effect: Innate.; Deal 11 damage.Exhaust.
- [Backstab+]
- Cost+: 0
- Effect+: Innate.; Deal 15 damage.Exhaust.

**Backstab** is an Uncommon Card for the Silent. It deals damage and exhaust. As an Innate card, it is always drawn on the first turn, taking one spot on your first card drawn. 

## Strategy
Backstab deals a single burst of damage to a single enemy. It does not cost Energy, essentially giving you a single-use free attack. 

With it being Innate, it is guaranteed that you will draw on the first turn, and is included on your draw count. This could be useful on lower floors, as Backstab has a respectable damage against enemy with lower health, but it could cripple you on higher floor since it could take a spot for a potentially more powerful card. Unless you have a appropriate set of Relics, it is not advised to take more than one copy of this card. 

### Synergies
 
- Bag of Marbles: Amplifies Backstab moderate damage up to a more respectable amount, allowing you to one-shot a low-health enemy.
- Akabeko: Similar to Bag of Marbles, Akabeko increases Backstab damage to a respectable amount. While Backstab hits only once, it is a guaranteed first turn draw due to its Innate nature, giving you a guaranteed burst of damage on the first turn.
- Bag of Preparation, Ring of the Snake, and Ring of the Serpent: The additional card draw lessens the drawback from Innate cards taking a space on your first draw.
- Gambling Chip and Gambler's Brew: Allows the player to discard and draw a new card in place of Backstab in case that it is not beneficial.
- Dead Branch: With Backstab having 0 cost, Dead Branch turns it into free damage and a card generation, lessens the drawback from its Innate nature by giving you a chance to get a more beneficial card for free.
- Shuriken and Kunai: Backstab gives you a reliable counter on these relic for free on the first turn. Along with some Attack cards you could potentially drawn on the first turn, they could gives you a momentum you need to scale the fight.
- Can help you take down minions of Gremlin Leader and Reptomancer in order to steer them to waste a turn summoning more minions.

 
- A strange strategy with Shuriken and Kunai comes from the fact that Backstab is free attack guaranteed to be drawn in the first turn, and taking 3 copies of them while having either of those relics guarantees that you could trigger Strength and/or Dexterity on the first turn for free while also dealing a burst of 33-45 damage. While those bonus can help you scale the fight, having a psuedo-Ninja Scroll that takes up 3 cards of your initial draw makes it more risky on a higher floor with more aggressive and punishing enemies.

## Trivia
- The Beta Art for this card depicts a Caesar salad, because Julius Caesar is a historical figure who was famously betrayed and stabbed to death by his senators on the Ides of March.

# Bag of Marbles

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Bag_of_Marbles

**Infobox:**
- Name: Bag of Marbles
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/f/f5/BagofMarbles.png/revision/latest?cb=20190923232819
- Description: At the start of each combat, apply 1 Vulnerable to ALL enemies.
- Flavor: A once popular toy in the City. Useful for throwing enemies off balance.
- Rarity: Common
- Class: Any

The Bag of Marbles is a common relic that applies 1 Vulnerable to all enemies at the start of each combat.

## Strategy
The Bag of Marbles naturally benefits decks with a turn 1 that involves dealing damage, by allowing the player to deal even more damage. Even if your turn 1 does not focus on dealing damage, the Vulnerable will help negate some Artifact charges on certain enemies, allowing your subsequent turns to be more powerful.

## Synergy

- Bottled Flame: If a powerful attack is bottled, the Vulnerable will allow that attack to become even more powerful.
- Innate attacks, such as Backstab, Dramatic Entrance and Mind Blast: Innate attacks are able to benefit from Vulnerable and deal more damage.
- Champion Belt: Applies Weak in addition to the Vulnerable. This makes turn 1 a lot safer, as well as speeding up Artifact negation by a large margin.
- Turn 1 Energy relics, such as Lantern and Ancient Tea Set: More Energy allows you to play more attack cards that benefit from Vulnerable.
- Anchor: Protects you for your first turn, allowing you to take advantage of Vulnerable.
- Bag of Preparation, Ring of the Snake and Ring of the Serpent: More card draw allows you to play more attacks.
- Ninja Scroll: Adds free attacks to your hand that benefit from Vulnerable.
- Mutagenic Strength: Makes all of your attacks played on turn 1 stronger.
- Akabeko: increases damage of your first attack, which is also amplified by Vulnerable.

- Bottled Lightning, Bottled Tornado and any Innate powers or skills, such as Infinite Blades+ and Boot Sequence: Innate cards take up some of your draw, therefore you are much less likely to draw attacks that benefit from Vulnerable.
- Gremlin Visage: Greatly lowers the amount of damage you can do on turn 1, thus making the Vulnerable a lot less useful.

Relic Navbox

# Bag of Preparation

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Bag_of_Preparation

**Infobox:**
- Name: Bag of Preparation
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/a/ad/BagofPreparation.png/revision/latest?cb=20200203150012
- Description: At the start of each combat, draw 2 additional cards.
- Flavor: Oversized adventurer's pack. Has many pockets and straps.
- Rarity: Common
- Class: Any

The Bag of Preparation is a common relic that draws an additional 2 cards at the start of each combat. Its effect is identical to the Ring of the Snake, the Silent's default starting relic. 

## Strategy
This relic is very powerful despite its rarity. Its effect synergizes with many other relics and cards, and the additional card draw increases the potency of your first turn. However, if you draw too many key cards and are unable to play them all, this relic could possibly set you back for a few turns.

## Interactions
 
- Cloak Clasp: Gives additional protection at the end of your first turn, which is generally the turn in which you are most vulnerable.
- Spirit Shield: Greatly increases the impact of a Spirit Shield played on the first turn. 
- Ring of the Snake, Ring of the Serpent, Snecko Eye: Additional draw from these relics makes your turn 1 very powerful, as you will have 9 cards in your hand (8 with Ring of the Serpent).  
- Gambling Chip: You can mulligan additional cards drawn by Bag of Preparation.
- Lantern and Ancient Tea Set: The extra Energy for the first turn along with additional card draw from Bag of Preparation greatly increases the impact of your first turn.
- Mutagenic Strength: More Strength for your first turn in addition to the card draw makes your turn 1 attacks much more potent.

 
- Ninja Scroll and Holy Water: The generated cards takes priority over Bag of Preparation, and could clog your hand as you cannot have more than 10 cards on your hand at a time, potentially rendering additional draw useless.

## Trivia
- The relic's art shows the same backpack as the card Prepared.

# Basic

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Basic

**Basic cards** are the cards in the default starting deck for your class. Basic cards are not normally acquirable otherwise, except by duplication (Duplicator and Dolly's Mirror), and from the Match and Keep event.

## Ironclad
- 1× Bash
- 5× Strikes
- 4× Defends

## Silent
- 1× Neutralize
- 1× Survivor
- 5× Strikes
- 5× Defends

## The Defect
- 1× Dualcast
- 1× Zap
- 4× Strikes
- 4× Defends

## Watcher
- 1x Eruption
- 1x Vigilance
- 4x Strikes
- 4x Defends

## Trivia

- The Ironclad is the only class with an uneven number of Strikes to Defends, with 5 and 4 respectively.
- The Silent starts with the most Basic cards, ⁣with 12 instead of 10. This is because of her starting relic, Ring of the Snake, drawing 2 cards at the start of combat.

# Big Fish

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Big_Fish

**Big Fish** is an event found exclusively in Act 1. The player must select one of three goodies dangling from the dungeon ceiling.

## Options

- **[Banana]** Heal 1/3 of your max HP.
    - If the player's HP is not divisible by 3, the HP gain is rounded down.

- **[Donut]** Max HP +5.
    - Like all HP gain, the extra hit points are healed when you get them.

- **[Box]** Receive a Relic. Become Cursed: Regret.
    - The Relic is a randomly-selected Common, Uncommon or Rare Relic.

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| *As you make your way down a long corridor you see a banana, a donut, and a box floating about. No... upon closer inspection they are tied to strings coming from holes in the ceiling. There is a quiet* cackling *from above as you approach the objects.* |
| *What do you do?* |
| Banana |
| *You eat the banana. It is nutritious and slightly magical, healing you.* |
| Donut |
| *You eat the donut. It really hits the spot! Your Max HP increases.* |
| Box |
| *You grab the box. Inside you find a relic!* |
| *However, you really craved the donut...* |
| *You are filled with sadness, but mostly regret.* |

## Strategy

**[Donut]** is generally the best choice. The player probably does not need much healing in Act 1, and Regret is a particularly nasty Curse.

If the path is close to a Merchant encounter, consider taking the Relic from **[Box]** - simply remove Regret before facing the boss. Also, if you haveOmamori, Du-Vu Doll, or Darkstone Periapt, they can help negate or reap benefit from obtaining Regret.

Black Star is a Boss Relic. It causes elites to drop two relics instead of only one. Black Star has no effect in events, even though e.g. Preserved Insect triggers in Dead Adventurer and The Colosseum.

The extra relic from Black Star will *never* be Peace Pipe, Shovel, or Girya. (Likely to avoid the edge case where both relic drops provide rest site option when the player already have one, thus exceeding the limit of three extra rest site options.)

Has great synergy with the "elite killer relics": Preserved Insect, Sling of Courage (can only be found in shops) and Slaver's Collar (boss relic).

## Trivia
Black Star's flavor text references the song of the same name by David Bowie. The song includes the lyric "In the villa of Ormen, stands a solitary candle." Ormen means serpent in Norwegian, and it is the name of a village in Norway.

**Blade Dance** is one of the most common ways to obtain Shivs for the Silent. Since multiple Shivs are created, cards boosting Shivs or multiple attacks are very effective with Blade Dance. # Blasphemy

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Blasphemy

**Infobox:**
- Name: Blasphemy
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/2/22/Blasphemy.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20191106145537
- Class: Watcher
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Rare
- Cost: 1
- Effect: Enter Divinity. Die next turn. Exhaust
- [Blasphemy+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: Retain. Enter Divinity. Die next turn. Exhaust
- Name: Blasphemer
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/5/56/Icon_Blasphemy.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202161412
- Description: At the start of your turn, die.
- Type: Technically a Buff.
- Stacking; Behavior: none

CardAutobox
**Blasphemy** is a Rare Skill for the Watcher. When played, she enters Divinity immediately without needing to accumulate any Mantra. However, she gets the Blasphemer buff, which instantly kills her at the start of the player's next turn. The card is Exhausted upon use, meaning it can only be played once per battle unless the player has Exhume or the Strange Spoon.  

Upgrading the card to **Blasphemy+** causes it to Retain, allowing the player to keep it in their hand for the exact right turn and hand to finish the battle.

## Strategy

- Obviously, if the player does not plan to end the fight the turn Blasphemy is used, it should not be played **unless** the player has Intangible, Buffer, or another source of death prevention such as a Fairy in a Bottle.
- Blasphemy synergizes extremely well with cards such as Signature Move due to its ability to instantly allow the Watcher to enter Divinity, which will triple output damage.
    - Blasphemy also synergizes well with low-cost cards that either deal damage or draw other cards, such as Cut Through Fate and Sands of Time, as Divinity lasts for one turn, meaning drawing cheap cards with decent attack power is a boon.
- By far, the worst cards to use with Blasphemy are Vault, and Meditate, as they immediately end your turn for setting up the next turn. For all intents and purposes, there is no next turn.

## Interactions

- Since the Blasphemer effect is technically a buff, it ***cannot*** be negated by Artifact, nor can it be cleansed by Orange Pellets.
- Since the damage is taken at the start of the next turn, rather than the end of the current turn, Intangible can only prevent it if you will have it next turn (either by having at least two stacks, or by having Incense Burner's counter at 5).

# Blights

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Blights

Blights are detrimental passive items, like a negative version of relics. They appear in Endless Mode. They are forced onto the player by Neow each time they defeat Act 3 bosses, and from blight chests, if the Blight Chests mod is on.
## Neow's Blights
Each time the player defeats the Act 3 boss and loops back to Act 1, they obtain a set of blights from Neow. The following is a list of blights that can be obtained from Neow.
| Image | Title | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | Grotesque Trophy | Upon pickup, obtain 3 Prides. |
|  | Mimic Infestation | Treasure rooms in future acts are replaced by Elites. Elites no longer drop Relics. |
|  | Muzzle | You can no longer increase your Max HP. All healing is halved. |
|  | Spear of Blight | Enemies deal 100% more damage. |
|  | Shield of Blight | Enemies have 50% more HP. |
|  | Time Maze | You cannot play more than 15 cards per turn.[1] |
[1] Curses do not count towards Time Maze's 15-card limit.

### Order
The set of blights that player obtains from Neow is in the following order.

#### 1st set

- Spear of Blight starts at a 100% increase
- Shield of Blight starts at a 50% increase
- Mimic Infestation

#### 2nd set

- Spear of Blight increases from 100% to 175%
- Shield of Blight increases from 50% to 100%
- Time Maze

#### 3rd set

- Spear of Blight increases from 175% to 250%
- Shield of Blight increases from 100% to 150%
- Muzzle

#### 4th set and afterwards

- Spear of Blight increases by 75% each set
- Shield of Blight increases by 50% each set
- Grotesque Trophy each set

## Blight Chests

With Blight Chests mod turned on, each boss chest from the 4th chest onward is replaced by a Blight Chest, where the player is forced to choose 1 from 2 random Blights to obtain (cannot skip). The following is a list of blights that can be obtained from Blight Chests. All Blights from Blight Chests stack its effect if more than 1 copy is obtained, like Spear and Shield blights.
| Image | Title | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | Accursed | Whenever you defeat a Boss, obtain 2 random Curses. |
|  | Ancient Augmentation | Enemies start combat with 1 Artifact, 10 Plated Armor, and 10 Regenerate. |
|  | Durian | Lose 50% of your Max HP. |
|  | Hauntings | Enemies start combat with 1 Intangible. |
|  | Scatterbrain | Draw 1 less card a turn. |
|  | Twisting Mind | At the end of your turn, add 1 random Status card to the top of your draw pile. |
|  | Void Essence | Lose 1 Energy permanently. |

## Strategy
So, you want new challenge as the usual Ascension 20 has become boring and too easy.

The Endless mode allows you to collect every relic, every card for your ultimate deck if you can survive long enough, as well as give you additional problems to overcome, as following.

- Time Maze: You cannot use any infinite combo. This should not be that much of a problem if you can consistently defeat the Timer Eater boss who imposes a tighter restriction of 12 card plays per turn.
- You cannot gain max HP. At an arbitrary long point of time in the run, the enemies become strong enough that any damage they deal will kill you, as well as become more durable. You will need to come up with a way to kill your enemies (or boss) in your first turn, or sustainably reduce the damage to manageable level, e.g. Wraith Form, Buffer 
- Innate curses that clog your first turn and generate themselves in your deck if you cannot deal with them properly. Fortunately, you can remove them at shop or rest site using Peace Pipe.
Up to this point, you are probably already familiar with the basics of surviving through A20. Block can stack no more than 999, and thus at some point enemies will deal such high damage that it goes beyond your max block. So eventually, Wraith Form and/or Buffer becomes a must in your deck build. Then there's the increasingly higher HP. Any infinite combo has a maximum damage output if only 15 cards are allowed for each turn. However, such builds are still available, as Wraith Form or Buffer can easily be infinetly duplicated with Nightmare strategy. Searing Blow is a card that can be infinitely upgraded, with each upgrade increasing more damage than the previous one. So at some point in the run, the upgrade of Searing Blow grants so much extra damage, that it outruns the Shield of Blight, making the player capable of one-shotting everything. Bottled Flame allows Searing Blow to always show up at turn 1.

### Blight chests mod
You have came up with plans and strategies to survive the usual endless mode, indefinitely. Welcome to the ultimate challenge in the game: Endless mode with Blight chests mod.

In this configuration, you can collect only 3 boss relics, as any chest after the first 3 gives you blights instead. In additional to the usual endless mode's problem, you will have to deal with the new blights, as following.

| Image | Title | Problem (at an arbitrary long point of time in the run) and possible solution |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | Accursed | You have too many innate Writhe cards that they sometimes occupy your entire first hand and you cannot play anything on your first turn. You will not have enough opportunities (shop/rest site) to remove them. A combination of Blue Candle, Tungsten Rod and Unceasing Top will allow you to exhaust the innate curses until you get your first usable (innate) card, but then you will be put in topdeck mode and have to use whatever you draw, which severely limits what strategy you can employ to workaround the other challenges from other blights. Normality can become fatal in topdeck mode as it immediately denies further card play. |
|  | Ancient Augmentation | You can no longer apply any debuff to any enemy. Searing Blow + Corpse Explosion strategy no longer works. First-turn-kill decks will become harder to guarantee wins on first turn, and you have to deal with all the problems on the turns afterwards. However it is easily manageable using other strategies. |
|  | Durian | Your max HP is 1. You will have to deal with combat without taking any damage. Monsters with Thorns can damage you without taking their turn, which may stop some first turn kill decks if encountering fight with more 2 or more monsters with Thorns. There are many ways to prevent damage, but the most reliable method would be Tungsten Rod and any source of Intangible, which gives you damage/HP loss immunity. |
|  | Hauntings | You will have to survive for however many turn it take each combat before you can deal damage normally. Can be solved using the same solution as with Durian, if you can find a way to sustainably generate Intangible, like duplicating[1] Wraith Form for example. |
|  | Scatterbrain | You cannot draw cards at the start of your turn. Innate and bottled cards still show up on your first turn. You can rely on Unceasing Top to always have card to play, but that puts you in topdeck mode. While you cannot draw any card normally, you still have some options for card manipulation: - Seek to add specific card to your hand (duplicate it if you run out, or collect as many copies as you need, since you can play Seek -> 1 card + another Seek in your deck), - Hologram to add card back to your hand from your discard pile. - Card like Well-Laid Plans to keep cards for your next turn. You can use Nightmare to preload your hand on the next turn. There is also Runic Pyramid to prevent you from discard your hand at the end of your turn, but you will have to manually put away cards to your discard pile with Concentrate as there are only 10 card slots in your hand. A bottled Seek will allow you to easily set up your card manipulation mechanics. |
|  | Twisting Mind | Clogs your draw with Status cards after your first turn. Like Accursed, you can exhaust them until you get a usable card with Medical Kit and Unceasing Top, but that puts you in topdeck mode. This is not a problem if you can manually manipulate your card, like with Scatterbrain, without drawing them. |
|  | Void Essence | Subtracts directly from the number of energies you passively gain each turn, i.e. the number 3 on your energy UI assuming no boss relic. Thus, boss relics that increase this number are wasted with a large stack of this blight. Other energy relics still work, e.g. Lantern still works on your first turn or Violet Lotus that triggers upon exiting Calm. There are many solutions for this problem, for example, Aggregate and Double Energy in combination with Ice Cream. |
[1] A common card manipulation in endless mode is the ability to duplicate any card you want. You need to have the target card and use Nightmare on it to duplicate it. Since Nightmare exhausts itself on use, you will need to have 2 copies of Nightmare so you can duplicate it before you run out if it. For Power and Attack cards specifically, you can simply use Dual Wield.

Fortunately, you can choose 1 blight to ignore, as the blight chests offer 2 choices (if the blight you want to ignore appears in 1 of the choices, you choose the other).

Category:Debuffs

# Block

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Block

Block is the amount of attack damage a character can take before the damage affects their HP.

Block is gained primarily through Skills, such as Defend.  However, some attacks, such as Dash grant block, and the Defect's Frost Orbs also grant Block. All block is typically removed at the start of your turn. However, some block can be carried over to the next turn with Dodge and Roll or with one of these buffs or relics:
- Blur: Grants the Blur buff, which prevents you from losing any Block at the start of next turn. Can be stacked.
- Barricade: Grants the Barricade buff, which prevents you from losing any Block at the start of your turn for the rest of this combat.
- Calipers: Causes you to lose 15 Block at the start of each turn instead of all of it. Overridden by Blur and Barricade.
Maximum Block is capped at 999.
Category:Game Mechanics
## Sources of damage that ignore block
In general, any card or effect that reads "Lose X HP" ignores Block.

Effects and cards that ignore an enemy's block:
- Poison
- Choke
- Melter does not directly ignore block, but removes all of it instead, so the block is technically ignored.
- Pressure Points
- Although not technically a damage, Judgment also ignores block if the target's health is low enough.

Effects and cards that ignore your block:
- Various Ironclad Cards that mention "Lose X HP"
- Playing any cards with Pain in your hand
- Ending your turn with Regret in your hand
- J.A.X.
- Playing any curse with Blue Candle

**Blood for Blood** is an Attack card for the Ironclad. It deals 18 damage, costs 1 less Energy for each bit of HP lost during the current combat.

Upon upgrade, it gains 4 damage and costs 1 less energy.

## Mechanics

- Because its cost lowers from lost HP, rather than damage, it is affected by effects like Offering and Combust.
- The cost decreases by the number of times you lose HP, not the amount of HP lost.
- If this card is created during combat (such as through Dead Branch, Attack Potion, or Foreign Influence), it will account for HP lost before it existed, unlike Masterful Stab.
- HP loss that is reduced to 0 by an effect such as Tungsten Rod does not lower the card's cost.

**Bludgeon** is a Rare Attack card for the Ironclad. It deals 32 damage.

Upon upgrade, it deals 10 more damage.

## Strategy

Bludgeon features a good energy-damage ratio, with nearly 11 damage per energy before being upgraded, and 14 when after being upgraded. However, its high energy cost means you can not put up a defense without some additional source of energy, and its applications with Double Tap are more limited. Bludgeon is more helpful against the low health of Act 1 enemies, and is very useful for them if obtained early, as it can finish encounters early with no risk for retaliation. Snecko Eye is great with Bludgeon, as having an average energy cost of 1.5 makes it have much better value.

# Blue Candle

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Blue_Candle

**Infobox:**
- Name: Blue Candle
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/1/1b/BlueCandle.png/revision/latest?cb=20190923232937
- Description: Curse cards can now be played. Playing a Curse will make you lose 1 HP and Exhausts the card.
- Flavor: The flame ignites when shrouded in darkness.
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Class: Any

Allows playing Curses, similar to what Medical Kit does for statuses but with an extra cost.

Playing a Curse does not cost any Energy.

## Tips

- "Lose 1 HP" is not damage and will ignore Block. However, it can be reduced by Tungsten Rod.
- If the Necronomicurse is played, a new one will be added to your hand. While this means you can't escape the Necronomicurse, you can play it as many times as you want, and that interaction can be exploited in a number of ways. It allows you to take arbitrary amounts of damage in one-damage increments, triggering useful on-damage effects like Rupture or Blood for Blood; each play still counts as an exhaust, so it will trigger on-exhaust effects like Dead Branch, Dark Embrace, Charon's Ashes; and each one counts as a card played, so it can trigger things like Panache or A Thousand Cuts.

## Interactions
- Strange Spoon will cause Curses to sometimes not be exhausted, but instead discarded. The HP is still lost.

## Trivia
- This relic is a reference to the Blue Candle item from The Legend of Zelda.
