# Bonfire Spirits

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Bonfire_Spirits

**Bonfire Spirits** is an event that can appear in Act 1, Act 2, and Act 3. You encounter an enchanted bonfire with dancing spirits. 

## Options

- **[Offer]** Choose a card in your deck and offer it to the spirits. The offered card will be removed from your deck, and you will receive a reward based on the card's rarity.

| Offer | Receive |
| --- | --- |
| Curse | Spirit Poop |
| Basic card | (Nothing) |
| Common OR Special card | Heal 5 HP |
| Uncommon card | Heal to full |
| Rare card | Heal to full + 10 max HP |

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| *You happen upon a group of what looks like purple fire spirits dancing around a large bonfire.* |
| *The spirits toss small bones and fragments into the fire, which brilliantly erupts each time. As you approach, the spirits all turn to you, expectantly...* |
| Offer |
| *You toss an offering into the bonfire.* |
| If you offer a Curse |
| If you offer a Basic card or are unable to offer any cards |
| *The spirits seem to be ignoring you now. Disappointing...* |
| If you offer a Common or Special card |
| *The spirits continue dancing. You feel slightly warmer from their presence..* |
| *You heal 5 HP.* |
| If you offer an Uncommon card |
| *The spirits dance around you excitedly, filling you with a sense of warmth.* |
| *You are healed to full HP.* |
| If you offer a Rare card |
| *The spirits dance around you excitedly before merging into your form, filling you with warmth and strength.* |
| *Your Max HP increases by 10 and you are healed to full HP.'' |

## Strategy

This event can be exploited for a quick healing or for a free card removal. Remember that offering a Common card still heals you for 5 HP, and removing a Basic card does not have any major downside. You can also use this event to remove a Curse, especially powerful ones like Normality or Pain, as the Spirit Poop that this event yields does not have any major gameplay effect except that it will reduce your score by 1.

In endless mode, removing Pride provide a common heal and is thus advisable if you aren't rid of them through other card removal sources yet.

## Notes

- Offering a removable Curse, with the exception of Pride (which is counted as a Special card), will give you Spirit Poop. Even though Spirit Poop is useless, you still get to remove a Curse from your deck. 
    - The only effect of Spirit Poop has, if you still have it by the end of the game, is that it gives a "Poopy" modifier to your score, which reduces your total score by 1.
- Basic cards are the default cards from your starting deck.
    - Strike
    - Defend
    - Bash
    - Neutralize
    - Survivor
    - Dualcast
    - Zap
    - Eruption
    - Vigilance
- Special cards (those not obtainable through card rewards, such as Pride or J.A.X.) behave exactly like Commons, and will heal the player for five HP.

# Book of Stabbing

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Book_of_Stabbing

**Infobox:**
- Name: Book of Stabbing
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/b/b9/Book-of-stabbing-pretty.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20210408115512
- HP: 160-162; 168-172 (Ascension 8+)
- In Party With: None
- Debut Act: Act 2
- Powers: Painful Stabs

The **Book of Stabbing** is an Elite encounter found in Act 2 of the Spire. Its scaling multi-hit attack, strong single-hit attacks, and ability to shuffle many Wounds into your discard pile make it a fearsome foe.

## Pattern
Every turn, the Book of Stabbing has an 85% chance of using Multi-Stab and a 15% chance of using Single Stab. Whenever you receive unblocked damage from one of its attacks, a Wound is shuffled into your discard pile.

Cannot use Multi-Stab 3 times in a row. Cannot use Single Stab twice in a row.

| Name | Intent | Effect | Ascension 3+ | Ascension 18+ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Multi-Stab |  | Deals 6 x N* damage. | Deals 7 x N* damage. | Deals 7 x N** damage. |
| Single Stab |  | Deals 21 damage. | Deals 24 damage. | Deals 24 damage. |
*N is equal to 2 plus the number of times Multi-Stab has been previously used in the fight.

**On Ascension 18+, N increments even on the Single Stab attack.

## Tips
- It is important to try and kill the Book as quickly as possible, because its attacks will only get worse and can become overwhelming.
- The Book suffers greatly against Weak, Thorns, and Strength reduction due to its scaling being solely said multi-hit attacks and its lack of ability to apply any kind of debuff on the player to reduce their ability to Block.
    - The Ironclad fares fairly well against the Book as he has a lot of powerful Block cards, can obtain Disarm to permanently reduce the Book's Strength, and can obtain Clothesline, Intimidate, and Uppercut to apply Weak.
    - The Silent is arguably the best character against the Book. Her access to Footwork and multiple cheap Block cards allow her to easier stack Block against the Book. Leg Sweep not only grants a huge Block, but also apply a large number of Weak. Neutralize and Sucker Punch are cheap attacks that apply Weak. Piercing Wail can shut down a Multi-Stab attack. Caltrops deals a large damage against Multi-Stab. Lastly, Malaise can potentially shut down the Book for the entirety of the fight.
    - The Defect has a harder time against the Book as it mainly relies on slowly scaling with Orbs, Creative AI, or Claw. Consider dealing a large amount of damage by invoking Lightning or Dark multiple times to finish off the Book quickly. Biased Cognition can also be used to give said Orbs a burst of damage and Frost an ability to generates a large Block against the Book.
    - The Watcher can deal with the Book quite well with her ability to burst it down during Wrath or Divinity using cards with high base damage such as Ragnarok and Wheel Kick. She can also gain a large number of Block using Mental Fortress, Nirvana, Talk to the Hand, or Wallop. Wave of the Hand can also apply a large number of Weak in a single use.

# Bosses

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Bosses

**Bosses** are incredibly difficult monsters that are encountered at the end of each Act. Compared to both normal monsters and elites, bosses typically sport a much higher health pool, much more damaging attacks, and utilize special gimmicks that either heavily cripple the player's deck or considerably buff themselves. Every boss has a unique portrait visible at the top of the Spire map, which can help plan a deck accordingly. The preceding map location will always be a Rest Site, allowing the player to heal before the fight; the only exception to this is the Corrupt Heart in Act 4 which always has a special elite encounter before it.

One boss is fought at the end of each Act. To advance to the next Act, the boss must successfully be defeated. At the end of Act 3, two bosses are fought in a row at Ascension 20.

Upon defeating the Act 1 and Act 2 bosses, the player is rewarded with gold, a choice between three rare cards, a choice between three boss relics, and occasionally, a random potion. The Act 3 and Act 4 bosses do not award the player any consumables or cards. The player is also healed to full health (75% of missing health starting at Ascension 5) at the end of every boss battle.

Slaying a boss will add 50 points to a run's score. Slaying a boss without taking damage, not including self-damaging cards such as Offering, adds an additional 50 points. Slaying all three bosses without taking any damage adds 200 points and overrides any previous flawlessness bonus.

Some relics will activate during boss fights:

- Pantograph will heal the player for 25 HP at the start of each boss combat.
- Slaver's Collar will give the player an additional Energy at the start of their turn.

Conversely, relics such as the Wing Boots cannot be used to skip boss fights, as all paths in an Act lead to the floor that contains the boss.

During the Mind Bloom Event in Act 3, choosing the **[I Am War]** option starts a fight with a random Act 1 boss for a random rare relic. This boss fight does not add towards the run's score, but does activate the Pantograph and Slaver's Collar relics.

The Act 4 boss cannot be fought on the first playthrough of any character minus the Watcher. To fight the Act 4 boss, the player must defeat the Act 3 boss with the Ironclad, the Silent, and the Defect at least once.

## Act 1
One of these bosses will appear on Floor 16.

# Bottled Flame

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Bottled_Flame

**Infobox:**
- Name: Bottled Flame
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/f/f1/BottledFlame.png/revision/latest?cb=20200203150918
- Description: Upon pick up, choose an Attack. Start each combat with this card in your hand.
- Flavor: Inside the bottle resides a flame that eternally burns.
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Class: Any

Upon pick up, choose an Attack card. At the start of combat, it will be in your hand.

The card is added to your normal starting hand. It takes the place of a drawn card. It is still considered to be drawn, so Snecko Eye does randomise its cost.

This relic will not appear if all your attack cards are starter-type.

Bottled Flame is one of the three **Bottle Relics**. All Bottle Relics let the user choose a card of one type and start each combat with that card in hand. Bottled Flame's effect is not the same as Innate. Duplicating a Bottled card will NOT draw the copy at the start of your hand (whereas it would if the card had Innate).

The Bottled card can not be removed from your deck, however, the card that you assign to this relic can still be transformed, and the new card will not be assigned to Bottled Flame in place of previous card. However description of relic still will be "Start each combat with 'Name of previous card' in your hand." This is a visual bug, as this relic will now have no effect.

- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/a/ac/BottledTornado.png/revision/latest?cb=20200203150935
- Description: Upon pick up, choose a Power card. Start each combat with this card in your hand.
- Flavor: The bottle gently hums and whirs.
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Class: Any

Upon pick up, choose a Power card. At the start of combat, it will be in your hand.

The card is added to your normal starting hand. It takes the place of a drawn card. It is still considered to be drawn, so Snecko Eye does randomise its cost.

This relic will not appear if there is no power in the deck.

Bottled Tornado is one of the three **Bottle Relics**. All Bottle Relics let the user choose a card of one type and start each combat with that card in hand. Bottled Tornado's effect is not the same as Innate. Duplicating a Bottled card will NOT draw the copy at the start of your hand (whereas it would if the card had Innate). It can only appear if your deck has at least 1 Power card.

The Bottled card can not be removed from your deck, however, the card that you assign to this relic can still be transformed, and the new card will not be assigned to Bottled Tornado in place of previous card. However description of relic still will be "Start each combat with 'Name of previous card' in your hand." This is a visual bug, as this relic will now have no effect.

Bottled Tornado is an Uncommon Relic.

# Bouncing Flask

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Bouncing_Flask

**Infobox:**
- Name: Bouncing Flask
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/3/3c/BouncingFlask.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016211321
- Class: Silent
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Cost: 2
- Effect: Apply 3 Poison to a random enemy 3 times.
- [Bouncing Flask+]
- Cost+: 2
- Effect+: Apply 3 Poison to a random enemy 4 times.

## Strategy
Bouncing Flask is a good source of single-target poison damage, as it adds 9 (12) Poison total if there is one enemy.

Bouncing Flask is less effective when there are multiple enemies, both because each enemy gets less Poison and because the Poison is applied randomly.

## Interactions

- Each bounce counts as a separate application of Poison. This means each bounce can remove 1 Artifact, apply additional damage from Sadistic Nature (up to 28 damage if both are upgraded), or add the bonus +1 poison from Snecko Skull (+3/+4 additional poison).

# Brimstone

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Brimstone

**Infobox:**
- Name: Brimstone
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/2/25/Brimstone.png/revision/latest?cb=20200203154018
- Description: At the start of your turn, gain 2 Strength and ALL enemies gain 1 Strength.
- Flavor: Emanates an infernal heat.
- Rarity: Shop
- Class: Ironclad

## Strategy
Brimstone works best if you have a deck that can make the most use of its Strength gain.  Cards like Sword Boomerang, Twin Strike, and Heavy Blade receive the damage boost 2-5 more times than other attacks, and Limit Break can be used to rapidly increase your strength even further. Reaper also works well with Brimstone, as the additional strength allows you to regain more health.

Players who intend to face the Corrupt Heart in Act 4 will want to consider how they can mitigate the enemy strength buff, since that boss has an attack that hits 12(15) times.  Any increase to the Heart's Strength makes this attack far more deadly, so cards like Disarm or Dark Shackles are quality pick ups. As with any build, Intangible and Weak can make the incoming damage more manageable.

# Bronze Automaton

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Bronze_Automaton

**Infobox:**
- Name: Bronze Automaton
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/e/e7/Bronze-automoton-pretty.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20180110053857
- HP: 300; 320 (Ascension 9+)
- In Party With: None
- Debut Act: Act 2
- Powers: Artifact 3
- Name: Bronze Orb
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/1/11/Bonrze-orb-pretty.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20180110053904
- HP: 52-58; 54-60 (Ascension 9+)
- In Party With: Only summoned by Bronze Automaton
- Debut Act: Act 2
- Powers: None

-The **Bronze Automaton** is one of the three bosses encountered at the end of Act 2.

It spawns minions to steal the players' cards and uses a powerful move called Hyper Beam to attempt to kill the player. Depending on which cards the orbs steal, this fight can be very dangerous.
## Pattern
Always starts with Spawn Orbs, then repeats the following:

1. Flail
1. Boost
1. Flail
1. Boost
1. HYPER BEAM
1. Stunned (does nothing)

On Ascension 19 and higher, Stunned is replaced with Boost.

| Name | Intent | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Spawn Orbs |  | Spawns 2 Bronze Orbs. |
| Boost |  | Gain 3 Strength and 9 Block. |
| Gain 4 Strength and 9Block. |  |  |
| Gain 4 Strength and 12 Block. |  |  |
| Flail |  | Deals 7 x 2 damage. |
| Deals 8 x 2 damage. |  |  |
| HYPER BEAM |  | Deals 45 damage. |
| Deals 50damage. |  |  |

## Bronze Orb
A Minion spawned by the Bronze Automaton.

### Pattern
Has a 75% chance of using Stasis, 7.5% chance of using Beam and 17.5% chance of using Support Beam every turn.

After Stasis is used, will now have a 70% chance of using Support Beam and a 30% chance of using Beam every turn. It cannot use the same move 3 times in a row.

Destroying a Bronze Orb that has stolen a card from you via Stasis will return the card into your hand in the same turn.

Note that cards in stasis are completely unaffected by any effect that would usually influence them. For example, Masterful Stab's cost will not increase if you are hit while it is in stasis.

| Name | Intent | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stasis |  | Steals the rarest card in the draw pile, or from the discard pile if the draw pile is empty. |
| Beam |  | Deals 8 damage. |
| Support Beam |  | Gives Bronze Automaton 12 Block. |

## Trivia
- The Hyper Beam attack is a reference to the Pokémon games, in which Hyper Beam is one of the strongest moves in existence, after which the user also has to skip the next turn to recharge.
    - It also shares its name with a Defect card of similar effect, both being powerful attacks that greatly cripple their users.
- The Bronze Orb shows a slight resemblance to the Sentry, even though there is no clear connection shown in-game.

# Bronze Scales

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Bronze_Scales

**Infobox:**
- Name: Bronze Scales
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/3/3e/BronzeScales.png/revision/latest?cb=20190923233120
- Description: Start each combat with 3 Thorns.
- Flavor: The sharp scales of the Guardian. Rearranges itself to protect its user.
- Rarity: Common
- Class: Any

**Bronze Scales** is a common relic that gives your character 3 Thorns at the start of each combat. This means every time an enemy lands a hit on you, blocked or not, they will take 3 damage.

## Strategy

Since it grants Thorns, enemies will take damage every time they land a hit on your character, whether it deals damage or not. This makes this relic especially effective against enemies that rely on multiple-hits attacks such as Book of Stabbing, Byrds, Snake Plant, and Corrupt Heart.

Also, since the enemy's Block fades at the start of their turn, it means that they have no way to prevent Thorns from directly damaging their HP.

## Synergy

 
- Block: Protects yourself from damage while dealing damage against enemy hits.
- Stacks fully with Caltrops, increases the potency of Thorns even further.
- Complements nicely with Flame Barrier, which itself grants a hefty amount of Block to prevent damage and has an effect similar to Thorns tied to it, which increases the damage against enemy hits even further.
- Reducing enemy Strength or applying Weak allows you to take more hits without receiving much damage. Consider cards like Disarm, Malaise, Piercing Wail, Blind, or Dark Shackles.

## Trivia
- The flavor text says that these scales belong to The Guardian. However, The Guardian's Sharp Hide buff works differently than Thorns, dealing damage to the player per attack card played instead of per hit landed.

# Buffs

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Buffs

A **buff** is a positive effect given to the character by certain Cards, Potions, or Relics. Buffs can also be applied to enemies through their moves or certain Relics, or they can simply start combat with the buff. All buffs are removed at the end of combat and do not carry over to the next fight. Certain relics (for example, Girya) apply buffs at the start of combat.

Buffs may stack by duration, lasting X turns, or by intensity, applying their effect with X power. Some buffs do not stack at all. However, most stack by intensity.

## Shared Buffs
Buffs that can be found from multiple sources in the game, both in the player's arsenal and on enemies.

# Bullet Time

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Bullet_Time

**Infobox:**
- Name: Bullet Time
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/1/1e/BulletTime.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016211321
- Class: Silent
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Rare
- Cost: 3
- Effect: You cannot draw additional cards this turn. Reduce the cost of all cards in your hand to 0 this turn.
- [Bullet Time+]
- Cost+: 2
- Effect+: You cannot draw additional cards this turn. Reduce the cost of all cards in your hand to 0 this turn.

-**Bullet Time** is a Rare Skill for the Silent. It inflicts No Draw status on the player, preventing them from drawing any cards for the rest of the turn, and all cards in hand have their costs reduced to 0 Energy. 

When Upgraded, Bullet Time costs 2 Energy instead of 3.

## Mechanics

- The No Draw status can be negated by Artifact, or removed with Orange Pellets.
- No Draw only prevents you from drawing cards from your deck; it will not prevent you from generating cards via e.g. the Dead Branch or Shiv-creating cards.

## Strategy
- Taking full advantage of Bullet Time requires more thought and effort than it might seem at first. The key thing to remember is that Bullet Time itself takes up a slot in any hand you draw it into, and does nothing but let you play the remaining cards. Furthermore, unlike with generic energy-gain cards, cards that draw other cards must be played before Bullet Time itself.
- If you're just drawing five cards a turn, Bullet Time will let you play four of them; if you already have an Energy relic, and most of your cards cost 1 or 0, Bullet Time will be completely useless (no better than a Curse) every time it's drawn. For it to be useful, the total cost of the other cards worth playing in your hand has to be higher than your Energy limit. In a normal deck that hasn't been intentionally built around it, this happens less frequently than you would expect.
    - Alternatively, instead of running a high-cost deck, you must at least ensure you have enough card-draw effects that you can use before Bullet Time consistently, specifically Acrobatics or Backflip. This requires 4 Energy or Bullet Time+. Other draws such as Prepared or Tools of the Trade aren't necessarily sufficient, since they don't give a net positive in the amount of cards you get. Escape Plan only replaces itself and may grant some Block, but does not increase the number of cards in your hand. 
- As a result of this, the decks that want Bullet Time are ones with lots of high-cost cards and few cards that cost 0 or even 1. It's also more valuable if you've made it to the late game and still haven't found any suitable Energy relics, forcing you to accomplish as much as you can with your starting 3.
- Curses and Statuses can weaken Bullet Time further; any deck that uses it is going to be vulnerable to them.

## Synergies
- Bullet Time is extremely useful with the Snecko Eye, since the extra draw and random costs increase the chance that it will let you play more than you could have otherwise. It also provides a degree of protection from bad cost rolls, since you'll always be able to play Bullet Time if you draw it, thereby enabling you to play all the other cards in your hand. The Snecko Eye will often reduce Bullet Time's cost below 3 Energy as well, meaning that there may still be spare Energy for drawing more cards before using Bullet Time.
- Since Bullet Time makes all Attacks cost 0, the Wrist Blade will make them stronger. 
- The Runic Pyramid can keep cards that weren't played during a turn to fill up a hand to play with Bullet Time.

# Burn

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Burn

**Infobox:**
- Name: Burn
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/b/bf/Burn.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016212459
- Class: Neutral
- Type: Status
- Rarity: Common
- Cost: Unplayable
- Effect: Unplayable.; At the end of your turn, take 2 damage.
- [Burn+]
- Cost+: Unplayable
- Effect+: Unplayable.; At the end of your turn, take 4 damage.

CardAutobox
**Burn** is an Unplayable Status card. **Burns** can be added to your draw pile or discard pile during a game by some enemies such as the Orb Walker. Unlike other Status cards, **Burn** does have an upgraded version. **Burn+** is created by the Hexaghost boss when it uses its Inferno attack and in all subsequent attacks.

Burn deals damage to you immediately upon ending your turn. As Burn deals damage instead of causing direct HP loss, it can be blocked. Only Burn cards that are in your hand at the end of the turn will deal damage to you, so if you can remove a Burn from your hand before the end of turn (e.g. by discarding or Exhausting it), it will have no effect. After a Burn damages you at the end of your turn, it is discarded, even if you have the Runic Pyramid.

## Burn Sources
- Enemies
    - Hexaghost (before using Inferno)
    - Orb Walker
    - Nemesis
    - Spire Spear
    - Corrupt Heart
- Cards
    - Immolate
    - Overclock
- Blights
    - Twisting Mind

## Burn+ Sources
- Hexaghost (after using Inferno)

## Interactions
- Evolve: Draw 1 more card for each Burn you draw. Stacking Evolves can allow you to draw 2 more cards when you draw a Burn. Can still lead to a hand of 10 Burns.
- Exhaust synergies can use Burns as exhaust fuel.
- Medical Kit allows Burns to be played and exhausted for no penalty.

# Burst

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Burst

**Infobox:**
- Name: Burst
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/4/47/Burst.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016211321
- Class: Silent
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Rare
- Cost: 1
- Effect: This turn, your next Skill is played twice.
- [Burst+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: This turn, your next 2 Skills are played twice.
- Name: Burst
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/d/d5/Icon_Burst.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202161515
- Description: Your next X Skills are played twice.
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: Counter

**Burst** is a Skill card for The Silent. It plays the next Skill card this turn a second time, for no Energy. As a Rare card, it can be obtained after defeating a Boss. It is The Silent's version of Double Tap and Amplify.

Upon upgrade, it will trigger again on the 2nd Skill card played in the same turn.

The second play is NOT added to your draw or discard pile.

The scaling buff from Burst (and also from Double Tap and Amplify) is the number of cards that will be played twice, not the number of times the card will be played. This means playing multiple Bursts will add to the number of skills that will be played twice that turn, not make the next skill play 3 or more times.

## Interactions

- The second play will not cost any Energy, but it will trigger any other consequences of playing the card. For example, a Bursted J.A.X. will trigger the self-damage twice.
- The second play of a card that costs X energy will use the same value of X as the first.
- The second play acts as a separate card. This has interactions including, but not limited to:
    - Ink Bottle, Letter Opener: Both plays count towards playing skills for their benefits. 
    - Velvet Choker: Both plays count towards the amount of cards played for the turn.
    - Time Eater's Time Warp power: Both plays increase the counter as usual. If the second skill is the 13th action on his counter, it will NOT occur, unlike Velvet Choker.

- The second play happens after the Skill is sent to the draw, discard or Exhaust piles. 
- The second play can trigger any Exhaust synergies, but only if the Skill Exhausts when played.
    - In other words, the copied Skill "not going to your discard pile" does NOT count as an Exhaust by itself.

# Busted Crown

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Busted_Crown

**Infobox:**
- Name: Busted Crown
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/f/f7/BustedCrown.png/revision/latest?cb=20200203152839
- Description: Gain 1 Energy at the start of each turn. On Card Reward screens, you have 2 fewer cards to choose from.
- Flavor: The Champ's crown... or a pale imitation?
- Rarity: Boss
- Class: Any

**Busted Crown **is a Boss Relic that grants 1 extra Energy each turn, but restricts the options available when picking cards.

While the player has this Relic, they will be offered 2 fewer cards on Card Reward screens. Note that this doesn't just apply to post-battle rewards - Tiny House, Sensory Stone, and other opportunities to pick cards will also be reduced.

However, only card rewards that can permanently add a card to the deck are affected by Busted Crown, card select screens of Foreign Influence, Discovery, Toolbox, Nilry's Codex, Attack Potion, Skill Potion, and Power Potion always consists of 3 cards. (these are also not affected by Question Card)

## Strategy
If your deck is at least nearly prepared to win the rest of the run, Busted Crown is effectively a free source of Energy. Early in the game, though, it can represent a crippling disadvantage.

When deciding whether to take the Crown, consider your options for getting more card selection. If you have Dream Catcher or a large amount of money, you may be able to make do. Bear in mind that the Rare boss reward cards will also be reduced!

## Synergies
Question Card adds another choice to card reward screens, leaving you with two options.

Like all Energy buffs, Busted Crown allows you to play expensive cards, cards with draw effects, and X-cost cards with less risk.

## Trivia
This item is likely a reference to the trinket "Cracked Crown" from the Binding of Isaac: Rebirth.

# Byrd

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Byrd

**Infobox:**
- Name: Byrd
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/a/a2/Byrd.png/revision/latest?cb=20181025012659
- HP: 25-31; 26-33 7+
- Debut Act: 2
- In Party With: 2 other Byrds ; Chosen
- Powers: Flying 3; Flying 4 17+
- Name: Flying
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/e/ea/Icon_Flight.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202162208
- Description: Takes 50% less damage on the next X attacks. Removed when attacked X times in a single turn. Charges are refilled back to X at the start of each turn if not fully removed.
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: Intensity

Byrds are weak enemies found in Act 2 that begin each battle with a flying buff. Until each Byrd is dealt attack damage three times (four times on Ascension 17+) in one turn, it will take half damage from all attacks. This combined with its Strength scaling and multi-hit attacks make the Byrd a fearsome foe for some decks.

## Pattern
Can only use Peck or Caw on the first turn with a 62.5% chance for Peck and 37.5% chance for Caw. Afterwards, has a 50% chance of using Peck, 20% chance of using Swoop, and 30% chance of using Caw. Cannot use Peck three times in a row and cannot use Caw or Swoop twice in a row.

Because Byrds have the Flying buff, they will only take half of the damage dealt until they are hit three(or four on Ascension 17+) times in a turn. Here is the sequence of events when a Byrd loses its Flying buffs:
1. It will get stunned instantly, interrupting its previous intent;
1. It will use Headbutt the following turn;
1. It will use Fly.
1. Returns to its original pattern when Flying.
| Name | Intent | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Caw |  | Gains 1 Strength. |
| Peck |  | Deals 1x5 damage. |
| Deals 1x6 damage. |  |  |
| Swoop |  | Deals 12 damage |
| Deals 14 damage. |  |  |
| Fly |  | Gains Flying 3. |
| Gains Flying 4. |  |  |
| Headbutt |  | Deals 3 damage. |

## Tips
- Because Byrds attack so many times in one turn and have low HP, Thorns is very powerful in this fight.
- Attacks that hit multiple enemies multiple times, such as Dagger Spray, are very useful for removing the Byrds' Flying buff.
- It is more important to attack a Byrd if it is buffing its Strength; its next turn will be much stronger unless it is knocked down or killed.
- Indirect forms of damage, such as from the Defect's orbs or Poison, ignore the Byrds' Flying buff and are therefore more powerful in this fight.
- If a Byrd is dealt attack damage more than enough times to knock it down with a single card, the Byrd will be knocked down after the card's effects are finished. Thus, using Whirlwind with 5 Energy will deal half damage to all Byrds 5 times.

## Trivia
- The name "Byrd" is just "Bird" spelled with a "y".

SwiftStrike.png|A Byrd as seen in the Swift Strike card art.

- Effect+: Discard your hand,; then draw that many cards.

**Calculated Gamble** is a Uncommon Skill card for the Silent. When played, the player's current hand is discarded and that many cards are drawn, effectively shuffling the player's hand.

When Upgraded, Calculated Gamble no longer Exhausts.

## Interactions
- Calculated Gamble works well with cards that have effects upon being discarded, such as Reflex and Tactician. It also plays well with cards that have their energy cost decreased upon the discarding of other cards, such as Sneaky Strike and Eviscerate.
- Calculated Gamble synergizes well with Tingsha and Tough Bandages, dealing three damage to a random enemy and adding three Block to the player respectively for every discard.
- Calculated Gamble does not synergize well with cards that enable Retain, such as Well-Laid Plans, as Calculated Gamble can discard a valuable card.
- Calculated Gamble's upgrade can be a large priority, since it's effect can be the core of specific decks.

## Trivia

- The card depicts a "false" die, as a fair die can never have both the 3-side and the 4-side visible. They should be on opposite sides.
    - This could be an oversight, or dice in the Spire universe simply work differently.

# Card Rewards

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Card_Rewards

**Card Rewards** are a type of reward that the player receives after defeating an enemy, elite, or boss. Each card reward allows the player to choose one of three cards, but the player can also skip the card reward altogether. Card rewards are the main way of adding cards to your deck.

When a card reward is generated, each card is determined independently, one after the other. However, the cards in a card reward are never the same. For each card, the game first decides its rarity. Then it randomly selects a card that has that rarity. Since different characters have slightly different numbers of basic, common, uncommon, and rare cards, the exact chance of a card appearing depends both on the chance of that rarity appearing and the number of cards of that rarity in the card pool.
## Card Rarity
The chance that a card reward generates a card of a given rarity depends on what type of encounter the player just completed. Elite card rewards contain more uncommon and rare cards than normal card rewards, and boss card rewards have exclusively rare cards. The odds are also adjusted depending on how long the player has gone without seeing a rare in a card reward.

The base rarity chances are as follows:
|  | Normal Combats | Elite Combats | Boss Combats | Shop* |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Rare | 3% | **10%** | 100% | 9% |
| Uncommon | 37% | 40% | 0% | 37% |
| Common | 60% | 50% | 0% | 54% |
*Shop chances are shown for comparison, Shops do not generate cards in the same way as card rewards.

These base rarity chances are offset based on a special percentage. This number starts at -5%, and it increases by 1% every time a common card is rolled. Whenever a rare card is rolled, it is reset back to -5%. This number maxes out at +40%. Note that only rolls for card rewards can cause a change to this offset.

- When the offset is negative, it decreases the chance that a rare card is chosen. If it is greater than the base rare chance, it will start to decrease base uncommon chance instead. A negative offset increases the common card chance, so that everything adds to 100%.

- When the offset is positive, it decreases the chance that a common card is rolled, and increases a chance that a rare card is rolled instead. Again, this guarantees that the chances sum to 100%.

While the card reward offset does not affect boss card rewards (which guarantee rare cards no matter what), the fact that rare cards are rolled actually does reset the offset to -5%.

However, the card rarity offset works the other way when it comes to the other times that the game has to determine a rarity for a card. An example of this is the merchant; while the shop cards are impacted by the card rarity offset, they do not change the offset, since it is not technically a card reward.

## Upgraded Cards
Whether or not a card is upgraded in a card reward is dependent on what act the player is in. Only common and uncommon cards can be upgraded this way, rare cards are never upgraded via random chance.

The chances that a card is upgraded are shown below:
|  | Act 1 | Act 2 | Act 3 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Normal | 100% | **75%** | 50% |
| Upgraded | 0% | 25% | 50% |

On Ascension 12 and beyond, the chances that a card is upgraded on the card reward screen is cut in half.

The chances for Ascension 12+ are:
|  | Act 1 | Act 2 | Act 3 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Normal | 100% | **87.5%** | 75% |
| Upgraded | 0% | 12.5% | 25% |

## Modifiers

- Dream Catcher - allows you to receive a card reward when you rest at a Rest Site. The card reward acts as one from a normal monster fight.
- Question Card - causes card rewards to include an additional card.
- Busted Crown - causes card rewards to include two fewer cards.
- Singing Bowl - allows the player to gain two max HP instead of choosing a card for card rewards.
- Tiny House - causes you to immediately receive a card reward. The chances are the same as those from a normal fight.
- Orrery - causes you to immediately receive 5 card rewards. The chances are the same as those from a normal fight.
- Prismatic Shard - causes card rewards to contain cards from every color, including colorless cards.
- Frozen Egg, Molten Egg, Toxic Egg - cause powers, attacks, and skills (respectively) to be upgraded in card rewards. These relics can allow rare cards to be upgraded, unlike in normal card rewards.
- N'loth's Gift - triples the chance of receiving rare cards from card rewards.
- Prayer Wheel - adds an additional card reward after normal combats.
Category:Game Mechanics

# Cards

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Cards

Cards are the main feature in battle in *Slay the Spire*.

## Card Types
- **Attack **- A card that deals direct damage to an enemy and may have a secondary effect. Attacks have pentagonal frames.

- **Skill **- A card that has more diverse effects to it, usually through providing defense, utilities, buffs, or debuffs. While it can be both offensive and defensive, it is distinct from Attack card in a way that it cannot deal direct damage, capable of doing so only indirectly through debuffs. Skills have rectangular frames.

- **Power** - A permanent upgrade for the entire combat encounter. Some Powers give flat stats like Strength or Dexterity. Some powers require certain conditions to be met that combat. Some powers provide a unique buff that can potentially alter the playstyle. Each copy of a given power can only be played **once** per combat. Powers have circular frames.

- **Status** - A card added to the deck during a combat encounter. They are designed to bloat the deck and prevent the player from drawing beneficial cards, with some of them having additional negative effects. Status cards are removed from the deck at the end of combat. Statuses have rectangular frames.

- **Curse** - An unplayable card added to the deck during in-game events. Similar to status cards, they are designed to bloat the deck and prevent the player from drawing beneficial cards, with some of them having additional negative effects. However, curse cards persist in the player's deck until removed by other means. Curses have rectangular frames.

## Card Rarity
The rarity of the card depends on the color of the banner behind its name, regardless of the card's faction:

- **Common** cards have a *grey* banner and frame.
- **Uncommon** cards have a *blue* banner and frame.
- **Rare** cards have a *golden* banner and frame.

The game additionally recognizes two additional classes of rarity:
- **Basic** cards are the default cards from the starting deck for your class. They have the same *grey* banner and frame as Commons, though certain events treat them as a lower tier when offered or transformed.
- **Special** cards cannot be obtained through normal card-drops, only through events or other means.

# Catalyst

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Catalyst

**Infobox:**
- Name: Catalyst
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/b/b2/Catalyst.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016211322
- Class: Silent
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Cost: 1
- Effect: Double the enemy's Poison.; Exhaust.
- [Catalyst+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: Triple the enemy's Poison.; Exhaust.

## Mechanics

Technically, Catalyst add 1x or 2x the enemy's current Poison value. This can cause unexpected interactions.

- Artifact blocks Catalyst's Poison.
- Snecko Skull adds 1 after Catalyst's poison.

## Strategy
Catalyst allows poison decks to output much needed burst damage, at the cost of being slightly unwieldy. Practically a necessity for pure poison decks to beat the Act 3 boss.
- Catalyst synergizes with Nightmare, allowing much greater scaling of poison damage.
- Catalyst synergizes with Well-Laid Plans, Runic Pyramid, since they reserve Catalyst in hand to be used at the optimal turn.

Act 3 bosses have counter-mechanisms for poison damage. The Awakened One and Time Eater dispel every debuff (including poison) at phase 2. Donu and Deca are not a single entity and have Artifact.

So tactical usage of Catalyst is needed. Especially when it's Time Eater, Recommendation is using Catalyst at a turn which is phase 1 and you can kill it in 2 turns.

## Centurion

### Pattern
If the Mystic is alive, has a 65% chance of using Slash and a 35% chance of using Defend every turn. 

If the Mystic is dead, Defend is replaced with Fury.

### Tips
This fight can be simplified greatly by focusing damage on the Centurion. If you can survive his attacks and deal enough damage to overcome the healing output by the Mystic, the Centurion will simply rotate between his weaker attack and defending, allowing you to kill him first. The Mystic is not much of a threat alone.
| Name | Intent | Effect | Asc 2+ | Asc 17+ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Slash |  | Deal 12 damage. | Deal 14 damage. | Deal 14 damage. |
| Fury |  | Deal 6 x 3 damage. | Deal 7 x 3 damage. | Deal 7 x 3 damage. |
| Defend |  | Ally gains 15 Block. | Ally gains 15 Block. | Ally gains 20 Block. |

## Mystic

### Pattern
If any enemy can be healed by 16 HP, will use Heal. Cannot use Heal three times in a row.

If not healing, has a 40% chance of buffing and a 60% chance of attacking. Cannot use the same move three times in a row.

In Ascension 17+, uses Heal if any enemy can be healed by 21 HP. Also, now cannot attack twice in a row.
| Name | Intent | Effect | Asc 2+ | Asc 17+ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Heal |  | Heal all enemies for 16. | Heal all enemies for 16. | Heal all enemies for 20. |
| Buff |  | All enemies gain 2 Strength. | All enemies gain 3 Strength. | All enemies gain 4 Strength. |
| Attack/Debuff |  | Deal 8 damage, apply 2 Frail. | Deal 9 damage, apply 2 Frail. | Deal 9 damage, apply 2 Frail. |

# Chaos

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Chaos

**Infobox:**
- Name: Chaos
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/8/8f/Chaos.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016203241
- Class: Defect
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Cost: 1
- Effect: Channel 1 random Orb.
- [Chaos+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: Channel 2 random Orbs.

CardAutobox
**Chaos** is an uncommon card for The Defect that provides a cheap but unpredictable source of Orbs. Upgrading **Chaos** causes it to Channel two Orbs instead of one.

As the art suggests, all four Orbs - Lightning, Frost, Dark, and Plasma - can be Channeled using **Chaos**.

## Strategy
Chaos is one of the most efficient sources of Orbs available to The Defect, and the only reusable way to Channel multiple Orbs. If your deck benefits from loading up many Orb slots or doing a lot of Evoking, Chaos will rarely disappoint.

In addition, Chaos is a useful "duct tape" card to smooth out any Orb-related deck. For instance, if you picked up a Thunder Strike but can't find a Ball Lightning to power it, a Chaos can serve the same role.

It's also a cheap, if unreliable, source of Plasma Orbs. Decks with many X-cost cards can make the most of these Energy windfalls.

That said, Chaos does introduce some variance. You can't count on it to produce the specific Orb you need, and bad rolls will occasionally end your run. When offered a Chaos, consider the percentage of good or neutral outcomes versus the percentages of "bricks".

Upgrading Chaos is highly recommended. Not only does the upgraded card double the effect, it also doubles the odds of getting the Orb you need.

## Synergies
Chaos has an obvious synergy with Compile Driver. The card draw provides much-needed "gas" when Chaos feeds you Plasma Orbs. Note that this increases the variance of the deck, as Compile Driver is significantly weaker if you only have one type of Orb.

The card works well with both Consume and Capacitor. The former can turn an upgraded Chaos into a guaranteed powered-up Evocation. The latter allows you to stack up more Orbs so you can cast Chaos without prematurely Evoking your Dark Orbs.

Chaos becomes extremely powerful with Echo Form, Channeling a whopping four Orbs for just one Energy. It's also a useful source of bulk Orbs to maximize your Biased Cognition.

While Chaos doesn't explicitly synergize with Rainbow, the two cards share synergies and coexist nicely.

## Hazards
Chaos is a terrible choice for Dark Orb decks. It will often prematurely Evoke a Dark Orb, effectively making it a Curse for most of the game.

The card is risky but useful in Frost Orb decks. These builds often aim to stack up enough Frost Orbs to completely neutralize enemy attacks, which Chaos undermines by bumping off Frost Orbs. That said, Chaos does generate 10 block for 1 Energy in these decks, in addition to whatever benefits the Orbs provide.

# Chest

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Chest

A **Chest** is an object that contain a number of rewards. Whenever the player encounters a chest, they can choose open it to obtain a reward inside, or they may skip the chest.

There are two different types of chests.

Category:Game Mechanics
## Boss Chest

A boss chest can only be found after completing a boss fight, and will allow the player a choice of one out of three Boss Relics. They can be skipped, but doing so is not ideal, as Boss Relics are very powerful.

## Non-boss Chest
Non-boss chests can be found in a Treasure Room. These chests will give the player one relic from the Common, Uncommon, or Rare relic pool. They will also have a chance to give the player a certain amount of gold.

There are 3 variations of non-boss chests, each with their own chances of appearance and rewards inside.

|  | Small Chest | Medium Chest | Large Chest |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |
| Chance | 50% | 33% | 17% |
| Relic Rewards |  |  |  |
| Common | 75% | 35% | 0% |
| Uncommon | 25% | 50% | 75% |
| Rare | 0% | 15% | 25% |
| Gold Rewards |  |  |  |
| Chance | 50% | 35% | 50% |
| Amount | 23-27 | 45-55 | 68-82 |

If Act 4 is unlocked and the player has not already picked up the Sapphire Key, the non-boss chest in each area contain the key, but linked to a relic, meaning the player can only pick one or the other. If the key is not picked, it will continue to show up in all later non-boss chests until it is picked.

The following relics will interact with non-boss chests:
- Matryoshka: Causes the next 2 non-boss chests you open to have 2 relics inside.
- N'loth's Hungry Face: Causes the next non-boss chest you open to be empty.
- Cursed Key: Whenever you open a non-boss chest, obtain a Curse.

# Clash

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Clash

**Infobox:**
- Name: Clash
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/f/fb/Clash.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016205731
- Class: Ironclad
- Type: Attack
- Rarity: Common
- Cost: 0
- Effect: Can only be played if every card in your hand is an Attack.; Deal 14 damage.
- [Clash+]
- Cost+: 0
- Effect+: Can only be played if every card in your hand is an Attack.; Deal 18 damage.

**Clash** is an Attack card for the Ironclad. It deals 14 damage for zero Energy, but can only be played if there are no Skills, Powers, Status, or Curse cards in the player's hand. As a Common card, it can be found as a reward after combats.

Upon upgrade, damage is increased by 4.

## Interactions

- The fewer cards of other types are taken, the easier it is to play Clash. However, with few Skills, key debuffs and Blocks may be hard to come by.

- Cards that let you Exhaust on demand, such as Corruption and True Grit+, have good synergy with Clash.
    - Second Wind and Sever Soul, both of which Exhaust all non-Attack cards, work brilliantly with Clash.
- Dual Wield can allow for more Clash for free damage.
- Unceasing Top draws only one card at a time, so it can easily enable Clash.
- Blue Candle and Medical Kit make it easier to get rid of unplayable cards.

# Claw

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Claw

**Infobox:**
- Name: Claw
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/4/47/Claw.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016203325
- Class: Defect
- Type: Attack
- Rarity: Common
- Cost: 0
- Effect: Deal 3 damage.; Increase the damage of ALL Claw cards by 2 this combat.
- [Claw+]
- Cost+: 0
- Effect+: Deal 5 damage.; Increase the damage of ALL Claw cards by 2 this combat.

CardAutoboxClaw is a common Attack card for The Defect. For zero Energy, Claw deals an escalating amount of damage that also amps up your other Claw cards. As a common card, Claw can be found as a post-battle reward and be purchased from the Merchant.

Upgrading Claw increases the base damage of the card from 3 to 5.

Claws added to your deck after Claw is played, such as through Discovery, Hello World or an Attack Potion, do not have their damage increased while they aren't part of your deck.

### Strategy
- Claw is a card that wants to be drawn and played as much as possible to stack up huge numbers. However, the support needed to execute this card's potential makes it not ideal for many decks, since a card like Streamline+ fills the niche of Claw without being as hard to pick.
- To get the most out of Claw, acquire only enough copies as to be drawn consistently as to not interfere with other deck functions such as Block or Card Draw. Consistency is better achieved by removing underperforming cards rather than by adding too many Claws.
- Upgrading Claw isn't recommended - instead, upgrade your support and draw cards like Skim and Scrape. Playing your non-upgraded Claws more often not only gives you bonus damage, but also deals the damage you've already accumulated. 
- Adding more card draw like Skim, Scrape, Unceasing Top, will help Claw reach its fullest potential. There are some good colorless card draw cards that also work well with Claw:
    - Secret Weapon
    - Deep Breath
    - Master of Strategy
    - Violence

- Replaying a Claw with Hologram and Echo Form helps accelerate claw damage, though these effects may be better reserved for other cards with more powerful effects.
- Adding Recycle to strip irrelevant cards from the deck allows the consistency of Claw plays to scale over the battle. Adding an Unceasing Top and exhausting every other card lets The Defect go infinite, though such combos still requires somehow generating block when against many enemies.
- All for One allows for even more Claws to be played, alongside other potentially important 0-cost cards such as Beam Cell for more damage and Vulnerable, and/or Steam Barrier for Block, etc.

## Trivia
- Before release the name of this card was "Gash" and was an Uncommon card.
- It takes 8 plays of Claw+ before a Claw+ outdamages a Streamline+. This means it takes 17 full Claw+ plays for the total damage to overtake 17 Streamline+ plays.
Defect Card Navbox
Category:0-Cost Cards

# Clockwork Souvenir

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Clockwork_Souvenir

**Infobox:**
- Name: Clockwork Souvenir
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/d/d9/ClockworkSouvenir.png/revision/latest?cb=20200203154031
- Description: At the start of each combat, gain 1 Artifact.
- Flavor: "So many intricate gears."
- Rarity: Shop
- Class: Any

Gives you an Artifact at the start of each combat.

## Synergy
Can be used with cards like Biased Cognition, or relics like Mutagenic Strength, to negate the debuffs that those inflict onto you, effectively giving you free, strong buffs.

It does *not* prevent the confusion from Snecko Eye, regardless of the order in which the relics were obtained.

It *always* prevents the weakness from Gremlin Visage, and the Strength loss from Mutagenic Strength, regardless of the order in which the relics were obtained.

## Trivia
- Interestingly, most mechanical enemies such as Sentry, Spheric Guardian, and Bronze Automaton have innate Artifact, while this relic, with mechanical theme, also grants Artifact.
    - The Defect, a robotic character, also has a card that grants Artifact, and currently is the only one that has access to Artifact via its own card pool.

# Colorless Cards

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Colorless_Cards

Colorless cards are available to all characters. These cards are generally not gained from normal card reward screens--adventurers must instead acquire them through a combination of merchant shops, events, relic effects, and card effects. All colorless cards provide a beneficial effect ranging from mildly to extremely powerful.

The Merchant always has two colorless cards in his stock. They are always Uncommon or Rare. Obtaining the  Prismatic Shard allows those colorless cards to appear in normal card reward screens as well.

All the other colorless cards, despite sharing a grey border with Common cards, are all special cards that can only be obtained from certain events, or generated by certain cards and relics.

# Combat Mechanics

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Combat_Mechanics

In Slay the Spire players will regularly encounter hostile monsters which will engage them in combat.

Combat is done as a turn based card game. The player uses cards from the deck they have built during the run to attack and defend themselves, while enemies use a preset of skills to fight back.
Category:Game Mechanics

## Turn structure
When in combat the player moves first. At the start of each turn the player draws 5 cards from their draw pile and gains 3 energy. Then they have the opportunity to play any number of cards, provided they have enough energy left. Every card reads its energy cost and playing it consumes that amount of energy from the players energy pool. Unless otherwise stated on the card, played cards are put on the discard pile after causing their effects. During their turn players can also drink, throw or discard potions at no cost.

Once players either have exhausted their resources or don't deem further actions beneficial, they can end their turn. When the player ends their turn, the remaining cards in their hand are discarded and their remaining energy is drained.

During the monsters' turn monsters use skills and attacks according to their intent, which players can see above their heads. After all monsters have moved, it's the players turn again and the cycle continues until one party is defeated.
## General Mechanics
- **HP** - HP represents the health of the player and the opponents they encounter. Certain effects can reduce or increase the remaining and/or maximum HP of the player. HP persists throughout each Act of the game. After successfully defeating the Boss of an Act the player is fully healed. If the remaining HP of the player reaches 0 they die and the game is over.

- **Damage** - Attacks deal damage. Unblocked damage results in loss of HP.

- **Block** - Block applies shields to any combatant for one turn of combat. The intensity of the shields determines how much damage it can take before breaking. Whenever a blocking target receives damage the shields are reduced first. Once an attack exceeds the shield intensity it breaks and the target starts taking HP damage. Unless prevented by other means all applications of Block are removed at the start of each turn in combat.

## Combat Conditions
During Combat both players and their opponents can be affected by a number of conditions both beneficial and detrimental:

**General Conditions**

Conditions that can affect both players and monsters:
| Name | Symbol | Description | Stacking | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Weakened |  | This unit deals 25% less damage with attacks | Duration |  |
| Vulnerable |  | This unit receives 50% more damage from attacks | Duration |  |
| Strength |  | This unit deals X additional damage with attacks | Intensity | Can be negative, resulting in damage reduction. |
| Artifact |  | Negates X incoming debuffs | Intensity |  |
| Thorns |  | Deals X damage to any attacker | Intensity | Attackers that hit multiple times will receive recoil damage for each individual hit. |
| Barricade |  | Prevents removal of Block at the start of turn | None |  |
| Metallicise |  | This unit gains X Block at the end of their turn | Intensity |  |
| Plated Armor |  | This unit gains X Block at the end of their turn. Taking unblocked damage removes one application of Plated Armor | Intensity | Attackers that hit multiple times will remove 1 application for each individual hit. |
| Intangible |  | All incoming damage and life loss is reduced to 1 | Duration |  |
| Regen |  | The Unit gains X HP at the start of each turn and the removes 1 application of Regen. | Intensity | Some monsters will have Regen that does not lower its applications. |

**Player exclusive**

# Combust

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Combust

**Infobox:**
- Name: Combust
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/e/e7/Combust.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016205732
- Class: Ironclad
- Type: Power
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Cost: 1
- Effect: At the end of your turn, lose 1 HP and deal 5 damage to ALL enemies.
- [Combust+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: At the end of your turn, lose 1 HP and deal 7 damage to ALL enemies.
- Name: Combust
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/0/07/Icon_Combust.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202161516
- Description: At the end of your turn, lose 1 HP(for each Combust played) and deal X damage to ALL enemies.
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: Intensity

**Combust** is a Power card for the Ironclad. It deals 5 damage to all enemies at the end of every of the user's turns after it's played, but costs 1 HP every time. This damage cannot be blocked.

Upon upgrade, it deals 2 more damage per turn.

As an Uncommon card, it appears as a reward for combat, although less often than Commons.

## Interactions
 
- HP loss reduction relics like Tungsten Rod can reduce or eliminate the HP loss from this card.
- Synergizes well with Rupture, granting 1 Strength per turn.
- Self-Forming Clay will grant 3 block each turn from **Combust**'s 1 HP damage.

 
- The damage from **Combust** will not reduce Plated Armor.

 
- Damage from multiple **Combust** cards stacks into one hit - this means one Rupture will only grant 1 Strength even with 2 or more **Combust** powers active.
- The damage from **Combust** is not affected by additional Strength.
- Synergizes negatively with draw on HP loss, such as with Runic Cube and Centennial Puzzle. The cards drawn from **Combust**'s HP loss are immediately discarded. This also impedes setups that put cards on top of the draw pile, such as Warcry and Headbutt.
- The damage caused by Combust is part of the buff. As a result it is not removed by Orange Pellets or prevented by Artifact.

**Infobox:**

CardAutobox
**Compile Driver** is an Attack for The Defect that draws 1 card for each different *type* of Orb the player currently has.  When Upgraded, it deals 3 additional damage.

## Interactions
- Positive
    - Rainbow and Chaos channel different orb types, inherently making Compile Driver draw multiple cards.
    - Capacitor, Runic Capacitor, and Inserter give Orb Slots, making it easier to have several types of orbs in play.
    - Cracked Core, Symbiotic Virus, and Nuclear Battery ensure that Compile Driver is playable for draw on turn one.
- Negative
    - Consume reduces the amount of orb slots, making it harder to draw with Compile Driver.

# Confused

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Confused

**Infobox:**
- Name: Confused
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/d/dc/Icon_Confused.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202161516
- Description: The costs of your cards are randomized on draw, from 0 to 3.
- Type: Debuff
- Stacking; Behavior: None

**Confused** is a debuff that randomizes the Energy cost of cards that you draw to be anywhere from 0 to 3. 

## Mechanics

- The cost of cards in your draw pile or discard pile is not changed until you actually draw the card.
- Extracting cards from the deck using an effect such as Secret Weapon does *not* randomize their cost.
- Cards keep their new cost until they are drawn again, or under another effect that change card cost, like the Mummified Hand or Streamline.
- Cards that have their cost changed by an effect, such as by Madness, Streamline, or cards created by Chrysalis, will still have their costs randomized upon being drawn.
- Cards that are Retained, such as by Well-Laid Plans, keep their cost between turns.
- X cost cards are not affected by **Confused** at all.
- Corruption overrides Confused entirely, and Skills will always cost 0.
    - Swivel does this to a lesser extent, making all Attacks cost 0 until an Attack is played. Once an Attack is played, any Attacks in hand that had a cost greater than 0 will return to that cost.
- If the player has **Confused** from Snecko Eye and an active Artifact, an Artifact charge will be consumed when Snecko applies **Confused** to the player using its Perplexing Glare, even though the **Confused** debuff does not stack.

## Sources of Confusion
- Enemies
    - Snecko
- Relics
    - Snecko Eye
- Snecko Oil has a similar effect, but only randomizes the cards currently in your hand, and does not cause Confused itself.

# Corpse Explosion

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Corpse_Explosion

**Infobox:**
- Name: Corpse Explosion
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/2/28/CorpseExplosion.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016211436
- Class: Silent
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Rare
- Cost: 2
- Effect: Apply 6 Poison.; When the enemy dies, deal damage equal to its max HP to ALL enemies.
- [Corpse Explosion+]
- Cost+: 2
- Effect+: Apply 9 Poison.; When the enemy dies, deal damage equal to its max HP to ALL enemies.
- Name: Corpse Explosion
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/1/12/Icon_CorpseExplosion.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202161517
- Description: On death, the enemy deals X times its Max HP worth of damage to all other enemies.
- Type: Debuff
- Stacking; Behavior: Intensity

**Corpse Explosion** is a Rare Skill for The Silent that applies Poison to one enemy and causes it to inflict a huge amount of damage to its companions upon death.

Upgrading Corpse Explosion increases the Poison from 6 (21 total damage) to 9 (45 total damage).

## Mechanics
- Applies 2 distinct debuffs in that order: poison and "Corpse Explosion".  So, an enemy with **one** artifact will only block poison.
- The "Corpse Explosion" effect lasts indefinitely (unless the enemy clears its debuffs).
- The fatal damage can come from any source--it does not have to come from Poison.
- It can stack, allowing an enemy to deal two or more times its max HP to all foes.
- Because the poison and explosion damage is dealt after Block is removed, very few enemies can block it.
- Corpse Explosion *does* trigger when Reptomancer's Daggers automatically die on their second turn.

## Strategy
Corpse Explosion is an exceptionally strong card when fighting multiple enemies. Even without the above-average amount of Poison, it can inflict massive amounts of area-of-effect damage and easily clear boards.

As a Poison enabler, it's strong but clunky. 9 Poison is the single largest printed amount of Poison, but two Energy is a big investment. Consider it a step up from Bouncing Flask in most situations.

A key decision when casting Corpse Explosion is whether to target an enemy with low HP to wipe it off the board earlier, or to target the enemy with the highest max HP to wipe the entire board at once. Generally, targeting the beefiest enemy and then focusing all of your attacks on it is the optimal play, though if a shuffle is imminent, it may be smarter to pick a weaker enemy and try to stack the effect again.

Corpse Explosion is an excellent workhorse for defensive decks. The Poison cuts through Block while the explosion scales the damage up, allowing you to fully focus on defense. It also negates up to two artifacts because of its two effects (poison and apply poison upon death).

Upgrading Corpse Explosion is recommended to increase its potency against single enemies.

## Synergies
- Burst allows Corpse Explosion to apply a huge amount of Poison and area-of-effect damage.
- Corpse Explosion triggers Sadistic Nature twice.
- The card synergizes with all Poison-matters cards like Bane and Catalyst. The large amount of Poison makes Corpse Explosion a particularly strong setup for the latter.

## Trivia
This card is most likely a reference to the Diablo II Necromancer Corpse Explosion ability; in addition to have the exact same name, the mechanics of the card are also the same (deal damage to other enemies based on the health of the target)

# Corrupt Heart

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Corrupt_Heart

**Infobox:**
- Name: Corrupt Heart
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/2/26/CorruptHeart.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20191022231336
- HP: 750; 800 9+
- In Party With: None
- Debut Act: Act 4
- Powers: Beat Of Death 1; Invincible 300; Beat of Death 2 19+ Invincible 200 19+
- Name: Beat of Death
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/0/00/Icon_BeatOfDeath.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202161411
- Description: Whenever you play a card, take X damage.
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: Intensity
- Name: Invincible
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/4/4f/Icon_Invincible.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202163112
- Description: Caps all damage and HP loss taken to X each turn.
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: None

-The **Corrupt Heart **is the final boss, fought in Act 4. It is very powerful; its innate powers and buffs it gains throughout the fight can prove very difficult to counter. Because of its Invincible buff, it can only take 300 (200) damage per turn, rendering strategies that rely on heavy damage less effective. Additionally, it will gain incredible amounts of Strength on its fourth buff and onward, so killing it quickly is also important.
## Pattern
Always starts with Debilitate. Uses Buff every 3 turns starting from turn 4.

Otherwise, has a 50% chance of using Blood Shots followed by Echo and a 50% chance of using Echo followed by Blood Shots.
| Name | Intent | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Debilitate |  | Applies 2 Vulnerable, 2 Weak, and 2 Frail in that order. Shuffles a Dazed, Slimed, Wound, Burn and a Void into the draw pile. |
| Blood Shots |  | Deal 2 x 12 damage. |
| Deal 2 x 15  damage. |  |  |
| Echo |  | Deal 40 damage. |
| Deal 45 damage. |  |  |
| Buff |  | Remove all Strength Down debuffs, gain 2 Strength and additional buffs: **1st Buff:** Artifact 2 **2nd Buff:** Beat of Death 1 **3rd Buff:** Painful Stabs **4th Buff:** Strength 10 **5th Buff onward:** Strength 50 |
## Tips

- Strength reduction and/or damage reduction is very effective against The Heart, since its Blood Shots only deal 2 damage initially. This includes:
    - Piercing Wail
    - Dark Shackles
    - Disarm
    - Malaise
    - Torii
- Do not use either of the first two cards in this list on a turn where The Heart buffs. It will clear the strength down debuff, then gain back the strength you made it lose from the card, essentially making you give The Heart free strength. 
- Poison damage is able to do more damage than the invincible buff would allow
- Any source of Weak will also be extremely valuable against both of The Heart's attacks.
- Sources of damage negation such as Intangible and Buffer can be very effective against the Echo attack. Intangible is also reasonably useful against Blood Shots, as it will always lower the damage to 12 (15), whereas Buffer would only negate 1 (2) of the attacks.
    - Incense Burner is a source of Intangible that can reliably block Blood Shots or Echo on turn two or three, if you end the Spire Shield and Spire Spear fight with it on 3 or 4. Because the attack pattern repeats every three turns, it will activate again on turn 9 or 10, during The Heart's third use of Blood Shots or Echo. Alternatively, it also works to set the relic to 0 or 1 to block the second and fourth cycles.
- Any effect that triggers on-damage or on-attack is very good against The Heart due to it triggering 12 (15) times for each Blood Shots that The Heart does. This includes:
    - Thorns
    - Static Discharge
    - Flame Barrier
    - Self-Forming Clay
- Medical Kit can be useful against The Heart, as it will allow you to remove the many statuses it will inflict on you, but beware of its Beat of Death power, as it will trigger whenever you play any card, including curses and statuses.
- Tungsten Rod or After Image can completely negate Beat of Death 1. Both of these, 2 copies of After Image, or gaining Intangible with either is necessary to negate Beat of Death 2, which is found on Ascension 19+ or applied on The Heart's second Buff action.
- Mitigating the debuffs from Debilitate is important to take less damage in the first attack cycle. This includes: 
    - Artifact, with one stack negating Vulnerable since it's applied first, and three negating all. Saving an Ancient Potion is a strong option for this strategy. 
    - Turnip will prevent Frail and Odd Mushroom will reduce the effect of Vulnerable, so buying the former in shops when possible and fighting the Fungi Beasts in the Hypnotizing Colored Mushrooms event can be worthwhile. 
    - While Weak isn't a major problem if the goal is to block the first cycle, Ginger will prevent it, which means that Frail will be negated by a second stack of Artifact since it's applied third. This is notable because Panacea+ provides two stacks, and so does an Ancient Potion combined with Sacred Bark. 
    - Clockwork Souvenir and Orange Pellets, both shop-exclusive relics, provide very reliable ways to deal with these debuffs, so checking the rightmost relic slot in shops, where such relics are always found, for these and purchasing them is a priority.
    - To help trigger Orange Pellets specifically on turn two or three, it's important to guarantee playing a power on those turns. This can be done by saving a Power Potion for the turn or holding a power (especially an Innate or Bottled one) in your hand by obtaining Runic Pyramid or playing Well-Laid Plans or Equilibrium to Retain it.
- Because Vault does not affect buffs on enemies, the Invincible damage cap is not reset for the extra turn.

## Trivia

- An early version of this boss, which didn't make it past the playtesting phase around two years before it was released, used to deal 1 blockable damage per second instead of per card played. This would make it the only timing-based gameplay mechanic outside of the Speed Climber Achievement and the Speedster and Lightspeed Scores.
- Mental Fortress activates before Beat of Death for every Stance-changing card, except for Indignation, which will activate after.

**Corruption** is a Rare Power card for the Ironclad.

After it is played, Corruption reduces the Energy cost of Skills to 0, but causes them to Exhaust.

Upon upgrade, it costs 1 less Energy to play it, from 3 to 2.

## Interactions
 
- In concert with Dark Embrace, this card will let you rapidly cycle through every skill in your deck.
- The Dead Branch relic synergizes extremely well with this card, replacing every exhausted skill card with a new card (potentially another 0 cost skill). This minimizes the major drawback of Corruption, which is potentially draining your deck of defensive skills during a long battle.
- Feel No Pain allows a free 3-4 defense per exhausted card, significantly increasing Corruption's defensive capabilities.
- When confused by Snecko or Snecko Eye, skills still cost 0.
- Strange Spoon gives a 50% chance for skills under the effects of this card to discard normally. This may not be helpful in all decks, however, as it reduces the benefits of other synergies like Dark Embrace, Dead Branch and Feel No Pain (as well as any strategic benefit from shrinking your draw pile).

# Council of Ghosts

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Council_of_Ghosts

**Council of Ghosts** is an event found exclusively in Act 2. A group of apparitions surrounds you, with one offering you a taste of their power.

## Options

*Numbers in parentheses are for Ascension 15 or higher.*

- **[Accept]** Receive 5 (3) Apparition. Lose 50% Max HP.

- **[Refuse]** Nothing happens.

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| *As you continue your ascent, thick black smoke begins to billow out of the ground and walls around you, coalescing into three masked forms that start to speak.* |
| '''Shape #1:'* *"Another puppet of Neow I think."* |
| **Shape #2:** "AGREED! SHE ALWAYS MAKES THE FUNNEST TOYS!" |
| *You notice an over-sized grin as the third addresses you.* |
| **Shape #3:** *"Ignore the others... Would you like a taste of our power?""* |
| Accept |
| **Shape #3:** *"Excellent!"* |
| *As the ghostly shape speaks, you notice its large mouth opening wider and wider. Thick black smoke spews forth and envelops the room. You cannot see or breathe...* |
| *Just before you lose consciousness, the sensation stops.* |
| *Whatever those things were, they are gone now. You continue on, feeling rather hollow.* |
| Refuse |
| **Shape #3:** *"How disappointing..."* |
| **Shape #1:** *"You will join us sooner or later."* |
| **Shape #2:** "HA HA HA HAHAHA!" |
| *The shapes fade away, leaving only the unnerving laughter ringing in your ears.'' |

## Strategy
This event is one of the most high-risk, high-reward. On one hand, you lose a hefty amount of your max HP, making it considerably harder to survive combats. On the other hand, that risk is offset by Apparitions obtained. Its Intangible can make a big incoming attack trivial. There are a few things to consider before you choose **[Accept]**.
- Unupgraded Apparition has Ethereal. This usually means you have to immediately use it the turn you draw it or it will be removed for the duration of that battle.
    - By utilizing Discard and Scry, you can move unwanted Apparition safely to your Discard Pile for further use.
    - Toxic Egg upgrades all Apparitions obtained, removing this downside.
    - Strange Spoon **will not** save Apparition from being Exhausted by Ethereal. It does have other synergy with it, as explained below.
- Cards that allow Apparition to be played multiple times, like Burst or Echo Form, greatly improve the value you can get from it, as you will get 2 Intangible from one use, extending its duration for a turn.
- Strange Spoon can possibly save some Apparition after it is used, discarding it instead of Exhausting it, allowing more uses from it.

## Trivia
- This is one of a few events that refers to Neow; the others are Cursed Tome and Sensory Stone.
    - This event also reveals that Neow is female.
- The shapes' knowledge of Neow and her power possibly means that they are of the similar caliber as her — possibly as another group of Ancients.

# Crowbot

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Crowbot

Crowbot was originally a planned 3rd character. It was located in the game's files as a sprite of a robotic-looking blue robot, similar in design to the Cultist.

Fans of the game theorized it would be the third character since it was found, as it seemed to fit the colour order of "red/green/blue" that already existed with the Ironclad and the Silent. Crowbot was theorized by the community to have mechanical abilities, a colour scheme of blue, and a large number of powers.

In an interview with one of the developers, Crowbot was confirmed to have been the planned third character. It was supposed to have a "mana" system to play cards instead of an energy system. During testing, the idea fell flat and the character was scrapped. The developers then began on a "gunner" character which eventually led to the Defect.

Afterwards, the third Character The Defect was added into the game's Beta branch in an update on April 26, 2018.

# Curse

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Curse

**Curses** are negative cards. Unlike Status cards, they stay in your deck outside of combat. Under normal circumstances, all curses are unplayable, and many impose an additional negative effect.

Curses can only Transform into other curses. When an effect (such as Cursed Key or Transform) generates a random curse, it can only become one of the following:
- Clumsy
- Decay
- Doubt
- Injury
- Normality
- Pain
- Parasite
- Regret
- Shame
- Writhe
The above curses and Pride are the only ones that can be removed from the deck.

## Interactions

### Card
*Numbers in parentheses are for upgraded cards.*
- Fire Breathing - Whenever you draw a Status or Curse card, deal 6(10) damage to all enemies.

### Relics
- Omamori - Negates the next 2 Curses you obtain.
- Blue Candle - Lets you play Curses, Exhausting the card at the cost of 1 HP.
- Darkstone Periapt - Increases your Max HP by 6 whenever you obtain a Curse.
- Du-Vu Doll - Starts each combat with 1 additional Strength for each Curse in your deck.
- Cursed Key - Gives you a Curse whenever you open a Chest.

### Events
*Numbers in parentheses are for Ascension 15 or higher.*
- The Divine Fountain - Lets you remove every removable Curse from the deck.
- Match and Keep - Has 1(2) pair(s) of a random Curse available for matching.
- Bonfire Spirits - Offering a Curse rewards you with Spirit Poop.

## List
| Name | Picture | Description | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ascender's Bane |  | Unplayable. Cannot be removed from your deck. Ethereal. | *(Obtained from Ascension level 10 and higher at the start of the game.)* |
| Clumsy |  | Unplayable. Ethereal. |  |
| Curse of the Bell |  | Unplayable. Cannot be removed from your deck. | *(Obtained from Calling Bell when acquired.)* |
| Decay |  | Unplayable. At the end of your turn, take 2 damage. |  |
| Doubt |  | Unplayable. At the end of your turn, gain 1 Weak. |  |
| Injury |  | Unplayable. |  |
| Necronomicurse |  | Unplayable. There is no escape from this Curse. (Cannot be Removed from your deck. When Exhausted, a new copy appears in your hand.) | *(Obtained when Necronomicon is acquired. Removed if Necronomicon is disacquired.)* |
| Normality |  | Unplayable. You cannot play more than 3 cards this turn. |  |
| Pain |  | Unplayable. While in hand, lose 1 HP when other cards are played. |  |
| Parasite |  | Unplayable. If transformed or removed from your deck, lose 3 Max HP. |  |
| Pride |  | Innate. At the end of your turn, put a copy of this card on top of your draw pile. Exhaust. | *(Obtained from the Grotesque Trophy Blight in Endless Mode.)* |
| Regret |  | Unplayable. At the end of your turn, lose HP equal to the number of cards in your hand. |  |
