# Cursed Tome

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Cursed_Tome

**Cursed Tome** is an event found exclusively in Act 2. It involves a cursed book with insight on Neow's origins. The player may read the book to obtain it or walk away.

## Options

*Numbers in parentheses are for Ascension 15 or higher.*

- **[Read]** 
    - **[Continue]** Lose 1 HP.
      - **[Continue]** Lose 2 HP.
        - **[Continue]** Lose 3 HP.
        - ***[Take]** Obtain the Book. Lose 10 (15) HP.
        - **The book may be Enchiridion, Nilry's Codex, or Necronomicon.
        - ***[Stop]** Lose 3 HP.

- **[Leave]** Nothing happens.

## Strategy
In most runs, it's never a problem whether taking the book is worth it-- It almost always is. Enchiridion guarantees a free Ability Card that usually gives huge boosts in combat, sometimes even turning the table. Nilry's Codex provides excellent support during combats, especially if your deck is in need of additional attacks/defences. And Necronomicon significantly boosts your damage output in each turn, and provides nice synergy with cards such as Whirlwind, Reaper, Choke, Dash, Streamline, Wallop and so on. The actual setback of obtaining the relics is the HP loss. 21 HP may be the difference between surviving and losing the run altogether. It's generally a great idea to take the book as long as you have enough HP to spare.

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| *In an abandoned temple, you find a giant book, open, riddled with* cryptic writings. |
| *As you try to interpret the elaborate script, it begins shift and morph into writing you are familiar with.* |
| Read |
| *Odd. The book seems to be about an Ancient named Neow.* |
| *This piques your interest, but you have a general feeling of malaise.* |
| Continue |
| *The Ancient of resurrection, Neow, was exiled to the bottom of the Spire.* |
| *You feel compelled to read more, but your body begins to ache.* |
| Continue |
| *Seeking vengeance, Neow blesses outsiders, using them for her own purposes.* |
| *You are starting to feel very weak and tired.* |
| Continue |
| *Those resurrected by Neow remember only fragments of their past selves, cursed to fight for eternity.* |
| *As you near the final page, your* old wounds begin to reopen! |
| Take |
| *Upon finishing the tome, you decide to take it with you. With proof in hand, will you retain your memories?* |
| Stop |
| *With incredible strain and willpower, you resist the trance of the tome and* SLAM *it shut. |
| *You turn and exit the temple, feeling drained...* |
| Leave |
| *You exit, feeling a dark energy emanating from the book on the pedestal.'' |

## Trivia

- Taking the book will require a minimum of 16 (21) HP. The  Tungsten Rod will reduce the health loss to 12 (17) HP.

# Custom Mode

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Custom_Mode

**Custom Mode** is a game mode unlocked by playing a Daily Climb. It allows the player to choose any number of custom modifiers, including Daily modifiers, to their run. It also allows them to customize Seed, Character and Ascension levels beyond those unlocked.

Playing on Custom Mode disables Achievements and the Leaderboards. 

Mods on the table below with a * next to them are Daily modifiers and may be selected for Daily Challenges. They have icons, which will appear to the right, on the top of the screen to identify the modifier selected.

Selecting two mods that are mutually exclusive will disable whichever one was selected first.

| Modifier | Icon | Effects | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Daily Mods |  | Embark on a run with exactly 3 random Daily Mods. | Overrides other mods except The Ending and Endless. |
| Draft* |  | Draft a starting deck of cards. | The draft consists of 15 choices of 3 cards each that must be chosen in order. These choices are unaffected by Busted Crown and Binary. Mutually exclusive with Sealed Deck.  Pandora's Box will not appear. |
| Sealed Deck* |  | Craft a deck from 30 random cards. | Similar to Draft, except the game presents 30 cards and you must pick 10 of them to create your deck. Mutually exclusive with Draft.  Pandora's Box will not appear. |
| The Ending |  | Enables the Final Act. | Enables the three Keys to access Act 4. Mutually exclusive with Endless. This modifier is hidden until the player defeats the Corrupt Heart with all four characters in Standard Mode. |
| Endless |  | Winning will return you to Act 1 with the same deck. But beware, the blight eventually consumes all... | Puts the game on repeat, and Neow will grant blights to make the game harder. Mutually exclusive with The Ending. |
| Blight Chests |  | Boss chests contain blights after beating Act 3 on Endless. | Whenever the player kills a boss after beating Act 3 for the first time this run, instead of a boss chest with a choice of 3 boss relics, the player will be given a blight chest with a choice of 2 blights.  Has no effect if Endless Mode is not enabled. |
| Hoarder* |  | Whenever you add a card to your deck, add two additional copies. You can no longer remove cards from your deck at the Merchant. | Transformed cards will produce 3 of the card they transform into, and curses will be added 3 at a time.  Also affects Draft, Sealed Deck, Specialized, and All Star.  Does not affect starting deck, Insanity, Chimera, Shiny, or My True Form.  Mind Blast becomes very powerful.  Smiling Mask will not appear. |
| Insanity* |  | Start with a random deck of 50 cards. | Mutually exclusive with Shiny.  Pandora's Box will not appear. |
| Chimera* |  | Your starting deck is a fusion of 4 characters. | Start with Bash, Survivor, Zap, Eruption, a Red, Blue and Green Strike and a Red, Green and Purple Defend. |
| Praise Snecko |  | Replaces your starting relic with Snecko Eye. | Works with other modifiers that replace your starting relic. |
| Shiny* |  | Starting deck is replaced with 1 of every rare card. | Grants 1 of each of your character's rare cards. Having the Cards or Diverse modifiers gives rare cards from other characters too.  Pandora's Box will not appear. |
| Specialized* |  | Start with 5 copies of a single card. | The card is a random card. Works with the "Cards" modifiers and Diverse. |
| Vintage* |  | Normal Enemies drop relics instead of cards. | Elites and Bosses will still drop cards. |
| Controlled Chaos* |  | Start with Frozen Eye. At the start of your turn, add 10 random cards to the bottom of your draw pile. | - |
| Inception |  | Replaces your starting relic with Unceasing Top. | Works with other modifiers that replace your starting relic. |
| All Star* |  | Start with 5 colorless cards. | The cards may be different and have random rarities. |
| Diverse* |  | Cards are not restricted by your character. | Grants an Orb Slot to a character that is not the Defect.  Prismatic Shard will not appear. |
| Red Cards* |  | Red cards now appear in rewards and shops. | Affects Sealed Deck, Shiny, Draft, and Insanity. |
| Green Cards* |  | Green cards now appear in rewards and shops. | Affects Sealed Deck, Shiny, Draft, and Insanity. |
| Blue Cards* |  | Blue cards now appear in rewards and shops. | Affects Sealed Deck, Shiny, Draft, and Insanity. Grants an Orb Slot to a character that is not the Defect. |

## Strategy
- In Act 1, this is a solid pick for decent AOE damage, and will help you get through a number of Act 1/Act 2 fights:
    - The Sentry elite fight
    - Any fights involving Slimes
    - Any fights involving Gremlins
    - The 3-Byrd fight in Act 2
    - 2 of the 3 elite fights in Act 2 (Gremlin Leader and Taskmaster + Slavers)
- After Act 2 this card pretty rapidly falls off, and generally is not recommended to take more than one during a run.

## Interactions
- Since it hits twice, Strength is twice as effective.
- Envenom can trigger twice (if unblocked).
- It tends to finish off weaker enemies, perfect for Gremlin Horn.
- This card is very effective against Byrds.
- Weak hurts the damage badly without any buffs.

# Dark Embrace

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Dark_Embrace

**Infobox:**
- Name: Dark Embrace
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/a/a6/DarkEmbrace.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20200128065538
- Class: Ironclad
- Type: Power
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Cost: 2
- Effect: Whenever a card is Exhausted,; draw 1 card.
- [Dark Embrace+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: Whenever a card is Exhausted,; draw 1 card.
- Name: Dark Embrace
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/c/c0/Icon_DarkEmbrace.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202161845
- Description: Whenever a card is Exhausted, draw X cards.
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: Intensity

**Dark Embrace** is a Power card for the Ironclad. After it is played, each time a card is Exhausted, you immediately draw 1 card per card Exhausted.

When Upgraded, Dark Embrace costs 1 Energy instead of 2. 

## Mechanics

- The Dark Embrace buff is stackable, so playing multiple copies will draw more and more cards for a single card Exhausted. 
- Ethereal cards Exhaust at the end of your turn, and effectively causes you to draw cards in advance of your next turn.

## Tips
- Dark Embrace is extremely powerful in concert with Corruption. Corruption allows you to play any Skill for free, and when that card Exhausts itself, Dark Embrace will draw an additional card to replace it. This can lead to explosive combos, particularly after using multiple copies of Dark Embrace.
- Dark Embrace makes it possible to copy Fiend Fire with Double Tap or Necronomicon. Normally, the second use of Fiend Fire does nothing because there are no more cards in hand to Exhaust, but having Dark Embrace will repopulate the hand with cards for the second Fiend Fire to burn.

# Darkling

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Darkling

**Infobox:**
- Name: Darkling
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/d/d0/Darkling.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20180922060146
- HP: 48-56; 50-59 (Ascension 7+)
- In Party With: 2 other Darklings
- Debut Act: Act 3
- Powers: Life Link
- Name: Life Link
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/c/c7/Icon_LifeLink.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202163113
- Description: Cannot be targeted for 2 turns once HP reaches 0. On its second turn after its HP reaches 0, revives with half HP if other Darklings have over 0 HP.
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: None

**Darklings** are an Act 3 encounter. The player will fight 3 Darklings at a time, and they all start with the Life Link buff.

## Pattern
On the first turn, all Darklings have a 50% chance of using Nip and a 50% chance of using Harden. The middle Darkling continues this pattern afterwards; it cannot use Chomp.

After the first turn, the outer 2 Darklings have a 30% chance of using Nip, 40% chance of using Chomp and 30% chance of using Harden.

Harden cannot be used twice in a row, Chomp cannot be used twice in a row and Nip cannot be used three times in a row.

After the HP of a Darkling reaches 0, the Darkling can no longer be targeted and Regrow will interrupt its current intent. It will use Reincarnate on the next turn. 

| Name | Intent | Effect | Asc 2+ | Asc 17+ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Nip |  | Deal D* damage. | Deal D* + 2 damage. | Deal D* + 2 damage. |
| Chomp |  | Deal 8 x 2 damage. | Deal 9 x 2 damage. | Deal 9 x 2 damage. |
| Harden |  | Gain 12 Block. | Gain 12 Block. | Gain 12 Block and 2 Strength. |
| Reincarnate |  | Revives with 50% HP. | Revives with 50% HP. | Revives with 50% HP. |
| Regrow |  | Does nothing. | Does nothing. | Does nothing. |
*D is chosen between 7 and 11 at the beginning of the battle.

## Notes
Kill effects *that work on minions* do have their kill effect on all Darklings regardless of whether it is the last Darkling (e.g. Sunder). However, fatal Kill effects that do not work on minions (i.e. Feed, Ritual Dagger, Lesson Learned, Hand of Greed) only work if you kill the final Darkling.

## Sources of Dazed
- Enemies

## Interactions
- Evolve: Draw 1 more card for each Dazed you draw. Stacking Evolves can allow you to draw 2 more cards when you draw a Dazed, potentially making Dazed actively beneficial. Can still lead to a hand of 10 dazed, however.
- Exhaust synergies can use Dazed as Exhaust fuel. In addition, any effects you may gain from exhausting a card are fulfilled at the end of the turn, since Dazed is Ethereal.
- Medical Kit allows Dazed to be played and exhausted for no penalty, though they already exhaust at the end of your turn.

## Notes
- Thanks to the Ethereal keyword, Dazed cards can be exhausted without the help of other cards. To take advantage of this, simply have the Dazed card in hand at the end of your turn. Only Dazed cards that end the turn in your hand will be exhausted. If you Discard a copy of Dazed, it will remain in your discard pile and will not be exhausted.

# Dead Adventurer

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Dead_Adventurer

**Dead Adventurer** is an event found exclusively in Act 1. The player finds the remains of a fellow traveler slayed by one of the Exordium's Elites. The player can risk a difficult fight for a free Relic, Gold, or both; or safely escape.

This event only appears on floor 7 and above.

## Options

*Numbers in parentheses are for Ascension 15 or higher.*

- **[Search]** Find Loot. 25% (35%) that an Elite will return to fight you.
    - **[Search]** can yield:
      - 30 Gold.
      - A random Relic.
      - Nothing.
    - Each reward only occurs once - if the player's first search found nothing and the second search found the Relic, the third search will either reward 30 Gold or start a battle.
    - Each subsequent **[Search]** increases the chance to encounter an Elite by 25%.
    - If the player successfully **[Search]** three times without encountering an Elite, the event will end with a short dialogue detailing the success.

- **[Escape]** End the search and resume your journey.
    - There is no penalty for choosing **[Escaping]** - the player keeps whatever they obtained from **[Search]**  and resume their journey.

The Event has a text at the beginning, describing how the unfortunate adventurer was killed. It gives a hint about which Elite you will fight:
- '''*"...eviscerated and chopped by giant claws."* :''' Lagavulin
    - Unlike its usual Elite battle, Lagavulin doesn't begin Asleep.  It instead starts the fight with Siphon Soul.  
- '''*"...scoured by flames."* :** 3 Sentries
- ***"...gouged and trampled by a horned beast."* :** Gremlin Nob

Defeating the Elite grants whatever rewards not yet found by **[Search]''', in addition to 25-35 gold. 
- Note that the Elite itself doesn't reward an additional Relic if you had already found one from **[Search]**.

Relics that triggers on Elites combat - Preserved Insect, Sling of Courage, and Slaver's Collar - also works on Elite combat of this event. The only exception is Black Star, which has no effect whatsoever in this fight.

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| *You come across a dead adventurer on the floor.* |
| *His pants have been stolen! Also, ... * |
| Lagavulin Chance Encounter |
| *...he looks to have been eviscerated and chopped by giant claws.* |
| 3 Sentries Chance Encounter |
| *...the armor and face appear to be scoured by flames.* |
| Gremlin Nob Chance Encounter |
| ''...it looks as though he's been gouged and trampled by a horned beast.* |
| *Though his possessions are still intact, you're in no mind to find out what happened here...* |
| Search |
| Obtain Gold |
| *You found some gold!* |
| Obtain a Relic |
| *You found a Relic!!* |
| Found Nothing |
| *Hmm, couldn't find anything...* |
| *Continue searching?* |
| Elite Encounter |
| *While searching the adventurer you are caught off guard!* |
| 3 Successful Searches |
| *Looks like you searched all his belongings without a hitch!* |
| Escape |
| *You exit without a sound.'' |

## Strategy

Keep in mind that there is a chance that **[Search]** might not yield gold or relics.

Ignore the odds - consider the Dead Adventurer Event to be an optional Elite fight, and imagine that you'll fight the Elite 100% of the time you press the **[Search]** button. If you're confident in your deck and you have plenty of HP, prepare for battle and press the button. You might be pleasantly surprised by a free Relic, but you could also be fighting an Elite for it.  

If you obtained a Relic from, **[Search]**, consider leaving immediately, as the Elite will only reward you with some gold, card selection, and a score bonus.

The Lagavulin fight spawned from this event is much more deadly than normal, as it does not begin asleep and will immediately use Siphon Soul.  If your deck does not have a reliable damage source outside of normal attacks, this fight will cause you to lose a huge amount of health,  especially on high ascension levels.

If you can't beat the Elite, but you don't think you can beat the Boss either, you may want to roll the dice anyway. Although the odds of getting a lifesaving Relic for free are extremely low, they're better than a guaranteed loss against the Boss.

## Trivia
- The dead adventurer has an internal name of "Nopants".

### Powers

# Debuff

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Debuff

A **debuff** is a negative ongoing effect given to the character or an enemy by certain Cards, Relics, or Potions.

Debuffs can be negated by the Artifact Buff. Orange Pellets will remove all debuff on the character if the player successfully played Attack, Skill, and Power in the same turn.

Debuffs may stack by duration, lasting X turns, or by intensity, applying their effect with X power. Some debuffs do not stack at all.

# Defect

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Defect

*"Combat automaton which became self-aware. Ancient technology allows manipulation of Orbs."*

The **Defect** is one of four playable characters in Slay the Spire. Once among the like of Orb Walkers and Bronze Automaton as one of many ancient automatons, it has since gained sentience and seeks its way out of the Spire. It attacks foes with a high-tech arsenal, array of Powers, and elemental evocations.
The Defect has a unique mechanic, the Orbs. Using cards and Relics, The Defect Channels these elemental spheres into a set of Orb slots, activating their passive effects each turn or Evoking them for a one-time burst. The Defect starts with three Orb slots, though cards and relics can add or consume them. It starts with 75 hp.

The Defect's starting Relic is Cracked Core, which Channels 1 Lightning at the start of each combat.

It was added to the beta build in Weekly Patch 22: Testing the Third Character during the early access. It was released to the public, along with the game and other two characters on January 23rd, 2019.

## Cards
### Starting Deck
- 4 Strike_B
- 4 Defend_B
- 1 Zap
- 1 Dualcast
Defect Card Navbox

## Gameplay

### Orbs
*Main article: Orbs*

The Defect begins with three Orb slots and considers the rightmost Orb to be the 'next' Orb to Evoke. Channelling an Orb inserts it into the rightmost empty slot. If every slot is full, each Orb will be shifted one slot to the right, popping the right-most Orb out of its slot and Evoking it. The Defect can have a maximum of 10 Orb slots.

Lightning, Frost and Dark orbs have a passive effect that activates at the end of the Defect's turn, from right to left, or oldest to newest. The passive effect of Plasma activates at the start of the Defect's turn. While these effects are initially weak, The Defect can increase Focus and channel additional copies to sharply increase their potency.

### Focus
*Main article: Focus*

**Focus** is a stat unique to The Defect that affects Orbs the same way Strength affects Attacks and Dexterity affects Block. Increasing Focus increases the magnitude of both the passive and Evoke effects of each Orb (except for Plasma). It is possible to reduce Orb effects to 0 by decreasing Focus.

## Relics
The Defect has fewer class-specific relics than the other classes, having only one class-specific rare relic rather than three (like the Ironclad and Silent) or two (like the Watcher). The Watcher has equally few overall, but instead of being short two Rare relics is short one Rare and one Boss relic.

Starting Relic: Cracked Core

Common Relic: Data Disk

Uncommon Relics: Gold-Plated Cables, Symbiotic Virus

Rare Relics: Emotion Chip

Boss Relics: Frozen Core (replaces Cracked Core), Inserter, Nuclear Battery

Shop Relic: Runic Capacitor

## Strategy
The Defect's game plan almost always involves implementing a long-term plan each battle. By developing Orbs, Powers, and cards with escalating effects, the Defect sets up an insurmountable late-game position and then destroys its enemies with its accumulated advantage. This is a radically different style from the Silent and the Ironclad, who tend to apply bursts of damage to take enemies out opportunistically.

Due to the nature of this approach to deckbuilding, the Defect may struggle in the early-game, when it is not capable of producing such unbreakable barriers on command. However, the Defect inarguably has one of the highest peaks regarding sheer dominance out of all characters - one example is the "Frost Turtle" build, which, when heavily optimized, allows the Defect to gain hundreds of block per turn consistently. Even the tankiest and most heavy-hitting enemies may be completely outclassed by the Defect.

However, the Defect notably struggles to win with a deck full of "good stuff". While it does have access to some individually strong cards, they don't present the sheer power that the other characters enjoy without support. However, due to the long-term nature of its best strategies, the Defect must sometimes take such individually strong cards, either to survive the first few acts or to provide frontloaded solutions while it sets up.

Juggling deckbuilding decisions between these two extremes of short-term benefit v.s. long-term power is thus an ongoing struggle during every Defect run, yet a rewarding one once all of the pieces fall into place. 

The Defect also has a higher number of chance-based effects, like Hello World, Chaos, and Creative AI.

The Defect's strongly synergistic cards encourage some powerful and well-supported archetypes. Identifying and focusing on one is a key aspect of the Defect strategy.

### Build types
Listed below are the standard synergies that Defect decks build towards, which may give you an idea of direction for your own runs. Some important things to keep in mind:
- Most of these builds aren't mutually exclusive. Think of each of the archetypes listed below as an engine that you can incorporate into your deck; depending on the situation, you are more than able to adapt or combine multiple of them.
- It's important to not "force" a particular build from the outset of the game. Build your deck to solve your immediate problems first and foremost, then allow an archetype to come to you organically. The only exception would be if you run into cards or relics in the early-game that are both individually impactful *and* form the crux of an entire archetype, and such situations are few and far between.

Focus Stacking

# Designer In-Spire

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Designer_In-Spire

**Designer In-Spire** is an event that can appear in Act 2, and Act 3. You encounter a shop with a snobbish owner, who reluctantly offers you his service.

If you would die to the **[Punch]** option, and do not have enough money for any other option, you will not encounter this event.

## Options

*Numbers in parentheses are for Ascension 15 or higher.*

- **[Adjustments]** Lose 40 (50) Gold. The reward presented will be one of these two:
    - Upgrade a card.
    - Upgrade 2 random cards.
- **[Clean Up]** Lose 60 (75) Gold. The reward presented will be one of these two:
    - Remove a card.
    - Transform 2 cards.
- **[Full Service]** Lose 90 (110) Gold. Remove a card, then upgrade a random card.
- **[Punch]** Lose 3 (5) HP.

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| *You discover a colorful shop with the banner* "IN-SPIRE" ''and walk in to see what's inside.* |
| *"No, no way. Nope. Can't let you in!" A man with ridiculous clothing appears at the entrance to bar you.* |
| **Designer:** *"This will not do, no no. What is this style?* Disgusting! *Are you bleeeeding? Groooss.* Business?? *You a customer? Fine. Whaaatever."* |
| *He lets out an exaggerated sigh and points at a list of services.* |
| *The services seem fine, but you would rather punch this smug man in his smug face.* |
| Adjustment, Clean Up, or Full Service |
| **Designer:** *"Okay, bye bye now."* |
| * ...should've punched him.* |
| Punch |
| *You punch him so hard your fist hurts.* |
| **Designer:** *"My* FACE!! *Now I'll have to-"* |
| *He fainted. Who's groooss and bleeeeding now?* |

## Notes
- If you have insufficient gold, not enough cards to upgrade, or not enough cards to remove, the corresponding option will be disabled.
    - If none of the first three options are available, you will be forced to select **[Punch]** to leave the event.

## Trivia
- The name of the shop is a pun on the word "Inspire". 
    - The shop belongs to a designer, who draws from many *inspir*ations.
    - The shop is literally *in* the *Spire''.

# Deus Ex Machina

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Deus_Ex_Machina

**Infobox:**
- Name: Deus Ex Machina
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/b/b6/DeusExMachina.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20191106145542
- Class: Watcher
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Rare
- Effect: Unplayable. When you draw this card, add 2 Miracles into your hand. Exhaust.
- [Deus Ex Machina+]
- Effect+: Unplayable. When you draw this card, add 3 Miracles into your hand. Exhaust.

CardAutoboxDeus Ex Machina adds 2 (3) Miracles to your hand when drawn.

## Interactions
 
- If the Master Reality buff is active, Deus Ex Machina's added Miracle cards (Gain ) will upgrade to Miracle+ (Gain ).

 
- Deus Ex Machina is only activated when the card is drawn. Adding Deus Ex Machina to your hand (such as with  or a Skill Potion) or placing it directly into your hand (such as with Secret Technique) will not activate the card.

- Be mindful of your hand size when using this card! If drawn into a full hand, such as after playing Scrawl, if your hand does not have enough space for the every generated Miracle, the excess Miracles will be placed into your discard pile except for one. Enabling the "Show Card Quick Select Keys" option in the options menu on PC can be a lot of help in this regard.

**Infobox:**
- Name: Deva Form
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/b/b6/DevaForm.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20190920011848

- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/7/7e/Icon_DevaForm.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202161846
- Description: At the start of your turn gain Energy N times and increase this gain by X.
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: Intensity[1][2]

CardAutobox

**Deva Form** is a Rare Power card for the Watcher that grants the player the **Deva** buff, which increases the amount of Energy the player gets at the start of their turn by one every turn; in other words, once Deva Form is played, the player will have one more Energy to spend every turn afterwards.

## Interactions
 
- Being a high-cost power card, Deva Form is a strong candidate for using alongside Omniscience.
- Conjure Blade can create extremely powerful Expungers using the excess energy generated by Deva Form.
- The energy drawback of Fasting is easily minimized by Deva Form.
- Deva Form, in general, makes X cost Cards much more accessible.

## Trivia

- A *deva* is a Hindu term for a deity.
- Though the Watcher is female, *deva* is a masculine term; the feminine equivalent is *devi*.
- The card art depicts the relics Singing Bowl, Vajra, and Juzu Bracelet.

**Devotion** adds 2(3) Mantra at the start of each turn. This can provide significant aid in reaching the Divinity stance.

Devotion ultimately ends up being a niche inclusion to the mantra build, and it must be upgraded. Devotion is unfortunately very slow, but in longer fights (such as boss fights), it can be very powerful. It stacks very well with itself, and if you can somehow put 3 of these into play, you can enter Divinity every turn with ease.

Dexterity is a buff that increases Block given by cards.

- Each point of Dexterity gives +1 Block per card.
- All player characters are capable of gaining Dexterity via relics or potions. The Silent, The Defect, and The Watcher are also capable of gaining Dexterity with cards.
- It is possible to have negative stacks of Dexterity. For every negative stack, each instance of Block is reduced by 1.
- Dexterity is applied before Frail.
- Despite the tooltip, Dexterity only applies to cards that **directly** gives your Block, which means it does not work for Powers and other buff-based cards.
    - For example, Metallicize will not be affected by Dexterity since it gives Block through its buff.

## Sources

### Cards
#### Silent Cards
- Footwork: 2(3) Dexterity

#### Defect Cards
- Reprogram: 1(2) Dexterity

#### Watcher Cards
- Fasting: 3(4) Dexterity

### Relics
- Oddly Smooth Stone: 1 Dexterity
- Kunai: 1 Dexterity for every 3 Attack cards played in a single turn.
- Duality: 1 temporary Dexterity for every Attack cards played this turn. Last until the end of your turn.

### Other
- Dexterity Potion: 2(4) Dexterity
- Speed Potion: 5(10) Dexterity. At the end of your turn, lose 5 (10) Dexterity.

CardAutobox
Discovery is a colorless Uncommon Skill that that presents you with 3 random cards from the card pool of the character you are playing, from which you may choose one to add to your hand (Adding one is mandatory). The card added to your hand has its cost reduced to 0 for the turn. Discovery then Exhausts.

Prismatic Shard does not affect the variety of colors of the card it generated. It however is affected by Run Modifiers, which could potentially allow it to present you with more than one color of cards. 

Upgrading Discovery causes it to no longer Exhaust.

It can only generate a card that is available through shop and rewards with some exceptions. It cannot generate a healing card.

# Distraction

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Distraction

**Infobox:**
- Name: Distraction
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/e/e3/Distraction.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016211544
- Class: Silent
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Cost: 1
- Effect: Add a random Skill into your hand.; It costs 0 this turn.Exhaust.
- [Distraction+]
- Cost+: 0
- Effect+: Add a random Skill into your hand.; It costs 0 this turn.Exhaust.

-**Distraction** is an Uncommon Skill for the Silent that generates a random Skill and reduces its cost to 0 for the turn, then Exhausts.

If you use Distraction as other character that is not the Silent, it will grant a random Skill card of the respective color of that character. For example, if you obtained this card as the Defect, it will grant you blue Skill cards. Prismatic Shard does not affect the variety of colors of the card it generated. It however is affected by Run Modifiers, which could potentially allow it to generate an Skill from more than one color of cards pools.

Upgrading Distraction decreases its cost to 0.

It can only generate cards that is available through shop and rewards. It cannot generate a healing card.

### Excluded Cards
- Alchemize *(Healing, as it could generate Regen Potion, and its potion can trigger Toy Ornithopter.)*
- Wish *(Healing, as it can trigger Bloody Idol.)*
- Bandage Up *(Healing)*
- Apparition *(Event-exclusive)*
- J.A.X. *(Event-exclusive)*
- Beta *(Card effect only)*
- Insight *(Cards effect only)*
- Miracle *(Cards, relics, and potion effect only)*
- Safety *(Card effect only)*

## Strategy
Distraction is almost always a low-powered card. The Silent has many Skills that are weak on their own but powerful in combination, so the Skill you get is unlikely to perform at full strength. Worse, The Silent has many 0-cost Skills like Setup that actually waste your Energy.

If you're desperate for Block and defensive Skills, then Distraction could be your only option. Otherwise, you're better off skipping the pick and instead picking a Skill you actually want.

## Synergies
Distraction synergizes with effects like Choke, Panache, and A Thousand Cuts that count the number of cards played.

- Foreign Influence
- Discovery

# Divinity

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Divinity

Divinity is one of the three Stances of the Watcher, with the others being Calm and Wrath.

Upon entering this Stance, you immediately gain .  While in Divinity, all Attacks deal triple damage. At the start of your next turn, if you are still in Divinity, you will automatically exit it.

Accumulating 10 or more Mantra causes the Watcher to enter Divinity. Once you have gained at least 10 Mantra, exactly 10 Mantra is immediately consumed (with excess stacks of Mantra remaining) and you enter Divinity. If you still have at least 10 Mantra at the start of the next turn, you will exit Divinity and immediately reenter it again.

# Donu and Deca

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Donu_and_Deca

**Infobox:**
- Name: Donu and Deca
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/0/04/Donu.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20180911020320
- HP: 250; 265 (Ascension 9+)
- In Party With: Each other
- Debut Act: Act 3
- Powers: Artifact 2; Artifact 3 (Ascension 19+)

-**Donu and Deca** are one of the three bosses encountered at the end of Act 3.

## Pattern

### Donu
Donu always starts with Circle of Power, then alternates between Beam and Circle of Power.
| Name | Intent | Effect | Asc 4+ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Circle of Power |  | All enemies gain 3 Strength. | All enemies gain 3 Strength. |
| Beam |  | Deal 10 x 2 damage. | Deal 12 x 2 damage. |

### Deca
Deca always starts with Beam, then alternates between Square of Protection and Beam.
| Name | Intent | Effect | Asc 4+ | Asc 19+ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Square of Protection |  | All enemies gain 16 Block. | All enemies gain 16 Block. | All enemies gain 16 Block and 3 Plated Armor. |
| Beam |  | Deal 10 x 2 damage, shuffle 2 Dazed into the discard pile. | Deal 12 x 2 damage, shuffle 2 Dazed into the discard pile. | Deal 12 x 2 damage, shuffle 2 Dazed into the discard pile. |

## Tips
Compared to the other Act 3 boss fights, the Donu and Deca fight is a simple but brutal slugfest. Their consistent attack patterns make them easy to predict, but they attack every turn and their damage scales rapidly due to Donu's Circle of Power. Furthermore, their plated armor grants them a deceptive amount of HP over the course of the fight, while their initial Artifact charges grant them a degree of resistance against powerful cards like Bash and Piercing Wail.

Most of the time, you should choose one of the two bosses to focus down before moving on to the other. Decks that cannot out-block the scaling damage from Circle of Power should typically kill Donu as quickly as possible. On the other hand, the Dazes that Deca shuffles into the discard pile can vastly slow down your draw as the fight wears on, particularly for decks lacking in card draw. These decks may prefer to kill Deca first.

## Trivia
- By killing Donu with Feed, the player gets the "Ooh Donut" achievement.
- Despite Deca's name, Deca is an octahedron.

# Double Tap

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Double_Tap

**Infobox:**
- Name: Double Tap
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/8/84/DoubleTap.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016205819
- Class: Ironclad
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Rare
- Cost: 1
- Effect: This turn, your next Attack is1 Attacks are] played twice.
- [Double Tap+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: This turn, your next 2 Attacks are] played twice.
- Name: Double Tap
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/a/aa/Icon_DoubleTap.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202161847
- Description: Your next X Attacks are played twice.
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: Counter

**Double Tap** is a Skill card for the Ironclad. It plays the next Attack card this turn a second time, for no Energy. As a Rare card, it can be obtained after defeating a Boss. It is Ironclad's version of Burst and Amplify.

Upon upgrade, it will trigger for the 2nd Attack card played in the same turn.

The second play is NOT added to your draw or discard pile.

The scaling buff from Double Tap (and also from Burst and Amplify) is the number of cards that will be played twice, not the number of times the card will be played. This means playing multiple Double Taps will add to the number of cards that will be played twice that turn, not make the next card play 3 or more times.

## Interactions
- The second play will not cost any Energy, but it will trigger any other consequences of playing the card. For example, a Double Tapped Hemokinesis will trigger the self-damage twice.
- The second play of a card that costs X energy will use the same value of X as the first.
- The second play acts as a separate card. This has interactions including, but not limited to:
    - Rage.
    - Shuriken, Kunai, and Pen Nib: Both plays count towards playing Attacks for their benefits. The second play can possibly receive triggered benefits.
    - Velvet Choker: Both plays count towards the amount of cards played for the turn.
    - Time Eater's Time Warp power: Both plays increase the counter as usual. If the second attack is the 13th action on his counter, it will NOT occur, unlike Velvet Choker.

- The second play happens after the Attack is sent to the draw, discard or Exhaust piles. This has interactions including, but not limited to:
    - Headbutt: The second play can return the original Headbutt into the deck.
    - Malleable: Snake Plant receives its armor from Malleable after the first play.
- The second play can trigger any Exhaust synergies, but only if the Attack Exhausts when played.
    - In other words, the Double Tap copy "not going to your discard pile" does NOT count as an Exhaust by itself.

- Description: Whenever you rest, you may add a card to your deck.
- Flavor: The northern tribes would often use dream catchers at night, believing they led to self improvement.
- Rarity: Common
- Class: Any

**Dream Catcher** is a common Relic that improves the Rest Site's "Rest" option: now you may add a card to your deck when sleeping.

It uses the regular card adding mechanic, meaning that you will be given 3 cards (or their upgraded versions) to choose from.

This relic does not spawn beyond floor 48, excluding Endless mode.

## Interactions
Dream Catcher will interact with Relics that affect your card rewards:
- Positive
    - Question Card will give you 4 choices instead of 3.
    - With Singing Bowl, you can get +2 Max HP instead of a card.
    - Molten Egg, Toxic Egg, and Frozen Egg will upgrade the card that you get from this.
    - Prismatic Shard will generate cards from all colors.
    - Fusion Hammer forces you to rest in most situations.
- Negative
    - Busted Crown will reduce the amount of choices by 2.
    - Coffee Dripper disables resting, making Dream Catcher useless.

**Dropkick** is an Attack card for the Ironclad. It deals 5(8) damage; if the target is Vulnerable, then it refunds its cost of 1 Energy and draws another card. As an Uncommon card, it appears as a reward for combat, although less often than Commons.

## Interactions
- Any method of applying Vulnerable consistently will turn Dropkick into free damage. Since Dropkick recovers its energy and draws an additional card, it will effectively have no cost, similarly to Flash of Steel.

- If something such as Madness reduces the cost of Dropkick to 0, it will still provide 1 energy if the enemy is Vulnerable, making it even more powerful.
    - However, if anything increases Dropkick's cost above 1, it will still only refund 1 energy, making it an undesirable choice in Snecko Eye builds.

# Du-Vu Doll

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Du-Vu_Doll

**Infobox:**
- Name: Du-Vu Doll
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/7/79/Du-VuDoll.png/revision/latest?cb=20190923233622
- Description: For each Curse in your deck, start each combat with 1 additional Strength.
- Flavor: A doll devised to gain strength from malicious energy.
- Rarity: Rare
- Class: Any

Du-Vu Doll is typically a bad relic, as adding curses to your deck is rarely worth a single strength. However, on Ascension 10 and above, your deck always has a Ascender's Bane in it, meaning that this relic always provides at least 1 strength, making it technically as valuable as a much better Vajra.

# Dual Wield

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Dual_Wield

**Infobox:**
- Name: Dual Wield
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/6/61/DualWield.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016205819
- Class: Ironclad
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Cost: 1
- Effect: Choose an Attack or Power card. Add a copy of that card into your hand.
- [Dual Wield+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: Choose an Attack or Power card. Add 2 copies of that card into your hand.

**Dual Wield** is a Skill card for the Ironclad. The player selects an Attack or Power in their hand, then creates a copy of that card. When Upgraded, Dual Wield creates 2 copies of the selected card instead of 1.

## Mechanics
- All characteristics of the selected card are copied. When copying a card with altered Energy cost or altered text, such as those related to Madness, Confused, Rampage, and Blood for Blood, the modifications are also copied.
- If the player's hand is full, the copied card(s) is sent to the discard pile.
- Copied cards only exist during the combat that Dual Wield is played, and will not carry over after the combat is finished.

## Bugs
If Ritual Dagger is the only valid card in hand for Dual Wield to select, then the copy(s) will be added to the right side of hand, and the original card will remain untouched, wherever it was in the hand.

However, if there are multiple options to select from, when Ritual Dagger is selected, it will be completely removed from the game for that combat, and 2 (3) copies will be created on the right side of your hand. This prevents Ritual Dagger from being upgraded.

Thus, playing Dual Wield on Ritual Dagger *sometimes* prevents Ritual Dagger from being able to be upgraded.

## Tips
- Any mechanic which creates 0-cost cards that are normally expensive can be very powerful with Dual Wield as the copies also cost 0. Potions that do this are power, attack and liquid memories. Relics include Mummified Hand and cards include Discovery, Infernal Blade, Madness and more.

- Duel Wield can copy powerful self-Exhausting cards like Feed and Pummel so they can be played repeatedly, or copy Powers to stack their effects. Consider discarding the copy instead of playing it, so that it can be copied more when drawn again. 
- Copies of Searing Blow will remain Upgraded, so Dual Wield works well when creating copies of a highly-Upgraded Searing Blow.

- Dual Wield doesn't Exhaust itself, allowing the player to repeatedly copy the same card. By Exhausting undesired cards with True Grit and similar cards, the player can create a deck containing nothing but a single powerful card or combo.

- Copying a "Strike" card with Dual Wield increases the power of Perfected Strike. Perfected Strike itself is a "Strike" card, so making copies of Perfected Strike makes them all more powerful.

- Prioritize copying key cards as quickly as possible, as having more copies makes it more likely to draw that card and Dual Wield again on future turns.

**Duplicator** is an event that can appear in Act 1, Act 2, and Act 3. You encounter a shrine with the power to duplicate a card.

- **[Leave]** Nothing happens.

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| *Before you lies a decorated altar to some ancient entity.* |
| Pray |
| *You kneel respectfully. A ghastly mirror image appears from the shrine and collides into you.* |

| *You ignore the shrine, confident in your choice.* |
## Notes
- Duplicating an upgraded card results in an upgraded copy.
- Duplicated copy of Ritual Dagger or Genetic Algorithm will carry over the value that the card has gained.
- Duplicated copy of Bottled card will NOT carry over its Bottled status. You are NOT guaranteed to draw a duplicated copy of a Bottled card on your first turn.

# Echo Form

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Echo_Form

**Infobox:**
- Name: Echo Form
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/9/93/EchoForm.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016203426
- Class: Defect
- Type: Power
- Rarity: Rare
- Cost: 3
- Effect: Ethereal. ; The first card you play each turn is played twice.
- [Echo Form+]
- Cost+: 3
- Effect+: The first card you play each turn is played twice.
- Name: Echo Form
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/d/d1/Icon_EchoForm.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202162042
- Description: The first X cards you play each turn are played twice.
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: Counter

CardAutobox

**Echo Form** is a Power card for The Defect that bestows a powerful card-doubling effect at a high price. As a Rare card, Echo Form is generally obtainable as a Boss reward and at high cost from The Merchant. However, it can rarely drop from an Elite or even a normal Monster.

Upgrading Echo Form causes it to lose the Ethereal keyword.

## Card Effect
Echo Form's printed text only loosely explains its behavior.

A more descriptive effect is that Echo Form causes the first card you play each turn to be played twice unless the enemy dies from the first play. In this case the next card will be doubled instead.

Though the doubled card appears to Exhaust, it does not count for any synergies Exhausting normally does.

Multiple stacks of Echo Form will cause more of your cards per turn to be played twice. (Your first card will not be played three or more times). If the first card you play is another Echo Form, you will have three stacks of Echo Form and two more cards this turn will be played twice.

The Amplify buff (as well as other card-doubling effects) is not applied to the copies created by Echo Form. For example, with two stacks of Echo Form active, playing Amplify and a power card will cause the power card to be played three times (one copy from Amplify and one from Echo Form), with one stack of Amplify left over.

## Interactions
 
- After Image, A Thousand Cuts: The duplicate card activates each power's respective effects.
- Claw, Rampage: Echo Form's second card will use the first card's damage and increase it in Claw's case.
- Genetic Algorithm, Ritual Dagger: Echo Form's second card will also increase Genetic Algorithm's Block and Ritual Dagger's damage (if Fatal).
- When triggering on an X card, the same value for X is used on the second play.

 
- Although the copied card has the Exhaust visual effects, it doesn't appear in the Exhausted pile or trigger effects that activate when a card is Exhausted.
- Mayhem: Mayhem's card will be doubled.

 
- Velvet Choker, Time Eater's Time Warp, Chosen's Hex : Echo Form's second card counts towards these objects' respective effects.
- Blue Candle, Medical Kit: Statuses or Curses played will be doubled, wasting Echo Form.

## Synergy
- Echo Form combines a big effect with a big cost. Three Energy is generally an entire turn, and the card has literally no effect when played. Before the card is upgraded, the player doesn't even get to pick which turn to sacrifice!

- The decision to upgrade Echo Form depends more on whether the card is an integral part of the deck. If so, there's no need to upgrade it as you'll play it as soon as you draw it. If not, deliberately Exhausting Echo Form can be a relevant option in battles that demand efficient plays.

- When your deck contains Echo Form, select paths that offer many Rest Sites and Events. The Defect will likely take a beating after each Echo Form, and you'll need to recover some health.

- The strongest cards to Echo Form include:
    - **Powers** - Echo Form acts as a free Amplify that The Defect can set up in advance. Copying Static Discharge, Self Repair, Biased Cognition, and even another **Echo Form** is a powerful play.
    - **Energy** - Doubling Meteor Strike, Fusion, Aggregate, and especially Double Energy generates massive resources. Echo Form also helps activate Sunder's Energy-producing effect.
    - **Multi-Channel** - Cards that generate two or more Orbs, especially Rainbow+ and Chaos+, outperform with an Echo Form. The surplus of Orbs can instantly recover from Fission or Evoke multiple times.

- When building around Echo Form, mitigate incoming damage by picking zero-Energy defensive tools like Orichalcum, Anchor, Boot Sequence, Buffer, and Energy-granting Relics like Cursed Key.

# Elites

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Elites

Elites are stronger monsters that are marked separately from normal ones on the map. Defeating an elite will grant you a random relic, 25-35 gold, a card reward and add a score bonus. Depending on the strength of one's deck, fighting elites may not always be a good idea, but the relics they grant can be very powerful. The same elite can appear multiple times in an act, but cannot be encountered twice in a row. The Dead Adventurer event completely ignores this.

Playing in Ascension Mode will make elites more common, as the Ascension 1 modifier makes them more common. In addition, higher ascension levels will make elites stronger and tougher.

Relics that affect elite encounters:
- Black Star: Instead of dropping 1 random relic, defeated elites will instead drop 2 random relics.
- Sling of Courage: The player will start each elite combat with 2 Strength.
- Preserved Insect: All enemies found in elite rooms will start combat with 25% less HP.
- Slaver's Collar: During Boss and Elite combats, gain Energy at the start of your turn.

With the exception of Black Star, these relics also work in the Dead Adventurer fight and the second fight in The Colosseum.

After unlocking Act 4, until the Emerald Key is obtained, one of the elites in each Act will appear as a burning elite icon. This 'super elite' will receive one of the following buffs, and it will drop the Emerald Key when defeated.

- (Act number + 1) increase in Strength.
- +25% max HP.
- (Act number*2 + 2) Metallicize.

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Energy

Energy is the resource used to play cards. The energy cost of a card is at the top left and typically ranges from 0-3, though there are some exceptions. The Ironclad, the Silent, the Defect, and the Watcher all start the game with 3 base energy, which can be increased with relics. There are also cards that generate temporary energy.

Some cards can have X Energy cost. These cards consume all of your remaining Energy upon use, and their effect varies with how much Energy was consumed.

# Entrench

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Entrench

**Infobox:**
- Name: Entrench
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/a/a2/Entrench.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016205819
- Class: Ironclad
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Cost: 2
- Effect: Double your Block.
- [Entrench+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: Double your Block.

**Entrench** is a Skill card for the Ironclad. Using it gives you Block equal to your current Block, effectively doubling your Block value.

Upon upgrade, it costs 1 Energy to play.

You will still gain Block when using Entrench after playing Panic Button in the same turn.

## Interactions
 
- Because Entrench can generate a very large amount of Block, it is quite possible to end up with excess Block on any given turn. Thus, using Barricade to conserve your Block can let it grow exponentially.
- This exponential growth of Block can be put to use offensively by playing Body Slam.

# Envenom

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Envenom

**Infobox:**
- Name: Envenom
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/1/17/Envenom.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016211544
- Class: Silent
- Type: Power
- Rarity: Rare
- Cost: 2
- Effect: Whenever an Attack deals unblocked damage, apply 1 Poison.
- [Envenom+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: Whenever an Attack deals unblocked damage, apply 1 Poison.
- Name: Envenom
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/b/b4/Icon_Envenom.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202162044
- Description: Whenever you deal unblocked attack damage, apply X Poison
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: Intensity

**Envenom** is a Rare Power for the Silent. Any time an Attack deals unblocked damage to an enemy, the victim also immediately gets 1 Poison.

When Upgraded, Envenom costs 1 Energy instead of 2.

## Mechanics

- The Envenom buff can stack, so playing multiple copies of Envenom causes each unblocked Attack to inflict more Poison.
- When using a multi-hit Attack (e.g. Dagger Spray, Eviscerate), every individual hit that deals unblocked damage will inflict Poison.
- The Envenom effect applies directly after the damage effect of a card, occurring before the other effects of the Attack played. This can be useful for cards like Bane, as it activates its double-hit even without prior poison, or Neutralize, which it can allow to apply Weak after potentially removing an Artifact stack.

## Tips

- Sadistic Nature and Envenom are a ruthlessly effective combo, as any unblocked Attack will also inflict 1 Poison and an extra 5 damage. This is particularly devastating with Shiv decks, making each Shiv deal 9 damage and stack Poison.
- The Snecko Skull effectively doubles the Poison inflicted by this card, producing even more damage in the long run. 
- Envenom is extremely useful for quickly removing stacks of Artifact, as each unblocked Attack will remove 1 stack of Artifact immediately.

# Events

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Events

Events are special scenarios that will only occur after entering an unknown location. Events are not guaranteed to occur, but they are the most probable outcome of entering an unknown location. The event a player encounters is chosen by both random chance and the current Act they are on; some events are exclusive to certain Acts while other events can appear in all three Acts. 

Events do not occur in Act 4, as there are no unknown locations to travel to in Act 4. 

Ascension 15 makes unfavorable events more likely to occur, which boosts the probability or intensity of some unfavorable occurrences of certain events.

# Evolve

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Evolve

**Infobox:**
- Name: Evolve
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/5/5d/Evolve.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016205819
- Class: Ironclad
- Type: Power
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Cost: 1
- Effect: Whenever you draw a Status card, draw 1 card.
- [Evolve+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: Whenever you draw a Status card, draw 2 cards.
- Name: Evolve
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/b/bd/Icon_Evolve.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202162045
- Description: Whenever you draw a Status, draw X cards.
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: Intensity

**Evolve** is an Uncommon Power card for the Ironclad. After it's played, an additional card will be drawn whenever a Status card is drawn.

Upon upgrade, drawing a Status card results in **two** extra card draws instead of one.

## Interactions
 
- A player may use powerful cards such as Power Through, Wild Strike, Reckless Charge, and Immolate without their deck suffering nearly as much, so long as **Evolve** is played before the Status cards from those cards are drawn. An upgraded **Evolve** gives a draw advantage to any status drawn, actually increasing draw instead of being neutral. It also works very well with Fire Breathing as you can draw more status cards to deal damage with.
- '''Evolve's** extra card draws can greatly help against enemies who flood your deck with Statuses, such as Sentries, Slime Boss, and Taskmaster.
- **Evolve** effectively counters the negative effect imposed by Mark of Pain.
- **Evolve** synergizes well with Exhaust-themed decks, as drawn Status cards can be exhausted by Second Wind or Fiend Fire while still taking advantage of **Evolve's** extra draws.

 
- Power Through adds status cards directly to your hand. These status cards are created, not drawn, so **Evolve** will not activate initially.
- **Evolve''' cannot draw cards beyond the 10-card hand limit.
- Curses do not count as Status cards.

# Exhaust

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Exhaust

Exhausting a card puts it in your Exhaust pile. Cards in this pile are effectively removed from combat and cannot be used again. If you Exhaust a card that was in your deck, it will be returned to your deck at the end of combat.

There are three main ways a card can become Exhausted:

1. Some cards Exhaust themselves when used (like Impervious). These cards normally have a much more powerful effect than others at the same cost, but can only be used once. Some of these will no longer Exhaust on use once Upgraded (like Calculated Gamble).
1. Some cards Exhaust other cards as part of their effect (like Burning Pact). Although this may seem like a downside, being able to remove cards you don't need can be an upside, especially if you have received a Curse or are fighting an enemy that can create Status cards.
1. Some cards have a keyword called Ethereal (like Carnage). Cards with this keyword will exhaust if they are in your hand at the end of the turn. If you discard them or use them before the end of the turn, they will not exhaust.

The only way to put a card from the exhaust pile back to your hand during combat is through use of the card Exhume.

# Exhume

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Exhume

**Infobox:**
- Name: Exhume
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/1/1b/Exhume.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016205820
- Class: Ironclad
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Rare
- Cost: 1
- Effect: Put a card from your Exhaust pile into your hand.; Exhaust.
- [Exhume+]
- Cost+: 0
- Effect+: Put a card from your Exhaust pile into your hand.; Exhaust.

Exhume is a Rare Skill card for the Ironclad. It returns an Exhausted card to the hand to be played again or shuffled into the deck, but Exhausts itself in the process.

Upgrading Exhume reduces its cost from 1 to 0.

## Interactions
 
- Exhume can recycle strong self-Exhausting cards like Bandage Up, Feed, Offering, and Pummel, allowing them to be used multiple times in one combat — or even in one turn!
- Because Ethereal cards Exhaust themselves at the end of the turn, Exhume can recover Ethereal cards like Carnage and Ghostly Armor.

 
- Exhume cannot choose another Exhume as its target. This prevents the player from creating infinite combos with two upgraded copies of Exhume. (For example, by having a Letter Opener.)

# Face Trader (Event)

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Face_Trader_%28Event%29

**Face Trader** is an event that can appear in Act 1 and Act 2. You found a mysterious man, who is very interested in your face.

## Options

*Numbers in parentheses are for Ascension 15 or higher.*

- **[Touch]** Lose HP equal to 10% of Max HP. Gain 75 (50) Gold.
- **[Trade]** Receive one of the following event relics:
    - Cultist Headpiece: You feel more talkative (Neutral Face).
    - Face of Cleric: Raise your Max HP by 1 after each combat (Good Face).
    - Gremlin Visage: Start each combat with 1 Weak (Bad Face).
    - N'loth's Hungry Face: The next non-boss Chest you open is empty (Bad Face).
    - Ssserpent Head: Whenever you enter a ? room, gain 50 Gold (Good Face).
- **[Leave] **Nothing happens.

## Strategy
Both the positive masks—Face of Cleric and Ssserpent Head—are extremely powerful if acquired early on Act 1 and 2. On the negative side: N'loth's Hungry Face remains a fairly minor penalty throughout. But by Act 3, the threat of a Gremlin Visage and the small number of remaining rooms/combats makes a roll increasingly dangerous (especially for a deck avoiding most combats). Therefore, it may be wise to gain the gold (or simply leave) in late acts, especially if your deck is reliant on Attacks.

On higher ascensions, it is almost always a bad idea to trade faces, even when encountering the Trader extremely early. The Ascension 15 modifier makes ? rooms far less valuable, making Ssserpent Head a much more dangerous pick up. The first turn in combat is by far the most important one, so rolling Gremlin Visage can absolutely cripple your setup phase. It also disables relics such as Clockwork Souvenir. Finally, if you are going for Act 4, N'loth's Hungry Face can cause you to be unable to take the Sapphire Key, causing you to lose a big spike of power or even being unable to reach the final act entirely. The chance that you will get Face of Cleric is not worth the overall risk of the event.

It is possible to save scum, by choosing to swap faces and close the game and reopen it if you get a bad face, thus resetting the event. This allows you to see whether the face will be good or bad and avoid the bad face if it happens.

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| *You walk by an eerie statue holding several masks...* |
| *Something behind you softly whispers, "Stop."* |
| *You swerve around to face the statue which is now facing you!* |
| ''On closer inspection, it's not a statue but a statuesque, gaunt man. Is he even breathing?* |
| **Eerie Man:** *"Face. Let me touch? Maybe trade?"* |
| Touch |
| **Eerie Man:** *"Compensation. Compensation."* |
| *Mechanically, he cranes out a neat stack of gold and places it into your pouch.* |
| **Eerie Man:** *"What a nice face. Nice face."* |
| *While he touches your face, you begin to feel your life drain out of it!* |
| *During this, his mask falls off and shatters. Screaming, he quickly covers his face with all six arms dropping even more masks! Amidst all the screaming and shattering, you escape.* |
| *His face was completely blank.* |
| Trade |
| **Eerie Man:** *"For me?* FOR ME? *Oh yes.. Yes. Yes.. mmm..."* |
| *You see one of his arms flicker, and your face is in its hand! Your face has been swapped.* |
| **Eerie Man:** *"Nice face. Nice face."* |
| Leave |
| **Eerie Man:** *"Stop. Stop. Stop. Stop. Stop."* |
| *This was probably the right call.'' |

## Notes
- The flavor text for the **[Trade]** option states that the reward is "50% Good Face. 50% Bad Face". However, the actual odds are 40% good face (Face of Cleric and Ssserpent Head), 40% bad face (Gremlin Visage and N'loth's Hungry Face), and 20% neutral face (Cultist Headpiece).

# Falling

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Falling

**Falling** is an event found exclusively in Act 3. You fall, and must sacrifice a card in order to survive the fall.

## Options

- **[Land]** **Lose (Random Skill)**
    - Cannot be Bottled card.

- **[Channel]** **Lose (Random Power)**
    - Cannot be Bottled card.

- **[Strike]** **Lose (Random Attack)**
    - Cannot be Bottled card.

If you have only Bottled cards in your deck, the only option available is **[Land]**, but you do not actually lose any cards as Bottled cards cannot be removed.

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| *As you head upwards hopping from one floating shape to another, you slip.* |
| *You begin to fall.* |
| *While in free fall you consider your options:* |
| *Land safely with your greatest techniques.* |
| *Channel a Power to survive the fall.* |
| *Strike at the wall to hang on to it.* |
| Land |
| *You land with extreme grace before continuing on.* |
| Channel |
| *Harnessing and expending some of your raw power, you manage to land unhurt.* |
| Strike |
| *You are able to latch on to the wall, and manage to make a short hop onto another stable platform.* |
| Land (with no valid cards to remove) |
| *You seem to fall as slow as a feather, reaching the bottom without a scratch.* |

# Fatal

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Fatal

**Fatal** is a keyword signifying that a following effect occurs when this card kills a non-minion enemy. There are kills which do not qualify as **Fatal** kills, detailed below.

Note that cards like Sunder and Relics like Gremlin Horn don't use the keyword and can be triggered by the exceptions described below.

## Fatal Exceptions
The following kills are exceptions to the **Fatal** qualifier:
 
- Minions do not count as **Fatal** kills. These are recognized by the  icon. For a list of minion enemies, see the Minion page. 
- If fighting Darklings reducing the HP of one of them to 0 does not count as a **Fatal** kill unless it was the final enemy from the batch.
- Defeating the first phase of the Awakened One does not count as a **Fatal** kill.

## Cards with Fatal
- Feed
- Lesson Learned
- Hand of Greed
- Ritual Dagger
Category:Keyword

# Feed

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Feed

**Infobox:**
- Name: Feed
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/4/44/Feed.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20200121024417
- Class: Ironclad
- Type: Attack
- Rarity: Rare
- Cost: 1
- Effect: Deal 10 damage.; If Fatal, raise your Max HP by 3. Exhaust.
- [Feed+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: Deal 12 damage.; If Fatal, raise your Max HP by 4. Exhaust.

## Strategy
The earlier in the run you can acquire Feed, the better.  If you draft Feed, you want to maximize its use by gaining max health from it every combat, and upgrading Feed can allow for even more max health.  It may take a few extra turns to draw Feed when the enemy is close to dying but on almost all non-elite non-boss fights it will be worth it. Feed works well in decks with high Strength, as the increased damage makes it easier to get land a kill with Feed and trigger its unique effect. Dual Wield can be used in encounters with multiple enemies in order to gain even more max health.

## Interactions
If fighting Darklings, then reducing the HP of one of them to 0 does not count as a kill until you have killed the final enemy from the batch. Nor will it count if you defeat the first phase of the Awakened One.

If you have Magic Flower, the Max HP increase does get affected, to a total of 5(6) Max HP.

## Notes
There is an *achievement* ("Ooh Donut!") related to this card, which is gained if **Donu is** killed by this card.

# Feel No Pain

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Feel_No_Pain

**Infobox:**
- Name: Feel No Pain
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/4/41/FeelNoPain.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016205820
- Class: Ironclad
- Type: Power
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Cost: 1
- Effect: Whenever a card is Exhausted,; gain 3 Block.
- [Feel No Pain+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: Whenever a card is Exhausted,; gain 4 Block.
- Name: Feel No Pain
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/2/2e/Icon_FeelNoPain.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202162207
- Description: Whenever a card is exhausted, gain X Block
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: Intensity

**Feel No Pain** is a Power card for the Ironclad. For the rest of the combat, Exhausting a card immediately applies Block. As an Uncommon card, it appears as a card reward.

Upgrading **Feel No Pain** increases the Block gain from 3 to 4.

## Interactions
- Ethereal cards Exhaust themselves at the end of the turn, which triggers **Feel No Pain**. This makes the card a particularly effective counter to accumulated Dazed (Sentries, Chosen), adds flexibility to ethereal attack/skill cards (Carnage, Ghostly Armor), and grants free block from ethereal curses (Ascender's Bane, Clumsy).
- Combining **Feel No Pain** with True Grit generates high block for one Energy. This in turn can provide heavy damage for Body Slam.
- Corruption synergizes strongly with **Feel No Pain**, granting a bonus 3-4 block for every 0 Energy skill card played.
- Using Fiend Fire with **Feel No Pain** can eliminate the need to block for the current turn while allowing maximum damage for Fiend Fire.

- Multiple copies of **Feel No Pain** stack, granting the total Block whenever a card is Exhausted.

- **Feel No Pain** is not affected by Dexterity or Frail.

CardAutobox
**Fission** is a Rare Skill for The Defect.  It removes all Orbs, granting the player 1 Energy and drawing 1 card for each Orb removed this way.  When Upgraded, it Evokes the Orbs instead of simply removing them--the difference is that Evoking the Orbs triggers their effects.  **Fission** Exhausts on use.

## Strategy
This card is very powerful when Upgraded, especially in builds that use Capacitor or Runic Capacitor to add additional Orb Slots.  It draws a lot more cards to use and gives you the Energy you need to fuel them, which can be used to fill your Orb slots back up again.

When combined with Plasma Orbs, **Fission** can generate tons of energy.

# Flex

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Flex

**Infobox:**
- Name: Flex
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/5/5a/Flex.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016205957
- Class: Ironclad
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Common
- Cost: 0
- Effect: Gain 2 Strength.; At the end of this turn, lose 2 Strength.
- [Flex+]
- Cost+: 0
- Effect+: Gain 4 Strength.; At the end of this turn, lose 4 Strength.

**Flex** is a Skill card for the Ironclad. It grants the user 2 (4) Strength and applies 2 (4) **Strength Down**, which reduces the user's Strength by 2 (4) when their turn ends. Strength Down is considered a Debuff, and so can be negated by some effects (see Interactions).

Upon upgrade, Strength and Strength Down both increase from 2 to 4.

## Interactions
 
- Cards which hit multiple times benefit the most from strength buffs since each hit is given the damage boost, such as Sword Boomerang or Pummel. Heavy Blade also carries an innate boost from strength.
- The Strength Down effect only removes as much Strength as the card gives (2 base, 4 upgraded). This means if an upgraded **Flex** is played (+4 strength) followed by Limit Break (doubles strength to +8) , the player will still only lose -4 strength at the end of the round leaving a +4 overall strength boost for the rest of combat.
- Since Strength Down is a Debuff, using Orange Pellets or having an active Artifact before use will negate the Strength Down effect while keeping the Strength boost.

CardAutobox
**Foreign Influence** is an Uncommon Skill for the Watcher that presents you with 3 random Attack cards of any color (Including colorless) from which you may choose one to add to your hand (Adding one is not mandatory). Foreign Influence then Exhausts.

Upgrading Foreign Influence reduces the cost of the card it adds to your hand to 0 for that turn.

It can only generate a card that is available through shop and rewards with some exceptions: it cannot generate a healing card.

Foreign Influence **does not** grant an Orb slot, so attacks that generate orbs are less useful.

### Excluded Cards
- Feed *(Healing)*
- Reaper *(Healing)*
- Lesson Learned *(Potential for the player to exploit its permanent Upgrade)*
- Bite *(Healing and event-exclusive)*
- Ritual Dagger *(Event-exclusive)*
- Shiv *(Cards effect only)*
- Smite *(Cards effect only)*
- Through Violence *(Card effect only)*

- Description: At the start of your turn, Scry X.
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: Intensity

CardAutobox

Foresight is a simple, but very powerful card. By scrying 3 (or 4 when upgraded) before you draw for turn, you can get all of the cards you don't need out of the way. If you scry just one card into the discard pile that you were never going to use, you effectively drew an extra card that turn. Additionally, it can allow you to dig for a certain card. For example, if you want to draw an Eruption, and your deck has 8 cards in it, scrying 3 cards into the graveyard allows you to draw the Eruption 100% of the time. Given it's power, most Watcher decks should want exactly one copy of Foresight.

# Forgotten Altar

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Forgotten_Altar

**Forgotten Altar** is an event found exclusively in Act 2. You encounter a forgotten statue that requires an offering.

## Options

*Condition in parentheses are for Ascension 15 or higher.*

- **[Offer: Golden Idol]** Obtain a special Relic. Lose Golden Idol. 
    - This option is available only if you have a Golden Idol to be offered.
    - In Endless Mode, choosing this option while already having Bloody Idol does not remove Golden Idol, allowing you to finish the event with no effect.
- **[Sacrifice]** Gain 5 Max HP. Lose 25% (35%) HP.
- **[Desecrate]** Become Cursed - Decay.

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| *In front of you sits an altar to a forgotten god.* |
| *Atop the altar sits an ornate female statue with arms outstretched.* |
| *She calls out to you, demanding sacrifice.* |
| Offer: Golden Idol |
| *As you gently set the idol onto the altar a cold wind swirls throughout the room.* |
| *The arms of the statue begin to discolor and crumble.* |
| *Your golden idol begins to dull in color and begins bleeding from its eyes.* |
| *The bleeding never ceases.* |
| Sacrifice |
| *You stand on the altar and cut your wrists.* |
| *As the blood spills out in sacrifice, the arms of the statue reach out and close around your eyes.* |
| *Everything goes dark.* |
| *You wake up a short time later feeling a new potential surging through you.* |
| Desecrate |
| *You lash out and smash the statue in front of you, breaking the magical hold the room had placed upon you.* |
| *A dark wail echoes all around you, and you can feel the cursed magic seep into your bones.* |

## Related

- The Act 1 event Golden Idol (Event) gives you the Golden Idol if you survive the boulder trap guarding it.
- The Act 3 event The Moai Head will alternatively trade the Golden Idol for 333 gold.

# Fossilized Helix

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Fossilized_Helix

**Infobox:**
- Name: Fossilized Helix
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/2/25/FossilizedHelix.png/revision/latest?cb=20200203152023
- Description: Prevent the first time you would lose HP in combat.
- Flavor: Seemingly indestructible, you wonder what kind of creature this belonged to.
- Rarity: Rare
- Class: Any

The **Fossilized Helix** is a Rare Relic. At the start of each combat, it gives 1 stack of the Buffer buff, preventing the first time the player loses HP.

## Interactions
- Positive
    - Large single-hit enemies like Transient can be shut down entirely for one turn.
    - Negating the first instance of damage can buy time at the start of a fight to set up.
- Negative
    - Pain, Regret, Brutality, Combust, Hemokinesis, Bloodletting, J.A.X., Blue Candle, and Corrupt Heart's Beat of Death can waste the Fossilized Helix on 1-3 HP instead of a bigger attack.
    - Blood for Blood, Static Discharge, Rupture, Runic Cube, Centennial Puzzle, Self-Forming Clay, and Emotion Chip will not activate when HP loss is prevented.
    - Buffer takes priority over Tungsten Rod, so if you take 1 damage, you will still lose a stack of Buffer.

## Trivia
The appearance and name of this relic may reference the Helix Fossil from the *Pokémon* series.

# Frail

- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/4/48/Icon_Frail.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202162210
- Description: Block gained from cards is reduced by 25%.
- Type: Debuff
- Stacking; Behavior: Duration

Frail is a status condition that reduces the amount of block points gained by 25%. Like Dexterity, it only affects block gained directly from card effects; block from relics, Metallicize, Plated Armor or frost orbs is not reduced.

The amount of block gained after reduction is rounded down. For example, basic Defend blocks for 5. While frail, it blocks for 3 instead of 3.75.

## Sources
- Enemies
    - Spike Slime
    - Fat Gremlin (only on Ascension 17+)
    - Spheric Guardian
    - Snake Plant
    - Shelled Parasite
    - Mystic
    - The Collector
    - The Champ
    - The Maw
    - Time Eater (only on Ascension 19+)
    - Corrupt Heart
- Cards
    - Shame

## Interactions
- Positive
    - Turnip prevents gaining Frail entirely.

# Frozen Core

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Frozen_Core

**Infobox:**
- Name: Frozen Core
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/1/1d/FrozenCore.png/revision/latest?cb=20200203152950
- Description: Replaces Cracked Core. If you end your turn with empty Orb slots, channel 1 Frost.
- Flavor: The crack in your core has been filled with a pulsating cold energy.
- Rarity: Boss
- Class: Defect

**Frozen Core** is a Boss Relic which can only be obtained by the Defect. It replaces Cracked Core and channels 1 Frost if you end your turn with empty Orb slots instead of channeling 1 Lightning at the start of combat.

Frost Orbs are added at the end of your turn but *before* the orbs trigger, meaning the new orb will add to your defense on that same turn.

You must possess Cracked Core for it to appear.

## Interactions
 
- Capacitor, Runic Capacitor, and Inserter give more Orb slots for Frozen Core to utilize.
- Dualcast, Multi-Cast and Fission can Evoke Orbs, making room for new free Orbs.

 
- Fast channeling like Chill, Rainbow or Tempest can entirely invalidate Frozen Core, making it only give 1 or even 0 frost orbs.
- Consume reduces the number of orb slots, making it harder for Frozen Core to channel new orbs.

# Fusion

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Fusion

**Infobox:**
- Name: Fusion
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/2/2d/Fusion.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016203509
- Class: Defect
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Cost: 2
- Effect: Channel 1 Plasma.
- [Fusion+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: Channel 1 Plasma.

CardAutobox
## Strategy
Fusion, as one major source of Plasma Orbs, is a card requiring much strategy to utilize.

- Using this card is just like “storing” your Energy in a bank. You used 2 energy, and gain it back when evoked. As for the “interest”, you gain one extra energy at the start of every turn. Sounds great, but it's actually not that good.
    - The reason is that you can't do much in the turn you play Fusion because you have already consumed 2 energy. On the other hand, your energy will likely to be wasted on the turn you evoke the orb, because you can't use it all up. All in all, unless you can control you deck very well, don't use Fusion in most cases.
    - It's usually not worth it to put some of your energy to later use, especially when Fusion and one of your critical cards (Creative AI, Echo Form, etc.) are both on your hand.

- Instead, try upgrading it as soon as possible, because lowering one energy cost gives Fusion a completely different character. It becomes an agile card which allows spending your extra energy for later and brings almost immediate profit.

## Trivia
As seen in this picture art, Plasma Orbs seem to be made of a fusion of the three other Orbs, **Lightning**, **Frost** and **Dark**.
