# Gameplay

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Gameplay

*Slay the Spire* is both a Roguelike and a deckbuilding game.
Category:Game Mechanics
## Neow, the Whale

At the start of each playthrough of Slay the Spire players will always encounter Neow, a large, whale-like creature.

If the player has at least encountered the boss of the first Act in the previous run, Neow will offer a selection of 4 starting bonuses.
- The first 2 options are always beneficial, often offering a common relic, gold, cards, potions, or a card upgrade.
    - As the second option Neow may offer to make the first 3 combats of this run have 1 HP. This is given in the form of the special relic Neow's Lament. The effect works on Monsters Bosses and Elites, but only for 3 combats. Thorough examination of the map ahead of time is crucial when given this option.
- The 3rd option is always a trade-off, requiring the player to give all their gold or even sacrificing HP, but offering potent starting bonuses like rare relics or rare cards.
- The 4th option has the player give up their starting relic in exchange for a random boss relic.
On the other hand, if the player has NOT encountered the boss of the first Act on the previous run, Neow will offer only the following two starting bonuses. (As of Weekly Patch 46)
- The first option will be +10% max hp.
- The second option will always be Neow's Lament.

## Traversing the Map
After speaking to Neow, the player is brought to the Act 1 Map. The Map is where the player chooses their path, manipulating what kinds of rooms they will encounter. Each Act has a separate map, which is randomly generated to be different for each run (following some rules). For an explanation of the icons and options available, see Map locations.
## Building a Deck

In the game, the player will fight monsters, complete events and collect items. Players start out with a basic deck and acquire cards during gameplay. In this way they can improve the quality of the deck.

As the player progresses on their way upwards the Spire they will encounter a number of opportunities to add cards to their Deck. Certain cards have meaningful ways of interacting with specific relics, enemies or cards. To further refine the deck they will also be given options to remove cards from the deck, to improve the overall consistency, as well as the option to Upgrade cards to stronger versions.

## Cards on Offer
Each card is drawn individually, one after another, with the rules below apply to each.

### Rarity
Rare cards start at a listed percentage (seen in the table below) minus 5% and the chance increases by 1% added every time a common card is rolled. Whenever 1% is added to the chance for rare cards, it is subtracted from the chance for commons and then the uncommons if necessary. When a rare card is rolled, the chance for it is reset back to the initial percentage. Only cards from card rewards affect these chances.

The rarity chances are as follows:
|  | Non-shop | Shop |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rare | 3% | **9%** |
| Uncommon | 37% | 37% |
| Common | 60% | 54% |

### Upgrade
Independent of rarity. You do not get upgraded cards on Act 1. The chance that the card is upgrade is 25% (or 12.5% on ascension 12 and beyond) on Act 2, and 50% (or 25% on ascension 12 and beyond) on Act 3.

*Note: The above are general rules, but they can vary depending on the room you are in, what relics you have, etc.*

## Card Types
There are several types of cards in the game:

- **Attack** - Usually deal direct damage to one or more enemies, with some adding a secondary effect.

- **Skill** - All sorts of temporary and strategic effects are in this card type. Commonly grant Block or other temporary buffs to the player or debuffs to one or more enemies.

- **Power** - A permanent upgrade for the entire combat encounter. Some Powers give flat stats like Strength or Dexterity, others require certain conditions to be met or add beneficial effects whenever a certain event occurs in battle. Once played, the Power card is removed for that combat.

- **Status** - Cards added to the deck during combat encounters that are designed to bloat the deck and prevent the player from drawing beneficial cards, with some of them having additional negative effects. Unlike Curses, Status cards are removed from the deck at the end of combat.

- **Curse** - Unplayable cards added to the deck during in-game events. Similar to status cards they are designed to bloat the deck and prevent the player from drawing beneficial cards, with some of them having additional negative effects during combat. Unlike Statuses, Curse cards persist in the player's deck until removed by other means.

## Card effects
Certain Keywords affect how cards behave during combat encounters:

- **Unplayable** - Cards that cannot be played normally, unless otherwise altered, and hence have no Energy cost.
- **Exhaust** - When played, cards that are exhausted are removed from the player's deck until the end of the encounter.
    - Although Powers do not have the Exhaust keyword, and will not activate any "on-Exhaust" effects, they will be removed from your deck for the remainder of battle when played.
- **Ethereal** - Cards that exhaust themselves if left in the player's hand at end of turn.

- **Innate** - Cards that are innate are guaranteed to be in the first few hands.
- **Retain**- Cards that are kept after ending your turn.

## Combat

Combat is performed as a turn-based card game. Players use cards from their built deck to fight the opponents that inhabit the Spire. Players draw a default hand of 5 cards, and have 3 Energy to play each turn. Each card has an energy cost. At the end of each turn, the remaining cards in the player's hand are discarded. Then the enemies have their turn. When the player tries to draw from an empty deck, the discard pile is shuffled back into the deck.

After defeating all opponents the player is rewarded with a choice from 3 cards to add to their deck as well as some Gold and sometimes a random Potion.

Certain rare combat encounters pit the player against Elite monsters, superior enemies which are harder to overcome than regular opponents. In exchange, players are rewarded with an additional Relic at the end of battle.

## Shop

When players encounter a Shop, they have an opportunity to buy cards and supplies alike in exchange for Gold. A shop always offers:

- 5 random Class-specific cards, one of them "on sale" (-50% Price)
    - The first two cards from here are always attacks,then two skills,finally followed by one power.
- 2 random Colorless cards, one of which is always a rare card.
- 3 random Relics, with one always being an exclusive shop-relic.
- 3 random Potions.
- A card removal service, which is one-time-use per merchant. This service costs 75 Gold initially, and increases by 25 every time it is used. Can be permanently decreased to 50 this run with the Smiling Mask.

## Events

On their journey, players can encounter a number of Non-Combat Events of wildly varying nature. Some are strictly beneficial, offering free card Upgrades, Relics or Gold. Most have a trade-off, requiring the player to sacrifice certain amounts of gold, HP or other items or even Curse the player, but grant stronger bonuses in return. Others, however, are harmful to the player and hinder their journey by damaging them, applying Curses, removing cards involuntarily or lowering their maximum HP.

## Chests (non-Boss)
For detail information, go to Treasure Room.

Sometimes players can happen across Chests while ascending the Spire. These chests open for free and always contain one random Relic. Some Relics can change what a Chest will give.

## Rest Site
For more information, go to Rest Site.

Every once in a while players will encounter a Rest Site. At a Rest Site, they have the option to either rest and heal 30% of their maximum HP or to smith and Upgrade one card in their deck.

The last encounter before a Boss is always a Rest Site.

Certain Relics can add more options, while others interact with campsites themselves.

## Boss
At the end of every Act, a Boss awaits the player. Bosses are very strong opponents which the player has to overcome in order to progress. All Bosses have powerful attacks and often unique skills and effects which the player has to fight around strategically.

Defeating a Boss will heal the player to full HP for the following Act. Bosses are NOT meant to be challenged while retaining your HP for future encounters. Defeating a Boss with 1 HP remaining is a perfectly valid and safe strategy (until Ascension Mode, at least...)

Bosses offer vastly superior rewards for their difficulty. Upon defeat, Players receive an increased Gold reward (typically 90-110 gold), a guaranteed Potion, a choice from 3 Rare Cards for their class, and a choice from 3 exclusive Boss Relics.

# Giant Head

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Giant_Head

**Infobox:**
- Name: Giant Head
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/0/0c/Giant-head-pretty.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20180110054002
- HP: 500; 520 8+
- In Party With: None
- Debut Act: Act 3
- Powers: Slow

Giant Head is an Act 3 elite encounter. Its high amount of HP and steadily scaling attacks make it a formidable foe for many decks. However, because of the Slow debuff it begins combat with, high-damage decks with the ability to play a decent number of cards each turn will have no problem taking it down.

## Pattern
50% chance of using Count and 50% chance of using Glare on the first 4 turns. Cannot use Count or Glare three times in a row. From turn 5 onward, always uses It Is Time.

In Ascension 18+, always uses It Is Time from turn 4 onward.
| Name | Intent | Effect | Asc 3+ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Count |  | Deals 13 damage. | Deals 13 damage. |
| Glare |  | Applies 1 Weak. | Applies 1 Weak. |
| It Is Time |  | Deals 30 + T* damage. | Deals 40 + T* damage. |
*T starts at 0 and increases by 5 every time the attack is used, up to 30 additional damage.

Whenever the Giant Head uses one of its first two abilities, it will count down from 5 to 1, reducing the count by 1 each time. (Will say "5", then "4", then "3", then "2", and finally "1."). When the countdown is finished, the Head will start using It Is Time.
## Tips
- Play all of your non-attack cards first, if possible; the Slow debuff will cause attacks to do more damage if played after several other cards. Also, it is preferable to play attack cards in an increasing order of damage so harder hitting cards can gain higher percentage bonuses.

# Gold

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Gold

Gold is a major resource in Slay the Spire. It can be spent at the Merchant for various items and bonuses. 

Alternatively, some Events will let you spend certain amounts of Gold for specific rewards.

Gold cannot be gained if you have the Ectoplasm Boss Relic.
Category:Game Mechanics
## Sources of Gold

The player starts each run with Gold, and Gold drops as a reward from most fights in the game.

### Enemies
- Normal Encounter: 10-20 Gold
- Elite Encounter: 25-35 Gold
- Boss Encounter: 95-105 Gold

### Events
- Face Trader
- Golden Shrine
- Wheel of Change
- Dead Adventurer
- The Ssssserpent
- World of Goop
- Wing Statue
- Knowing Skull
- The Joust
- The Nest
- Mind Bloom
- The Moai Head
- Tomb of Lord Red Mask

### Chests

- Small Chest: 23-27 Gold
- Medium Chest: 45-55 Gold
- Large Chest: 68-82 Gold

### Relics
- Golden Idol
- Maw Bank
- Tiny Chest
- Old Coin
- Tiny House
- Ssserpent Head
- Ceramic Fish

### Cards
- Hand of Greed
- Wish

## Interactions

### Positive
- Golden Idol makes gold gain from combat greater.
- Bloody Idol heals the player every time gold is gained.
- Smiling Mask, The Courier, and Membership Card make shop prices lower.

### Negative
- Ectoplasm makes obtaining further gold impossible.

# Golden Idol (Event)

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Golden_Idol_%28Event%29

**Golden Idol** is an event found exclusively in Act 1. The player can claim the powerful Golden Idol for a price, or safely walk by.

## Options

*Numbers in parentheses are for Ascension 15 or higher.*

- **[Take]** Obtain Golden Idol. Trigger a trap, sending a huge boulder rolling towards the player.
    - The player must choose how to defend themselves.
      - **[Outrun]** Become Cursed - Injury
      - **[Smash]** Take damage equal to 25% (35%) of Max HP
      - **[Hide]** Lose 8% (10%) Max HP

- **[Leave]** Nothing happens

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| *You come across an inconspicuous pedestal with a shining gold idol sitting peacefully atop. It looks incredibly valuable. * |
| ''You sure don't see any traps nearby.* |
| Take |
| *As you grab the Idol and stow it away, a giant boulder smashes through the ceiling into the ground next to you.* |
| * You realize that the floor is slanted downwards as the boulder starts to roll towards you.* |
| Outrun |
| RUUUUUUUUUUN! |
| *You barely leap into a side passageway as the boulder rushes by. Unfortunately it feels like you sprained something however.* |
| Smash |
| *You throw yourself at the boulder with everything you have. When the dust clears, you can make a safe way out.* |
| Hide |
| SQUISH! |
| *The boulder flattens you a little as it passes by, but otherwise you can get out of here.* |
| Leave |
| *If there was ever an obvious trap, this would be it.* |
| *You decide not to interfere with objects placed upon pedestals.'' |

## Strategy
The Golden Idol is used for Events in future Acts. It's also a strong Relic in its own right, granting 25% more Gold from battles. It's generally a good idea to **[Take]** it.

**[Outrun]** is mostly a poor choice. Curses (even ones that do nothing besides be a curse like Injury) make your deck quite a bit worse, especially in act 1 where your deck does not have many cards.  The extra gold can make it easier to afford a remove at a shop, but then you effectively have one less remove throughout the run as well as the money spent.

**[Smash]** option is also often a bad choice. The damage hit often means either avoiding an Elite or taking an extra rest at a Rest Site instead of an upgrade, reducing the total strength your deck leaves act 1 with by quite a lot.

Sacrificing max HP via **[Hide]** is often the safest option. The max health penalty often does nothing immediately, and only starts to harm you later on in the run, by which point the extra gold from the Golden Idol has helped you become stronger.

## Related
- Not to be confused with the event Golden Shrine.
- The Act 2 event Forgotten Altar will trade the Golden Idol for a Bloody Idol and avoid negative options.
- The Act 3 event The Moai Head will trade the Golden Idol for 333 gold.

## Trivia
- The grinning golden statue protected by a rolling boulder trap is a reference to the opening scene of the first Indiana Jones movie, *Raiders of the Lost Ark*.

# Golden Shrine

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Golden_Shrine

**Golden Shrine** is an event that can appear in Act 1, Act 2, and Act 3. You encounter a shrine of gold and riches.

## Options

*Numbers in parentheses are for Ascension 15 or higher.*

- **[Pray]** Gain 100 (50) Gold.

- **[Desecrate]** Gain 275 Gold. Become Cursed - Regret.

- **[Leave]** Nothing happens.

## Strategy
Picking the [Pray] option is generally the safer option as it grants gold with no consequence, while picking [Desecrate] will require planning and consideration.

Gaining 275 gold itself outweighs the cost rise of card removal: 75 for removing the Regret (if it is the first removed card) and 25 more for each removed card (In typical runs, it's highly unlikely to encouter 8 shops to remove cards). However, obtaining a Curse can effect deck builds and card draws, and Regret causes damage that bypasses block. If a shop is still far ahead or is not in the optimal route (perhaps with inadequate rest sites or elites), the downside of Regret is hard to neglect. Consider carefully if you don't have ways to deal with Curses.

However, if you have the ability to deal with the negative side, such as Omamori which completely negates the Curse, or Blue Candle that enables you to exhaulst the Curse with 1 HP, taking the 275 gold is a good option as it may well be the difference between getting great shop relics and getting nothing.  Relics that have synergy with Curses such as Du-Vu Doll or high gold gain such as Membership Card may also make you consider taking the Curse and the gold. 

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| *Before you lies an elaborate shrine to an ancient spirit.* |
| Pray |
| *As your hand touches the shrine, gold rains from the ceiling showering you in riches.* |
| Desecrate |
| *Each time you strike the shrine, gold pours forth again and again!* |
| *As you pocket the riches, something weighs heavily on you.* |
| Leave |
| *You ignore the shrine.* |

## Related
- Not to be confused with the Golden Idol event.

# Grand Finale

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Grand_Finale

**Infobox:**
- Name: Grand Finale
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/9/94/GrandFinale.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181019121104
- Class: Silent
- Type: Attack
- Rarity: Rare
- Cost: 0
- Effect: Can only be played if there are no cards in your draw pile.; Deal 50 damage to ALL enemies.
- [Grand Finale+]
- Cost+: 0
- Effect+: Can only be played if there are no cards in your draw pile.; Deal 60 damage to ALL enemies.

**Grand Finale** is a card for the Silent. It deals an impressive 50 damage to all enemies, and costs no Energy, but it can only be played if your Draw Pile is empty. This makes it very difficult to use effectively, or at all.

Upon upgrade it deals an additional 10 damage to every enemy.

## Strategy

You should never take Grand Finale unless you have a way to keep cards between turns, either from Well-Laid Plans or Runic Pyramid. This lets you keep Grand Finale in your hand until you reach the bottom of your draw pile. However, you will still need to carefully manage the number of cards in your draw pile using cards with extra draw, to ensure that you have exactly 0 cards at some point during your turn.

Alternatively, if your deck is small enough that you can reliably draw the entire deck every turn, you can play this card every turn (possibly more than once per turn).

Assuming you have a deck which can reliably play Grand Finale, it will be more effective the smaller your deck. In a deck which shuffles every 2-3 turns it could easily serve as your primary offense. 

Act 3 onward has enemies which need 2 or more uses of Grand Finale at times to kill them, especially more with bosses. Nightmare can allow for much quicker damage in longer fights if used correctly.

# Gremlin Leader

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Gremlin_Leader

**Infobox:**
- Name: Gremlin Leader
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/d/d9/Gremlin_Leader.png/revision/latest?cb=20180912002705
- HP: 140-148; 145-155 (Ascension 8+)
- In Party With: 2 random Gremlins
- Debut Act: 2
- Powers: None

Gremlin Leader is an Elite encounter found only in Act 2.

Gremlin Leader can only have a maximum of 3 Gremlin minions at a time.

## Pattern
When there are 0 other enemies, will have a 75% chance of using Rally! and a 25% chance of using Stab.

When there is 1 other enemy:

If the last move was Encourage, will have a 50% chance of using Rally! and 50% chance of using Stab.

If the last move was Stab, will have a 62.5% chance of using Rally! and a 37.5% chance of using Encourage.

The last move could not have been Rally!, since Rally! results in at least 2 other enemies.

When there's 2 or 3 other enemies, will have 66% chance of using Encourage and a 34% chance of using Stab.

Cannot use the same move twice in a row.
| Name | Intent | Effect | Asc 3+ | Asc 18+ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Encourage |  | All enemies gain 3 Strength. All minions gain 6 Block. | All enemies gain 4 Strength. All minions gain 6 Block. | All enemies gain 5 Strength. All minions gain 10 Block. |
| Rally! |  | Summons up to 2 random Gremlins. | Summons up to 2 random Gremlins. | Summons up to 2 random Gremlins. |
| Stab |  | Deals 6 x 3 damage. | Deals 6 x 3 damage. | Deals 6 x 3 damage. |
## Tips
- If you lack considerable damage to burst down the Gremlin Leader, killing the gremlins spawned will increase the likelyhood of her not attacking (Rallying and Encouraging instead), hence giving you turns to continue chipping her health, as well as removing their abilities (such as the Fat Gremlin's Weak). This also means that the new gremlins spawned do not carry the old gremlins' Strength buffs.
- Any minion from this fight (i.e. spawned gremlins or gremlins that come in the fight) will retreat and be defeated if the Gremlin Leader is defeated.
- While Gremlin Leader may summon minions continually, it is important to kill Gremlin Wizards; their attacks are very strong. Killing a Fat Gremlin may also help kill the Leader faster due to its Weak debuff no longer being applied.
- Gremlin Leader continually buffs her allies' Strength, so killing her quickly is important to avoid her attacks from becoming too deadly.

## Trivia
- Gremlin Leader is confirmed to be female by one of the developers.

## Notes

# Gremlin Nob

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Gremlin_Nob

**Infobox:**
- Name: Gremlin Nob
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/3/3b/Gremlin-nob-pretty.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20180110071016
- HP: 82-86; 85-90 8+
- In Party With: Act 1; Solo; Act 2; 1 Taskmaster The Colosseum
- Debut Act: Act 1
- Powers: None
- Name: Enrage
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/d/d0/Icon_Rage.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202163651
- Description: Whenever you play a Skill, gains X Strength.
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: Intensity

The **Gremlin Nob** is an Elite enemy found primarily in Act 1. However, one also appears in Act 2's  Colosseum Event alongside a Taskmaster, provided the player opts to fight. The enemy may seem to have low damage values for an elite, but the Enrage buff it grants itself combined with the Skull Bash's applied Vulnerable make for a tough fight for most decks.
### Move
| Name | Intent | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bellow |  | Gains 2 Enrage. |
| Gains 3 Enrage. |  |  |
| Rush |  | Deal 14 damage. |
| Deal 16 damage. |  |  |
| Skull Bash |  | Deal 6 damage and apply 2 Vulnerable. |
| Deal 8 damage and apply 2 Vulnerable. |  |  |
### Pattern
Always starts with Bellow. Afterwards, has a 33% chance of using Skull Bash and a 67% chance of using Rush. Cannot use Rush 3 times in a row.

At 18+, uses Skull Bash on the 2nd turn and uses Rush twice afterwards. Repeats this pattern for the entire fight.

## Tips
- With the exception of the first turn, where it has yet to apply Enrage, playing Skills will make the Gremlin Nob much more threatening. Since most Block-granting cards are also Skills, it can be worth more to **not** play them and take the damage instead. Before using a Skill to mitigate damage, consider how much longer the fight might take.
    - With the Ironclad's Basic deck, the fight is about being as aggressive as possible until the very end. Use Bash to apply Vulnerable as much as possible, and play every Strike attack you're dealt. When you feel the Nob will only have one turn left to live, it can be beneficial to play a Defend versus a Skull Bash. Burning Blood will absorb some of the impact of the fight at the end.
    - With the Silent's Basic deck, the fight becomes more painful. The objective, however, does not change. Neutralize helps to mitigate some of the damage. Taking 4 or 10 damage should be much more manageable. Otherwise, lay in with Strikes whenever possible.
    - With the Defect's Basic deck the fight plays out similar to the Silent. Despite the strength gain it may be worth it to cast Zap early in the fight (especially if you traded away your starting relic) and Dualcast late in the fight. Dualcast often lets you finish him off a whole turn earlier, making the strength gain irrelevant.
    - With the Watcher's Basic deck, focus on maintaining aggression and play strong offensive cards. It is usually worth to take damage as the Watcher's style of gameplay can deal excessive amounts of damage in a single turn. Playing cards which enable Wrath or Divinity such as Eruption or Blasphemy to deal a large amount of burst damage can easily finish off the Gremlin Nob. 
    - Powers and Potions can both be effective at mitigating damage in place of Skills.
- If the player is fighting the Gremlin Nob in the  Colosseum event, it is probably better to kill the Gremlin Nob before the Taskmaster; the Gremlin Nob will continue to gain Strength when you play Skills.

## Trivia
- The Gremlin Nob is a reference to the Ork Nob from Warhammer 40k.
- According to the flavor text of the Gremlin Horn relic, Gremlin Nobs maintain consistent growth from birth to death.
- The second fight of the Colosseum event used to contain two Gremlin Nobs. On 17 January 2019 this was changed to one Gremlin Nob and a Taskmaster instead.
- The Gremlin Nob wields a skeleton of a creature which is extremely similar to the rat-like rodent infested by the Fungi Beast. However, there are no rodent monsters in the game.

- HP: 23-25; 22-26 7+
- In Party With: Act 1; 3 other Gremlins; Act 2; Gremlin Leader; With 1 other Gremlin initially; With up to 2 other summoned Gremlins
- Debut Act: Act 1
- Powers: None

*This article is about the 5 small gremlin enemies that appear in groups.*

*For the Act 1 Elite, see Gremlin Nob.*

* For the Act 2 Elite, see Gremlin Leader.*

*For gremlin-related relics, see Gremlin Horn and Gremlin Visage.*

*Gremlins are also mentioned in the Wheel of Change and Match and Keep Events.*

## Fat Gremlin

### Move
| Name | Intent | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Smash |  | Deal 4 damage, apply 1 Weak. |
| Deal 5 damage, apply 1 Weak. |  |  |
| Deal 5 damage, apply 1 Weak and Frail. |  |  |

## Mad Gremlin

### Move
| Name | Intent | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Scratch |  | Deal 4 damage. |
| Deal 5 damage. |  |  |

## Shield Gremlin

### Move
| Name | Intent | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Protect |  | Target gains 7 Block. |
| Target gains 8 Block. |  |  |
| Target gains 11 Block. |  |  |
| Shield Bash |  | Deals 6 damage. |
| Deals 8 damage. |  |  |

### Pattern
If there are other enemies, always uses Protect on one of them and will never target itself.
If there are no other enemies to protect, it will always use Shield Bash unless it intends to Protect that turn, in which case it will Protect itself.

## Sneaky Gremlin

### Move
| Name | Intent | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Puncture |  | Deals 9 damage. |
| Deals 10 damage. |  |  |

## Gremlin Wizard

### Move
| Name | Intent | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Charging |  | - |
| Ultimate Blast |  | Deal 25 damage. |
| Deal 30 damage. |  |  |
### Pattern
Spends 2 turns Charging, then uses Ultimate Blast on the 3rd. From there onward, will Charge for 3 turns and then use Ultimate Blast.

On 17+, the Gremlin Wizard will continue to use Ultimate Blast after the 3rd turn without Charging.

## Tips

- In general, it is best to focus on killing any Sneaky Gremlins first, followed by Fat Gremlins, then Shield Gremlins, and finally Mad Gremlins. If a Gremlin Wizard is present, start focusing on him as soon as is necessary to kill him before he uses Ultimate Blast.
    - Sneaky Gremlins deal the most direct damage, and should be dealt with on the first turn if possible, before they can be protected by a Shield Gremlin and before a Fat Gremlin can weaken you.
    - Fat Gremlins apply Weak, which can make killing the other gremlins more difficult, so they should often be dealt with next.
    - Shield Gremlins will only deal damage to you if they have no allies left to protect. Thus, it is good to kill them after the high priority targets have been dealt with, but before every other gremlin has been killed. You may need to adjust your priorities based on which gremlins the Shield Gremlin chooses to protect. It may be good to attack the Shield Gremlin first if a Gremlin Wizard is present, as the Shield Gremlin may interfere with killing the Gremlin Wizard quickly.
    - Angry Gremlins do the least damage initially, but their damage will increase as you attack them. Thus, it is best to Block their attacks for the first few rounds until you can afford to focus on them and kill them quickly.
    - Gremlin Wizards are a bit trickier to deal with. While they only attack once every three turns, their damage can be difficult to Block in Act 1. Ideally, you should kill them before they get a chance to use Ultimate Blast, which may require focusing on them before other lower priority gremlins.

## Trivia
- A Gremlin Visage can be acquired in the Face Trader event. It however does not look like any existing Gremlin in the game.
- They are summoned as minions by the Gremlin Leader.
- The Shield Gremlin is named "GremlinTsundere" in the source code.

# Hand of Greed

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Hand_of_Greed

**Infobox:**
- Name: Hand of Greed
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/0/0c/HandOfGreed.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20200121203550
- Class: Neutral
- Type: Attack
- Rarity: Rare
- Cost: 2
- Effect: Deal 20 damage.; If Fatal, gain 20 Gold.
- [Hand of Greed+]
- Cost+: 2
- Effect+: Deal 25 damage.; If Fatal, gain 25 Gold.

CardAutobox
**Hand of Greed** is a rare colorless card which provides 20(25) gold when used to kill an enemy.

While expensive at shops, it does not exhaust and can be used to kill multiple enemies per battle, eventually paying for itself with the right usage. If acquired from a Neow Blessing at the beginning of the run it can provide considerable reward.

The kills must be considered Fatal to provide the gold reward. Not all enemies count as fatal kills (exceptions detailed below).

## Interactions
 
- Bloody Idol will heal 5HP for each Fatal kill by **Hand of Greed** which generates gold.
- The smaller slimes which split off from the Large Acid Slimes and Large Spike Slimes can each count as Fatal kills.

 
- Minions do not count as Fatal kills. These are recognized by the  icon. For a list of minion enemies, see the Minion page. 
- If fighting Darklings reducing the HP of one of them to 0 does not count as a Fatal kill unless it was the final enemy from the batch.
- Defeating the first phase of the Awakened One does not count as a Fatal kill.

**Havoc** is a Skill card for the Ironclad. It plays the card which would have been drawn next, then Exhausts it. As a Common card, it can be found as a reward after combats.

**Havoc** can exhaust unplayable status cards and Power cards won't be exhausted. Upon upgrade, **Havoc** costs 0 energy.

**Headbutt** is an Attack card for the Ironclad. It deals 9 damage, then prompts the player to select a card from their discard pile, which will then be the next card drawn. As a Common card, it can be found as a reward after combats.

## Interactions
 
- Combined with any ability to draw more cards, it's possible to play a desired card twice in one turn: just play it once, use **Headbutt** to retrieve it, then play it again.
    - If for some reason you wanted to, you could also use **Headbutt** to retrieve **Headbutt**, then use it again to retrieve another **Headbutt**, and so on.
- Pairs well with Havoc to place a high-cost card on top of the draw pile and play it for less total energy.

 
- Doesn't pair well with Mayhem, as the card retrieved is drawn before Mayhem's effect happens.

# Health

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Health

**Health** or **HP** is a vitality resource. Should the player run out of HP, they will be defeated and the run will end. There are various ways that HP can be permanently increased or decreased by it total amount, or has its portion restored.

## Altering Max HP

The player can increase or decrease their maximum health, or max HP, using various methods. The changes in max HP persists throughout the run.

### Increasing Max HP

Increasing max HP raises the max HP by a set amount and also heal the player for the same amount. For example: 
- The player has 45/60 HP
- The player increases their max HP by 5.
- Their max HP is raised by 5, to 65.
- Their current HP is also healed by 5, to 50.
- Their overall HP is now 50/65. 

#### Card
*Numbers in parentheses are for upgraded card.*

- Feed - Increases max HP by 3 (4) if Fatal.

#### Relics
- Strawberry - Increases max HP by 7.
- Darkstone Periapt - Increases max HP by 6 whenever you obtain a Curse. 
    - Unlike Du-Vu Doll, it does not require you to keep a Curse in your deck. You still retain the increased max HP even if you remove a Curse from your deck.
- Pear - Increases max HP by 10. 
- Singing Bowl - Gives an option to increases max HP by 2 instead of adding a card to your deck.
- Mango - Increases max HP by 14. 
- Tiny House - Increases max HP by 5.
- Face of Cleric - Increases max HP by 1 after each combat.
- Lee's Waffle - Increases max HP by 7 and heal all of your HP.
Max HP increased by these relics are not tied to the relics themselves. You may lose one of these relics to N'loth and still retain max HP gained.

#### Potion
*Numbers in parentheses are enhanced amount through possessing Sacred Bark.*

- Fruit Juice - Increases max HP by 5 (10).

#### Events
*Numbers in parentheses are for Ascension 15 or higher.*

- Neow - Could offer an option or two to increase your max HP. The amount varies, based on your current character.
- Bonfire Spirits - Offering a rare card also increases max HP by 10 in addition of fully heals you.
- Big Fish - Choosing **[Donut]** increases max HP by 5.
- Forgotten Altar - Choosing **[Sacrifice]** increases max HP by 5 at the cost of taking damage equal to 25% (35%) of your max HP.

### Decreasing Max HP

Decreasing max HP lowers it by a set amount, but the player still retains their current HP. For example: 
- The player has 45/60 HP
- The player decreases their max HP by 5.
- Their max HP is lowered by 5, to 55.
- Their current HP stays the same, at 45.
- Their overall HP is now 45/55. 

The player cannot lower their max HP below 1.

#### Card
- Parasite - Decreases max HP by 3 if it is transformed or removed from your deck.

#### Events
*Numbers in parentheses are for Ascension 15 or higher.*

- Neow - Could offer an option to decrease your max HP in an exchange for a reward. The amount varies, based on your current character.
- Golden Idol - Choosing **[Hide]** decreases your max HP by 8% (10%). 
- Council of Ghosts - Choosing **[Accept]** decreases your max HP by 50%. 
- Vampires(?) - Choosing **[Accept]** decreases your max HP by 30%. 
- The Moai Head - Choosing **[Jump Inside]** decreases your max HP by 12.5% (18%), but fully heals you.

#### Blights

- Muzzle - You can no longer increase your Max HP. All healing is halved.
- Durian - Lose 50% of your Max HP.

## Healing

Though scarce, the player does have many options offered to restore their HP and avoid defeat. As stated above, the player may indirectly heal their HP by increasing their max HP. However, there are also many other ways that simply restore a lost portion of your HP.

### Direct Healing

The following methods simply restore a portion of the player HP.

#### Rest Site
By default, the main method to restore your HP is to  **Rest** at Rest Sites.  **Resting** heals you for 30% of your max HP. A number of relics affects  **Rest**.
- Regal Pillow - Increases the heal from  **Rest** by the flat amount of 15.
- Coffee Dripper - Disables  **Rest** option, prohibiting you from healing via this method.

#### Entering New Act
By default, the player is healed by 100% of their *missing HP* once they enter a new Act. The amount is lowered to 75% of their *missing HP* on Ascension 5 and higher.

#### Cards
*Numbers in parentheses are for upgraded card.*

- Reaper - Heals up to 4 (5) HP per enemy, assuming they take full damage from this card and the player has no Strength.
    - The healing is increased by 1 HP per Strength per enemy, assuming they take full damage from this card.
- Self Repair - Heals 7 (10) HP at the end of combat.
- Bandage Up - Heals 4 (6) HP.
- Bite - Heals 2 (3) HP.

#### Relics
- Burning Blood - Heals 6 HP at the end of each combat.
- Blood Vial - Heals 2 HP at the start of each combat.
- Toy Ornithopter - Heals 5 HP whenever the player uses a potion.
- Meat on the Bone - Heals 12 HP at the end of combat if the player's HP is at or below 50%.
- Pantograph - Heals 25 HP at the start of boss combats.
- Bird-Faced Urn - Heals 2 HP whenever the player plays a Power card.
- Black Blood - Heals 12 at the end of each combat.
- Bloody Idol - Heals 5 HP whenever the player gain Gold.
- Meal Ticket - Heals 15 HP whenever you enter a shop room.
- Eternal Feather - Heals 3 HP for every 5 cards in your deck when you enter a Rest Site.

#### Potions
*Numbers in parentheses are enhanced amount through possessing Sacred Bark.*
- Blood Potion - Heals 20% (40%) of max HP.
- Regen Potion - Grants 5 (10) Regeneration, healing up to 15 (55) HP over 5 (10) turns.

#### Events
*Numbers in parentheses are for Ascension 15 or higher.*

- Bonfire Spirits
    - Offering a common or special card heals 5 HP.
    - Offering an uncommon or rare card heals you to full.
- Wheel of Change - Should you land on  **the heart**, you will be healed to full.
- Big Fish - Choosing **[Banana]** heals 33% of max HP.
- Hypnotizing Colored Mushrooms - Choosing **[Eat]** heals 25% of max HP, at the cost of being Cursed: Parasite.
- The Cleric - Choosing **[Heal]** heals 25% of max HP, costing 35 Gold.
- The Library - Choosing **[Sleep]** heals 33% (20%) of your max HP.
- Mind Bloom - Choosing **[I am Healthy]** heals you to full, at the cost of being Cursed: Doubt.
    - The option is only available on floor 41 and above, replacing **[I am Rich]**.
- The Moai Head - Choosing **[Jump Inside]** heals you to full, at the cost of decreasing your max HP by 12.5% (18%).
- Winding Halls - Choosing **[Press On]** heals 25% (20%) of your max HP, at the cost of being Cursed: Writhe.

### Reviving

It is possible that, should the player die by an attack, they restores their HP instead. This is technically another method of healing, and are affected by modifiers.

Currently, there is only 2 ways to revive.

#### Relic
- Lizard Tail - If the player would die, heals 50% of max HP. Works only once per run.

#### Potion
*Numbers in parentheses are enhanced amount through possessing Sacred Bark.*
- Fairy in a Bottle - If the player would die, heals 30% (60%) of max HP and discard the potion.

### Healing Modification

Through the following 2 relics and 1 blight, the player can have their healing altered:
- Magic Flower - Healing is 50% more effective during combat, including reviving and indirect healing from increasing max HP should they occur during combat.
- Mark of the Bloom - You can no longer heal by any method, includes:
    - Direct healing via cards, relics, potions, events.
    - Reviving.
      - This effectively means the player cannot prevent their death, as the heal from reviving is negated and their HP stays 0.
    - Indirect healing from increasing max HP via cards, relics, potions, events.
      - Max HP is still increased, for the purpose of calculating score.
    - Rest.
    - Entering new Act.
- Muzzle - You can no longer increase your Max HP. All healing is halved.

Category:Game Mechanics

## Interactions
 
- This card, especially after being upgraded, scales with Strength well enough to take gigantic chunks out of boss HP. It synergizes incredibly well with Limit Break.

# Heel Hook

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Heel_Hook

**Infobox:**
- Name: Heel Hook
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/7/75/HeelHook.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016211834
- Class: Silent
- Type: Attack
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Cost: 1
- Effect: Deal 5 damage. ; If the enemy has Weak, gain and draw 1 card.
- [Heel Hook+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: Deal 8 damage. ; If the enemy has Weak, gain and draw 1 card.

**Heel Hook** is an Uncommon Attack for The Silent that effectively deals "free" damage if an enemy is Weak. Upgrading Heel Hook increases the damage from 5 to 8. It's Silent's version of Dropkick.

## Strategy
Heel Hook is generally a poor choice. Without a Weak enemy, it's an even less effective Strike. In the best case, it's a slightly stronger Flash of Steel.

To make the most of Heel Hook, ensure that at least one enemy can remain consistently Weak, and use a small deck to increase the chances of chaining one Heel Hook into another.

Generally, you should look for more powerful and consistent Attacks instead of picking Heel Hook.

Heel Hook can be built around to make an infinite deck.

## Synergies
Heel Hook obviously needs many cards that inflict Weak.

The card becomes stronger with A Thousand Cuts, Envenom, and other cards that encourage playing many cards each turn.

Reducing Heel Hook's cost to 0 using Madness, Mummified Hand, or similar effect will gain you one Energy, increasing the odds of your being able to play the card you just drew.

# Hexaghost

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Hexaghost

**Infobox:**
- Name: Hexaghost
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/0/03/Hexaghust.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20180905114311
- HP: 250; 264 9+
- Debut Act: Act 1
- In Party With: None
- Powers: None

-**Hexaghost** is one of the three bosses encountered at the end of Act 1.

## Pattern

Starts with Activate, followed by Divider. After this, each of its attacks lights one green flame. Once there are six flames, it will use Inferno, and then snuff out all flames. The attack pattern, and the number of flames on that move, are as follows:

- 0. Sear
- 1. Tackle
- 2. Sear
- 3. Inflame
- 4. Tackle
- 5. Sear
- 6. Inferno

After it has used its first Inferno attack, Sear will give the player Burn+ card instead of the regular Burn. This deals 4 damage instead of 2.
| Name | Intent | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Activate |  | Nothing. |
| Divider |  | Deals (H+1) x 6 damage. H = (Current Player HP divided by 12), rounded down. |
| Inferno |  | Deals 2 x 6 damage, shuffles 3 Burn into the discard pile. Upgrades all Burn. |
| Deals 3 x 6 damage, shuffles 3 Burn into the discard pile. Upgrades all Burn. |  |  |
| Sear |  | Deals 6 damage, shuffles a Burn into the discard pile. |
| Deals 6 damage, shuffles 2 Burns into the discard pile. |  |  |
| Tackle |  | Deals 5 x 2 damage. |
| Deals 6 x 2 damage. |  |  |
| Inflame |  | Gains 2 Strength and 12 Block. |
| Gains 3 Strength and 12 Block. |  |  |

## Tips

1. With most decks the Hexaghost is a battle against time. The damage after the initial Divider is minor, but over time the combination of Inflame with accumulating burn cards will overwhelm you. Surviving the Hexaghost is often a matter of killing it before Inferno hits or as quickly as possible after.
1. Cards and relics which exhaust, transform, or otherwise utilize status cards can significantly reduce the challenge of this battle. Examples: Storm of Steel, Evolve, Fiend Fire, Medical Kit.
1. It is actually practical to enter this fight with low health, as Divider attack scales with your current health. The lower your health is, the easier to block damage from Divider attack. Consider foregoing resting at a Rest Site prior to this boss.
1. With it utilizing barrages of low-damage attack and slow scaling, Weak, Thorns, and strength reduction (such as Disarm, Dark Shackles, or Malaise) are invaluable.

## Trivia

- Similar to the Guardian's "DESTROY DESTROY DESTROY," and Slime Boss's "Slime... CRUSH!!!," in a pre-release version from even before Early Access, Hexaghost used to say "DIVIDER!!" when using that attack on turn two.

# Hyperbeam

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Hyperbeam

**Infobox:**
- Name: Hyperbeam
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/f/f3/Hyperbeam.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016203511
- Class: Defect
- Type: Attack
- Rarity: Rare
- Cost: 2
- Effect: Deal 26 damage to ALL enemies.; Lose 3 Focus.
- [Hyperbeam+]
- Cost+: 2
- Effect+: Deal 34 damage to ALL enemies.; Lose 3 Focus.

CardAutobox

## Strategy
Hyperbeam functions best as a theme. Zero orb reliance makes the downside moot, trading consistent damage/block for massive upfront burst. In which case as many copies should be taken as possible. Plasma orbs are unaffected by Focus loss.

Alternatively the card *can* still be useful in an orb-based deck if used with discretion, as Hyperbeam is powerful enough to handle certain room encounters on its own. It can also be used to excellent effect as a 'finisher', played on the last turn to carve off the last of an enemy's HP. 

Although rare, if Hyperbeam is obtained on other characters (e.g. via Prismatic Shard) the downside is also moot (as other characters don't have orbs in the first place) making it a very strong pick. 

## Interactions
 
Having an Artifact will prevent the Focus lost for the next use of Hyperbeam.

# Hypnotizing Colored Mushrooms

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Hypnotizing_Colored_Mushrooms

**Hypnotizing Colored Mushrooms** is an event found exclusively in Act 1. The player encounters a field of dangerous fungi.

This event only appears on floor 7 and above.

## Options

- **[Stomp]** Anger the Mushrooms.
    - The player has to fight 3 Fungi Beasts.
      - The fight always rewards the player with Odd Mushroom, a Relic exclusive to this event.

- **[Eat]** Heal 25% HP. Become Cursed: Parasite.

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| *You enter a corridor full of hypnotizing colored mushrooms.* |
| *Due to your lack of specialization in mycology you are unable to identify the specimens.* |
| *You want to escape, but feel oddly compelled to eat a mushroom.* |
| Stomp |
| Ambushed!! |
| *Rodents infested by the mushrooms appear out of nowhere!* |
| Eat |
| *You give in to the unnatural desire to eat. As you consume mushroom after mushroom, you feel yourself entering into a daze and pass out. As you awake, you feel very odd.* |
| *You Heal 25% of your HP, but you also get infected.* |

## Strategy
Both options are painful - Fungi Beasts can deal some serious damage, and Parasite will inevitably lose you some HP. The choice is mainly determined by how much HP the player has, and whether they can survive the battle and clear the Act.

The combination of Fungi Beast boosting their Strength and applying Vulnerable on death make it very likely that the player will have to deal with very high incoming damage numbers when taking them out one by one. A safer approach can be to equally lower the HP of each Fungi Beast and then finish them all at once with cards like Cleave, Dagger Spray or Doom and Gloom once they are low enough.

Like all battles, the Fungi Beasts award Gold, card selection, and points in addition to the Odd Mushroom, a very useful relic against enemies that utilize Vulnerable.

If your HP is low, eating the mushrooms both prevents the Fungi Beasts battle and restores some HP. Parasite will need to be removed later, but it's preferable to death by mouse-mushroom ambush. You may also consider this option if you haveOmamori, Du-Vu Doll, or Darkstone Periapt.

- Flavor: The smoke imbues its owner with the spirit of the burned.
- Rarity: Rare
- Class: Any

The **Incense Burner** is a Rare Relic that grants 1 Intangible every 6 turns. 
## Tips
The counter for the Incense Burner is maintained between combats. As such, it is worthwhile to plan out the last combat before a boss fight and end that combat on a turn such that you become Intangible on a turn that the boss will surely attack. For example, ending the last combat in Act 1 when the Incense Burner reads 3 ensures that you will become Intangible on the turn that Slime Boss uses Slam.

Here are the numbers to block a boss' big attack by ending your previous fight when the counter reads a specific number:

Slime Boss: 3

The Guardian: 4

Hexaghost: For the Divider attack: 4, for Inferno attack: 3

Bronze Automaton: 0 for HYPER BEAM

Corrupt Heart: 0,1,3,4

If you use Infernal Blade as other character that is not the Ironclad, it will grant a random Attack card of the respective color of that character. # Infinite Combo

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Infinite_Combo

An **infinite combo** is a setup that allows you to keep playing the same cards forever in a single turn, either spending no Energy or continually regaining the energy used. Infinite combos are powerful as they allow you to keep attacking until you win the battle, keep gaining Block until nothing can harm you, or keep gaining energy to spend it all at once on a cost X card.

As most infinite combos work by continually drawing the same cards, the setup requires you to have very few cards in your draw and discard piles. This is helped by avoiding adding cards to your deck other than core cards in the combo and removing them whenever possible. Cards that Exhaust and Power cards may still be used.

Some infinite combos rely on the Sundial combined with a card that allows you to draw two or more cards. Such cards are listed below. This works by playing a multi-draw card with an empty draw pile and fewer than that many cards in the discard pile, which adds two counts to the Sundial. The discard pile must contain a card, usually an Attack, that allows you to draw the multi-draw card again. If the multi-draw card can draw more than two cards, you can include some additional extra cards in the combo.

Necronomicurse can be used in a different kind of infinite combo. Whenever it is exhausted, another copy of it is added to your hand. Blue Candle can be used to play and exhaust these indefinitely with no energy cost, and Tungsten Rod negates the HP loss.

The following achievements can be easily completed if you can set up an infinite combo; however, there are other ways to complete them:
- Infinity: play 25 cards in a single turn.
- Neon: Channel 9 Plasma in a single turn.
- Perfect: defeat a boss without taking any damage.
- The Transient: Defeat the Transient before it fades away.
- You Are Nothing: defeat a boss on turn 1.
## Counters
The Time Eater counters infinite combos with its Time Warp power, which ends your turn and causes it to gain Strength for every 12 cards you play. The Corrupt Heart counters Blockless infinite combos with its Beat of Death power, dealing damage to you each time you play a card, and its Invincible power, which requires the combo to be performed over several turns. Beware also of Thorns and Sharp Hide.

Pain, Normality, Velvet Choker or Time Maze will block infinite combos in most cases. The Tungsten Rod negates Pain, and the Blue Candle or any other means of exhausting the curses can provide an escape.
## Cores
The following combinations of cards and relics may be used in an infinite combo.
### Colorless
- Flash of Steel and either another Flash of Steel or Finesse
- Impatience, any 0-cost card (up to two with Impatience+) and either Flash of Steel, Finesse or another copy of Impatience
- Unceasing Top and any 0-cost card; requires your hand to be otherwise empty
- Sundial combo: Impatience (and an Attack costing up to 2 that lets you draw it again)
- Necronomicurse, Blue Candle, Tungsten Rod and Panache
### Red
- Any two or more of Flash of Steel, Finesse or Dropkick (Dual Wield can be used to duplicate one)
- Sundial combos: Pommel Strike+, Burning Pact with Necronomicurse and 0(1) extra card
- Necronomicurse, Blue Candle, Tungsten Rod and any of the following:
    - Dark Embrace and any number of 0-cost cards
    - Feel No Pain
    - Charon's Ashes
### Green
- Any two or more of Flash of Steel, Finesse or Heel Hook
- 2 × Acrobatics, Tactician and any 0-cost card (or 1-cost card if Tactician is upgraded)
- Sundial combos: Acrobatics with 0(1) extra card (more when combined with Reflex), Backflip, Expertise
- 2x Nightmare, Adrenaline, and a means to generate Intangible and damage. This combo can pulled off without shuffling your discard pile, but might require a Well-Laid Plans to set up reliably.
- Necronomicurse, Blue Candle, Tungsten Rod and any of the following:
    - A Thousand Cuts
    - After Image
### Blue
Claw is especially effective when played in an infinite combo. Zap+ may be used to cycle Lightning orbs and combine with Thunder Strike as a finisher.
- 2 × Skim, Fusion+ and any 0-cost card
- 2 × Coolheaded+, Fusion+, using Blizzard as a finisher
- Meteor Strike and either 2 × Skim and up to one 0-cost card or Unceasing Top
- All for One and Hologram+ both with cost reduced to 0, and any number of other 0-cost cards; this combo does not depend on shuffling your discard pile.
- Sundial combos: Coolheaded+, Skim with 1(2) extra cards
### Purple
Most infinite combos for the Watcher requires changing stances that would harness the extra energy generated by either Calm or Divinity. Mental Fortress can provide infinite block (against Thorns, Beat of Death, etc.) while Talk to the Hand offers the same by attacking. Flurry of Blows can offer damage for non-energy generating combos and Brilliance can destroy with mantra generating combos. These combos can be categorized by the two main stances involved.

#### Neutral

- Sundial combos: Cut Through Fate with 0(1) extra cards, Empty Mind with 1(2) extra cards.

#### Calm & Neutral
- 1-cost Calm card (e.g. Inner Peace, Fear No Evil), 2 × Empty Mind, N × Flurry of Blows. May require an enemy that intends to attack to reach Calm. Allows any many Flurry of Blows as can fit in hand. Variations include:
    - 2 × Empty Mind+ allows adding any 0-cost card to the loop (e.g. Consecrate, Halt). And if the 0-cost card is Just Lucky, N × Weave can also be added to the combo.

#### Calm & Wrath

- Rushdown, 1-cost Calm card, 1-cost Wrath card (e.g. Eruption+, Indignation). May require an enemy that intends to attack to reach Calm. Variations include:
    - Violet Lotus and/or Sundial allows the usage of 2-cost Calm card such as Vigilance or generate extra energy.

#### Divinity & Neutral

- Pray+, Prostrate, Empty Mind => Requires an extra Insight to initiate the combo. This is energy neutral. A variation is to use 2 × Prostrate+ and 1 Empty Mind+ to generate 1 energy per divinity cycle.

#### Divinity & Calm

- Pray+, Master Reality, 1-cost Calm card => Requires an extra Insight+ to initiate the combo. A complete 20 Mantra cycle would generate 3 energy.
- Pray+, 1-cost Calm card, 1-cost Draw 2+ card (e.g. Inner Peace/Empty Mind/Sanctity) => Requires an extra Insight to initiate the combo. A complete cycle uses 20 Mantra to enter and exit *both* Divinity and Calm *twice* and would generate 1 energy. The extra energy can be used to play an extra card but would require a Draw 3+ card to be card neutral. Variations include:
    - Vigilance and Inner Peace allows for a energy neutral blocking combo.
    - Inner Peace and Wheel Kick allows for a energy neutral attacking combo.

#### Divinity & Wrath

- Pray+, Prostrate, Rushdown, 1-cost Wrath card => Requires an extra Insight to initiate the combo. This is energy neutral.

## Interactions
- Panache, A Thousand Cuts, After Image, Kunai, Letter Opener, Shuriken will keep triggering as you play more cards.
- Tingsha and Tough Bandages activate every time Tactician is discarded.
- Runic Pyramid and Equilibrium allow you to keep more cards in your hand, making it easier to set up an infinite combo.
- Purity, Burning Pact, True Grit+ and Recycle allow you to exhaust unnecessary cards. Corruption can sometimes also be used this way.
- Sundial or The Abacus allow you to steadily gain energy or Block respectively while playing an infinite combo.
- Madness can allow infinite combos with more cards, such as Pommel Strike.

# Innate

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Innate

Innate is a keyword which causes the card to always start in your opening hand. Technically, it works as if cards with Innate are on the top of your draw pile before your first draw, thus meaning it does take a draw space from your starting hand. Despite this, if you have more Innate cards than your starting hand could draw, you will draw all of them, exceeding your starting hand size up to the maximum hand size limit of 10. If you have more than 10 Innate cards, the remainder will be randomly placed on top of your draw pile. Additonally, having 6 or more Innate cards will still allow Ring of the Snake, Ring of the Serpent and Bag of Preparation to activate and draw 1 or 2 more cards on top of those Innate cards.

Although working similarly, Innate is a separate mechanic from the Bottled Relics, which add a specified card to your starting hand each combat. Cards with the "Innate" keyword will keep that effect if duplicated by an event. The Bottled Relics, however, will not affect any duplicates of the chosen card.

A discarded Innate card will be reshuffled into your draw pile like any other cards.

## Innate Cards

### Ironclad Cards
- Upgraded Brutality

### Silent Cards
- Backstab
- Upgraded After Image
- Upgraded Infinite Blades

### Defect Cards
- Boot Sequence
- Upgraded Chill
- Upgraded Storm
- Upgraded Hello World
- Upgraded Machine Learning

### Watcher Cards
- Upgraded Alpha
- Upgraded Battle Hymn
- Upgraded Establishment

### Colorless Cards
- Dramatic Entrance
- Mind Blast

### Curses
- Pride
- Writhe

# Inserter

**Infobox:**
- Name: Inserter
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/f/fd/Inserter.png/revision/latest?cb=20200203153052
- Description: Every 2 turns, gain 1 Orb slot.
- Flavor: Push. Pull. Stack. Repeat.
- Rarity: Boss
- Class: Defect

## Interactions
Like many other Relics with turn timers, this can be intentionally set up so that it triggers at the start of combat, allowing the player to play their first turn with 1 extra orb slot.

The Inserter encourages a very slow, orb-focussed strategy, where the inserter can provide long-term value. In any combat shorter than 6 turns, this is often worse than Runic Capacitor, which provides its orb slots immediately, and is a Shop Relic, costing only ~150 gold.

## Synergy
This relic has strong synergy with Consume, which looks to sacrifice the player's orb slots for Focus - one of the most powerful buffs on the Defect.

## Trivia
This relic is a reference to the Inserter device from Factorio.

# Intangible

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Intangible

**Infobox:**
- Name: Intangible
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/2/2f/Icon_Intangible.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202163112
- Description: Reduce ALL damage and HP loss you take to 1. (Lasts X turns)
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: Duration

**Intangible** is a decaying Buff that reduces all damage and HP loss you take to 1. It lasts 1 round for each stack of Intangible you have.

Intangible applies to ***all ***damage and HP loss. Damage from Exploders, Thorns, Poison, powers like Combust, cards such as Offering, damage multipliers like Vulnerable and Slow, etc. will all come out to 1 damage per hit. The only exception is if the player has The Boot and attacks while Nemesis has Intangible active, in which case The Boot will increase the damage to 5 instead of 1.

## Sources of Intangible
- Wraith Form
- Apparition
- Ghost in a Jar
- Incense Burner
- Hauntings

## Enemies with Intangible
- Nemesis

# Intent

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Intent

PAGENAMEs are symbols floating over the heads of enemies that indicate what that enemy will do on their turn.

If the enemy is attacking, the attack damage and number of attacks will be provided. In most cases this is exactly reliable, and is adjusted by debuffs such as Vulnerable on the player and Weak on the enemy.

The relic Runic Dome renders the player unable to see the intent, although cards like Spot Weakness and Go for the Eyes still glow yellow if an enemy's intent would trigger their effect.

| Intent | Name | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | Aggressive | This enemy intends to Attack for a total of 0-4 damage. |
|  | This enemy intends to Attack for a total of 5-9 damage. |  |
|  | This enemy intends to Attack for a total of 10-14 damage. |  |
|  | This enemy intends to Attack for a total of 15-19 damage. |  |
|  | This enemy intends to Attack for a total of 20-24 damage. |  |
|  | This enemy intends to Attack for a total of 25-29 damage. |  |
|  | This enemy intends to Attack for a total of 30+ damage. |  |
|  | Defensive | This enemy intends to Block. |
|  | Strategic (Debuff) | This enemy intends to inflict a Negative Effect on you. |
|  | This enemy intends to inflict a powerful Negative Effect on you. |  |
|  | Strategic (Buff) | This enemy intends to use a Buff. |
|  | Aggressive (Debuff) | This enemy intends to attack and inflict a Negative Effect on you. The weapon changes based on the damage that will be dealt. |
|  |  |  |
|  |  |  |
|  |  |  |
|  |  |  |
|  | Aggressive (Defense) | This enemy intends to attack and Block. The weapon changes based on the damage that will be dealt. |
|  |  |  |
|  |  |  |
|  |  |  |
|  | Aggressive (Buff) | This enemy intends to attack and use a Buff. The weapon changes based on the damage that will be dealt. |
|  | Defensive (Buff) | This enemy intends to Block and use a Buff. |
|  | Defensive (Debuff) | This enemy intends to Block and inflict a Negative Effect on you. |
|  | Cowardly | This enemy intends to escape. |
|  | Sleeping | This enemy is asleep. It will do nothing on its turn. |
|  | Stunned | This enemy is stunned. It will do nothing on its turn. |
|  | Unknown | This enemy intends to do an action that is not any of the above, which can be one of the following: - Splitting. - Exploding. - Summoning Minions. - Changing form. - Reviving itself. - Doing nothing. |

## Trivia

- Defensive (Debuff) is only used by one enemy in the entire game, being Time Eater.

**Iron Wave** is an Attack for the Ironclad. It grants 5 Block, then deals 5 damage (7 Block and 7 damage when Upgraded).

## Tips
- Iron Wave is a very efficient card, effectively a Strike_R and Defend_R rolled into one. While it may not be the best pick when nearing the end of a run, it shines early on and can still carry itself decently once Upgraded.
- Since Iron Wave is an Attack that grants Block, it can be effective against the Gremlin Nob and the Chosen, who punish the player for using Skills.
