# Ironclad

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Ironclad

*"The remaining soldier of the Ironclads. Sold his soul to harness demonic energies."*

The **Ironclad** is one of four playable characters in Slay the Spire. He wields an arsenal of powerful strikes, boasts formidable defensive options, and draws fiendish strength from his demonic benefactors to empower himself in various ways. He starts off with 80 HP, highest of the playable characters, and can manipulate Exhaust.

The Ironclad's starting Relic is Burning Blood, which heals 6 HP after combat.

## Cards
### Starting Deck
- 5 Strike
- 4 Defend
- 1 Bash
Ironclad Card Navbox

## Relics
Starting Relic: Burning Blood

Common Relic: Red Skull

Uncommon Relics: Paper Phrog, Self-Forming Clay

Rare Relics: Champion Belt, Charon's Ashes, Magic Flower

Boss Relics: Black Blood (replaces Burning Blood), Mark of Pain, Runic Cube

Shop Relic: Brimstone

### General Build Archetypes
These are the standard types of decks that may give you an idea of direction for your deck, or what you want to go for. Keep in mind that none of these builds are mutually exclusive. Many of them are more of a general strategy, which can be adapted or combined into multiple builds in a single deck.

| High Defense Deck |
| --- |
| - This strategy focuses on building up Block over multiple turns, potentially eliminating incoming damage. Plated Armor is an excellent fit in this build. - Essential cards include Body Slam, Entrench, and Barricade. - Barricade may be substituted by Calipers, provided that you have a consistent Block per turn. - Keep in mind that Barricade+ costs 2 energy and won't instantly boost your damage/block, so playing it may weaken you on the turn played. - Body Slam and Juggernaut are excellent sources of damage, which is still important to win. - Though not an intuitive choice, Second Wind can be used to thin out extraneous Block cards once enough Block is built up, letting the player more reliably draw attacks and rely on Entrench to maintain their Block and be sure to prioritize upgrading it because 2 energy cost is more reasonable for this type of build. - Although, this can be mitigated with Feel No Pain because it effectively synergies with offering a passive defense build. More importantly many of Ironclad's card exhaust by themselves if not used, so it helps with deck management. - Strength reduction from Disarm and Weak from Intimidate, Clothesline, and Uppercut can help reduce enemies' attack damage, allowing you to maintain your Block. - Furthermore Shockwave affecting all enemies is a must especially if one gets the Champion Belt - Flame Barrier is a must as it is the Ironclad's best defense as it is also a passive offense. - Any source of Dexterity is necessary to maintain any shields especially with the Ironclad having higher defenses then the other characters. - Having additional sources of energy such as Lantern, Seeing Red, Bloodletting, and Offering especially when both are upgraded. This is especially true for the later as it also let's you draw more cards to move through your deck faster. - Self-Forming Clay would be essential for this build if one has Bloodletting or Offering, allowing for passive block at the start of the next turn. - Sentinel is excellent for this type of strategy as having a way to exhaust such as True Grit provides both energy and exhausting Sentinel will refresh 2 energy if done last. It can also help with status cards if you have Feel No Pain. - Thorns such as Bronze Scales work perfectly as this is the Ironclad's most steam gathering deck build to go for. - While Reaper isn't much healing, it could be pivotal for surviving until the next encounter. - Having an Artifact can help prevent getting Frail or having the Turnip or Orange Pellets will essentially provide a much more worry free game. |

| High Strength Deck |
| --- |
| - This build focuses on increasing Strength and multiplying its power through the choice of attacks. Attacks that hit multiple creatures, or hit multiple times scale more effectively with Strength. - Spot Weakness, Flex, Limit Break, Demon Form, and Inflame are cards that offer Strength. - A helpful tip with Flex, in particular, is that if you have an Artifact before you use Flex, or trigger the effect of Orange Pellets after using Flex, you won't lose the Strength gained from it on the next turn. This gives Flex good synergy with sources of Artifacts, such as Clockwork Souvenir or Panacea. - Limit Break also allows you to benefit permanently from temporary strength effects such as Flex. - Whirlwind/Heavy Blade, Sword Boomerang, Twin Strike, etc. are all cards that synergize well with Strength. - Reaper becomes a very powerful healing tool with high Strength, especially when paired with a Magic Flower. - Vulnerability cards such as Bash, Trip, and Thunderclap work very well with the high damaging attacks offered to you with high Strength. - If Limit Break is upgraded, you can cast it multiple times for exponential strength gain. Headbutt and a small deck size help you cast it more often. Relics and potions that grant some initial strength are very helpful in case you draw Limit Break within the first few turns. - Additional sources of energy are very useful such as Lantern, Seeing Red, Bloodletting, and Offering. - Rupture is a must if you go for Seeing Red or Offering allowing you take full advantage of the strength, especially if upgraded. |

| Searing Blow Deck |
| --- |
| - Upgrade Searing Blow every opportunity you can. Its damage increases more with each upgrade, reaching 100+ damage after ten upgrades. - Vulnerable is extremely good in a Searing Blow deck, as when upgraded a lot the extra damage can easily reach 40-50+ - The deck should be kept small to cycle back to Searing Blow as often as possible. - If you decide to go for a Searing Blow deck, you should always take the path that gives you the most campfires - Most must-upgrade cards become less valuable, as their upgrade is taking away from Searing Blow's power. - You generally only want to aim for a Searing Blow deck if you meet the following criteria: - You get it early in Act I (preferably before your first campfire) - You have a path that can take you through at least 3+ campfires in Act I - Card synergies: - Headbutt let you play it an extra time each deck cycle - Dual Wield gives you additional copies if you manage to get it in the same hand as Searing Blow. - If you get Dual Wield in a Searing Blow deck, you should prioritize cards that help you find the combo: - Secret Weapon+ is probably the best one in bringing Searing Blow to your hand. - Violence is also good if your deck is small and you don't have many Attacks remaining. - Runic Pyramid will ensure that you get the combo at some point. - All exhaust cards can be very good at thinning your deck during combat. - Double Tap let your Searing Blow deal double damage - Armaments- can continually ramp up your Searing Blow damage during combat - Relic synergies: - Warped Tongs will continually upgrade your Searing Blow over time during combat. - Wing Boots allows you to take additional campfires that you normally won't be able to get to. - Necronomicon doubles the damage of Searing Blow every time you play it. - Pen Nib - double damage of Searing Blow but requires some planning to execute. - Paper Phrog has a minor synergy but at higher Searing Blow levels the increase of damage from this relic is significant. - Dolly's Mirror - if you get this after you have upgraded your Searing Blow a few times, it will effectively double the strength of the deck. |

| Corruption + Dead Branch Deck |
| --- |
| - While the focus is corruption, Feel No Pain and Juggernaut will essentially carry the entire deck ensuring passive block and damage for extreme survival. - Corruption makes all Skills cost 0 in exchange for exhausting them upon use, but Dead Branch would generate a replacement for used skill. If Dead Branch generates another Skill, then you can use another Skill again for free. - Most of Ironclad Skills grant high Block, allow you to easily tank damage once you use multiple of them. If possible, use Barricade beforehand to allow Block you've gained not to be wasted between turns. - Some of Ironclad Skills grant Energy. Special notes goes to Seeing Red which normally cost 1 un-upgraded. With Corruption, it becomes a free 2 Energy generation. Spend Energy gained on other crucial cards on your hand, such as Power card or Attacks. - Fiend Fire can generate a lot of random cards with Dead Branch, which gives more chance to generate random 0-cost Skills cards |

| Corruption + Dark Embrace Deck |
| --- |
| - Unlike the normal exhaustion and defense strategies above (which focus on building up power over time), your goal here is to try and make your deck almost entirely out of skills, get out Corruption and Dark Embrace together, then burn through your entire deck in one turn to raise your defense, with doubling effects from Entrench played last, finally followed by one or more Body Slams to kill the enemy in one hit. - The essential cards are Corruption, Dark Embrace, Entrench, and Body Slam, plus cards like Impervious,Shrug It Off, and Sentinel to build defense before you double it with Entrench. Provided you keep your deck overwhelmingly tilted towards skills and fill it with lots of card draw, you should only need to draw Corruption and Dark Embrace before you start comboing off; the rest of the combo will be found as you draw your deck. Multiple copies of Entrench or Body Slam (or things that duplicate them) are still extremely valuable; you also want to upgrade Corruption, Dark Embrace, and Body Slam to reduce the cost of the combo so you can deploy it faster. - It's also important to have cards that let you dig for your combo, such as Shrug It Off, Burning Pact, and Offering. Beyond just letting you dig for your combo, these let you draw past attack cards when comboing off. - Hitting your hand maximum is a serious problem, especially if you obtain multiple copies of Dark Embrace or large numbers of card-drawing skill cards.Bloodletting can help you play other cards to get them out of your hand and can provide the energy you need to play Corruption and Dark Embrace as soon as possible. Burning Pact allows you to get unwanted cards out of your hands while drawing a large amount. Once the combo is deployed, Sentinel will both provide additional Block and a large amount of free energy to play out the rest of your hand. True Grit can be used to avoid cards getting clogged in your hand, but it's extremely important to upgrade it to avoid the risk of having it hit your combo pieces. Offering both draws you cards and gives you energy to play your non-skills. - Double Tap and Dual Wield can amplify the final blow by doubling your Body Slam, while Secret Weapon can dig for your Body Slam. Do not upgrade your Secret Weapon, since you want it to be exhausted so Dark Embrace will let you draw a card off it. - Powers that provide persistent benefits to your defense or exhaustion intended to help you over multiple turns or which give you minor benefits for exhausts and blocks are somewhat less useful to you, since your goal is to combo off in a single turn for overwhelming damage rather than slowly accumulating benefits; but they're still worth collecting, since they give you a backup strategy in case you can't get all your combo pieces or something else goes wrong.Barricade is particularly useful because it allows you to, if necessary, split your combo over multiple turns, or to accumulate Block slowly before you finally get everything you need to go off. - An alternative but similar strategy is to use Juggernaut, Corruption, and Feel No Pain. Each defensive skill played is worth an additional 10-14 damage.Iron Waves are good fallbacks. - Removals should focus on getting rid of your Strikes rather than your Defends; while your Defends aren't as good as your other Block cards, they can still be cycled through for free once you have Corruption and Dark Embrace out. |

| Perfected Strike Deck |
| --- |
| - Perfected Strike+ strike cards (Strike_R, Pommel Strike, Twin Strike, Wild Strike, Swift Strike). - Strike Dummy will add to the overall damage making it a must have. - Your deck will become very heavy, lots of draw like Battle Trance, Shrug It Off, Warcry, and especially Offering will be important, as will in-battle upgrade effects like Apotheosis, Armaments+, and Warped Tongs. - Having at least two copies of Fire Breathing especially when upgraded will take advantage of the wounds from wild strike. - You will also need to be on the lookout for strong defensive Relics, such as: Self-Forming Clay, Orichalcum, Anchor, Horn Cleat, or Captain's Wheel. - Necronomicon synergizes very well with Perfected Strike+. - Prayer Wheel works very well with this deck as it gives you twice as many occasions to add Strike cards. - Dual Wield increases the power of the deck a lot more than usual, increasing the damage of each Perfected Strike by up to 6, and increasing the amount to be drawn. - An extra energy such as Seeing Red or Lantern is particularly important to be able to play multiple copies if desired. - Only take Mark of Pain if you have a Fire Breathing beforehand. - A few exhaust cards such as True Grit+ and Second Wind will help mitigate wounds and provide defense. |

| Status + Evolve Deck |
| --- |
| - Uses powerful cards with drawbacks that inflict Status cards, such as Wild Strike, Power Through, Reckless Charge and Immolate, with Evolve to negate the loss of draws. - Exhaust cards like True Grit, Sever Soul, Second Wind, and Fiend Fire can keep you from becoming overwhelmed in long term fights. Shrug It Off can give Block even with Dazed from Reckless Charge. Feel No Pain also pairs well with cards that create Dazed, effectively granting you 3-4 block per Dazed card in hand at the end of your turn. - True Grit and Evolve are your high-priority targets for upgrades, as True Grit+ lets you decide which card to Exhaust, and Evolve+ increases your draws instead of replacing them, greatly speeding up your deck. - Mark of Pain effectively loses its downside. - With an upgraded Evolve, a 9 card Fiend Fire happens easily. - Top it off with Fire Breathing for a nice passive AoE damage. A normal draw full of Status can easily turns into 30-50 damage to ALL enemies. With multiple copies this can easily be your main source of damage. - Only run multiple copies of Fire Breathing if you're quickly and consistently getting out Evolve, or you'll only slow your deck down. - This build mitigates the power of most Status inflicting enemies, and synergizes well with many other deck types. - Medical Kit greatly improves your ability to manage your Status cards, improving your performance in long-term fights. It also negates the self-damage from Immolate. - Card draw like Battle Trance and Pommel Strike+ is important for digging through your deck and getting Evolve set up as soon as possible. |

| Masochist Deck |
| --- |
| - Utilizes Rupture and cards that deal damage to you, aiming to finish fights quickly. - Each use of Rupture increases Strength gained per trigger. You may stack it 2 or 3 times to quicken your Strength growth. - After applying Rupture, use Brutality or Combust. Their health cost per turn means you would gain 1 Strength every turn. - Unless you want additional card draw or AoE damage, you would not need more than 1 copy of these two, as stacking them increases health loss but not Rupture's Strength gain. - Strength gain from Rupture is consistent if built for, but it can be slow. Limit Break+ can help multiplying your Strength to finish fights before you lose too much health. - Hemokinesis, Offering, and Bloodletting are the other cards that self harm. - TheBlue Candle allows you to hurt yourself by exhausting curse cards. - Reaper benefits from the Strength gain and provides some much needed healing. - Necronomicon can double the healing provided. - J.A.X. is a chance encounter, but grants you both health loss to trigger Rupture while also grants you Strength on its own. - Any cards that benefit from Strength gain are good here. - Self-Forming Clay and Magic Flower are essentials if found as both can prevent too much damage from occurring. - Draw to get your combo together is very helpful. Make sure to get some defense to keep outside damage taken low. - Blood for Blood does significant damage and will quickly become cheap or free with Brutality or Combust. Having a solid 0-cost attack lets you take advantage of the extra cards drawn from Brutality, and can tide you over if you don't find Rupture early on (or draw it early in the fight). - The Pain Curse card can enable easy Rupture scaling. If you obtain a Pain in the early game, perhaps even as part of Neow's blessing, it may be worth building towards a Masochist deck. This can be further empowered with Runic Cube, allowing you to cycle through more cards than usual whenever Pain is in your hand. |
|  |

| Fiend Fire Deck |
| --- |
| - Gather a lot of cards, especially cards with card draw and energy like Battle Trance. - With a lot of cards in your hand use Fiend Fire to deal high damage to target. - Fiend Fire scales very well with Strength. - Runic Pyramid can help you gather a large number of cards. |

| Dropkick Infinite Deck |
| --- |
| - Get Dropkick and remove as many other cards as possible. Once you have 2 Dropkicks or 1 Dropkick + Dual Wield, you can play Bash + lnfinite Dropkick. Upgraded Offering is very useful in this build because it can draw 5 cards, which means that you can infinite kicks with a 10 card deck. - This is an easy to assemble but strong build. It can be done with restarting short games to get Dropkick early. |

| Snecko Eye Deck |
| --- |
| - If you manage to get Snecko Eye during first Boss fight, you can go for cards with high energy costs as main damage dealer: Bludgeon, Carnage and Immolate are the best, while Sever Soul and Fiend Fire can help with clutter. - Dual Wield is what makes this build shine: getting two zero cost Bludgeons is usually enough to finish a fight. - Defensively it's possible to focus exclusively on Flame Barrier. - Going for Perfected Strike build is a sound strategy prior to getting Snecko Eye, since Boss rewards are rather random. |

| Rampage Deck |
| --- |
| - Keep the deck small with cards to support your Rampage, preferably upgraded one, and use it repeatedly. - A balance between draw power like Battle Trance, Warcry, etc. and defense is good as Rampage can scale up quickly as main damage source with appropriate support cards, Shrug It Off is a great card as it provide both. - Best support card for Rampage is Double Tap, which ram up the power twice, and Headbutt can allow you to search for Rampage to be used  more frequently. - If possible, Vulnerable relics and cards can be devastating for enemies if combined with a well scaled Rampage. - Avoid cards that give Status like Wild Strike, Reckless Charge, or Immolate. It can make Rampage become inaccessible or less likely to be drawn later in fight, which defeat the purpose of the card. Only take them if you have Evolve+, and even then just reckless charge unless you have  Medical Kit or Second Wind to prevent situations where your hand is full of status cards. - Do not use Havoc unless you have Frozen Eye. - Unlike in a Claw deck, only 1 Rampage should be taken. |

## Unlocks

# J.A.X.

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/J.A.X.

**Infobox:**
- Name: J.A.X.
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/0/08/J.A.X..png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016212611
- Class: Neutral
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Special
- Cost: 0
- Effect: Lose 3 HP.; Gain 2 Strength.
- [J.A.X.+]
- Cost+: 0
- Effect+: Lose 3 HP.; Gain 3 Strength.

**J.A.X.** can only be obtained through the "Augmenter" Event.

- Being a constant source of Strength that does not exhaust, J.A.X. finds use in many Ironclad self-harm related builds and Silent Shiv-related builds. However, the Defect does not have enough direct damage cards to make the HP loss worth it in most cases, though it does have some incredible synergy with the cards Scrape and All for One.

## Interactions
- Intangible reduces all HP loss to 1, including from J.A.X..
- Runic Cube: Whenever you play J.A.X., draw 1 card.
- Blood for Blood: Each time you use J.A.X., decreases Blood for Blood's cost by 1.
- Reaper: Useful for regenerating HP lost through J.A.X.
- Heavy Blade, Pummel, Riddle with Holes: Significantly benefit from Strength.
- Rupture: Is triggered every time J.A.X. is used, furthering the Strength gain.
- Shivs: Each Shiv's damage is increased by 2 for each J.A.X. used. Since Shivs are easily created in multiples, this adds up quickly.

## Trivia
- The card's name is a play on words referring to "getting jacked", as in getting buff.

### Pattern
Always starts with Chomp.

# Judgment

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Judgment

**Infobox:**
- Name: Judgment
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/1/15/Judgment.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20191003145447
- Class: Watcher
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Rare
- Cost: 1
- Effect: If the enemy had 30 or less HP, set their HP to 0.
- [Judgment+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: If the enemy had 40 or less HP, set their HP to 0.

CardAutobox

Judgment will instantly kill an enemy who has 30(40) or less HP. This bypasses the enemy's Block, concerning only their remaining HP.

If the enemy does not have 30(40) or less HP, Judgment will do nothing.

Judgment is especially useful for enemies with high block but low HP, such as Spheric Guardian.

Judgement does not actually deal damage, so it will not trigger a Spiker's thorn effect nor the Guardian's sharp hide effect. Judgement will also bypass the Corrupt Heart's invincibility buff, and can execute it if its under 30 (40) HP, even if its invincibility buff is maxed out for the turn

# Keys

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Keys

: *This article is about the keys used to enter Act 4. For the unrelated relic, see Cursed Key.*

Once the Act 3 Boss has been defeated with all characters except the *Watcher* at least once in a normal run, three **keys** will begin to appear in subsequent normal runs. If all three keys are collected in the run, the run will not end after the Act 3 boss; instead, the player will enter Act 4.
## Ruby Key

The Ruby Key is obtained by taking the Recall action at Rest Sites. The key may be obtained at any Rest Site along the run.

## Emerald Key

The Emerald Key is obtained by defeating a buffed Elite that appears on the map with an animated flame behind its icon. One such Elite will appear in each act until the key is obtained.

## Sapphire Key

The Sapphire Key is obtained from a Treasure Room chest (including chests found in ? Rooms). It appears linked with a Relic, such that only the key or the relic may be taken. If the relic is taken, the key will keep appearing in subsequent chests until it is taken.

If you have the relic Matryoshka, you'll be able to take one of the relics freely, since the additional relic won't be linked with the Sapphire Key.

Category:Game Mechanics

# Keywords

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Keywords

A **Keyword** is a word or term that has a specific, predefined meaning within the game's mechanics. They often appear in bold on cards and relics.

## Core Mechanics
These are fundamental concepts of the game that are referenced by many cards and effects.
| Icon | Term | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | **Energy** | The resource used to play cards. By default, you gain 3 energy at the start of your turn. |
|  | **Draw** | The act of taking cards from your Draw Pile and adding them to your hand. By default, you draw 5 cards at the start of your turn. |
|  | **Discard** | The act of moving a card from your hand to the Discard Pile. Unplayed cards are typically discarded at the end of each turn. Some card effects also cause you to discard cards during your turn; effects on cards like Tactician and Reflex only trigger from these specific discards, not the end-of-turn cleanup. |

## Combat Keywords
These keywords relate to buffs, debuffs, and stats that are active during combat.
| Icon | Keyword | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | **Artifact** | A Buff that prevents the next Debuff you would receive. Each stack of Artifact negates one Debuff. |
|  | **Block** | A temporary defense that reduces incoming Attack damage. Block is removed at the start of your next turn. |
|  | **Dexterity** | A Buff that increases the amount of Block gained from cards. |
|  | **Poison** | A Debuff that deals damage at the start of the affected creature's turn. The amount of Poison is then reduced by 1. |
|  | **Strength** | A Buff that increases the damage of Attack cards. |
|  | **Vulnerable** | A Debuff that causes the affected creature to take 50% more damage from Attacks. |
|  | **Frail** | A Debuff that reduces the amount of Block gained from cards by 25% for 1 turn. |
|  | **Weak** | A Debuff that causes the affected creature to deal 25% less damage with Attacks. |

## Card-Specific Keywords
These keywords describe effects, types, and properties of cards.
| Icon | Keyword | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | **Attack Card** | A card type. Attack cards are primarily used to deal damage to enemies. Their damage is affected by Strength, Vulnerable, and Weak. |
|  | **Curse** | A card type. Curses are unplayable cards that have negative effects and clutter your hand and deck. |
|  | **Ethereal** | An effect on a card. If an Ethereal card is in your hand at the end of your turn and has not been played, it is Exhausted. |
|  | **Exhaust** | Removes a card from your deck for the rest of the current combat. |
|  | **Innate** | Cards with Innate start each combat in your opening hand. |
|  | **Power Card** | A card type. When played, Power cards grant the player a Buff that provides an ongoing effect for the rest of combat. Some Powers have side effects as part of their effect (e.g., Berserk applying Vulnerable, which expires over turns). |
|  | **Retain** | An effect on a card. You can choose to keep a card with Retain in your hand at the end of your turn instead of discarding it. |
|  | **Skill Card** | A card type. Skill cards are non-Attack cards that provide Block, draw cards, or apply other effects. |
|  | **Status** | A type of unplayable card that clutters your hand and deck, often added by enemy attacks. They are removed from your deck at the end of combat. |
|  | **Unplayable** | A card that cannot be played from your hand. Often found on Curses and Status cards. |

## Character-Specific Keywords
These are mechanics that are primarily associated with a single character class.
| Icon | Keyword | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | **Channel** | A mechanic exclusive to the Defect. Channeling an Orb places it in the next available Orb slot. If all slots are full, the rightmost Orb is Evoked. |
|  | **Evoke** | A mechanic exclusive to the Defect. Evoking an Orb removes it and triggers its special effect. |
|  | **Orb** | A mechanic exclusive to the Defect. Orbs are objects that have a passive effect each turn and an Evoke effect when consumed. |
|  | **Stance** | A mechanic exclusive to the Watcher. Being in a Stance provides a ongoing benefit (e.g., dealing double damage in Wrath, gaining Block in Calm). Entering a new Stance removes the old one. |

## Game Structure
These terms define the nested structure of a Slay the Spire game. Many card and relic effects refer to these states.

- **Turn**
:A player turn consists of being dealt cards from your Draw Pile and gaining Energy (by default, 5 cards and 3 Energy). The player can then play cards until they run out of Energy or choose to end their turn. After the player's turn, each enemy has a turn to attack or apply other effects.

- **Combat**
:A combat consists of a series of turns, alternating between the player and the enemies. Combat ends when either the player's HP is reduced to 0, or all enemies are defeated. Effects that last "until the end of combat" or "for the rest of combat" expire when it concludes.

- **Act**
:The Spire is divided into three main Acts (four with the true ending). Each Act is a map the player progresses through, containing multiple combats, elite encounters, rest sites, ? events, and a final boss.

- **Run**
:A full run consists of a single attempt to climb the Spire by progressing through the Acts. A run ends when the player is defeated or when they defeat the final boss of the last Act.

# Knowing Skull

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Knowing_Skull

The **Knowing Skull** is a rare Event found exclusively in Act 2. You encounter a talking skull that can grant many rewards, albeit for a bloody price.

You can encounter this event only if you have 13 or more HP.

## Options

- **[Riches?]** Obtain 90 Gold. Lose 10% of your Max HP (Minimum of 6 HP).

- **[Success?]** Obtain a random Uncommon Colorless card. Lose 10% of your Max HP (Minimum of 6 HP).

- **[A Pick Me Up?]** Obtain a Potion. Lose 10% of your Max HP (Minimum of 6 HP).

- **[How do I leave?]**  End the event. Lose 10% of your Max HP (Minimum of 6 HP).

Each time a reward is selected, the cost for that reward increases by 1 HP.

Rewards may be selected repeatedly for as much health as you are willing to spend. The event will not end until **[How do I leave?]** is selected.

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| *You find yourself in an old, decorated chamber. In the center of the room, a large skull sits atop an ornate pedestal. As you approach, the skull* bursts into flames *and turns to face you.* |
| *"WHAT IS IT YOU SEEK? WHAT IS IT YOU OFFER?"* |
| *In sync with its final words, the door behind you* slams shut.* |
| Riches? |
| *"YOU MORTALS NEVER CHANGE. IT IS DONE."* |
| *Gold rains down on you.* |
| Success? |
| *"PERHAPS THIS WILL HELP?"* |
| *You obtain a card.* |
| A Pick Me Up? |
| *"DRINK UP!"* |
| *You obtain a potion.* |
| How do I leave? |
| *"BEHIND YOU, MORTAL."* |
| *You peek behind the skull. Surely enough, there is a door.'' |

## Tips
- With Bloody Idol relic, choosing the **[Riches]** option will grant you 5 HP of healing to heavily offset the damage.
- Tungsten Rod relic reduces the HP cost of each reward by 1 HP. The cost for each reward still increases each time it is selected.

# Lagavulin

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Lagavulin

**Infobox:**
- Name: Lagavulin
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/c/c0/Lagavulin-zzz-pretty.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20180110054024
- HP: 109-111; 112-115 (Ascension 8+)
- In Party With: None
- Debut Act: 1
- Powers: Metallicize 8; Asleep

-The **Lagavulin** is an Elite enemy found only on the first act of the Spire. It hits heavily and consistently, but is found asleep for the first three turns of combat, unless encountered in the Dead Adventurer Event. This allows the player to decide when to start the fight properly, within reason.

## Awakening
Lagavulin will start with the unique debuff "Asleep", as well as a Metallicize buff, preventing it from taking any action, but granting it 8 Block at the start of every turn. Lagavulin will wake up at the end of its 3rd turn or when any HP damage is taken through the Block, and will lose its Metallicize buff in the process.

When Lagavulin wakes up by being attacked, it will be stunned for one turn. If Lagavulin wakes up on its own, it will begin the fourth turn unstunned.

## Pattern
Will attack twice, then uses Siphon Soul; repeats this pattern for the entire duration of the fight.
| Name | Intent | Effect | Asc 3+ | Asc 18+ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Attack |  | Deal 18 damage. | Deal 20 damage. | Deal 20 damage. |
| Siphon Soul |  | Inflicts -1 Dexterity, then -1  Strength. | Inflicts -1 Dexterity, then -1  Strength. | Inflicts -2 Dexterity, then -2  Strength. |
## Tips
- Use the three turns before Lagavulin wakes up to prepare for the fight by using Powers and/or using Skills.
    - Alternatively, it may be more reasonable to deal damage instead of buffs/debuffs if a large amount of damage is possible.
- Try to stay mostly aggressive for the fight; its Siphon Soul ability will gradually make the fight harder which can be lethal.
- The Defect can be an easier character to fight against Lagavulin with than the others, as its Focus (which dictates how effective orbs are) will not be decreased by Siphon Soul.
- If you have one Artifact charge when Siphon Soul is used, it will block the dexterity debuff since that is applied first. 

## Trivia
- Lagavulin comes from Gaelic language '*Lag a’ Mhuilinn*' which means 'hollow of the mill'.
- Lagavulin references a distillery located in Islay, Scotland. A whiskey with the same name is produced there.

- Effect+: Deal 13 damage. If Fatal, Upgrade a random card in your deck. Exhaust.

CardAutobox**Lesson Learned** will upgrade a random card in your deck if it is used to kill an enemy. After being used it exhausts, whether it has killed an enemy or not.

The kills must be considered Fatal to upgrade a card. Not all enemies count as Fatal kills (exceptions detailed below).

## Interactions
 
- **Lesson Learned** is capable of upgrading itself.
- Exhume can be used to return **Lesson Learned** to your deck, allowing for more than one use or kill per battle.
- Strange Spoon gives a 50% chance that **Lesson Learned** will not exhaust on use.

 
- Minions do not count as Fatal kills. These are recognized by the  icon. For a list of minion enemies, see the Minion page. 
- If fighting Darklings, reducing the HP of one of them to 0 does not count as a Fatal kill unless it was the final enemy from the batch.
- Defeating the first phase of the Awakened One does not count as a Fatal kill.
- The card it upgrades will not be upgraded during the fight itself, and only from the next fight onward.

# Limit Break

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Limit_Break

**Infobox:**
- Name: Limit Break
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/8/8c/LimitBreak.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016210818
- Class: Ironclad
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Rare
- Cost: 1
- Effect: Double your Strength. ; Exhaust.
- [Limit Break+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: Double your Strength.

**Limit Break** is a Rare Skill card for the Ironclad. It doubles the player's current Strength, then Exhausts. When Upgraded, Limit Break does not Exhaust and can be played multiple times per combat.

## Interactions
 
- Limit Break works well with Strength-boosting Relics such as Vajra, Girya, Du-Vu Doll, and Red Skull.
- Strength Potions can be used to provide an initial +2 Strength, which can then be doubled with Limit Break.
- Flex Potions and Flex provide some Strength and an equal amount of the Strength Down debuff. Using the Flex Potion/playing Flex and using Limit Break during that same turn will double the Strength added without affecting the Strength Down debuff, keeping a large amount of extra Strength. 
- Headbutt can return Limit Break+ to the top of the deck, allowing Limit Break to be used on multiple turns quickly.
- Exhume can get back a non-Upgraded Limit Break for an extra use.

- **Limit Break** requires an existing Strength modifier to have an effect (as 2 times 0 is still 0). Without any Strength buff or debuff, Limit Break does nothing.

 
- Negative Strength, such as from Lagavulin's Siphon Soul debuff, will also be doubled by Limit Break.

# Living Wall

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Living_Wall

**Living Wall** is an event found exclusively in Act 1. Three friendly statues emerge from the stonework to offer their assistance
## Options

- **[Forget]** Remove a card from your deck.

- **[Change]** Transform a card in your deck.

- **[Grow]** Upgrade a card in your deck.

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| *As you come to a dead-end and begin to turn around, walls* slam down *from the ceiling, trapping you!* |
| *Three faces materialize from the walls and speak.* |
| ''"Forget what you know, and I'll let you go."* |
| *"I require change to see a new space."* |
| *"If you want to pass me, then you must grow."* |
| Forget, Change, or Grow |
| *Satisfied, the walls in front of you merge back into the ceiling, leaving a path forward.'' |

## Strategy
There's no price or drawback to any choice. The only caveat is that once the player chooses a statue, they can't change their mind. Be sure to check your deck *before* choosing.
- **[Forget] **This option should almost always be chosen if the player has a removable Curse (with the possible exception of Parasite) in their deck. Removing the unwanted, detrimental card is a strong option.
- **[Change] **While this option is indisputably the weakest out of the three, it can be useful in decks that have no leaning yet or lack enough decent cards to beat the boss. This option is preferable to upgrading a Strike but less desirable than simply removing it in most cases.
- **[Grow] **This option should be chosen if the player has a card in their deck that would be significantly stronger when upgraded. This includes cards that scale more when they are upgraded, cards that increase in debuff, buff, or draw, cards that become Innate or no longer Exhaust, and the unique Searing Blow.

**Loop** is an Uncommon Defect Power.

## Strategy
Loop can be seen as a substitution of Capacitor. Rather than focusing on increasing the number of slots, Loop utilizes the use of a single slot (the “active” orb slot).

Plasma and Dark Orb benefits the most from this power. For dark orbs, Loop can be used to accelerate the process of gaining damage. And for Plasma ones, every Loop you play will be produced into pure energy.

Loop can also be used with Frost Orbs in a pinch, as it gives more free block if you need to block a specific attack.

# Malaise

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Malaise

**Infobox:**
- Name: Malaise
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/d/d1/Malaise.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016211834
- Class: Silent
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Rare
- Effect: Enemy loses X Strength. Apply X Weak.; Exhaust.
- [Malaise+]
- Effect+: Enemy loses X+1 Strength. Apply X+1 Weak.; Exhaust.

**Malaise** is a Rare card for The Silent which permanently reduces one enemy's Strength and applies many turns of Weak. As an X-cost card, it consumes all remaining Energy when played. 

Strength Reduction is applied before Weak, and will be negated by Artifact in that sequence. Enemies with a single Artifact charge will only have Weak applied on them, as Strength Reduction gets negated by the Artifact. 2 or more Artifact charges will completely nullify this card's effect, removing 2 Artifact charges in the process.

Upgrading Malaise increases the Strength loss and Weak count by 1. This will trigger even if you play Malaise with 0 Energy remaining, effectively applying 1 Strength Loss and 1 Weak for no cost.

## Strategy
Malaise is a deceptively strong card. It has a potential to be the strongest source of permanent Strength reduction. Its Strength reduction severely punishes the Snake Plant, Hexaghost, and other enemies that rely on multi-strike, low damage attacks. Its Weak applied can also cripple a hard-hitting enemy for many turns.

The Silent has access to a number of Energy-increasing cards, which can power Malaise up further.

### Synergies
 
- Well-Laid Plans can Retain Malaise until a turn with respectably generated Energy.
- Burst interacts with Malaise the same way as any other X-cost card: Malaise will be played twice at X Strength, where X is the amount of Energy remaining. 
    - For example, playing Burst with 3 energy, then playing Malaise (with 2 energy), will reduce Strength by 4 and apply 4 Weak (barring Artifact). This is particularly powerful with Chemical X, as the bonus application is applied twice.
- Malaise applies two debuffs for the purpose of Sadistic Nature.
- Ice Cream helps the Silent conserve energy between turns, further increasing Malaise's strength.
- Chemical X overperforms with this card, potentially reducing an enemy's Strength by two or three points for free.
- Paper Krane cripples the enemy even further with empowered Weak, softening even a single, hard-hitting attack to be more manageable.
    - Malaise can also applies a longer-lasting Weak with a single use, making Paper Krane even more effective in a longer fight.
- Bag of Marbles, Red Mask, and Twisted Funnel help clear innate Artifact charges to allow Malaise to be used with its full potential.
- Hexaghost, Snake Plant, and Byrd are severely crippled by this card, as they mostly rely on multi-hit attacks.

 
- Malaise, especially its upgraded form, can be used to clear 2 stacks of Artifact in a clutch. This is generally not advised, but it can be used in a case that you want to apply other debuff, such as Poison.
- Corrupt Heart can have its Blood Shots, a rapid attack, nullified once with Malaise. However, its Strength Reduction will be periodically cleared, and its first use of Buff grants it 2 charges of Artifact, making future Malaise harder to use.
    - Corrupt Heart however cannot remove Weak via Buff and has to wait until it runs out, which could be invaluable if Weak is applied beforehand in a large quantity.  

 
- Malaise is very impractical when there is a large number of enemies, as you can use it on only one of them and it consumes all of your remaining Energy. 
- Enemies with innate Artifact, such as Sentry, Spheric Guardian, and Donu and Deca make it harder to efficiently or quickly use Malaise.
    - Donu and Deca are especially good at countering this card. They come in a pair, have innate 2 (3 Ascension 19+) charges of Artifact and steadily and rapidly scale their Strength up, rendering Malaise moot in no time.
- The Champ, Awakened One, and Time Eater can remove all debuffs. While Malaise could make the beginning of the fight easier, you could potentially still have to face their fully-powered attack later in the fight.
    - All three of them can also regain Strength lost before gaining even more Strength to top it off.
    - Awakened One and Time Eater also regain their health, making the long fight much harder.

# Mark of Pain

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Mark_of_Pain

**Infobox:**
- Name: Mark of Pain
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/d/df/MarkofPain.png/revision/latest?cb=20200203153107
- Description: Gain 1 Energy at the start of each turn. Start combats with 2 Wounds in your draw pile.
- Flavor: This brand was used by the northern tribes to signify warriors who had mastered pain in battle.
- Rarity: Boss
- Class: Ironclad

Gain 1 Energy at the start of each turn. At the start of combat, add 2 Wounds to your draw pile.

Wounds are added *after* drawing your initial hand of cards on Turn 1 of a combat, so they will never appear there. However, they are added in relic pickup order; so if you gained a Bag of Preparation *after* gaining Mark of Pain, the Wounds can be drawn in the two additional draws. If you gained Bag of Preparation *before* gaining Mark of Pain, the additional two draws will not contain Wounds. Gambling Chip's interface is usable after relics have finished triggering, so it will always have a chance to draw Wounds. If your deck contains fewer cards than your initial draw size, you will draw your entire deck and *then* Wounds will be added to your empty draw pile.

Mark of Pain is a Boss Relic.

# Mark of the Bloom

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Mark_of_the_Bloom

**Infobox:**
- Name: Mark of the Bloom
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/0/0b/MarkoftheBloom.png/revision/latest?cb=20200203153722
- Description: You can no longer heal.
- Flavor: In the Beyond, thoughts and reality are one.
- Rarity: Event
- Class: Any

A relic gained through the "Mind Bloom" event, an Act 3 event.

## Effect
Healing is now impossible by any means. This includes:
- Direct healing via cards, relics, potions, events,  Resting, and entering new Acts.
- Revival, as no HP is restored when the player would be revived and so their HP stays at 0. 
- Indirect healing from increasing max HP via cards, relics, potions, events. Max HP will still increase for the purpose of calculating score, but the player's current HP will not increase accordingly.

CardAutobox
Master Reality is a Power card for the Watcher. When Master Reality's buff is active, any cards created during combat are automatically upgraded.

List of Watcher cards affected by Master Reality:
- Smite cards created by Battle Hymn and Carve Reality
- Through Violence created by Reach Heaven
- Safety created by Deceive Reality
- Expunger created by Conjure Blade
- The card chosen through Foreign Influence
- Miracles created by Deus Ex Machina
- Insights created by Evaluate, Pray, and Study
- Beta created by Alpha
- Omega created by Beta
Cards generated from other classes may also be affected if they are somehow obtained, such as with Prismatic Shard. Notable examples include:

- Shivs generated by Blade Dance or the many other cards which generate them
- The card duplicated by Nightmare

## Interactions
 
- Playing an Alpha card after playing Master Reality will produce Beta+ (cost reduced from 2 to 1), which in turn will produce Omega+ (damage increased from 50 to 60).
- Cards created via the , Enchiridion, and Nilry's Codex will be upgraded once the Master Reality buff is active.
- Cards created by Colorless Cards such as Discovery, Metamorphosis, and Chrysalis will all be upgraded.
- Cards that are returned from stasis into your hand from killing one of the Bronze Automaton's Bronze Orbs are upgraded by this card.

**Masterful Stab **is an Attack card for the Silent. It starts at 0 cost, but increases cost whenever you lose HP.

## Mechanics

- The cost increases by the number of times you lose HP, not the amount of HP lost.
- The cost of the card is not limited to 3.
- If this card is created during combat (such as through Dead Branch, Attack Potion, Metamorphosis, or Foreign Influence), it will start at base cost, ignoring any HP you lost before it existed, unlike Blood for Blood.

## Interactions
- Snecko Eye: Masterful Stab's cost will be overwritten by Confused whenever it is drawn, but can still increase in cost between draws.

## Old Masterful Stab
Prior to Weekly Patch 39, Masterful Stab had the following card text: Can only be played if there are no other cards in your hand. Deal 16(21) damage.

# Match and Keep

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Match_and_Keep

**Match and Keep **is an event that can appear in Act 1, Act 2, and Act 3.

You are forced to play a card matching game. You get 5 attempts to match cards. Any cards you match, you add to your deck, regardless of whether you want the card or not. The following cards will be available for matching:

- 1 pair of Basic colored cards (Bash, Neutralize, Zap, or Eruption).
- 1 pair of Common colored cards
- 1 pair of Uncommon colored cards
- 1 pair of Rare colored cards
- 1 pair of a random Curse
- 1 pair of Uncommon Colorless cards
    - Replaced by an additional pair of Curses on Ascension 15 or higher
The color of each colored card will be dependent on which character you are playing as.

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| *A gremlin is madly shuffling cards on a table. This monster seems to be a harmless one. You approach him out of curiosity.* |
| **Gremlin:** *Twelve cards! Match them to keep them! Five tries, no do-overs. * |
| **Gremlin:** ''Are you ready? Let's start!* |
| Finish |
| *You complete the gremlin's game and look up.'* |
| * He disappeared?'' |

## Strategy
- If you don't want to add any cards to your deck, you can just pick the same 2 cards 5 times and not add any cards to your deck
    - However, you could pick 2 matching cards initially, though the odds of this are somewhat low, at only 1/11.

- Be wary of the Curses that the game offers. On Ascension 15+, the second pair of curses can be the same curse as the first pair, so be more careful when on high ascension levels, unless you seek curses.
- The Rare card offered is most likely to be beneficial to your deck, so try to see which card it is to decide whether or not to match it.

# Mayhem

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Mayhem

**Infobox:**
- Name: Mayhem
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/d/dd/Mayhem.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016212653
- Class: Neutral
- Type: Power
- Rarity: Rare
- Cost: 2
- Effect: At the start of your turn, play the top card of your draw pile.
- [Mayhem+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: At the start of your turn, play the top card of your draw pile.
- Name: Mayhem
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/1/18/Icon_Mayhem.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202163413
- Description: At the start of your turn, play the top X card of your draw pile.
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: Intensity

**Mayhem** will play the top card of your Draw Pile at the start of each turn.

The cost of the played card is ignored, meaning high cost cards can be potentially played for free. 

## Interactions
 
- Playing a Curse or Status card via **Mayhem** will place the card into your discard pile, bypassing end-of-turn negative effects from cards such as Doubt and Burn.
- Cards with X Energy cost that are played via **Mayhem** will be treated as if all of your energy was spent, without actually costing any energy.

 
- Playing **Mayhem** with Echo Form will cause Mayhem's automatically played card to be played twice, rather than allowing you to choose the first card. Playing a card too fast at the start of your turn will play the chosen card twice then mayhem will trigger making the card played by mayhem played only once (having plasma as defect delays mayhem trigger making it easier to choose which card to play twice before mayhem triggers).
- The card is played after you have drawn your hand, which prevents the use of effects like Headbutt to set up a particular card for **Mayhem** to play for free, but allows you to play that card at the best point in your turn.

 
- If **Mayhem** plays an Ethereal curse like Ascender's Bane or Clumsy, the card will be placed into your discard pile rather than exhausted.
- Mayhem can force you to unexpectedly incur negative effects (notably, if it plays Blasphemy, you will die the next turn)

# Melter

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Melter

**Infobox:**
- Name: Melter
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/7/71/Melter.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016203602
- Class: Defect
- Type: Attack
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Cost: 1
- Effect: Remove all Block from the enemy.; Deal 10 damage.
- [Melter+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: Remove all Block from the enemy.; Deal 14 damage.

CardAutobox
Melter is an uncommon Attack for The Defect. It destroys all of the targeted enemy's Block, then inflicts a decent amount of damage. As an Uncommon card, Melter can appear as a post-battle reward and be purchased from The Merchant.

Upgrading Melter increases the card's damage from 10 to 14.

### Strategy
- Melter is a tech card - it's exceptionally strong against certain enemies. Luckily, high-Block enemies are particularly annoying, and it's a solid beatstick against the others.

- Melter excels against the Spheric Guardian, effectively dealing 50 or more damage and setting up an easy turn-one kill. It also rips through the abilities of Shelled Parasite and Snake Plant, and punishes Monsters with armor-granting abilities like Darkling, Centurion, and most Minions. It beats The Guardian up immediately after it transforms, and speeds up the Donu and Deca final battle.

- Melter destroys Block before inflicting its damage, meaning it will deal damage directly to Health. 

- Players will almost never encounter multiple high-shield enemies at once, making redundant copies of Melter unnecessary in small decks.

- As a solid standalone utility card, Melter is an oddity among The Defect's highly synergistic card pool. Its effect can translate into a big burst of damage, making it play nicely with efficient, aggressive cards like Hyperbeam.

- The armor-removing effect is not a Debuff, so Melter will not trigger Sadistic Nature and is not nullified by Artifact.

### Trivia
Melter's art depicts what the card does best - melting a Spheric Guardian.

# Merchant

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Merchant

**Infobox:**
- Name: Merchant
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/f/f9/MerchantWithProps.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20200529191011

The **Shop** is one of the Map Locations, and it is the primary way for the player to spend their Gold.

## Wares for Sale
On Ascension 16+, shop prices are increased by 10%.

### 5 Colored Cards (Class-Specific)
There will always be 2 Attack cards, 2 Skill cards, and 1 Power card.
- Common: 45 - 55 Gold
- Uncommon: 68 - 82 Gold
- Rare: 135 - 165 Gold
One of the cards will always be On Sale, reducing its cost by 50%.

### 2 Colorless Cards
There will always be an uncommon Colorless card on the left, and a rare one on the right.
- Uncommon: 81 - 99 Gold
- Rare: 162 - 198 Gold

### 3 Relics
The Relic on the right will always be a Shop Relic. This is the only source of Shop Relics.
- Common: 143 - 157 Gold
- Uncommon: 238 - 262 Gold
- Rare: 285 - 315 Gold
- Shop: 143 - 157 Gold

### 3 Potions
- Common: 48 - 52 Gold
- Uncommon: 72 - 78 Gold
- Rare: 95 - 105 Gold

### Card Removal Service
- Can only be used once per shop.
- Costs 75 Gold initially, increases cost by 25 Gold every time it is used at any shop.

## Interactions
- The Courier: When you buy a Card, Relic, or Potion, it is replaced by a random item of the same type. In addition, all purchases have a 20% discount. This stacks multiplicatively with Membership Card (for a combined 60% discount), except for card removal (which takes the better discount).
    - The Colorless cards may be replaced by a colorless card of a different rarity, however, and the Shop Relic will be replaced by a Common, Uncommon, or Rare relic.
- Membership Card: All shop items and services have a 50% discount. Stacks with The Courier.
- Smiling Mask: The Card Removal Service now always costs 50 gold.
- Meal Ticket: Whenever you enter a shop room, heal 15 HP.
- Maw Bank: If you buy an item at the shop, this relic is disabled and no longer provides 12 Gold per floor. This includes the card removal service.

## Merchant

The **Merchant** is the friendly NPC who sells items at the Shop.

### Description
The Merchant is a blue skinned man sitting on a blue-green rug next to some cards, a small chest, a bag, and a knife. He is wearing a mask covering his face (similar to the Smiling Mask Relic) and a blue cloak. He is friendly towards the player, if not a little rude and brash, and talks to them while they view and purchase his wares, mostly small talk, or statements revealing his greed.

### Trivia
- In the game's soundtrack, the music which plays while the player is visiting the Shop is titled "Meet the Merchant". 
    - This could be a reference to the Meet the Team videos for Team Fortress 2.
- One of his quotes "I used to be like you" suggests he was similar to the players in some manner in the past. It is implied, since this quote is only shown in Act 4, that the Merchant was once also a puppet of Neow. Of course,  it could also just be a reference to the memetic *Skyrim* NPC quote "I used to be an adventurer like you, then I took an arrow in the knee."
- One of his quotes, "Stay a while and listen", is a reference to, and direct quote from, Deckard Cain from the Diablo series.

# Meteor Strike

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Meteor_Strike

**Infobox:**
- Name: Meteor Strike
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/1/15/MeteorStrike.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016203602
- Class: Defect
- Type: Attack
- Rarity: Rare
- Cost: 5
- Effect: Deal 24 damage.; Channel 3 Plasma.
- [Meteor Strike+]
- Cost+: 5
- Effect+: Deal 30 damage.; Channel 3 Plasma.

CardAutobox
Meteor Strike is an Attack card for The Defect that deals a huge amount of damage, channels a lot of Plasma orbs, and has a notoriously restrictive Energy cost.

Upgrading Meteor Strike increases its damage from 24 to 30.

## Strategy
- Meteor Strike requires The Defect to generate two extra Energy just to play it! The payoff is worth the effort - big damage, up to 3 Evokes, and six Energy to play with the following turn.

- Taking Meteor Strike without high-powered Energy generation can be risky. However, since Energy-generating cards are far more common than Meteor Strike, it is not unreasonable to take Meteor Strike and then immediately start looking for such cards. Keep an eye out for cards like Fusion, Aggregate, Double Energy, and Energy-generating Boss Relics like Cursed Key.

- Since Meteor Strike provides no defense, expect to take some damage the first time it's played. Subsequent plays will actually generate Energy, since remaining Plasma Orbs will probably be Evoked.

- Plasma Orbs consistently generate Energy each turn, so Meteor Strike stabilizes a single-turn Energy boost like Double Energy into an Energy advantage that can last through the rest of the battle.

- Meteor Strike obviously requires Energy generation. Relics are best, but in practice, a combination of Relics and Skills will probably be necessary. TURBO is actually a good choice, as the Plasma Orbs offset Void's Energy loss.

- Subsequent Meteor Strikes will likely Evoke some Plasma Orbs and refund their own costs. Add Skim and Machine Learning to keep the combo going.

- Playing Meteor Strike with an active Echo Form is frankly ridiculous.

- One of Meteor Strike's strongest synergies is Tempest. Tempest Evokes the Plasma orbs, enabling a 12-Energy turn. Meteor Strike then Evokes the Lightning Orbs, dealing 45 total damage and restoring the Plasma.

- Because Plasma Orbs aren't affected by Focus, consider playing Meteor Strike alongside Hyperbeam.

- Snecko Eye can reduce Meteor Strike's cost enough to play without Energy generation. Snecko Eye will also never make a card cost more than 3, making the combo pure upside.
- If played as a non-defect character (with 1 empty orb slot) it will cost 5 energy and refund 4 from evokes for a net loss of 1 energy.

# Mind Bloom

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Mind_Bloom

**Mind Bloom** is an event found exclusively in Act 3. Your imagination manifests into reality. In this ephemeral moment, all your wishes can come true, though not without consequences.

## Options

*Numbers in parentheses are for Ascension 15 or higher.*

- **[I am War]** Fight a Boss from Act 1. Obtain a Rare Relic, normal rewards and 50 (25) gold.

- **[I am Awake]** Upgrade all Cards. Obtain Mark of the Bloom, prohibiting you from healing.

- **[I am Rich]** Gain 999 gold. Become Cursed - 2 Normalities.

- **[I am Healthy]** Heal to full HP. Become Cursed - Doubt.

The first option will always be **[I am War], **and the second option will always be **[I am Awake].** However, the third option will either be **[I am Rich] ** on floors 35 - 40** or **[I am Healthy] ** on floor 41 and above.

If **[I am War]''' is selected, Pantograph and Slaver's Collar will work as if it is another Boss encounter.

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| *While walking and traversing through the chaos of the Spire, your thoughts suddenly begin to feel very... real...* |
| *Imaginings of monsters and riches begin to manifest themselves into reality.* |
| *The sensation is quickly fleeting. What do you do?* |
| I am Rich / I am Healthy |
| *Can it really be this easy?* |
| I am Awake |
| *Everything makes sense now.* |
| *The lack of memories, the ascent, the Ancient One.* |
| *This is the way it always was.* |
| *This is the way it always will be.* |
| *All will be forgotten again soon...* |

## Strategy
- **[I am War] **is generally the safest option. It gives the player a random Rare Relic and 50 Gold with little cost; by the time the player is in Act 3, their deck will typically be strong enough to slaughter the Act 1 boss with ease. The relic it gives may be skipped if the player is attempting the "Who Needs Relics?" Achievement.

- **[I am Awake] **is typically the most dangerous of the three options, as there is no way to negate its downside. Unless the player is very confident in their deck, or this event is found near the end of the act, taking this option is not viable. In addition, this option gives the player the Mark of the Bloom relic, so it cannot be taken if the player is attempting the "Who Needs Relics?" achievement.

- **[I am Rich] **is a strong option if the player has ways to handle Curses (Omamori,  Du-Vu Doll, Darkstone Periapt, any reliable way to remove curses) and is even more powerful with ways to leverage the gold efficiently (Membership Card, The Courier, plenty of upcoming Merchants). The money it gives the player is also useful for increasing your score. Be careful, as the Normalities this option grants are dangerous.

- **[I am Healthy] **is useful if the player is very low on HP, but it is not useful in other circumstances, unless the player is running Fire Breathing, has Du-Vu Doll or is not confident in their ability to fight an Act 1 boss.

# Minion

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Minion

**Infobox:**
- Name: Minion
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/6/60/Icon_Minion.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202163414
- Description: Minions abandon combat without their leader.
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: None

Minion is a Buff inherent to summoned enemies. It has no positive effect, and is used only to indicates the behaviour the enemy that has it.

Gameplay-wise, Minions abandon combat without their leader. This means that if only enemies with Minion remain, they will flee or disappear and the combat is won by the player.

Effects attached to keyword Fatal only activates on  non-Minion. For example, Feed only raises Max HP on killing a non-Minion.

When the leader of the Minion attempts to summon them, their intent will turn Unknown. 

## List of Minion summoners
- Gremlin Leader
    - Start the combat with 2 random Gremlins summoned. 
    - May summon up to 2 them again if one or more are dead. 
    - Can have up to 3 Gremlins present at a time.
      - Fat Gremlin
      - Mad Gremlin
      - Shield Gremlin
      - Sneaky Gremlin
      - Gremlin Wizard
- Bronze Automaton
    - Starts the combat by summoning 2 Bronze Orbs. 
    - Will not summon them again.
- The Collector
    - Starts the combat by summoning 2 Torch Heads. 
    - May summon up to 2 them again if one or more are dead.
    - Can have up to 2 Torch Heads present at a time.
- Reptomancer
    - Starts the combat by summoning 1 (2) Dagger(s).
    - May summon them again throughout the combat until the number of Daggers reaches its limit.
    - Can have up to 4 Daggers presents at a time.

## Trivia
- Apart from the mechanical Bronze Automaton, all of the enemies that can summon Minions are female.

# Miracle

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Miracle

**Infobox:**
- Name: Miracle
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/5/5c/Miracle.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20190918002430
- Class: Neutral
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Special
- Cost: 0
- Effect: Retain. Gain . Exhaust.
- [Miracle+]
- Cost+: 0
- Effect+: Retain. Gain . Exhaust.

CardAutobox **Miracle** is a special 0-cost card for the Watcher. It grants Energy when played and then Exhausts. Like many cards generated by her cards and relics, it has Retain.

It cannot be obtained by itself; instead, Miracles are added to your hand via other means. 

### Sources
- Deus Ex Machina: Adds 2(3) Miracle to your hand when drawn.
- Collect: Adds 1 Miracle+ at the start of the turn for X(+1) turns.
- Pure Water: Adds 1 Miracle to your hand at the start of combat.
- Holy Water: Adds 3 Miracles to your hand at the start of combat.
- Bottled Miracle: Add 2 Miracles to your hand.

## Strategy
Miracle is a simple Energy-generating card. However, its Retain allows you to keep it in your hand until the moment you would like to use it. Early on, it is perfect for an extra attack in Wrath to finish off an enemy. Later on, it can enable you to play a key card that is expensive, or allow you to use an extra card to gain Block or to change Stance.

### Synergies
 
- Crush Joints can be played immediately after for Vulnerable, and its 1 cost means you would always be able to play it after a use of Miracle.
- Sanctity can be played immediately after for card draw. With Energy gained from Miracle you could play an additional card or two.
- Conjure Blade benefits greatly from this card, as you can wait until a safe turn, or when you have accumulated high energy, before playing it for a deadly Expunger.
- As it sits in your hand, it grants you Block from Cloak Clasp and increase Block gained from Spirit Shield. 
- Ice Cream allows you to accumulate energy for future turns. With it, you can play all Miracles in advance so it does not clog up your hand.
- Dead Branch generates a card after Miracle is used, which you may use right after with Energy gained.

 
- Apart from Deus Ex Machina and Bottled Miracle, Miracle are usually granted to you at the start of a combat or already upgraded, making Master Reality obsolete in most circumstances.

# Mummified Hand

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Mummified_Hand

**Infobox:**
- Name: Mummified Hand
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/4/4d/MummifiedHand.png/revision/latest?cb=20190923234527
- Description: Whenever you play a Power, a random card in your hand costs 0 for the turn.
- Flavor: Frequently twitches, especially when your pulse is high.
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Class: Any

Whenever you play a Power, a random card in your hand costs 0 until it is played. The description states that it lasts until the end of the turn, but this is not in fact the case. If you play the card, then return it to your hand by whatever means, it no longer benefits from this cost reduction.

Mummified Hand is an Uncommon Relic.

## Notes
- This relic gives rise to a unique archetype for the Defect, the so-called powerbuild. Using cards like Heatsinks, Storm and Creative AI to make crazy combos. This strategy is explained in more detail on the Defect page under Power matters.
- As with other effects that reduce the cost of a random card, Mummified Hand will never "waste" itself by targeting a card that already costs 0. This includes skills affected by Corruption, and holds true even when it triggers from playing Corruption itself; the power's effect is applied before Mummified Hand.

# Mutagenic Strength

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Mutagenic_Strength

**Infobox:**
- Name: Mutagenic Strength
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/2/2a/MutagenicStrength.png/revision/latest?cb=20200203153737
- Description: Start each combat with 3 Strength that is lost at the end of your turn.
- Flavor: "The results seem fleeting, triggering when the subject is in danger." - Unknown
- Rarity: Event
- Class: All

A relic that can only be obtained through the "Augmenter" event. It starts your combat with 3 Strength, but also 3 Strength Down.

## Synergy
This relic synergizes with Clockwork Souvenir, as the Strength that you lose at the end of the turn will be negated by the Artifact that it provides, thus letting you keep the Strength for the rest of combat.

However, if there are more important uses for the Artifact (for example, to negate Bias from Biased Cognition or to negate Vulnerable from debuff-largeDebilitate), then Mutagenic Strength has a negative synergy with Clockwork Souvenir.

It is important to keep in mind that on the relic bar, if Mutagenic Strength is on the Right side of Clockwork Souvenir, then Mutagenic Strength activates Before Clockwork Souvenir (which is unintuitive), and the Artifact gained from Clockwork Souvenir is not immediately consumed, allowing the possibility for Orange Pellets to remove Strength Down in turn 1, thus preserving the Artifact.

# N'loth

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/N%27loth

'''N'loth** is an event found exclusively in Act 2. You encounter a peculiar creature, offering you a gift in exchange for a relic for him to feed on.

## Options

- **[Offer]''' One of two randomly chosen Relics you own. Obtain N'loth's Gift.

- **[Leave]** Nothing happens.

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| *An odd creature with a hunched back sprouting several tentacles is scrounging through a pile of trash and debris in front of you. As you approach, he shuffles towards you in a non-threatening manner.* |
| ''"N'loth hungry. Feed N'loth."* |
| Offer |
| *Holding the relic out towards him, N’loth snatches it out of your hand with his tentacles, dislocates his jaw, and slurps down your offer in one quick gulp.* |
| *He gives you a large, toothy grin as more tentacles appear from behind his cloak, these ones brandishing an impossibly neat looking box. He pushes it towards you until you take it.* |
| Leave |
| *You shake your head. N'loth hunches even further and sighs, then scuttles away.'' |

## Strategy
- It is possible to offer a Relic that no longer has any use (ex: Omamori, Neow's Lament, Matryoshka, Calling Bell, Maw Bank), thereby getting N'loth's Gift at no consequence.
- Relics with effects that activate when you pick them up e.g. Old Coin, Calling Bell, Mango, Maw Bank, Tiny House will not cause you to lose their effects if you give them to N'loth, so those can be given to obtain N'loth's Gift for free.

## Trivia
- His face can be acquired in the Face Trader event.

# Necronomicon

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Necronomicon

**Infobox:**
- Name: Necronomicon
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/7/78/Necronomicon.png/revision/latest?cb=20190923234548
- Description: The first Attack played each turn that costs 2 or more is played twice. When you take this relic, become Cursed.
- Flavor: Only a fool would try and harness this evil power. At night your dreams are haunted by images of the book devouring your mind.
- Rarity: Event
- Class: Any

Necronomicon is a Relic obtained through the Cursed Tome Event.

Picking up this relic will give the player a Necronomicurse, an unplayable Card that cannot be removed from your deck by any means and cannot be truly Exhausted. Attempting to Exhaust it will simply put it back to your hand.

This relic can be triggered on an X card, so long as it consumes 2 or more Energy. The second play will use the same value for X as the first.

The Necronomicurse counts for Du-Vu Doll and Darkstone Periapt.

A card that has had its cost reduced to below 2 by any effect will *not* be played twice. The card must spend 2 energy - not have an original cost of 2.

Interestingly, the Omamori will in fact negate the Necronomicurse entirely.

## Trivia
- This relic (especially its appearance) is a reference to the Necronomicon from *Spelunky*, which references the *Evil Dead* franchise, which in turn references the Necronomicon from the writings of H.P. Lovecraft, in which it is an evil tome containing otherworldly secrets that will drive humans to insanity merely from learning them.
- Despite Necronomicon's description, Necronomicurse is scripted to have its existence tied with Necronomicon. Should Necronomicon be removed by any means (possibly via N'loth), Necronomicurse will be removed from the deck as well.

- Effect: Unplayable.; There is no escape from this curse.

CardAutobox**Necronomicurse** is received when you get the Necronomicon from the Cursed Tome event. This curse cannot be removed from your deck by any means (unless Necronomicon is removed, possibly by N'loth). When it is exhausted, Necronomicon will flash and put another one in your hand.

## Strategy
- Necronomicurse counts for Du-Vu Doll.
- Omamori will negate the Necronomicurse entirely, but only if Omamori is acquired first.
- If the Necronomicurse is played with Blue Candle, it will be returned to your hand after being exhausted; while this means you can't escape the Necronomicurse, you can play it this way as many times as you want, and that interaction can be exploited in a number of ways.
    - It allows you to take arbitrary amounts of damage in one-damage increments, triggering useful on-damage effects like Rupture or Blood for Blood.
    - Alternatively, the Tungsten Rod negates the HP loss, allowing you to keep playing the Curse for free.
    - Each play still counts as an exhaust, so it will trigger on-exhaust effects like Dead Branch, Dark Embrace, and Charon's Ashes.
    - Each one counts as a card played, so it can trigger things like Panache or A Thousand Cuts.

## Trivia
- The Necronomicon is a reference to ''Evil Dead's'' Necronomicon Ex-Mortis, which is a reference to the Necronomicon in Lovecraft mythos.
- Despite Necronomicon's description, Necronomicurse is scripted to have its existence tied with Necronomicon. Should Necronomicon be removed by any means (possibly via N'loth), Necronomicurse will be removed from the deck as well, however, if the curse was copied (by Duplicator or  Dolly's Mirror for example) only one copy will be removed.

# Nemesis

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Nemesis

**Infobox:**
- Name: Nemesis
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/6/60/Nemesis-pretty.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20180915212824
- HP: 185; 200 (Ascension 8+)
- In Party With: None
- Debut Act: 3
- Powers: Intangible every 2nd turn

The **Nemesis** is an Elite encounter found in Act 3.

Nemesis is a large ghost-like enemy wearing a six-eyed goat skull similar to the Silent's, and wielding a scythe. Smoke billows from the skull's eye sockets. 
- The main trick of the Nemesis is their use of Intangible, a buff that reduces all damage dealt to it to 1. 

## Pattern
Has a 50% chance of using Debuff or attacking on the first turn.

Afterwards, has *approximately** a 35% chance of using Debuff, 35% chance of attacking and 30% chance of using Scythe.

It cannot use Debuff or Scythe twice in a row, nor can it use Attack three times in a row.

*The exact AI of Nemesis is a bit more complicated, but the numbers are still almost completely accurate.
| Name | Intent | Effect | Asc 3+ | Asc 18+ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Debuff |  | Shuffles 3 Burns into your discard pile. | Shuffles 3 Burns into your discard pile. | Shuffles 5 Burns into your discard pile. |
| Attack |  | Deals 6 x 3 damage. | Deals 7 x 3 damage. | Deals 7 x 3 damage. |
| Scythe |  | Deals 45 damage. | Deals 45 damage. | Deals 45 damage. |
## Tips
- The Nemesis is Intangible every other turn starting from the 2nd, giving the fight a clear tempo of attack and defend. The buff switches on/off right after Nemesis acts. All incoming damage (including Poison and Thorns) is reduced to 1 during the Intangible turn. Players should generally avoid attacking while Intangible is up, but applying Poison or using power cards is recommended.
- Nemesis' attacks do not increase in power through the fight, but without a source of Exhaust the player will eventually be overwhelmed with Burn cards, so they should take care not to let the fight last too long.
- The Boot bypasses Intangible's damage reduction, so all unblocked attack damage dealt will be increased to 5. This is not run-changing, but serves some use in this fight.
- Judgment also ignores Intangible and can finish off a severely damaged Nemesis.

## Trivia
- Its resemblance to the Silent may mean that it is the Silent's "Nemesis", likely related to the text in the Sensory Stone event.
- The Pagan imagery of both the Silent and Nemesis hint at ritualistic conflict. Wearing similar ornaments, the Nemesis is revered by the Silent's tribe in some way, possibly a fallen predecessor or mythical enemy.

# Neow

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Neow

*"Hello... Again..."*

**Neow** is an NPC in Slay the Spire. She is a large, whale-like creature with light blue skin and six bright yellow eyes. Neow lies at the foot of The Spire and welcomes the player to every run.

Neow blesses adventurers with rewards based on their previous success, offering gold, relics, or cards, unless they failed to reach the Boss of the Exordium, in which case she offers only two options instead of the usual four, and one of them is the aptly named relic Neow's Lament. It weakens the monsters in the first few encounters in the Spire to 1 HP, sometimes even giving the adventurer a free shot at an elite monster.

## Blessings
If you failed to reach the Boss of the Exordium in your last run, the Blessings you can have are:
- Max HP +8/6/7/7 (Ironclad/Silent/Defect/Watcher)
- Enemies in the next three combat will have one health.

If you reached the Boss of the Exordium, Neow will offer you four Blessings, and you can choose one of them. The first Blessing will be a card-related reward from the following list:

- Remove a card.
- Transform a card.
- Upgrade a card.
- Choose a card to obtain. (Choose one of 3 random cards from your Class)
- Choose an uncommon colorless card to obtain.
- Obtain a random rare card.
The second Blessing will be a reward that isn't directly related to your cards, chosen from the options below:

- Max HP +8/6/7/7 (Ironclad/Silent/Defect/Watcher)
- Enemies in the next three combat will have one health.
- Obtain a random common relic.
- Receive 100 gold.
- Obtain 3 random potions.

The third Blessing is a composite of one disadvantage and a better reward. It can be a combination of any disadvantages and rewards below, with exceptions noted:

- Disadvantages:
    - Lose max health
      - 8/7/7/7 (Ironclad/Silent/Defect/Watcher)
    - Take damage
      - Damage is equal to (Current HP / 10, rounded down) * 3
        - The amount of damage is not static. It is affected by Ascension 6 (lose 10% of HP at the start of the run) and Ascension 14 (reduced max HP).
    - Obtain a Curse
    - Lose all gold
- Rewards:
    - Remove 2 cards. (Does not pair with Obtain a Curse)
    - Transform 2 cards.
    - Gain 250 gold. (Does not pair with Lose all gold)
    - Choose a rare card to obtain.
    - Choose a rare colorless card to obtain.
    - Obtain a random rare relic.
    - Max HP +16/12/14/14 (Ironclad/Silent/Defect/Watcher) (Does not pair with losing max health)

The last Blessing offered will always be: 
- Replace your starter relic with a random Boss Relic.

## Trivia
- Little is known about Neow as she is not very talkative herself. However her actions suggest that she begrudges the Spire and wants to destroy it, and does so by sending resurrected adventurers up the Spire.
- Neow is depicted as possessing powerful magical abilities, which go as far as resurrecting the dead, which she shows whenever an adventurer dies atop the Spire, so they can continue their duty.
- The Cursed Tome event gives more insight on Neow's origins.
- The Sensory Stone event references the Defect's first interaction with Neow.
- After defeating the Corrupt Heart, an extra screen plays after the credits, depicting Neow saying "Has ... it ... been ... done?/The Spire sleeps ... and so shall I"
- Her name may be an onomatopoeia of a whale song.
