# Nilry's Codex

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Nilry%27s_Codex

**Infobox:**
- Name: Nilry's Codex
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/e/e2/NilrysCodex.png/revision/latest?cb=20190923234615
- Description: At the end of each turn, you can choose 1 of 3 random cards to shuffle into your draw pile.
- Flavor: Crafted by the infamous game master himself. Said to expand one's mind.
- Rarity: Event
- Class: Any

Nilry's Codex is one of the three potential rewards from Cursed Tome event.

At the end of your turn (before you discard), three random cards are displayed. You may select one of them to shuffle into your draw pile, or you can skip the selection if none of the choices are desirable.

Nilry's Codex can only generate a card that is available through shop and rewards, with some exceptions. It also cannot generate healing cards.

### Excluded Cards
**Attacks**
- Feed *(Healing)*
- Reaper *(Healing)*
- Lesson Learned *(Potential for the player to exploit its permanent Upgrade)*
- Bite *(Healing and event-exclusive)*
- Ritual Dagger *(Event-exclusive)*
- Shiv *(Cards effect only)*
- Smite *(Cards effect only)*
- Through Violence *(Card effect only)*

**Skills**
- Alchemize *(Healing, as it could generate Regen Potion, and its potion can trigger Toy Ornithopter.)*
- Wish *(Healing, as it can trigger Bloody Idol.)*
- Bandage Up *(Healing)*
- Apparition *(Event-exclusive)*
- J.A.X. *(Event-exclusive)*
- Beta *(Card effect only)*
- Insight *(Cards effect only)*
- Miracle *(Cards, relics, and potion effect only)*
- Safety *(Card effect only)*

**Powers**
- Self Repair *(Healing)*
- Omega *(Card effect only)*

## Interactions

- The cards are considered created during combat rather than added to the deck, so they will not be upgraded by Molten Egg, Frozen Egg, and Toxic Egg, but will be upgraded by Master Reality.

## Trivia
- This relic references Codex, a tabletop game made by David Sirlin. "Nilry's" is almost "Sirlin" spelled backwards.

# Normality

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Normality

**Infobox:**
- Name: Normality
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/a/a5/Normality.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20180120063427
- Class: Curse
- Type: Curse
- Rarity: Curse
- Cost: Unplayable
- Effect: Unplayable.; You cannot play more than 3 cards this turn.

CardAutobox

**Normality** is a Curse that limits the player to playing three cards in a single turn while it remains in their hand.

## Strategy
Normality's ability to limit a turn to three cards makes it a particularly deadly Curse. If the player has access to cards that can Discard or Exhaust other cards, such as Purity, Normality is a high-priority target.

Drawing Normality instantly puts it into effect; in other words, if the player has already played three or more cards and draws Normality, they will no longer be able to play cards for their turn.

A Merchant or a Rest Site with the Peace Pipe should be the player's first priority if they add Normality to their deck.

### Hazards
Copies of cards created by Echo Form and cards that are played twice due to cards such as Double Tap will count as played cards. This makes Normality difficult to play around if the player is relying on these types of cards. Using expensive or X-cost cards during a turn can limit the effect of Normality as fewer cards will be played overall.

Blue Candle will not be able to exhaust Normality after three cards have been played, as exhausting Normality this way counts as a play itself. If Normality is drawn and the player has Blue Candle, they should exhaust Normality before they play three cards.

Drawing Normality while having the Runic Pyramid is almost always fatal, especially during Elite and Boss fights. 

### Synergies
Normality synergizes well with Velvet Choker, as Velvet Choker reduces the total number of playable cards per turn to six, lessening Normality's effect. This synergy is *very* situational, however; consider looking for alternative synergies, as Normality is dangerous.

## Sources

- Cursed Key
- Choosing **[I Am Wealthy]** during the Mind Bloom event (2 Normalities)
- Transforming another Curse

# Offering

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Offering

**Infobox:**
- Name: Offering
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/4/47/Offering.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016210818
- Class: Ironclad
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Rare
- Cost: 0
- Effect: Lose 6 HP.; Gain .Draw 3 cards.Exhaust.
- [Offering+]
- Cost+: 0
- Effect+: Lose 6 HP.; Gain .Draw 5 cards.Exhaust.

Offering is a Skill card for the Ironclad. It grants 2 Energy and 3 card draws, in return for 6 HP. As a Rare card, it can be obtained after defeating a Boss.

Upgrading Offering increases the number of cards drawn from 3 to 5.

### Strategy
- Offering causes HP loss, not damage, and is not reduced by Block. The life loss downside is mitigated by the Ironclad's Burning Blood.

- The life-loss effect will trigger Runic Cube, adding an additional draw.
- Offering can also trigger Rupture for Strength gain.

- Offering is exceptionally strong in decks loaded with one- and zero-cost Attacks. In particular, Anger loads your deck with free Attacks, and Bite recovers the HP loss. Adding a Panache stacks up lots of bonus area-of-effect damage. 

- Combining Offering with Unceasing Top massively increases both of their strength. The Top provides extra cards to spend surplus Energy from Offering, prolonging the chain of free draws. With a few Angers shuffled into the deck, a few Seeing Red, and a few points of Strength, turns with hundreds of damage can be executed pretty reliably.

- Offering also provides the Energy needed to execute expensive combos like Impervious + 2 Entrenches + Body Slam.

- While the life loss is a relevant cost, the player should consider that enemies attack most turns. Unless the deck is extremely defensive, ending the combat a turn or two earlier could easily prevent six or more damage.

- Many enemies, particularly bosses, use weak attacks and Debuffs for a few turns before executing an overwhelmingly strong finishing move. Offering enables the player to beat the clock and slay the foe before it can perform the coup de grace.

The **Omamori** is a Common Relic that negates the next 2 Curses you obtain, preventing them from being added to your deck.

This relic negates *any* Curse, including but not limited to the Necronomicurse and Curse of the Bell. It is the only way to get the Necronomicon and Calling Bell relics without incurring their respective curses.

This relic does not spawn beyond floor 48, excluding Endless Mode.

## Interactions
- Positive
    - Cursed Key
    - Calling Bell
    - Necronomicon
    - Numerous Events
- Negative
    - Du-Vu Doll and Darkstone Periapt both benefit from getting Curses.
    - Fire Breathing benefits from drawing curses

## Tips
- Due to the way transforming works, it counts as removing a card, then adding a card. Thus, if an event such as Augmenter transforms 2 curses, they will both be removed (instead of transformed)
- During daily challenges, consider skipping this relic to try and get the Curses! score modifier.
- Picking up a Grotesque Trophy during **Endless Mode** will neutralize any charges that **Omamori** has, leaving the remainder as Prides added to your deck.

# Ominous Forge

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Ominous_Forge

**Ominous Forge** is an Event that can appear in Act 1, Act 2, and Act 3. You encounter a seemingly abandoned forge that still has a fire lit in its furnace.

## Options

- **[Forge]** Upgrade a card (Requires an upgradable card).
- **[Rummage]** Obtain Warped Tongs. Become Cursed - Pain.
- **[Leave]** Nothing happens.

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| *You duck into a small hut. Inside, you find what appears to be a forge. The smithing tools are covered with dust, yet a fire roars inside the furnace. You feel on edge...* |
| Forge |
| *You decide to put the forge to use and...* |
| CLANG CLAAANG CLANG! |
| *...improve your arsenal!* |
| Rummage |
| *You decide to see if you can find anything of use. After uncovering tarps, looking through boxes, and checking nooks and crannies, you find a dust covered relic!.* |
| ''Taking the relic, you can't shake a sudden feeling of sharp pain as you exit the hut. Maybe you disturbed some sort of spirit?* |
| Leave |
| *There doesn't seem to be anything of use. You exit the way you came, the flames of the furnace casting eerie shadows on the walls inside the hut..'' |

## Strategy
- **[Forge] **is generally the strongest option here, as it allows you to upgrade whichever card you choose. There is no downside to this option aside from not obtaining Warped Tongs.
- **[Rummage] **can also be a viable option if the player has Omamori or Tungsten Rod to negate the Pain curse, a relic such as Du-Vu Doll to benefit from the curse, or a shop shortly after the event to remove the curse. Warped Tongs are also helpful if the player has no cards with good upgrades upon encountering the event or if they are reliant on Searing Blow. In addition, Warped Tongs will work on cards added to your deck after the event, unlike the singular card upgrade. Rupture and Self-Forming Clay also have a great synergy with Pain.
- **[Leave] **does nothing and is worse than **[Forge] **in every way. If you have no upgradeable cards and no way to deal with Pain, however, choosing to leave is probably the best option.

# Omniscience

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Omniscience

**Infobox:**
- Name: Omniscience
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/a/a1/Omniscience.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20191216175546
- Class: Watcher
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Rare
- Cost: 4
- Effect: Choose a card in your draw pile. Play the chosen card twice and Exhaust it. Exhaust.
- [Omniscience+]
- Cost+: 3
- Effect+: Choose a card in your draw pile. Play the chosen card twice and Exhaust it. Exhaust.

CardAutobox

**Omniscience** plays a card you select from your Draw Pile two times and then exhausts it from your deck. The energy cost of the targeted card is disregarded.

X-cost cards will be played with the Energy you have available *after* playing Omniscience.

## Interactions
 
- Using Omniscience on another Omniscience will play the latter twice, allowing you to choose two more cards to then play twice, resulting in 4 cards played at once.
- Omniscience's exhaust mechanic is irrelevant for power cards, since power cards are removed from play after being used regardless.
- Since the Energy cost of the played card is disregarded, high-cost/high-yield cards such as Deva Form and Ragnarok are strong candidates for use.
- Playing Indignation twice will allow entering Wrath and then applying 3(5) Vulnerable to all enemies.
- Playing Inner Peace twice will allow entering Calm and then drawing 3(4) additional cards.
- Against Time Eater with Time Warp buff, playing Omniscience as the 12th card can bypass the card limit, Time Warp counter still progresses, but the forced end turn effect is ignored until all doubled cards are played, moreover, if playing Omniscience as the 12th into choosing other Omnisciences, then more cards could be played before forced to end turn.
- If during an Omniscience chain, an Omniscience is played as the 12th card, then it is equivalent to playing the Omniscience as the 12th card fresh from hand, ignoring any effects of previously played Omnisciences.

 
- Targeting a card that ends your turn will end your turn immediately, without playing a second copy.
- Activating a card whose conditions wouldn't work, such as Signature Move while you still have attack cards in your hand, will result in the card not activating.
- Any other restrictions on the number of cards you can play in a turn are not ignored by this. So playing an Omniscience as the third card, when a Normality is in hand will result in the card being exhausted without ever being played. The same is true for Velvet Choker.
- Against Time Eater with Time Warp buff, playing Omniscience as the 11th card cannot bypass the card limit unless another Omniscience is selected to be the 12th card play, that is, if the 11th card Omniscience selects Strike, only the first copy of Strike can be played.

# Orange Pellets

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Orange_Pellets

**Infobox:**
- Name: Orange Pellets
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/6/6d/OrangePellets.png/revision/latest?cb=20200203154213
- Description: Whenever you play a Power, Attack, and Skill in the same turn, remove all of your Debuffs.
- Flavor: "Made from various fungi found throughout the Spire, they will stave off any affliction."
- Rarity: Shop
- Class: Any

**Orange Pellets** is a relic that can only be found in the shop. It removes all your debuffs if you play a Power, Attack, and skill in the same turn.

## Notes
- Note that this relic can remove the debuffs inflicted on yourself via certain cards, such as Biased Cognition, Fasting, and Wraith Form; this can make such cards far more valuable.  Flex also works via a debuff and will provide strength for the rest of the combat if it can be removed that turn. The same goes for Speed and Flex potion. 
- Related to the above, the Confused debuff that is inflicted by the Snecko Eye relic *will* be removed. Any cards that were previously drawn will retain their current costs for the rest of combat. The bonus card draw effect will also remain active.
- Negative stat debuffs, such as negative Strength, Dexterity and Focus can be removed by this relic. However, it only removes *overall negative* stat levels. If other effects kept you at positive or neutral stats despite the debuffs (for instance, by playing Inflame after losing 1 Strength) Orange Pellets will not unwind the stat loss; it can only bring you back to neutral.
- If the last card played to activate this relic applies a debuff, that debuff will be removed. Debuffs from a subsequent play (such as those enabled by the Necronomicon), however, will remain.
- Triggering this relic will not remove the "Die next turn" effect from Blasphemy. 

## Trivia
- This relic, especially its artwork, is a reference to consumable items called pellets of various colors in Dark Souls 3.
    - Dark Souls 2 also has similar items, but they are called troches instead.

# Orb Slots

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Orb_Slots

**Orb slots** are a feature of The Defect, which limits how many Orbs you can have channeled at once. If you channel more Orbs than you have Orb slots, then the rightmost Orb will be Evoked to make room.

The Defect begins with three Orb slots and considers the rightmost Orb to be the **active Orb**, being the one that will get Evoked first. Other classes begins with 0 Orb slots. They will gain 1 Orb slot once they are able to obtain Defect cards from card reward, usually through Prismatic Shard or some game modifier.

Player can increase and decrease the number of Orb slots by playing cards, possessing some relics, or drinking Potion of Capacity. Losing a slot with an Orb equipped does not Evoke it. A character can have at most 10 Slots. If a character has 0 Slots, Orbs can no longer be Channeled. Orb slots do not carry over between combats.

## Related
### Cards
These cards modify the number of the player's Orb slots. Numbers in parentheses are for upgraded versions:
- Capacitor: Gain 2(3) Orb slots.
- Consume: Lose 1 Orb slot.
### Relics
These relics modify the number of the player's Orb slots, or interact with an empty Orb slot.
- Inserter: Gain 1 Orb slot every two turns.
- Runic Capacitor: Start each combat with 3 additional Orb slots.
- Frozen Core: Channel 1 Frost per turn if there is an empty Orb slot.
- Prismatic Shard: Start each combat with 1 Orb slot if you are not playing Defect if Base Mod is installed.

### Other
- Potion of Capacity: Gain 2 (4) Orb slots.
Category:Game Mechanics

**Orb Walker** is an Act 3 Monster. It can be found alone as a normal enemy, or it can be found in the Sphere event paired with an additional Orb Walker.

## Pattern
Has a 60% chance of using Laser and a 40% chance of using Claw every turn. Neither move can be used three times in a row.

| Name | Intent | Effect | Asc 2+ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Laser |  | Deals 10 damage. Shuffles 1 Burn into the draw pile and adds another into the discard pile. | Deals 11 damage. Shuffles 1 Burn into the draw pile and adds another into the discard pile. |
| Claw |  | Deals 15 damage. | Deals 16 damage. |

## Tips
The best strategy to defeat the solo Orb Walker is to be very aggressive. Consider blocking if your attacks in hand are subpar. Because of its buff, the Orb Walker can snowball very quickly. As with most heavy-hitters, Weak can be a very powerful asset to buy you more time. The Weak Potion is also effective as the three Weak will lessen damage every single turn, and the Orb Walker always attacks.

In its Event encounter, focusing on one and then the next is typically the best strategy. Area of Effect damage or cards such as Corpse Explosion are also immensely helpful.

## Trivia
- Though this monster bears resemblance to a Sentry and seems to be man-made, it doesn't have the Artifact Buff.
- The Orb Walker's resemblance to the Repulsor seems to have no clear connection, apart from that they are both robotic monsters.
- Two Orb Walkers used to be an Act 3 Elite encounter until it was replaced by the Reptomancer.

# Orbs

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Orbs

**Orbs** is a mechanic used by The Defect, one of the playable characters. The Defect begins with 3 Orb Slots that can store elemental spheres. Each sphere's passive effect is triggered every turn, and the spheres can be Evoked for an active burst.
Category:Game Mechanics
## Orb Slots
*Main Article: Orb Slots*

The Defect begins with three Orb slots and considers the right most Orb to be the **active Orb**. Other classes begin with 0 Orb slots. They will gain 1 Orb slot after obtaining Prismatic Shard or some game modifier — obtaining Defect cards without one of these will cause Channelling orbs to fail.

Player can increase and decrease the number of Orb Slots by playing cards, possessing some relics, or drinking Potion of Capacity. Losing a slot with an Orb equipped does not Evoke it. A character can have at most 10 Slots. If a character has 0 Slots, Orbs can no longer be Channeled. Orb Slots do not carry over between combats.

## Orb Interaction
### Channel
*Main Article: Channel*

**Channeling** an Orb inserts it into the rightmost empty slot. If every slot is full, each Orb will be shifted one slot to the right, popping the active Orb out of its slot and **Evoking** it.

At the end of The Defect's turn, it uses the passive effect of **channeled** orbs, right to left. The effect of these orbs can be increased by gaining the Focus buff.

### Evoke
*Main Article: Evoke*

**Evoking** an Orb shatters it and unleashes a high-powered effect. Unlike passive effects, Evoking an Orb activates instantly. Orbs can be Evoked by **channeling** too many Orbs or cards that specify Evoking them. After Evoking an Orb, each Orb to its left shifts to fill its slot.

### Focus
*Main Article: Focus*

**Focus** is a stat unique to The Defect that affects Orbs the same way Strength affects Attacks and Dexterity affects Block. Increasing Focus increases the magnitude of both the passive and Evoke effects of each Orb (except for Plasma Orbs). It is possible to reduce Orb effects to 0 by decreasing Focus.

## Orb Types
There are currently four types of Orbs — **Lightning**, **Frost**, **Dark**, and **Plasma**.
### Lightning

**Passive: **Deal 3 (+ Focus) Damage to a random enemy.

**Evoke:** Deal 8 (+ Focus) Damage to a random enemy.

#### Cards
- Zap - Channel 1 Lightning.
- Ball Lightning - Channel 1 Lightning.
- Chaos - Possible to Channel 1 (or 2) Lightning.
- Static Discharge  - Channel 1 (2) Lightning whenever you receive unblocked attack damage.
- Storm - Channel 1 Lightning whenever you play a Power card.
- Tempest - Channel X (X+1) Lightning.
- Electrodynamics - Channel 2 (3) Lightning.
- Rainbow  - Channel 1 Lightning, then  1 Frost, then 1 Dark.

#### Relic
- Cracked Core - Channel 1 Lightning at the start of each combat.

#### Strategy

- Lightning Orbs are straightforward damage-dealers that chip away at enemies' Health each turn and Evoke a big damage burst. Lightning Orbs' passives activate at the end of the player's turn, before the enemy's Block has worn off. This means it can't bypass Block, but it can push through some sneaky finishing damage if sufficiently worn down beforehand.

- The random nature of these Orbs spreads the pain around, so reducing enemy numbers with Attack cards to focus the Lightning damage onto the most dangerous enemy is an ideal strategy. Alternatively, Electrodynamics will apply Lightning damage to all foes, allowing you to take on groups of foes effectively. 

- When building a Lightning deck, plan whether the Orbs' passive or their Evoke will deal the bulk of your damage. Increase your Focus and add more Orb slots to maximize the passive damage, or reduce Orb slots and add more Channel effects to Evoke more often. Trying to do both can make the deck inconsistent and unable to handle high-health enemies.

- The damage dealt by Lightning is not affected by any effects except Focus, Intangible, and Lock-On. It's not reduced by Weak, isn't increased by Vulnerable, ignores Strength and Thorns, and doesn't count as Attack damage for effects like Angry.

### Frost

**Passive: **Gain 2 (+ Focus) Block.

**Evoke:** Gain 5 (+ Focus) Block.

#### Cards
- Cold Snap - Channel 1 Frost.
- Coolheaded - Channel 1 Frost.
- Chaos - Possible to Channel 1 (or 2) Frost.
- Chill - Channel 1 Frost for each enemy in combat.
- Glacier - Channel 2 Frost.
- Rainbow - Channel 1 Lightning, then  1 Frost, then 1 Dark.

#### Relic
- Frozen Core - Channel 1 Frost if you end your turn with empty Orb slots.

#### Strategy

- Frost Orbs are defensive tools that provide a small but relevant defense boost each turn and Evoke to counter stronger blows. Frost Orbs' passives activate at the end of the player's turn, but after effects like Orichalcum have triggered.

- At the beginning of combat, Frost Orbs are the weakest of the bunch, the Block too minor to counter even feeble attacks. However, once The Defect has Channeled a few copies and boosted Focus, they form a line of defense that few enemies can penetrate, and regenerate it turn after turn.

- When building a Frost deck, the challenge is surviving the early game until your Frost Orbs can fully defend you. One option is to bolster them with Skills that grant Block, accepting that those Skills will become useless once your Frost defenses are prepared. Another option is to simply tank the early-game damage and recover with Self Repair. 

- The Block granted by Frost isn't affected by Dexterity or Frail, which makes it particularly strong against enemies that use such effects to proactively reduce Block. The repeatable card-free Block is also relevant against Gremlin Nob and Chosen.

### Dark

**Passive: **Add 6 (+ Focus) Damage (= Y) to this Orb's Evoke.

**Evoke:** Deal Y Damage to the enemy with the lowest Health.

Y starts at 6 when the Orb is first Channeled.

#### Cards
- Darkness - Channel 1 Dark.
- Doom and Gloom - Channel 1 Dark.
- Chaos - Possible to Channel 1 (or 2) Dark.
- Rainbow - Channel 1 Lightning, then  1 Frost, then 1 Dark.

#### Relic
- Symbiotic Virus - Channel 1 Dark at the start of each combat.

#### Potion
- Essence of Darkness - Channel 1 (2)Dark for each Orb slot.

#### Strategy

- Dark Orbs are beatsticks that trade Lightning's reliable damage for a bigger Evoke effect. The Dark Orb's passive has no effect on combat at all, and only serves to stockpile damage into the Evoke ability. Dark Orbs' passives activate at the end of the player's turn.

- Dark Orbs are the most challenging Orb to build around. The Defect must Channel the Orb early, survive while it charges, and Evoke it at the appropriate time. The Dark Orb gains less from Focus than other Orbs — it's generally smarter to simply charge it for a few more turns. However, the payoff is massive damage that's more predictable than that of a Lightning Orb.

- The key to mastering the Dark Orb is ensuring it can be Evoked at the right time, onto the right enemy. Dark Orb decks demand a high number of Evoke cards, and benefit the most from multi-Evoke cards like Multi-Cast that can multiply the hard-won damage. If Evoked with Recursion, the Channeled Dark Orb will retain the stockpiled damage. Use reliable Attacks like Melter to groom enemies' HP so the Evoked damage can land on a key target. Try to Evoke Cracked Core's Lightning Orb as soon as possible, so the Dark Orb is ready for action. 

- A key decision in Dark deck construction is how many Orb slots to maintain. Increasing the count allows the player to charge more Dark Orbs at once, but reducing it makes it easier for Channel effects to Evoke them. In either case, minimize the number of Channel effects in the deck to avoid prematurely Evoking Orbs.

- Like Lightning Orbs, Dark Orbs' damage is affected only by Focus, Intangible, and Lock-On.

### Plasma

**Passive:** Gain 1 Energy.

**Evoke:** Gain 2 Energy.

#### Cards
- Chaos - Possible to Channel 1 (or 2) Plasma.
- Fusion - Channel 1 Plasma.
- Meteor Strike - Channel 3 Plasma.

#### Relic
- Nuclear Battery - Channel 1 Plasma at the start of each combat.

#### Strategy

- Plasma Orbs grant Energy. This simple effect powers greedy decks loaded with impractically-costed, absurdly powerful cards and fuels long chains of huge plays. Unlike other Orbs, Plasma Orbs are unaffected by Focus, and their passive effects trigger at the beginning of The Defect's turn.

- A single Plasma Orb is a significant boon to The Defect, like a Velvet Choker with no downside. The key is making the most of the extra Energy without Evoking the Orb and losing the passive. Alternately, the Orb can be Evoked at the right time to access the 2 Energy and fuel a huge turn.

- When The Defect can Channel multiple Plasma Orbs, the challenge is simply spending all the Energy. This is the time to jam all the Meteor Strikes, Sunders, Echo Forms, and other flashy bombs that are too pricey for more sensible decks. There's nothing more satisfying than sinking a dozen Energy into a massive Tempest or Multi-Cast. 

- Creative AI, Hello World, and other repeatable card-draw and card-generation effects are great ways to dump excess Energy, and Unceasing Top can become hilariously overpowered. Draw effects in general are quite good with Plasma Orbs, especially if the deck is likely to Evoke them.

## Trivia
As seen in the Fusion card art, **Plasma Orb** seems to be created from the fusion of the three other orbs.

# Orichalcum

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Orichalcum

**Infobox:**

- Description: If you end your turn without Block, gain 6 Block.
- Flavor: A green tinted metal of an unknown origin. Seemingly indestructible.
- Rarity: Common
- Class: Any

**Orichalcum** is a common relic that gives you  6 Block at the end of your turn, but only if you end it without Block. It is a good defense relic, though you always need to take it into account when defending.

## Interactions
 
- Orichalcum will function with Metallicize, Thread and Needle, Plated Armor, or the Defect's Frost orbs, as those only grant block at the end of your turn.
- Orichalcum will always trigger before Cloak Clasp, regardless of the order in which the player obtains them.

 
- Orichalcum works very poorly with After Image, since playing any card will disable Orichalcum.

## Trivia
- Orichalcum is a metal mentioned in several ancient writings, including the story of Atlantis in the *Critias* of Plato. It was, most likely, an alloy of copper/gold and zinc/tin (granting its green color) and due to the fact that tin was rare at the time, thus justifying its mythical origin/existence.

An enemy Buff that adds a Wound to your deck every time you take unblocked attack damage. It is possessed innately by the Book of Stabbing, and gained by the Corrupt Heart after its third use of its Buff ability.

## Tips
This power can be dangerous, since both enemies that have it are capable of doing several attacks per turn and potentially giving you several Wounds at a time. However, you can exploit the fact that the enemy's damage is split across several attacks by reducing the enemy's strength with cards like Piercing Wail or Dark Shackles. You can also deal damage back to the attacker with Thorns or Flame Barrier.

If you're playing as the Ironclad, you can even take advantage of the Wounds that you get. Evolve negates the draws you waste by drawing Wounds, Evolve+ gives you even more draws for each Wound you draw, and one or more Fire Breathing cards will deal damage back to the attacker every time a Wound is drawn. If you're not playing as the Ironclad or if you don't have these cards, you can get rid of the Wounds by using cards to Exhaust them, or by using the Medical Kit relic.

# Panic Button

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Panic_Button

**Infobox:**
- Name: Panic Button
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/0/08/PanicButton.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016212657
- Class: Neutral
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Cost: 0
- Effect: Gain 30 Block. You cannot gain Block from cards for 2 turns.; Exhaust.
- [Panic Button+]
- Cost+: 0
- Effect+: Gain 40 Block. You cannot gain Block from cards for 2 turns.; Exhaust.
- Name: No Block
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/6/67/Icon_NoGuard.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202163537
- Description: You may not gain Block from cards for the next X turns.
- Type: Debuff
- Stacking; Behavior: Duration

CardAutobox

This gives you the No Block debuff, which sets the "Block gained" value of all cards to 0 for the duration. The cards can still be played.

The turn in which you play Panic Button counts as the first turn for its debuff. So, in reality, this card only prevents block gained for the rest of this turn, and the turn after.

## Interactions

- Only stops direct block from card effects, not from Frost and Relics.
- Does not prevent Block from Entrench (dissimilar to analogous Catalyst interactions).
- Does not prevent Block from buffs, such as Rage, Metallicize, Feel No Pain, After Image.
- Does not affect Block from Wallop and Talk to the Hand (enemy debuff).
- Affects the Block buff from Dodge and Rolls played *after* Panic Button, but not before.

## Bugs
- If the Dexterity buff is *after* the No Block debuff on the status list, then Dexterity is applied *after* the block gets zero'd out. (Last checked: v2.1.)

- Description: Your next Attack deals double damage.
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: None

Every 10th Attack you play deals double damage.

Pen Nib gains 1 charge every time an Attack card is played. The charges carry over between fights.

At 9 charges, Pen Nib will grant double damage on the next attack, and then reset to 0.

Pen Nib calculates all damage modifiers (Strength, Vulnerable, Weak) before the double damage, and is correctly shown in the tooltip before confirming your Attack.

The bonus applies to the entire attack card (so multi-hit cards will get it on every attack.)

However, note that

Double Tap
produces a duplicate card, so in that case the bonus will only apply to one of them. On the other hand, a double-tapped card counts as two plays for the purpose of charging the nib.

Pen Nib is a Common Relic.

# Perfected Strike

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Perfected_Strike

**Infobox:**
- Name: Perfected Strike
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/7/77/PerfectedStrike.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016210818
- Class: Ironclad
- Type: Attack
- Rarity: Common
- Cost: 2
- Effect: Deal 6 damage.; Deals 2 additional damage for ALL your cards containing "Strike".
- [Perfected Strike+]
- Cost+: 2
- Effect+: Deal 6 damage.; Deals 3 additional damage for ALL your cards containing "Strike".

**Perfected Strike** is an Attack card for the Ironclad. It deals 6 damage plus 2 for every card with "Strike" in its name in the player's draw pile, discard pile, and hand. As a Common card, it can be found as a reward after combats.

Upgrading Perfected Strike increases the damage bonus for each "Strike" from 2 to 3.

The bonus damage is added to the base damage of the card, and all the damage is dealt in one shot, meaning strength bonuses are applied only once and not multiple times. In combat, the first line of the card's text is updated to reflect the additional damage.

Each copy of Perfected Strike counts itself as a "Strike".

The eligible cards are:
- **Perfected Strike**
- Pommel Strike
- Strike
- Twin Strike
- Wild Strike
- Swift Strike

In game modes where you have access to cards of every color, it additionally counts:
- The Defect's Strike
- The Silent's Strike
- The Watcher's Strike
- Sneaky Strike
- Thunder Strike
- Meteor Strike
- Windmill Strike

### Strategy
- Perfected Strike is one of the most powerful Attacks in early Ironclad decks. Simply dropping one into the starting deck deals 18 damage without an upgrade, and it only increases from there.

- Picking Perfected Strikes early is a reliable strategy. Not only are they strong on their own, but their power grows over time as more Perfected Strikes and other "Strike" cards are obtained.

- As a Common, the card is often sold by the Merchant at a low price, so players looking to build a Strike deck should pick routes that include his carpet.

- When packing Perfected Strikes, avoid the Vampires(?) Event and Pandora's Box Relic, since this will remove your starting Strikes and reduce the card's power.

- Changing the total number of "Strike" cards in your deck, discard pile, and hand during combat affects Perfected Strike's additional damage. This means that its power decreases when "Strikes" are Exhausted or put in Stasis by Bronze Orbs, and increases when "Strikes" are created by Dual Wield.
- Strike Dummy pairs well with Perfected Strike, as it boosts the damage of Perfected Strike and all the other Strike cards used to boost Perfected Strike.

# Piercing Wail

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Piercing_Wail

**Infobox:**
- Name: Piercing Wail
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/0/0a/PiercingWail.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016211925
- Class: Silent
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Common
- Cost: 1
- Effect: ALL enemies lose 6 Strength this turn.; Exhaust.
- [Piercing Wail+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: ALL enemies lose 8 Strength this turn.; Exhaust.

**Piercing Wail** is a common Skill for The Silent.  It causes all enemies to lose 6 Strength for one turn, but this card Exhausts.  Upon Upgrade it causes all enemies to lose 8 Strength instead.

Because this card lessens the attack damage of each hit, it is especially useful against enemies such as Book of Stabbing that tend to hit multiple times per turn.

## Strategy
Piercing Wail works by applying a debuff, Shackled, which reapplies lost Strength at the end of the enemy turn. If you use Piercing Wail on the turn that an enemy clears their debuffs, you can use it to permanently remove 6-8 points of Strength, to a minimum of +0. This is relevant against The Champ, Awakened One, and Time Eater, all of whom raise their Strength over the course of the fight.

The opposite is true in the Corrupt Heart fight. If you use this card on a turn where the Heart buffs, it will permanently give the heart strength.

# Poison

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Poison

**Infobox:**
- Name: Poison
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/0/05/Poison.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202023747
- Description: At the beginning of its turn, the target loses X HP and 1 stack of poison.
- Type: Debuff
- Stacking; Behavior: Intensity and Duration

Poison is a negative status effect (Debuff) that the Silent can apply to enemies.

At the beginning of a Poisoned enemy's turn, they lose HP equal to the # of Poison stacks they have. Then the Poison stack decreases by 1.

This damage will go through an enemy's Block.

The total possible damage that poison can deal over time can be calculated using the following formula: x*(x+1)/2, where x is the amount of current poison stacks. However, since fights generally do not last long enough for all the poison to expire, much of the calculated damage will never be realized before the fight ends.

Other characters can access Poison cards through the A Note For Yourself event, Prismatic Shard, or Foreign Influence (Watcher).

## Effects that add Poison
Cards:
- Deadly Poison: 5(7)
- Poisoned Stab: 3(4)
- Bouncing Flask: 3 x 3(4)
- Crippling Cloud: 4(7)
- Corpse Explosion: 6(9)
- Noxious Fumes: 2(3) per turn
- EnvenomAddPoison: 1 per unblocked attack
- Catalyst: +1x(+2x) existing Poison.

Potions:
- Poison Potion: 6

Relics:
- Twisted Funnel: 4 at start of combat.
- Snecko Skull: +1 whenever Poison is applied.
- The Specimen: Equal to dead enemy's Poison.

## Effects that take advantage of Poison
- UsePoisonBane: Attacks a second time if the enemy is Poisoned.
- Catalyst
- Snecko Skull
- The Specimen

## Other Interactions
- Sadistic Nature: Deals 5(7) damage every time Poison is applied.
- Poison is able to do more damage than the Corrupt Heart's invincible buff would normally allow

Category:Silent
Category:Debuffs

# Potions

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Potions

Potions are one-time-use items that can only be used in combat with the exception of Fruit Juice, Entropic Brew, and Blood Potion, which can be used in most scenarios. The player can typically hold up to 3 of them, or 2 on ascension levels 11 and higher. Potion Belt increases the number of potions you can hold by 2, which mean you can hold up to 5 potions with it, or 4 on ascension levels 11 and higher.

Using a potion does not require Energy and does not count as playing a card.

When a potion is offered to you, the rarity chances are:
- 65% for a Common potion.
- 25% for an Uncommon potion.
- 10% for a Rare potion.

## Obtaining Potions
 
- Potions are occasionally dropped as a reward after combat. The default chance of a potion dropping is 40% and resets at the start of each Act. If a potion drops, the chance decreases by 10%. If a potion doesn't drop, the chance increases by 10%. 
    - With White Beast Statue, a potion will always drop after combat.
- Potions can be bought at the  Merchant's Shop.
- If you reached the boss of the first Act, Neow may offer you 3 potions.
- Some Events offer potions.
    - Lab offers you 3 random potions.
    - The Woman in Blue allows you to buy 1 random potion for 20 gold, 2 for 30 gold, and 3 for 40 gold.
    - Knowing Skull grants you a random potion at the cost of 10% of your HP, with 6 at minimum.
- Using the card Alchemize creates 1 random potion (other than Fruit Juice).
- Obtaining Cauldron offers you 5 random potions.
- Obtaining Tiny House offers you 1 random potion.
- Entropic Brew fills all your empty potion slots, including its slot, with random potions (cannot generate Fruit Juice while in combat).

 
- Obtaining Sozu prohibits you from obtaining any more potions, including potions obtained from Entropic Brew. However, you are still able to use potions you already have on you.

## Other Interactions
- We Meet Again! offers you a choice to give Ranwid 1 random potion you have in exchange for a Relic.
- Toy Ornithopter heals 5 HP whenever you use a potion.
- Sacred Bark doubles the effectiveness of potions except:
    - Ambrosia
    - Blessing of the Forge

# Pray

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Pray

**Infobox:**
- Name: Pray
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/a/a2/Pray.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20191002191006
- Class: Watcher
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Cost: 1
- Effect: Gain 3 Mantra. Shuffle an Insight into your draw pile.
- [Pray+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: Gain 4 Mantra. Shuffle an Insight into your draw pile.

CardAutobox

Pray is, unfortunately, rarely worth taking. The issue with Pray is that it does literally nothing on the turn you cast it, unless you're entering Divinity. Additionally, because you had to draw Pray, then draw the Insight, just to draw 2 cards, the end result is that you didn't draw any cards. This makes Pray one of the worst cards in the game for a normal deck, unless you're incredibly committed to achieving Divinity. However, if you can assemble a small enough deck (less than 9 cards) that can somehow generate a lot of energy, a Pray+ can essentially re-draw itself and an Insight over and over.

Ultimately, one of the best ways to consider Divinity cards is to consider how many cycles through your deck it takes to achieve Divinity. For example, a card that gives 3 mantra takes 4 deck cycles to reach Divinity, while a card that gives 4 mantra would take 3 deck cycles. Thus, you should ultimately achieve to have your mantra cards give a total of either 5 or 10 mantra each deck cycle. Devotion and Damaru can also help with this. As an example of a great Divinity deck, a deck with an upgraded Pray, a Worship, and a Damaru can easily achieve 10 Mantra in just 2-3 turns.

Watcher Card Navbox

- Flavor: The wheel continues to spin, never stopping.
- Rarity: Rare
- Class: Any

**Prayer Wheel** is a Rare Relic. Its effect causes all normal fights to drop two card rewards instead of one.

After ending a normal non-elite/boss fight, it will give two separate card rewards. Both can be activated, effectively doubling the cards the player receives from normal combat. This choice functions just like a normal choice after combat, and functions as expected with Question Card and Singing Bowl.

This relic does not spawn beyond floor 48, excluding Endless mode.

## Old Prayer Wheel
Before Patch 25, Prayer Wheel was a common relic that made non-boss chests contain a card reward.

**Predator** is an Uncommon Attack for The Silent.  It deals a decent amount of damage for 2 Energy and draws 2 cards on the next turn.

## Strategy
- Predator is good for Cycle/Draw decks as it increases your options on the turn following it.
    - That said, 15 damage for 2 energy is only slightly better than 2 strikes.
- Predator is an ok pick for early-game damage if your deck needs it.  Against Gremlin Nob and Lagavulin having strong early front-loaded damage is key to winning the fight without taking too much damage.

# Prepared

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Prepared

**Infobox:**
- Name: Prepared
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/8/83/Prepared.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016211925
- Class: Silent
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Common
- Cost: 0
- Effect: Draw 1 card.; Discard 1 card.
- [Prepared+]
- Cost+: 0
- Effect+: Draw 2 cards.; Discard 2 cards.

**Prepared** is a Skill for the Silent. When played, you draw 1 card, then discard 1 card of your choice. 

When Upgraded, you draw 2 cards and discard 2 cards instead of 1.

## Strategy

- Prepared is a low-risk pick. Even though it is a net disadvantage in terms of card quantity, this is only a problem if you are sure you can play every card in your hand most of the time. However, be wary of taking too many copies of Prepared, as multiple uses in a single turn will unnecessarily discard more than is likely necessary.

- Upgrade to Prepared+ as soon as possible. The additional draw lets you see more cards and assemble stronger plays, and the additional discard enables cards like Eviscerate and Tactician more effectively.

## Synergies
Prepared is a key component of any discard deck - it draws you closer to the relevant cards, enables them, and lets you discard cards at will, all while leaving your entire Energy reserve available.

Prepared is especially strong with Tactician, Reflex, Sneaky Strike, and Eviscerate, efficiently drawing and enabling them in one move.

## Trivia
The card art shows the same bag from Bag of Preparation.

# Pride

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Pride

**Infobox:**
- Name: Pride
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/b/b3/Pride.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181020132843
- Class: Curse
- Type: Curse
- Rarity: Curse
- Cost: 1
- Effect: Innate.; At the end of your turn, put a copy of this card on top of your draw pile.Exhaust.

CardAutobox
**Pride** is a Curse which has three effects:
- Innate: It always starts in your first hand of the combat.
- On play (1 Energy): Exhaust it.
- At end of turn, if it's still in your hand: Add another copy of it to the top of your Draw Pile.
Therefore, if you choose to spend 1 energy to Exhaust Pride, it will be removed. If you choose not to Exhaust it, it will create another copy.

## Obtaining
Internally, Pride has "Special" rarity, meaning it cannot be obtained the same way other Curses are obtained.

Pride can only be obtained from the Grotesque Trophy Blight, which is only available when playing an Endless run in Custom Mode.

## Updating History
- Weekly Patch 31: Custom Mode
    - Pride curse will no longer appear from Calling Bell and a few other sources.

# Prismatic Shard

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Prismatic_Shard

**Infobox:**
- Name: Prismatic Shard
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/c/c9/PrismaticShard.png/revision/latest?cb=20200203154300
- Description: Combat reward screens now contain colorless cards and cards from other colors.
- Flavor: Looking through the shard, you are able to see entirely new perspectives.
- Rarity: Shop
- Class: Any

Prismatic shard is a relic you can obtain only from a shop, which lets combat reward screens contain colorless cards and cards from other characters (cards from the original color can still be obtained).

If you are playing a character that is not the Defect and do not have any game modifier that allow an access to Defect cards, your character will obtain one Orb slot upon picking up Prismatic Shard.

Despite the description claiming that this relic affects (only) combat card rewards, it actually affects ALL card rewards that do not specify its color. Dream Catcher, Orrery, and Tiny House are all affected by Prismatic Shard. However, Sensory Stone event is not affected, since the event specifies the card rewards to be colorless. The Library event is also not affected, since the 20-card selection is not considered a card reward.

This relic only affects card rewards and does not affect mid-fight card generation (such as Dead Branch, Discovery, Attack Potion, etc.).

If using the Diverse game modifier, this relic will not spawn because the game modifier provides the same effect.

## Trivia
- The artwork for this relic is based on a dispersive prism, which breaks up light into the colors of the rainbow, hence this relic giving you cards of different colors. 
    - Its name is also most likely a reference to an item of the same name in Stardew Valley.

CardAutobox

Purity typically isn't a very good card, as it requires you to exhaust cards that you've already drawn. By removing 3 cards with a Purity, you've effectively lost 4 drawn cards just to make your deck smaller. That said, it has fantastic synergy with Runic Pyramid, as it allows you to exhaust useless attacks/defends that were clogging up your hand. It can also be good if your deck is almost able to go infinite, or if your deck is full of card draw.

# Question Card

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Question_Card

**Infobox:**
- Name: Question Card
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/6/6e/QuestionCard.png/revision/latest?cb=20190923235204
- Description: On future Card Reward screens you have 1 additional card to choose from.
- Flavor: "Those with more choices minimize the downside to chaos." - Kublai the Great
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Class: Any

This relic does not trigger when it gets picked up and then entering the card reward screen.

Only card rewards that can permanently add a card to the deck are affected by Question Card, card select screens of Foreign Influence, Discovery, Toolbox, Nilry's Codex, Attack Potion, Skill Potion, and Power Potion always consists of 3 cards. (these are also not affected by Busted Crown)

This relic does not spawn beyond floor 48, excluding Endless mode.

## Interactions
- Positive
    - Prayer Wheel, Dream Catcher, Tiny House, and Orrery let you see more card rewards.
    - Molten Egg, Toxic Egg, and Frozen Egg make more cards appear upgraded.
    - N'loth's Gift makes more rare cards appear.
    - Busted Crown's downside is partially mitigated, by making future card rewards 2 cards instead of 1.
- Negative
    - Singing Bowl adds a separate option to card rewards that can not be used at the same time as Question Card.
    - Vintage drastically reduces the amount of card rewards.

## Trivia

- This relic is likely a reference to the item "There's Options" from *The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth*, which has a similar appearance and function.

Rainbow is unique in the fact that the upgrade may not be beneficial in specific decks. Having it Exhaust can get it out of the way, but having it not Exhaust can allow for more Orbs to be played and the ability to Evoke 3 Orbs over the course of a battle.

**Rampage** is an Attack card for the Ironclad. It deals 8 damage, then 5 more for every time Rampage is played in a combat. As an Uncommon card, it appears as a reward for combat, although less often than Commons.

Upon upgrade, the amount its damage increases by per-play is increased to 8.

Notes:
- In early phase of the run, a deck is likely to be quite small, so Rampage can be a good source of damage.
- Rampage requires a Long-term duration ability, so Rampage deck easily transits to Block-based deck, such as Body Slam or Barricade deck.

## Interactions
- Duplication Potion and Double Tap: Rampage's damage will be scaled twice, and the second card play will have the increased damage from the first card play.
- Dual Wield: Rampage's scaled damage will be copied, but both copies will scale separately.

# Reaper

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Reaper

**Infobox:**
- Name: Reaper
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/6/6a/Reaper.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016210951
- Class: Ironclad
- Type: Attack
- Rarity: Rare
- Cost: 2
- Effect: Deal 4 damage to ALL enemies. Heal HP equal to unblocked damage.; Exhaust.
- [Reaper+]
- Cost+: 2
- Effect+: Deal 5 damage to ALL enemies. Heal HP equal to unblocked damage.; Exhaust.

**Reaper** is a Rare Attack card for the Ironclad. It deals 4 damage to all enemies, then heals the player for the combined HP lost by the enemies. Upgrading Reaper increases the damage dealt per enemy from 4 to 5.

## Interactions

- Because the health restored is based on the damage dealt, anything that increases damage, including Vulnerable, Strength buffs, Relics, Stances, and upgrading Reaper will increase the amount of health restored. 
    - Similarly, effects that reduce damage, such as Weak or enemy Buffs, will reduce the health restored.
- Reaper restores health equal to the HP the enemy loses. For instance, dealing 4 damage to an enemy with 1 HP will only restore one point of health, and blocked damage is not healed.
- The heal from Reaper applies *after* taking damage from Thorns and Sharp Hide, and cannot be used to avoid death by these effects.
- As a healing card, Reaper cannot be created by Infernal Blade or Metamorphosis.
- Due to its long animation requiring the red orbs needing to touch the character, using Reaper as a finishing blow against certain enemies that have fast death animations and/or are in spots farther away from the character can sometimes cause the reward screen to show up and the battle to end before the healing is able to work.

## Strategy
- Reaper is a clunky card - not only is it situational, but it's expensive at 2 Energy. When playing a deck with Reaper, take care not to get too greedy. It's easy to make poor plays in the hope that Reaper will restore more health in the future. At the same time, however, Reaper can also be one of the most powerful cards in the entire game. With enough Strength gain, Reaper can gain an incredible amount of health each fight.

- In fights with one or two enemies, it's usually advisable to play Reaper as soon as possible to avoid drawing it in the future. With more enemies, you can hold out longer, but be careful - wait too long, and you may need to kill the enemy you had hoped to drain.

- In general, you should play Reaper as soon as enemies give you an opening unless you'll lose more HP that turn by using it than by blocking, or you have a reliable way of gaining large amounts of Strength, such as Demon Form or an upgraded Limit Break.

- Reaper is generally not worth spending a Smith action to upgrade - it only increases the damage by 1, which usually translates to at most 3-5 extra damage/health.

## Synergies
- Reaper performs well with cards that inflict Vulnerable, which sharply increases the amount of health restored.

- Reaper's best friends are Strength buffs. Not only does Strength increase the amount of Health restored, but you don't need to worry about timing it like you would with Vulnerable.

- Reaper is an excellent utility for self-damaging decks, especially ones with Rupture. It gives you more health in mid-battle, allowing the usually short-lived deck to effectively fight longer battles against bosses.

- Consider combining it with Dual Wield or Double Tap to maximize its potential.

- Strange Spoon can be a double-edged sword - more plays means more HP, but the card's utility generally decreases with the number of enemies and less empty health to heal.

# Rebound

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Rebound

**Infobox:**
- Name: Rebound
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/d/d0/Rebound.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016203604
- Class: Defect
- Type: Attack
- Rarity: Common
- Cost: 1
- Effect: Deal 9 damage.; Put the next card you play this turn on top of your draw pile.
- [Rebound+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: Deal 12 damage.; Put the next card you play this turn on top of your draw pile.
- Name: Rebound
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/9/95/Icon_Rebound.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202163652
- Description: The next X cards you play this turn are placed on top of your draw pile.
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: Counter

CardAutobox

Rebound is an Attack card for The Defect that combines good damage with a unique deck-manipulating effect. As a common card, Rebound is often offered as a post-battle reward and can be purchased inexpensively from The Merchant.

Upgrading Rebound increases its damage from 9 to 12.

### Strategy
- It's easy to accidentally draw the Rebounded card with zero energy left, or to Rebound the wrong card. Carefully sequence the turn, anticipating next turn's draws and enemy Intents, to squeeze the most power out of Rebound's unique effect.

- Take special care to consider your enemies' attack sequences. You don't want to draw a fifth attack card when you really need to Block, or a defensive card if the enemy is Vulnerable.

- If you just want to play Rebound for damage and don't need to place any cards on your deck, simply make it your final play before ending your turn.

- Upgrading Rebound marginally increases its power level and is not recommended.

- Rebound's effect speeds up the progression of Streamline and Claw, and can help combine Amplify with a Power card. It techs against Status-heavy foes like Chosen and Book of Stabbing by guaranteeing at least one good draw in the following turn. It also interacts well with Chaos and Rainbow+ to rapidly fill your orb slots.

- Cards that are consumed when played, such as Power cards, cards with Exhaust, and cards duplicated by Echo Form are not placed on top of your deck by Rebound, but they *will* consume the Rebound effect.

- It is possible to get two copies of the Rebound effect by playing it with an active Echo Form. This will cause the following two cards to be Rebounded, and both stacks will wear off at the end of the turn.

- The Rebounded card is placed onto the draw pile after its effect resolves, so cards like Skim will not draw themselves.

- Rather counterintuitively, Rebound *cannot* set up a free play of a specific card with Mayhem, as Mayhem triggers *after* you draw your cards, including the card at the top of your Draw Pile.

# Regenerate

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Regenerate

**Infobox:**
- Name: Regenerate
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/7/7e/Icon_Regen.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202163756
- Description: At the end of your turn, heal X HP.
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: Intensity

Regenerate is a buff that heals the character's health at the end of the turn. It is currently exclusive to various enemies and cannot be obtained by the player.

Its major difference from Regeneration, which the player can get from Regen Potion, is that Regenerate does not decay. Due to this reason, the fight cannot be stalled for it to wear off. In fact, Regenerate itself makes the fight even longer.

## Sources of Regenerate
- Awakened One: Starts with 10 (15 on Ascension 19+) Regenerate
- Empowered Elites that hold Emerald Key: Starts with 3/5/7 Regenerate on Act 1/2/3.
## Notes
- Not to be confused with Regeneration, which decays over time and is available to the player using Regen Potion.
Category:Buffs

# Regeneration

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Regeneration

**Infobox:**
- Name: Regeneration
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/7/7e/Icon_Regen.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202163756
- Description: At the end of your turn, heal X HP and reduce Regen by 1.
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: Intensity and Duration

Regeneration is a buff that heals the character's health at the end of the turn. "End of turn" will not be evaluated if you win the battle — if you kill the final enemy, Regeneration will not trigger.

Regeneration works similar to Poison. The number represents the amount it will heal and the turns left. After each turn, the number decreases by one. When the number reaches 0, Regeneration wears off. 

Because of its linear decay per turn, multiple Regen Potions stack quadratically: taking one can restore 15 HP over 5 turns (5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 HP), but taking two in succession and starting off with 10 Regeneration can restore drastically more than that in the first two turns (10 + 9 + 8 + ... + 1 for a total of 55 HP over 10 turns). It can be improved even further with the assistance of Sacred Bark.

## Sources of Regeneration
- Regen Potion: Gives the player 5 Regeneration (10 with Sacred Bark)

## Notes
- Not to be confused with the Awakened One's or buffed elite's Regenerate ability, which heals at a flat rate at the end of every turn without decaying.
Category:Buffs

# Relics

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Relics

**Relics** are permanent items that provide a passive bonus for the rest of the run. Most relics are available to all characters, with some exceptions (indicated for each relic). The Ironclad and Silent each have access to 11 unique relics while the Defect and Watcher only have 9 apiece.

Starter Relics are granted upon starting a run with the corresponding character.

Common, Uncommon, and Rare Relics can be found from a variety of sources. Usually, the odds of getting a particular rarity of relic is 3:2:1 (50%/33%/17%). Chests have their own rarity chances, which result in the chances of getting each rarity being (49%/42%/9%).

Boss Relics can only be found from Bosses (or in Neow's starting choice, traded for Starter Relic).

Event Relics can only be found from specific event outcomes.

Finally, Shop Relics can only be purchased from the Merchant.

# Reprogram

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Reprogram

**Infobox:**
- Name: Reprogram
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/9/9d/Reprogram.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20210408071552
- Class: Defect
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Cost: 1
- Effect: Lose 1 focus. Gain 1 Strength. Gain 1 Dexterity.
- [Reprogram+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: Lose 2 focus. Gain 2 Strength. Gain 2 Dexterity.

CardAutobox
**Reprogram** is an Uncommon Skill for The Defect, which causes it to gain 1 (2) Strength and Dexterity at the cost of losing 1 (2) Focus. Upgrading **Reprogram** increases the attribute changes (both loss and gain) from 1 to 2.

**Reprogram** can serve as a powerful, reusable source of Strength and Dexterity if you are not using Orbs affected by Focus. 

## Interactions
 
- The focus loss of **Reprogram** is considered a debuff. As such, Artifacts will negate the focus loss while still providing the strength/dexterity gains. Core Surge and Clockwork Souvenir are reliable sources of Artifacts for The Defect.
- Orange Pellets can be used to remove the focus loss, if you have negative focus. While Artifacts will always block Focus Down, it's only considered a debuff for Orange Pellets if you have negative focus. For instance, if you gain one focus from Defragment and then use Reprogram and go back to zero focus, you cannot undo that loss with Orange Pellets, but if you use Reprogram first and then activate Orange Pellets (keeping in mind that powers will activate before Orange Pellets, so powers that give you focus will still cancel it out), the negative focus will be undone. 
- Plasma orbs are not affected by focus, so Meteor Strike and Fusion work well with Reprogram.
- If you are committed to using Reprogram and don't mind the Focus loss, Hyperbeam has no downsides.
- All for One can allow you to play several Claws (or other 0-cost attacks) in one turn, allowing you to benefit from the Strength gain multiple times.
- The Dexterity gained by Reprogram allows Steam Barrier to last longer and yield more Block for free.
- Since Reinforced Body applies Block multiple times, the Dexterity gained from Reprogram applies multiple times as well.

## Strategy
**Reprogram** is a rather powerful Card, although it does ruin orb decks (unless you have either Orange Pellets and many powers or a way of gaining Artifacts and/or Focus and either ending battles fast or being able to gain Focus steadily for the combat). Due to this, **Reprogram** is the type of card to decide what type of deck you choose (despite there being various types of orb ignoring Defect decks). Note that Plasma is not affected by the Focus loss.

If you somehow manage to obtain **Reprogram** as a character other than the Defect, it is a great card since no other characters can use focus (without other Defect cards).

# Reptomancer

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Reptomancer

**Infobox:**
- Name: Reptomancer
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/1/14/Reptomancer.png/revision/latest?cb=20180927061640
- HP: 180-190; 190-200 (Ascension 8+)
- Debut Act: Act 3
- In Party With: 2 Daggers
- Powers: None
- Name: Dagger
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/4/45/Dagger.png/revision/latest?cb=20180829084556
- HP: 20-25
- Debut Act: Act 3
- In Party With: Reptomancer + Dagger
- Powers: None

The **Reptomancer** is an elite encounter fought in Act 3. Her ability to summon Daggers quickly, especially on high Ascension levels, makes her a formidable opponent. Cards that affect more than one enemy, such as Die Die Die and Cleave, are key to defeating the Reptomancer.

## Pattern
Always uses Summon on the first turn. 

After the first turn, has a 33% chance to use any of her 3 moves. If 4 or more Daggers are present, 67% chance of using Snake Strike and 33% chance of using Big Bite. 
- Cannot use Snake Strike twice in a row, cannot use Big Bite twice in a row, and cannot use Summon 3 times in a row. 
- Maximum of 4 Daggers.
| Name | Intent | Effect | Asc 3+ | Asc 18+ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Summon |  | Summons a Dagger. | Summons a Dagger. | Summons 2 Daggers. |
| Snake Strike |  | Deals 13 x 2 damage and applies 1 Weak. | Deals 16 x 2 damage and applies 1 Weak. | Deals 16 x 2 damage and applies 1 Weak. |
| Big Bite |  | Deals 30 damage. | Deals 34 damage. | Deals 34 damage. |

## Dagger
A minion spawned by the Reptomancer.

### Pattern
Uses Stab as its first move. Uses Explode as its second move.

Dagger is not buffed at all in any Ascension stages.
| Name | Intent | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stab |  | Deal 9 damage and shuffle 1 Wound into the discard pile. |
| Explode |  | Deal 25 damage. Dagger instantly dies after this attack. |

# Rest Site

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Rest_Site

**Rest Sites** are one of the Map Locations, and are a major part of the strategy on each Act.

By default, rest sites only offer a choice between Rest and Smith. More options can be added by specific Relics. Only one option can be chosen at each rest site.

There will always be a rest site immediately before the Boss, regardless of what path you chose. The only exception to this rule is Act 4, where the rest site is the first room in the Act.

## Options

| Icon | Description | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | **Rest:** Heal for 30% of your max HP. | - Rounded down |
|  | **Smith:** Upgrade 1 card of your choice. |  |
|  | **Lift:**  Permanently gain 1 Strength. | - Requires Girya. - Maximum of 3 uses per run. |
|  | **Toke:** Remove 1 card from your deck. | - Requires Peace Pipe. |
|  | **Dig:** Obtain a random Relic. | - Requires Shovel. |
|  | **Recall:** Obtain the Ruby Key. | - Available in normal runs when Act 4 is unlocked. - Maximum of 1 use per run. |

## Interactions
- Ancient Tea Set: Whenever you enter a Rest Site, start the next combat with 2 Energy.
- Coffee Dripper: You can no longer  **Rest** at Rest Sites.
- Dream Catcher: Whenever you  **Rest**, get a random card reward choice.
- Eternal Feather: Upon entering a Rest site, heal for 3 HP per 5 cards in your deck, rounded down.
- Fusion Hammer: You can no longer  **Smith** at Rest Sites.
- Girya: Adds the  **Lift** option to gain a permanent 1 Strength, up to 3 times per run.
- Peace Pipe: Adds the  **Toke** option to remove a card of your choice from your deck.
- Regal Pillow: Increases the heal from  **Rest** by 15 HP.
- Shovel: Adds the  **Dig** option to obtain a random Relic.
- If you have 2 out these 3 relics: Shovel,Peace Pipe andGirya, the third one will not spawn.

# Retain

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Retain

**Retain** is a keyword that allows you to keep cards in your hand after the end of turn. Some cards have the Retain keyword built in to the card, which lets you keep that card at the end of turn.

Cards with Ethereal still exhaust at the end of your turn even if you attempt to Retain them (with the exception of Meditate), and self-discarding cards (Burn, Decay, Doubt, Regret, and Shame) still discard at the end of your turn even if you attempt to Retain them.

### Cards
These following cards have Retain built into them:
- Crescendo
- Flying Sleeves
- Protect
- Tranquility
- Perseverance: Its Block is increased every turn it is Retained. 
    - The amount of Block does not reset upon use, but it will not increase again until it is Retained in your hand.
- Sands of Time: Its cost is reduced every turn it is Retained. 
    - The cost does not reset upon use, but it will not decrease again until it is Retained in your hand.
- Windmill Strike: Its damage is increased every turn it is Retained. 
    - The amount of damage does not reset upon use, but it will not increase again until it is Retained in your hand.
- Worship: Has Retain once upgraded.
- Blasphemy: Has Retain once upgraded.
- Insight
- Miracle
- Safety
- Smite
- Through Violence
These following cards can be used to Retain other cards:
- Well-Laid Plans: At the end of your turn, choose 1(2) cards on your hand to Retain.
- Equilibrium: Gain Block and Retain what was left on your hand at the end of your turn.
- Meditate: Retain 1(2) cards from your discard pile, enter Calm then immediately end your turn.
This following card interacts with Retained cards:
- Establishment: Whenever a card is Retained, lower its cost by 1.
## Trivia
- Despite Runic Pyramid having an effect similar to Retain, it does not Retain your hand, but merely prevents you from discarding your hand at the end of your turn.  
Category:Keyword

# Riddle with Holes

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Riddle_with_Holes

**Infobox:**
- Name: Riddle with Holes
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/d/d5/RiddleWithHoles.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20190821181236

# Ring of the Serpent

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Ring_of_the_Serpent

**Infobox:**
- Name: Ring of the Serpent
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/5/58/RingoftheSerpent.png/revision/latest?cb=20200203153215
- Description: Replaces Ring of the Snake. At the start of your turn, draw 1 additional card.
- Flavor: Your ring has morphed and changed forms.
- Rarity: Boss
- Class: Silent

The **Ring of the Serpent** is a Boss Relic which can only be obtained by the Silent. It replaces the Ring of the Snake and draws 1 additional card at the start of your turn instead of 2 additional cards but only at the start of combat. 

On mobile versions, a bug causes it to make you draw two extra cards per turn instead of one. 

You must possess Ring of the Snake for it to appear.

Since it replaces Ring of the Snake, you actually lose 1 card draw on turn 1 ( 7 vs 6 cards ), card neutral on turn 2 (12 vs 12), and only starts to be positive on turn 3 (17 vs 18).

If a deck can confidently deal with the loss of early card draw, (Bag of Preparation, Acrobatics, etc.) it may be worth considering to take it so you can better handle longer fights such as bosses. However, other Boss Relics are likely to be of more value while also keeping your Ring of the Snake.

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Ritual_Dagger

**Infobox:**

- Type: Attack
- Rarity: Special
- Cost: 1
- Effect: Deal 15 damage. If Fatal, permanently increase this card's damage by 3.; Exhaust.
- [Ritual Dagger+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: Deal 15 damage. If Fatal, permanently increase this card's damage by 5.; Exhaust.

CardAutobox
**Ritual Dagger** is a Colorless Card that can only be obtained from The Nest Event.

Killing an enemy with **Ritual Dagger** will increase the card's damage by 3(5) for the rest of the run. Using it will exhaust it, whether it kills an enemy or not.

Some enemies do not count for kills to increase **Ritual Dagger**'s damage, listed below under Interactions.

## Interactions
 
- Exhume can be used to return **Ritual Dagger** to your deck, allowing for more than one use or kill per battle.
- Strange Spoon gives a 50% chance that Ritual Dagger will not exhaust on use.
- Playing this card twice with an effect such as Echo Form or a Duplication Potion will allow you to still get the bonus damage, even if the first hit did not kill, but the second did.

 
- Minions do not count as kills. These are recognized by the  icon.
- As with all Fatal cards, if fighting Darklings reducing the HP of one of them to 0 does not count as a kill unless it was the final enemy from the batch.
- Defeating the first phase of the Awakened One does not count as a kill.
- Using Omniscience to kill two separate enemies with **Ritual Dagger** will not cause it to upgrade twice, only once.
- Killing enemies with Ritual Daggers that were copied with Dual Wield will not increase in your kill count.
- Dual Wield will NOT preserve the original copy if it was manually selected/chosen. It only preserves the original copy if Ritual Dagger was the only valid target in hand, and chosen automatically.

# Runic Pyramid

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Runic_Pyramid

**Infobox:**
- Name: Runic Pyramid
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/8/8e/RunicPyramid.png/revision/latest?cb=20190923235358
- Description: At the end of your turn, you no longer discard your hand.
- Flavor: The runes are indecipherable.
- Rarity: Boss
- Class: Any

At the end of your turn, you no longer Discard your hand. 

Runic Pyramid is a Boss Relic.

## Tips
- While keeping your entire hand is extremely powerful, keep the ten-card hand limit in mind — if you're unable to reliably play, discard, or otherwise dispose of five cards a turn, the pyramid will eventually cause you to draw fewer cards.  
- It interacts particularly badly with Wounds, Curses, and other Unplayables, non-Ethereal cards that can linger in your hand forever or even fill it entirely. However, end of turn effects (Burn, Decay, Doubt, Regret, and Shame) will still discard themselves at the end of the turn. Pain and Normality are particularly harmful. For this reason, a Blue Candle can be a particularly useful pairing for dealing with curses (or a Medical Kit for dealing with Wounds).
    - This drawback can be circumvented with cards that Discard or Exhaust cards from your hand, such as Survivor or True Grit.
- This relic is particularly powerful with small cycle-based decks, such as Rampage. If you can get your deck down to 10 cards after powers and exhausts are played, you can guarantee you'll see that key card every turn.
- Despite having a similar effect, this relic does not Retain your hand. It merely stops you from discarding cards at the end of your turn. Cards that synergize with Retain, specifically Establishment, have no additional synergy with Runic Pyramid.

# Rupture

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Rupture

**Infobox:**
- Name: Rupture
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/3/38/Rupture.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20210408071643
- Class: Ironclad
- Type: Power
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Cost: 1
- Effect: Whenever you lose HP from a card,; gain 1 Strength.
- [Rupture+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: Whenever you lose HP from a card,; gain 2 Strength.
- Name: Rupture
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/e/ef/Icon_Rupture.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202163757
- Description: Whenever you lose HP from a card, gain X Strength.
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: Intensity

Rupture is a Power card for the Ironclad. Every time a card causes the player to lose HP, they gain 1 Strength immediately. When Upgraded, the player gains 2 Strength instead of 1.

## Interactions

- Aside from cards that cause the player to lose HP immediately when played (such as Bloodletting), other card-related effects trigger Rupture as well:
    - Pain triggers Rupture every time the player plays a card while Pain is in hand.
    - Burn and Decay trigger Rupture if any damage from them is unblocked.
    - Losing HP from Regret also triggers Rupture.
- The amount of HP lost does not affect the amount of Strength gained; losing 2 HP from Hemokinesis and losing 3 HP from Bloodletting will both only trigger the Strength gain a single time. It is the number of instances of HP loss that affects how much Strength is gained.
    - However, multiple copies of Rupture stack as expected, granted more Strength each time a card causes the player to lose HP.
- Brutality and Combust work extremely well with Rupture, as they automatically trigger its effect every turn. Keep in mind that stacking multiple Brutalities or Combusts will not cause Rupture to trigger extra times (as stacking these cards simply increases the amount of HP lost at once). will not trigger a single Rupture multiple times. However, multiple Ruptures will stack, and be triggered by Brutality or Combust.
- J.A.X. is an excellent card to use with Rupture, getting even more Strength mileage out of the HP loss.
- If HP loss is prevented by Tungsten Rod or Buffer, no Strength is gained.
- Damaging effects that are indirectly triggered by cards, such as Thorns, Sharp Hide, and Beat of Death, will *not* activate Rupture..

# Rushdown

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Rushdown

**Infobox:**
- Name: Rushdown
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/e/e8/Rushdown.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20191106145554
- Class: Watcher
- Type: Power
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Cost: 1
- Effect: Whenever you enter Wrath, draw 2 cards.
- [Rushdown+]
- Cost+: 0
- Effect+: Whenever you enter Wrath, draw 2 cards.

CardAutobox
**Rushdown** is a Power card for the Watcher. After it is played, you immediately draw 2 cards when entering the Wrath Stance.

When Upgraded, Rushdown's cost becomes 0.

## Mechanics

- The Rushdown buff is stackable, so playing multiple copies of Rushdown will draw even more cards upon entering Wrath.
- Rushdown triggers after the card that enters Wrath is put into the discard pile.

## Infinite Combos
Rushdown is a key component of Stance-based infinite combos. All that is required for an infinite combo, in addition to Rushdown itself, is:

- A deck that is thin enough to hold all cards in hand
- 1 card that enters Wrath and 1 card that enters Calm, with these characteristics:
    - They cost at most 2 Energy in total (or at most 3 Energy if you have Violet Lotus)
    - They deal any amount of damage, or you have another damage source such as Panache or Letter Opener

Once the whole deck is held in hand, enter Calm, then enter Wrath. You will immediately draw the Calm and Wrath cards again and gain 2 Energy from exiting Calm. 

## Trivia 
- During beta testing for the Watcher, Rushdown was called Adaptation and triggered on all Stance changes.

Watcher Card Navbox
Category:Buffs
