# Scrap Ooze

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Scrap_Ooze

**Scrap Ooze** is an event found exclusively in Act 1. You came across a large, slime-like creature that has eaten a lot of metal pieces, and maybe something valuable.

## Options

*Numbers in parentheses are for Ascension 15 or higher.*

- **[Reach Inside]** Lose 3 (5) HP. 25% chance to find a Relic.
    - If you failed to find a Relic, you can repeat **[Reach Inside]** until you find one.
      - Each subsequent **[Reach Inside]** cost 1 additional HP and has additional 10% chance to find a Relic.

- **[Leave]** Nothing happens.

## Dialogue
| Encounter |
| --- |
| *As you walk into the room you hear a gurgling and the* grinding *of metals. Before you is a slime-like creature that ate too much scrap for its own good. From the center of the creature you see glints of strange light, perhaps something magical? It looks like you can get some treasure if you just reach inside its... opening. However, the acid and sharp objects may hurt.* |
| Reach Inside |
| Found Nothing |
| Ouch! |
| *All you find is corroded metal and a bit of* burning pain. |
| ''However, you're still convinced there's a relic...* |
| Found a Relic |
| *Success!* |
| *After rummaging through the metal and burning acid, you finally grab hold of a relic and yank it out.* |
| *You pull your way out of the ooze damaged but rewarded.* |
| Leave |
| *You decide to leave the area.* |
| *The slime pays no attention, content with its meal.'' |

## Strategy
Even though this event seems to be a simple "pay HP for reward", consider it the same as Elites fight. For a Relic from this event, you will inevitably lose some HP, and the chance is not favorable up until you lose 10+ HP. Plan your action accordingly: Can you afford to lose 10+ HP here? Is there a Rest Site nearby? Are there many fights further from this point? Sure, it may be based on your luck more than an Elites fight, but it is good to take precautions for the worst outcome.

# Scrape

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Scrape

**Infobox:**
- Name: Scrape
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/9/94/Scrape.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20210408071828
- Class: Defect
- Type: Attack
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Cost: 1
- Effect: Deal 7 damage.; Draw 4 cards.Discard all cards drawn this way that do not cost 0.
- [Scrape+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: Deal 10 damage.; Draw 5 cards.Discard all cards drawn this way that do not cost 0.

CardAutobox
**Scrape** is an Attack card for The Defect that combines solid damage with a powerful card-draw effect. As an uncommon card, Scrape can be acquired as a battle reward card or purchased from the Merchant.

### Strategy
- Scrape is a critical piece of The Defect's 0-cost archetype, drawing into your key cards while dealing relevant damage. Some zero-cost synergies include:
    - Claw, Beam Cell, upgraded Dualcast, and double-discounted Streamline to stack up massive damage.
    - Go for the Eyes and fully-discounted Force Field for combined attack and defense.
    - FTL, Steam Barrier, TURBO, Finesse, Flash of Steel, and Double Energy generate "real" card draw and surplus Energy.
    - Be careful when using this with a 0-energy build featuring All for One, as Scrape can sometimes discard All For One.
    - Hologram enables The Defect to recover useful, but non-0-cost cards from the discard pile.

- Note that Curses, Statuses, and X-cost cards like Tempest do not cost 0, and will be discarded by Scrape.

- When The Defect is Confused, cards whose costs are reduced to 0 will not be discarded, while cards whose costs are increased above 0 will be discarded.

- Because Scrape draws through your deck faster, it allows you to shuffle more often. This can be used to enable effects like Sundial.

- Scrape's effect is much stronger than it initially appears. You can immediately play every card you draw, even if you played Scrape with your final Energy.

- You don't even need many 0-cost cards to get value from Scrape — upgrading your starting Zap and Dualcast reduces their costs to 0, and even two Claws can become exceptionally powerful during a long game.

- Be sure to check upgrades while building around Scrape. Many of The Defect's cards drop to 0 cost when upgraded.

- Scrape is one of the few Attacks that can actually draw cards. This makes it useful against Chosen, Gremlin Nob, and other enemies that punish non-Attack cards.

- Be careful not to inadvertently draw Dazed, Clumsy, or Ascender's Bane with Scrape — they will be discarded instead of Exhausted.

- When you have eight or fewer cards in your deck, check your decklist before playing Scrape. If your remaining cards aren't particularly powerful, you may want to deliberately discard them so you'll reshuffle next turn.
- As Scrape puts cards that do not cost 0 directly into the discard pile, it can be used to increase the block that Stack grants without having to use any energy on the cards that Scrape drew.

# Scry

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Scry

Scry is a mechanic unique to the Watcher.
Category:Game Mechanics

## Mechanic

Whenever you Scry, you will look at a certain number of cards on top of your draw pile. You then may choose to discard any number of them. 

Scry does not reshuffle your deck. If you have fewer cards in your draw pile than the Scry amount, the Scry applies to whatever is left in the draw pile.

Scrying displays top and bottom cards in order from left to right.

### Scry Card
These cards have Scry. Numbers in parentheses are for upgraded version:
- Cut Through Fate: Scry 2(3) cards.
    - Keep in mind that the leftmost card that is not chosen to be discarded will immediately be drawn after you confirm your discard choice.
- Just Lucky: Scry 1(2) card(s).
- Third Eye: Scry 3(5) cards.
- Foresight: At the start of your turn *before* you draw your cards, Scry 3(4) cards.
    - This effectively allow you to discard a number of cards before it is drawn.
These cards have interaction with Scrying in general:
- Nirvana: After you Scry, gain Block.
- Weave: After you Scry, return from discard pile to your hand.
    - If you Scry and choose to discard Weave, it will return to your hand after confirming your discard choices, effectively allow you to both discard it from the next draw and use it to attack an enemy.

### Others
- Golden Eye: Whenever you Scry, Scry 2 additional cards.
- Melange: Whenever you shuffle your draw pile, Scry 3.
## Trivia
- Before the Watcher was released, the blue card Reprogram used to have an effect akin to Scry 4(5), albeit worded differently. It got reworked after the Watcher was released, as to make Scrying a unique mechanic of the Watcher.

## Notes

# Searing Blow

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Searing_Blow

**Infobox:**
- Name: Searing Blow
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/d/dc/SearingBlow.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016210951
- Class: Ironclad
- Type: Attack
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Cost: 2
- Effect: Deal 12 damage.; Can be Upgraded any number of times.
- [Searing Blow+]
- Cost+: 2
- Effect+: Deal 16 damage.; Can be Upgraded any number of times.

**Searing Blow** is an Attack card for the Ironclad. It deals 12(+) damage. As an Uncommon card, it appears as a reward for combat, although less often than Commons.

This card is unique because it can be Upgraded any number of times.  Each upgrade causes the card to deal sequentially more damage. There's no limit to how many times this damage bonus can apply.

The damage increase from an upgrade increases each time:
| Upgrades | Damage | Damage Increase |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 (base) | 12 | (base) |
| 1 | 16 | +4 |
| 2 | 21 | +5 |
| 3 | 27 | +6 |
| 4 | 34 | +7 |
| 5 | 42 | +8 |
| 6 | 51 | +9 |
| 7 | 61 | +10 |
| 8 | 72 | +11 |
| 9 | 84 | +12 |
| 10 | 97 | +13 |
| 11 | 111 | +14 |
| 12 | 126 | +15 |
| 13 | 142 | +16 |
| 14 | 159 | +17 |
| 15 | 177 | +18 |
| n | n(n+7)/2 + 12 | n+3 |

## Tips
- Warped Tongs can continually upgrade **Searing Blow** over the course of a battle, even with other cards in your hand that have not yet been upgraded.
- Armaments and Apotheosis upgrade Searing Blow even if it has already been upgraded once.
- Blessing of the Forge and Lesson Learned also will upgrade Searing Blow.

Self-Forming Clay is an Uncommon Relic.

## Tips
- Self-Forming Clay is activated by cards that cost your HP. Therefore, assuming the block it produces actually gets used, it will effectively negate the disadvantage of paying 3 HP, and can even turn paying 1 or 2 HP to your advantage. # Sentry

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Sentry

**Infobox:**
- Name: Sentry
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/5/5f/Sentry-pretty.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20180110054044
- HP: 38-42; 39-45 (Ascension 8+)
- In Party With: Act 1 - 2 other Sentries; Act 2 - Spheric Guardian
- Debut Act: 1 + 2
- Powers: Artifact 1

The **Sentry** is a Monster found on the first act of the Spire with two companion Sentries as an Elite encounter, and found on the second act in a normal encounter with a Spheric Guardian. Its moderate damage and aggressive Status-flooding make them dangerous in a group of 3 on the first act.

## Pattern
When encountered in three as an Elite, 1st and 3rd sentries will always start with Bolt while the 2nd sentry will always start with Beam. Afterwards, all sentries will keep alternating between their two moves.

When encountered with the Spheric Guardian, always starts with Bolt and then alternates between its two moves every turn afterwards.
| Name | Intent | Effect | Asc 3+ | Asc 18+ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Beam |  | Deal 9 damage. | Deal 10 damage. | Deal 10 damage. |
| Bolt |  | Shuffles 2 Dazed into the discard pile. | Shuffles 2 Dazed into the discard pile. | Shuffles 3 Dazed into the discard pile. |

## Tips
- It is usually a good idea to kill the front or back sentry, to ensure that you never need to block for more than one sentry's damage.
- The easiest time against the 3x Sentry elite fight will be in the beginning, before the Discard pile is ever shuffled into the draw pile. Larger decks may end up drawing more useful cards than Dazed, but will also take longer to draw (and so Exhaust) the Statuses.
- Attacks that target more than one enemy, such as Whirlwind or Dagger Spray, are very effective against this elite encounter.
    - In contrast, attacks that apply debuffs, Bash in particular, will not be as useful in this fight due to the sentries' Artifact buff.
- Ironclad has a series of cards that are especially useful in this combat. Fire Breathing is incredibly effective against the sentries and can easily win the fight on its own once the Dazed cards have been shuffled into the draw pile. Dark Embrace and Evolve can deal with the negative effect of Dazed cards filling your draw slot. Feel No Pain almost garantees the requested Block for one sentry, making the combat much easier after taking down the first sentry.
- Be careful with going into wrath Stance when playing Watcher in this combat, especially after the discard pile shuffle. Going into wrath without a garanteed kill can easily lead to taking massive damage, as the next draw may just be a handful of Dazed.

- In Party With: None; Fungi Beast

**Shelled Parasite** is a Monster fought in Act 2 of the Spire.

## Pattern
On turn 1, Shelled Parasite has a 50% chance of using Suck and a 50% chance of using Double Strike.

Afterwards, has a 40% chance of using Double Strike, a 40% chance of using Suck, and a 20% chance of using Fell.

Cannot use Double Strike or Suck three times in a row, and cannot use Fell twice in a row.

It is stunned if its Plated Armor is reduced to zero, interrupting its current intent.

In Ascension 17+, Shelled Parasite always starts with Fell on turn 1.
| Name | Intent | Effect | Asc 2+ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Double Strike |  | Deals 6 x 2 damage. | Deals 7 x 2 damage. |
| Suck |  | Deals 10 damage, gains HP equal to unblocked damage dealt. | Deals 12 damage, gains HP equal to unblocked damage dealt. |
| Fell |  | Deals 18 damage and applies 2 Frail. | Deals 21 damage and applies 2 Frail. |

## Strategy
Due to Shelled Parasite's ability, it may be a good idea to use a high damage attack first in the turn, then hit as many times as possible once the Block is broken to lower its total stacks of Plated Armor. Doing so will make future attacks take more HP from Shelled Parasite.

# Shining Light

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Shining_Light

**Shining Light** is an event found exclusively in Act 1. You find a mass of magical light that compels you to walk inside it.

## Options

*Numbers in parentheses are for Ascension 15 or higher.*

- **[Enter]** Upgrade 2 random cards. Take 20% (30%) of your max HP in damage.

- **[Leave]** Nothing happens.

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| *You find a shimmering mass of light encompassing the center of the room.* |
| *Its warm glow and enchanting patterns invite you in.* |
| Enter |
| *As you walk through the light, you notice that the light is absorbed into you.* |
| ''It's* scorching hot*! However, the pain quickly recedes.* |
| *You feel invigorated, as though you received a well deserved slap.* |
| Leave |
| *You walk around it, wondering what could have been.'' |

## Strategy
This event is strong because it allows the player to upgrade two cards at once without using a Rest Site. Even if it upgrades two Strikes or Defends, those cards are much more powerful for Act 1, the Act where this event is found. However, do consider your HP and whether you can afford to lose a fairly large amount of it going forward.

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Shiv

**Infobox:**
- Name: Shiv

- Class: Neutral
- Type: Attack
- Rarity: Special
- Cost: 0
- Effect: Deal 4 damage.; Exhaust.
- [Shiv+]
- Cost+: 0
- Effect+: Deal 6 damage.; Exhaust.

CardAutobox**Shiv** is a 0-cost card for the Silent. It cannot be obtained by itself; instead, Shivs are added to your hand by other cards.

Shivs can be buffed by the Accuracy card.

## Sources of Shivs
- Blade Dance: Add 3(4) Shivs.
- Cloak and Dagger: Gain 6 Block, add 1 (2) Shiv.
- Infinite Blades: Start each turn with 1 Shiv.
- Storm of Steel: Discard your hand, add 1 Shiv per card discarded.
- Cunning Potion: Add 3 (6) Shiv+ to your hand.
- Ninja Scroll: Start each combat with 3 Shivs in hand.

## Interactions

- Accuracy: Shivs deal 4(6) more damage this combat.
- Strength works fully for Shivs.
- Finisher counts each Shiv played.
- Dead Branch will trigger any time a shiv is played.
- After Image and A Thousand Cuts benefit from any cards played, a strong synergy with Shivs.
- Choke works extremely well with Shivs, as it bypasses Block and activates every time a card is played.
- Can easily use Envenom to quickly apply Poison stacks.
- Wrist Blade increases all Shiv damage by 4
- With the right deck, Panache can be triggered multiple times in a turn.
- Pen Nib and Nunchaku are easily cycled by Shivs.
- Ornamental Fan, Shuriken, and Kunai all work with Shivs.
- Master Reality, if you somehow obtain it, increases the damage of Shivs by 2.
- Shivs also work well with effects that trigger on Exhaust, such as Feel No Pain, if you can obtain them.

- Velvet Choker makes it hard to play low impact cards like Shivs.
- Strange Spoon makes it possible for played Shivs to discard instead of exhaust, causing them to return to your draw pile.

# Silent

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Silent

*"A deadly huntress from the foglands. Eradicates foes with daggers and poisons."*

 The **Silent **is one of four playable characters in Slay the Spire. She is a huntress themed on a rogue fantasy build. This cunning character weakens her foes with numerous cuts and poison, while using cheap tricks and agility to avoid their attacks. With many powerful cards that draw and discard, the Silent ensures that she will always be one step ahead of her enemy. She starts with a relatively low 70 hp.  

The Silent's starting Relic is Ring of the Snake, which draws 2 additional cards when starting combat. 

## Cards
### Starting Deck
- 5 Strikes
- 5 Defends
- 1 Survivor
- 1 Neutralize

Silent Card Navbox

## Relics
Starting Relic: Ring of the Snake

Common Relic: Snecko Skull

Uncommon Relics: Ninja Scroll, Paper Krane

Rare Relics: The Specimen, Tingsha, Tough Bandages

Boss Relics: Hovering Kite, Ring of the Serpent (replaces Ring of the Snake), Wrist Blade

Shop Relic: Twisted Funnel

## Strategy
The Silent does not have any reliable ability to heal or gain an abundance of starting health. Therefore, she is often focused on damage mitigation through Block and Weak chaining, and gaining explosive advantage to end the encounter at opportune times. Many of her cards draw cards, reduce costs, or give additional Energy, allowing her to chain momentum together to overcome low individual impact.

### Starting Deck & Relic
The Silent's starting deck is the largest of the 4 characters, at 12 cards, compared to the Ironclad's, Defect's and Watcher's starting deck, each of which have 10 cards. This means more Strikes and Defends are encountered in Act 1, and it's slightly more difficult to remove all starting cards from The Silent's Deck. The Silent's starting deck is also the cheapest, with its 2 non-Strike non-Defend cards costing 1 and 0. This means it's easier to take strong 2-cost card options earlier in the game, such as Dash, Predator, and Leg Sweep.

Her starting Relic, Ring of the Snake, ensures that the first turn of every fight is slightly stronger than all of the other turns. This makes Innate cards slightly better for Silent, since they only take up 1 of 7 cards instead of 1 of 5 cards. The "Bottle Relics" (Bottled Flame, Bottled Lightning, and Bottled Tornado) have improved utility for similar reasons.

Owing to these properties, the Silent's early-game performance is by far the weakest out of the four characters. Her lack of upfront damage leaves her ill-equipped to deal with Act 1 Elite encounters, particularly the Lagavulin and Gremlin Nob, if players do not fix the damage density of her starting deck. Thus, even getting a run started can be a challenge with the Silent, particularly on high Ascension levels. However, if players can overcome this hurdle, they will realize Silent's incredible late-game potential, where her performance is conversely the strongest on average. Her access to the strongest damage mitigation tools in the game, as well as consistent long-term scaling damage and card manipulation, make even decks that seem weak able to clear the Act 3 boss gauntlet and even the Corrupt Heart with correct play.

### Synergies
Listed below are the standard synergies that Silent decks build towards, which may give you an idea of direction for your own runs. Some important things to keep in mind:
- Most of these builds aren't mutually exclusive. Think of each of the archetypes listed below as an engine that you can incorporate into your deck; depending on the situation, you are more than able to adapt or combine multiple of them.
:*In particular, the different aspects of Silent's strategies can organically mesh with each other — you can have part of your damage or block plan be from one source and part from another. Keep synergies in mind, but don't turn down powerful cards just because they don't appear to match a synergy that you have.
- It's important to not "force" a particular build from the outset of the game. Build your deck to solve your immediate problems first and foremost, then allow an archetype to come to you organically. The only exception would be if you run into cards or relics in the early-game that are both individually impactful *and* form the crux of an entire archetype, and such situations are few and far between.

#### General
Cards that are generally good in any Silent strategy include:
- Well-Laid Plans. The ability to hold key cards for when you need them most is amazing, and part of why Silent is so strong into the late-game. You can hold that crucial Burst + Catalyst for when you've stacked up a critical mass of Poison, Wraith Form for an enemy's biggest hits, etc. Even outside of these examples, simply holding over damage or block on a turn where you don't need either one quite yet can let you answer whatever the enemy throws at you.
- Alchemize. Potions are an incredibly strong resource in *Slay the Spire*, especially as you climb the Ascension levels, owing to their ability to be deployed whenever you need them, or saved for crucial fights. A card that provides more of this resource thus makes every deck stronger.

Discard & Draw

#### Offensive
Poison

Shiv Deck
#### Defensive
Dexterity Stacking + Weak Chain

Non-Dexterity Mitigation

- Type: Buff

CardAutobox

**Simmering Fury** will put your character into Wrath and draw 2(3) cards at the start of the next turn.

## Interactions
 
- Since Wrath is entered at the start of the next turn, being in Calm at the end of the turn in which you play Simmering Fury will allow you to use the extra Energy from exiting Calm on the next turn.
- Simmering Fury pairs well with Meditate, since it places you in Calm (for additional energy when entering Wrath) and allows you to select a card to exit Wrath for the next turn to prevent taking double damage.

 
- Simmering Fury's Wrath occurs after Mantra is given. This means if you have played Simmering Fury but at the start of the next turn you accrue enough Mantra to enter Divinity (from Devotion or Damaru), you will briefly enter Divinity but then immediately enter Wrath. This will give you the extra 3 Energy from entering Divinity and counts as two switches in Stance for Mental Fortress, but you'll miss out on the benefits of the Divinity stance.

- Can be played for 0 energy. At 0 energy it doesn't do anything, but allows you to synergize with cards/relics that benefit from playing attacks/cards or playing 0-cost cards.
- Chemical X may be worth picking up for Skewer, as the Silent has other strong X-cost cards such as Malaise and Doppelganger.

# Slay the Spire

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Slay_the_Spire

**Infobox:**
- Name: Slay the Spire
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/4/49/SsColor.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20180114201345
- Developer: Mega Crit Games
- Publisher: Mega Crit Games
- Platform: Microsoft Windows, macOS, Linux, Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, iOS, Android
- Release date: Jan 23, 2019 (Microsoft Windows, macOS, Linux); May 21, 2019 (PS4); June 6, 2019 (Nintendo Switch); August 14, 2019 (Xbox One); June 13, 2020 (iOS); February 3, 2021 (Android)
- Genre: Deckbuilder Roguelike
- Mode: Single-player
- Requirements: Minimum; OS: Windows XP, Vista, 7, 8/8.1, 10; Processor: 2.0 Ghz; Memory: 2 GB RAM; Graphics: 1Gb Video Memory, capable of OpenGL 3.0+ support (2.1 with ARB extensions acceptable); Storage: 1 GB available space

**Slay the Spire** is a deck-building roguelike made by Mega Crit.
## Background
Slay the Spire is a game in which you climb The Spire, ascending its floors through three acts, encountering many enemies, bosses, and events along the way. The paths through each act all lead to a final floor where a challenging boss encounter awaits. The content of each floor and the available paths through each act are procedurally-generated, so each run will be a different experience. 

Slay the Spire is a game primarily about survival, collecting cards, and building a powerful deck to wipe out your foes. Good luck and happy deckbuilding!

This game also has mods that you can download and play with via Steam Workshop.

## Links
- Steam
- GOG
- Mega Crit's website

# Slime Boss

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Slime_Boss

**Infobox:**
- Name: Slime Boss
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/b/b1/Slime-boss-pretty.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20180110071215
- HP: 140; 150 9+
- In Party With: None
- Debut Act: Act 1
- Powers: Split

-The **Slime Boss** is one of the three bosses encountered at the end of Act 1.

## Pattern
Will always go through the pattern of Goop Spray, Preparing, Slam, and then repeat.

Split occurs when its HP is at 50% or below.

| Name | Intent | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Goop Spray |  | Shuffles 3 Slimed to your discard pile. |
| Shuffles 5 Slimed to your discard pile. |  |  |
| Preparing |  | Nothing. |
| Slam |  | Deals 35 damage. |
| Deals 38 damage. |  |  |
| Split |  | Splits into an Acid Slime (L) and a Spike Slime (L) with current HP. Interrupts previous intents. |
## Tips
- Slam hits for quite a bit of damage, so try and force him to split by his 3rd turn by dealing 70+ total damage, or use Weak and/or a lot of Block.
- Since the slimes left after split have health equal the boss's, it's a good idea to try to get it as far below half health as you can in one turn, so the new slimes have less health and are easier to deal with. The same strategy applies to the smaller slimes when they split.

## Trivia
- The name “Slime Boss” is a parody of “Crime Boss” due to the fact that this boss has a Mafia-style hat and also splits into other slimes, a reference to the elusive and neverending nature of mob families.

## Gallery

Evolve.png|Slime Boss as seen in the Evolve card art.

# Slimed

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Slimed

**Infobox:**
- Name: Slimed
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/a/a2/Slimed.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016212734
- Class: Neutral
- Type: Status
- Rarity: Common
- Cost: 1
- Effect: Exhaust.

CardAutobox
**Slimed** is a Status card that can be given by slime enemies. Unlike Wounds, Slimed can be Exhausted but costs 1 Energy in the process.

## Sources of Slimed
- Enemies
    - Spike Slimes of various sizes
    - Acid Slimes of various sizes
    - Slime Boss
    - Time Eater
    - Corrupt Heart
- Blights
    - Twisting Mind

## Interactions
- Evolve: Draw 1 more card for each Slimed you draw. Stacking Evolves can allow you to draw 2 more cards when you draw a Slimed. Can still lead to a hand of 10 Slimed, however. (***Verification needed: Slimed statuses given by the Time Eater does not appear to trigger the Evolve effect upon being drawn at the beginning of the turn.)
- Exhaust synergies can use Slimed as exhaust fuel. In addition, Slimed can be played for any benefits from exhausting, such as from Feel No Pain.
- Medical Kit has no effect on Slimed, unlike other statuses. Since Slimed is already playable, it has no effect.
- Slimed's cost can be changed by any effect that normally changes a card's cost, such as Mummified Hand or Confused.

# Sling of Courage

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Sling_of_Courage

**Infobox:**
- Name: Sling of Courage
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/9/93/Sling.png/revision/latest?cb=20190923235524
- Description: Start each Elite combat with 2 Strength.
- Flavor: "A handy tool for dealing with particularly tough opponents."
- Rarity: Shop
- Class: Any

The **Sling of Courage** is a Shop Relic. At the start of Elite battles, you gain 2 Strength. 

This relic also works in the Dead Adventurer event, as well as the second fight of the Colosseum event. 

Bosses and Elites are separate encounter types, and as such the Sling of Courage has ***no effect*** during boss fights. Keep this in mind when considering purchasing it.
## Trivia
- This relic references the tale of David and Goliath, in which the gigantic Goliath was slain by David, who was wielding only a stone and slingshot. Since then, the phrase "David and Goliath" has taken on a more popular meaning, usually denoting a situation where a smaller, weaker opponent faces a much bigger, stronger adversary.

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Slow

- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/1/13/Icon_Slow.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202163927
- Description: Whenever you play a card, the enemy receives 10% more damage from attacks this turn.
- Type: Debuff
- Stacking; Behavior: Intensity

Slow is a Debuff which the Giant Head always begins the fight with. Can also be applied to all enemies in a Daily Modifier.

## Effect
For every card you have played this turn, enemy takes 10% more damage from Attacks, ***not compounding***.

Slow resets at end of turn; enemy does NOT carry over stacks of Slow from turn to turn.

Only applies to damage caused by playing Attack cards.

Ex) If you play 2 cards, Attacks deal 20% extra damage; 5 cards, 50%; 11 cards, 110%; etc.

# Sneaky Strike

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Sneaky_Strike

**Infobox:**
- Name: Sneaky Strike
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/e/ed/SneakyStrike.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20210408072002
- Class: Silent
- Type: Attack
- Rarity: Common
- Cost: 2
- Effect: Deal 12 damage.; If you have discarded a card this turn,gain .
- [Sneaky Strike+]
- Cost+: 2
- Effect+: Deal 16 damage.; If you have discarded a card this turn,gain .

-**Sneaky Strike** is an Attack card for The Silent that can deal damage at effectively zero Energy. Upgrading Sneaky Strike increases the damage dealt from 12 to 16.

## Strategy
Sneaky Strike is a standard act 1 damage card. It is usually worth it with one or two discard effects in addition to the base deck.

Most Silent deck will benefit from the addition of draw manipulation like Acrobatics or Prepared, and Sneaky Strike can be part of the damage solution. At uncommon Eviscerate will usually be preferred as it fills the same role more efficiently. 

When playing with Sneaky Strike, play slowly and sequence your moves carefully. Accidentally playing Sneaky Strike before your discard enabler can be a fatal mistake.

-Remember that Sneaky Strike alone is basically a 2*Strike. If the deck is built around draw&discard, Sneaky Strike can be a decent 12/16 damage with 0 energy. But it WILL take up your draw slot and is very weak if no discard card is drawn. If cards that discard other cards such as Survivor is played, but no draw cards are played, even if you play Sneaky Strike, you may find yourself holding only 2 remaining cards, and the energy gain wasted.

## Synergies
Sneaky Strike requires a huge number of discard effects to function, as well as card draw to find it.

Tools of the Trade makes this much easier to play, because it guarantees a discard every turn for the remainder of combat. However, it won't help you if you draw Sneaky Strike before (or on the same turn as) the power.

Reducing the card's cost with Enlightenment, Madness, or Snecko Eye makes it generate Energy, enabling very high-tempo plays.

Like 0-cost cards, Sneaky Strike should be accompanied by card draw or expensive cards to make the most of the 'refunded' Energy.

Decks with Calculated Gamble to accelerate draw can sprinkle in Sneaky Strike for a bit of extra damage.

## Trivia
Early in development, Sneaky Strike was named Underhanded Strike, an apt name given the tender spot being pummeled in the card's art.

# Snecko

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Snecko

**Infobox:**
- Name: Snecko
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/4/44/Snecko.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20180916025017
- HP: 114-120 ; 120-125 7+
- In Party With: None
- Debut Act: 2
- Powers: None

**Snecko** is a Normal Encounter found in Act 2. Its usage of Confused combined with its ability to make the player Vulnerable may make it appear to be a strong encounter, but many higher-cost decks will benefit from the Confused and defeat the snecko easily. Lower cost decks, however, may have a more difficult time.

## Pattern
Always starts with Perplexing Glare.

Afterwards, it has a 60% chance of using Bite and a 40% chance of using Tail Whip every turn.
Snecko cannot use Bite 3 times in a row.
| Name | Intent | Effect | Asc 2+ | Asc 17+ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Perplexing Glare |  | Inflicts Confused. | Inflicts Confused. | Inflicts Confused. |
| Tail Whip |  | Deals 8 damage, applies 2 Vulnerable. | Deals 10 damage, applies 2 Vulnerable. | Deals 10 damage, applies 2 Vulnerable and 2 Weak. |
| Bite |  | Deals 15 damage. | Deals 18 damage. | Deals 18 damage. |

## Tips
- Because Snecko inflicts Confused, deck filled with costly cards (such as those using Perfected Strike) will actually benefit from the debuff rather than suffer.
    - Decks that rely on low-cost cards can instead negate the Confused debuff with any source of Artifact or Orange Pellets.
- Odd Mushroom is useful in this fight because it makes the Vulnerable Snecko applies less potent.

## Trivia
- The name 'Snecko' is a combination of the words 'Snake' and 'Gecko'.
- The move Tail Whip may be a reference to the Pokémon games, in which there exists a move with the same name that lowers your opponent's defense, making them more Vulnerable.

# Snecko Eye

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Snecko_Eye

**Infobox:**
- Name: Snecko Eye
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/5/5e/SneckoEye.png/revision/latest?cb=20200203153257
- Description: Draw 2 additional cards each turn. Start each combat Confused.
- Flavor: An eye of a fallen snecko. Much larger than you imagined.
- Rarity: Boss
- Class: Any

The **Snecko Eye** is a Boss Relic. You draw an additional 2 cards at the start of each turn, but begin each combat inflicted with the Confused debuff.

## Effect
- All cards drawn have their costs randomized from 0 to 3 Energy. See the Confused page for an exhaustive list of effects.
- The player is inflicted with Confused at the start of combat before the Clockwork Souvenir gives themArtifact. As a result, Confused is never blocked by the Clockwork Souvenir.
- If Confused is removed by the Orange Pellets, newly drawn cards for the rest of the combat will not have their costs randomized. However, any cards that had their costs changed already will keep those costs for the rest of combat. 
- Placing a card into your hand with a card like Seek or Secret Weapon does *not* count as drawing, and will not randomize the cards' costs. This includes cards created during combat such as Shiv and cards copied with Nightmare or Dual Wield.

## Tips
- The Snecko Eye's extra 2 cards per turn provides enormous value on its own.
- Each card drawn has a 25% chance of costing 0, increasing the value of effects that draw extra cards.
- Every card's average energy cost is 1.5 with Snecko Eye. Consequently, cards costing 2 or more have better value than they normally do, and cards costing 1 or less have worse value than usual. However, many low-cost cards are still valuable enough to take with Snecko Eye.
- The possibility of drawing 0-cost cards greatly complicates the analysis of how the Snecko Eye impacts your energy. Assuming 3 energy, 7 card draw, and prioritizing playing lower cost cards, the average number of card plays per turn is 3.83.
- The Snecko Eye works especially well with the Gambling Chip to clear out high-cost or low-value cards on turn 1 and draw to replace them.
- Since the Snecko Eye commonly results in unspent Energy at the end of turns, it works very well with Ice Cream to conserve that Energy. This also means that you can ignore playing high-cost and low-value cards, even if you do have enough Energy to play them.
- Snecko Eye is very strong with many cards; among them are Bullet Time, Nightmare , Meteor Strike and Bludgeon. These cards take advantage of Snecko Eye's randomized cost and draw in varying ways.
- Snecko Eye doesn't affect cards that cost X, which can make them a bit more valuable as it provides a place to spend Energy that the Snecko Eye would otherwise waste.
- Cards with variable cost (Masterful Stab, Blood for Blood, and Force Field) will have their costs replaced by randomized costs when drawn. Their cost-reducing effects only apply if the conditions are newly met while they are in your hand (e.g. Blood for Blood will have its cost randomized when drawn, but that new cost can be reduced if you lose HP while it is in your hand). Their costs will be randomized again when next drawn.
- Corruption overrides Confused entirely, and Skills will always cost 0. 
    - Swivel does this to a lesser extent, making all Attacks cost 0 until an Attack is played. Once an Attack is played, any Attacks in hand that had a cost greater than 0 will revert to that cost.

# Snecko Skull

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Snecko_Skull

**Infobox:**
- Name: Snecko Skull
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/d/d7/SnakeSkull.png/revision/latest?cb=20190923235544
- Description: Whenever you apply Poison, apply an additional 1 Poison.
- Flavor: A snecko skull in pristine condition. Mysteriously clean and smooth, dirt and grime fall off inexplicably.
- Rarity: Common
- Class: Silent

It increases each *individual * Poison stack by +1.
## Interactions
- Each Noxious Fumes turn is +1 poison to all enemies. Playing multiple Noxious Fumes will still only grant +1 poison. So a Noxious Fumes of 4 would only deal +5 poison per turn.
- Each Bouncing Flask attack is +1 poison (+3 in total, or +4 in total when upgraded.)
- Each Envenom strike is +1 poison (granting +2 poison each in total, effectively doubling Envenom). This is counted separately, so a non-upgraded Poisoned Stab with one Envenom active will inflict a total of 6 poison (3 base poison +1 Snecko, then 1 Envenom poison +1 Snecko).
- When playing Catalyst, +1 poison is added AFTER the current poison is doubled/tripled. For example, if your enemy has 8 poison currently, and you play an upgraded catalyst, they'll have 25 poison (8*3+1).

# Spheric Guardian

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Spheric_Guardian

**Infobox:**
- Name: Spheric Guardian
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/9/91/Spheric-guardian-pretty.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20180106093658
- HP: 20 (+40 Block)
- In Party With: Nothing; Sentry; 2 Shapes(Act 3)
- Debut Act: Act 2
- Powers: Barricade; Artifact 3
- Name: Barricade
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/a/af/Icon_Barricade.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202161410
- Description: Block is not removed at the start of its turn.
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: None

**Spheric Guardian** is a Monster found in Acts 2 and 3 of the Spire. Its low HP of 20 is counteracted by its high amounts of Block, which it will continue to build up as the fight continues. In order to ensure its tankiness, it starts with Barricade as a buff and 3 charges of Artifact.

## Pattern
Always starts with Activate, then uses Attack/Debuff. Afterwards, alternates between Slam and Harden every turn.
| Name | Intent | Effect | Asc 2+ | Asc 17+ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Slam |  | Deal 10 x 2 damage. | Deal 11 x 2 damage. | Deal 11 x 2 damage. |
| Activate |  | Gain 25 Block. | Gain 25 Block. | Gain 35 Block. |
| Harden |  | Deal 10 damage, gain 15 Block. | Deal 11 damage, gain 15 Block. | Deal 11 damage, gain 15 Block. |
| Attack/Debuff |  | Deal 10 damage, apply 5 Frail. | Deal 11 damage, apply 5 Frail. | Deal 11 damage, apply 5 Frail. |

## Tips
- Although the constant Blocking can make this enemy seem like an impenetrable wall, Poison can be used to ignore it and attack the HP directly, so long as all 3 charges of Artifact are cleared first.
- Bag of Marbles, Red Mask, and Twisted Funnel can strip off 1 stack of Artifact for each relic.
- The Frail debuff this enemy applies can be very dangerous when combined with the large amounts of damage it can dish out. If you can apply debuffs fast enough, applying a Weak debuff or using a card such as Disarm can do a great deal to mitigate these attacks.
    - In contrast, if you have Turnip or Orange Pellets, the Frail debuff can be completely negated. Thus, gaining enough Block for the enemy's attacks is less challenging.
- If this enemy is accompanied by other enemies, it is usually worth killing the other enemies first. While the Spheric Guardian will continue to build Block, dealing with more than one attack while Frail can be overwhelming.
- If playing as the Defect, a very useful card in this fight is Melter, which will remove the enemy's Block and deal significant damage, almost effectively ending the fight.
- If playing as the Watcher, Judgment will instantly kill it.

Melter.png|Spheric Guardian as seen in the Melter card art.

-The **Spire Shield and Spire Spear **is the Elite encounter always fought in Act 4. Their block, damage, and Surrounded mechanic make them a tough adversary.

The player starts combat between the two enemies, facing right, and can use targeting cards or potions to face the opposite direction. Additionally, using a Smoke Bomb Potion will not work until one of the two enemies is killed.

## Spire Shield
Despite its lower HP, the Spire Shield is the tankier of the two enemies. Its Smash attack may be dangerous in the beginning of the fight, but Spire Spear will begin to hit much harder.

### Pattern
1. 50% chance of using Bash then Fortify or Fortify then Bash.
1. Uses Smash.
1. Repeat.
| Name | Intent | Effect | Asc 3+ | Asc 18+ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bash |  | Deals 12 damage. If the player has at least 1 Orb slot, has a 50% chance to apply -1 Focus. Otherwise, applies -1 Strength. | Deals 14 damage. If the player has at least 1 Orb slot, has a 50% chance to apply -1 Focus. Otherwise, applies -1 Strength. | Deals 14 damage. If the player has at least 1 Orb slot, has a 50% chance to apply -1 Focus. Otherwise, applies -1 Strength. |
| Fortify |  | All enemies gain 30 Block. | All enemies gain 30 Block. | All enemies gain 30 Block. |
| Smash |  | Deals 34 damage. Gains Block equal to its damage output. | Deals 38 damage. Gains Block equal to its damage output. | Deals 38 damage. Gains 99 Block. |

## Spire Spear
Spire Spear, despite having more HP than Spire Shield, is the more offensive of the two enemies and will buff its Strength throughout the fight to hit even harder.

### Pattern
1. Uses Burn Strike
1. Uses Skewer
1. 50% Chance of using either Burn Strike then Piercer or Piercer then Burn Strike
1. Repeat 2 through 4.

| Name | Intent | Effect | Asc 3+ | Asc 18+ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Burn Strike |  | Deals 5x2 damage. Adds 2 Burns into your discard pile. | Deals 6x2 damage. Adds 2 Burns into your discard pile. | Deals 6x2 damage. Adds 2 Burns on top of your draw pile. |
| Piercer |  | All enemies gain 2 Strength. | All enemies gain 2 Strength. | All enemies gain 2 Strength. |
| Skewer |  | Deals 10x3 damage. | Deals 10x4 damage. | Deals 10x4 damage. |

A buff associated with large slime-type enemies, most notably the Slime Boss. Any large slimes dropped to or below 50% health will get their turn interrupted, and will split into two smaller slimes as their new turn action.

The health of the new slimes is equal to the amount of health the parent slime had when it split, (e.g. the slime boss splitting at 60 HP will result in one Spike Slime (L) and one Acid Slime (L), each with 60 HP) and killing the parent before it can take its turn will prevent any additional slimes from being spawned.

# Spot Weakness

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Spot_Weakness

**Infobox:**
- Name: Spot Weakness
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/5/56/SpotWeakness.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016211045
- Class: Ironclad
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Cost: 1
- Effect: If the enemy intends to attack, gain 3 Strength.
- [Spot Weakness+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: If the enemy intends to attack, gain 4 Strength.

Spot Weakness is an Uncommon Skill for the Ironclad. If the target intends to attack, the player gains 3 Strength (4 Strength if the card is Upgraded).

Spot Weakness can still target enemies that don't intend to attack, but has no effect when played.

If the selected enemy's attack has some extra effect, such as the Blue Slaver's Rake attack, Spot Weakness will still grant Strength. It will also still grant Strength if the enemy's attack will do zero damage.

## Strategy
- Although the Runic Dome hides enemy intents, this card can help reveal if the enemy is attacking this turn, as it will either fail if they are not, or it will grant the player Strength. This is useful against non-deterministic enemies like Thieves, but it can also lead to a waste of Energy.

- The Strength gained from Spot Weakness is repeatable and lasts for the rest of the battle, which makes it an excellent enabler for Limit Break.

- The Strength bonus is more effective when combined with multi-attack cards like Sword Boomerang, Heavy Blade or Pummel.

- Spot Weakness is a strong utility card for defensive Block-heavy decks. It sets up future power turns while the player defends against incoming attacks.

- The card is more reliable than it initially appears, since most enemy turns are attacks. The times when it's inactive are also the turns that it's least useful - if the enemy doesn't intend to attack, the player can go all-out with attacks instead of playing defensive cards.

# Stack

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Stack

**Infobox:**
- Name: Stack
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/9/9f/Stack.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016203704
- Class: Defect

- Effect: Gain Block equal to the number of cards in your discard pile.
- [Stack+]
- Cost+: 1

CardAutobox
**Stack** is a common Skill for The Defect that grants Block, scaling with the number of cards in your Discard Pile.

Upgrading **Stack** adds 3 Block to the card's effect.

**Stack** doesn't count itself for its effect.

## Strategy
**Stack** is a powerful Block generator with high variance. As long as you don't draw it in your first hand of the deck, it's at least as strong as Defend. If you draw it in your third or later hand, it's more effective than Leap.

While Stack's effect scales with your deck's size, you don't need a huge deck to get big value. In a deck of only 20 cards, Stack has a 50% chance of providing 10 or more Block.

When playing Stack, carefully sequence your plays to maximize its value. Generally, Stack is strongest as your last play of the turn, but be careful not to empty your deck and reshuffle your discard pile!

# Stance

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Stance

Stances are a mechanic unique to the Watcher. 

## Mechanic

There are three Stances in the game: Calm, Wrath, and Divinity. There is also the lack of any Stance, or 'no Stance'. Changing from one Stance to another will be mechanically considered as *exiting* the old Stance, alongside *entering* the new one. Any action that includes either of these two processes is considered *changing* or *switching* your Stance.

These following cards interact with Stance changing in general:
- Flurry of Blows: After changing your Stance, returns from discard pile to your hand.
- Mental Fortress: After changing your Stance, gain Block.

Other characters can enter and exit Stances as well, provided that they have a means to do so.

## Calm
Upon leaving this Stance, gain .
### Cards
These cards allow you to enter Calm:
- Vigilance: Gain Block then enter Calm.
- Tranquility: Immediately enter Calm.
- Fear No Evil: After dealing damage, enter Calm if the target intends to Attack.
- Inner Peace: Enter Calm if you are not in Calm.
- Meditate: After choosing what to retain, enter Calm and end your turn.
These cards have interaction specifically for Calm:
- Inner Peace: If you are in Calm, draw cards.
- Like Water: At the end of your turn, if you are in Calm, gain Block.

### Others
- Teardrop Locket: Start each combat in Calm.
- Violet Lotus: Whenever you exit Calm, gain an additional ; effectively causes Calm to generate  upon exiting.
- Stance Potion: Gives you a choice to enter Calm.
## Wrath
Within this Stance, deal and receive double damage.
### Cards
These cards allow you to enter Wrath:
- Eruption: Deal damage, then enter Wrath. 
- Crescendo: Immediately enter Wrath.
- Indignation: Enter Wrath if you are not in Wrath.
- Simmering Fury: Enter Wrath at the beginning of the next turn.
- Tantrum: Deal damage, then enter Wrath.
These cards have interactions specifically for Wrath:
- Halt: Gain additional Block if you are in Wrath.
- Indignation: If you are in Wrath, apply Vulnerable to all enemies.
- Rushdown: Draw cards whenever you enter Wrath.
### Others
- Stance Potion: Gives you a choice to enter Wrath.

## Divinity
Upon entering this Stance, gain . While in this Stance, deal triple damage. Leave this Stance at the start of your next turn. Divinity can be entered by gaining 10 Mantra, consuming 10 Mantra in the process.
### Cards
- Blasphemy: Immediately enter Divinity without consuming Mantra.
### Other
- Ambrosia: Immediately enter Divinity.
## No Stance
The absence of a Stance. Leaving a Stance is still considered changing Stance even if you do not enter a new Stance, and will trigger Flurry of Blows and Mental Fortress.
### Cards
These cards allow you to exit your current Stance:
- Empty Body: Gain Block then exit your current Stance.
- Empty Fist: Deal damage then exit your current Stance. 
- Empty Mind: Draw cards then exit your current Stance.
Category:Game Mechanics
Category:Stance

# Status

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Status

**Statuses** are negative cards that are shuffled into your deck during combat. However, unlike Curses, they will be removed at the end of combat. Under normal circumstances, most statuses are Unplayable (with the exception of Slimed), and some impose an additional negative effect. They cannot be upgraded, with the exception of Burn.

Status cards can be added to your deck either through Monster attacks, or through an effect on a card or a Relic.

## Interactions
- Evolve: Whenever you draw a Status, draw 1(2) card(s).
- Fire Breathing: Whenever you draw a Status or Curse card, deal 6(10) damage to all enemies.
- Medical Kit: Lets you play Statuses, which will Exhaust them.

## Relics that create Status cards
- Mark of Pain: At the start of combat, add 2 Wounds to your draw pile.

## Cards that create Status cards

- Ironclad
    - Wild Strike: Deal 12(17) damage. Shuffle a Wound into your draw pile.
    - Reckless Charge: Deal 7(10) damage. Shuffle a Dazed into your draw pile.
    - Power Through: Add 2 Wounds to your hand. Gain 15(20) Block.
    - Immolate: Deal 21(28) damage to ALL enemies. Add a Burn into your discard pile.
- Defect
    - TURBO: Gain 2(3) . Add a Void into your discard pile.
    - Overclock: Draw 2(3) cards. Add a Burn into your discard pile.

## Enemies that create Status cards

### Monsters

- Acid Slime M and L - When using their Corrosive Spit (1 and 2 Slimeds to discard pile, respectively).
- Spike Slime M and L - When using their Flame Tackle (1 and 2 Slimeds to discard pile, respectively).
- Chosen - When the player uses non-attack cards while afflicted with Chosen's Hex debuff (1 Dazed to draw pile).

## Synergy
- Steam Barrier works well as a clutch source of Block. It gives a competent amount of block for zero energy. Works specially well on lower floors.
    - This card is particularly useful on an expensive turn. Use it with Boot Sequence or Chill to gains a significant amount of Block while spending the rest of your energy on other cards.
- Steam Barrier gets worse as the fight goes on. Either its Block is reduced significantly or enemy scales over it. Try to finish the fight as quickly as possible.
- Steam Barrier will be generated by Hello World with its base, maximum amount of Block. It can be use as a throwaway source of Block.
- Its Block is still affected by Dexterity. On a circumstance where you can reliably gain Dexterity, such as with Kunai or Reprogram, Steam Barrier can remain relevant throughout the fight.
- This is a rare occasion when the card does not work well with Echo Form, as its potency will diminish twice as fast.
- All for One can bring back Steam Barriers for emergency Block.

## Trivia
- Formerly named *Steam Power*.

# Strange Spoon

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Strange_Spoon

**Infobox:**
- Name: Strange Spoon
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/7/71/StrangeSpoon.png/revision/latest?cb=20200203154314
- Description: Cards which Exhaust when played will instead discard 50% of the time.
- Flavor: Staring at the spoon, it appears to bend and twist around before your eyes.
- Rarity: Shop
- Class: Any

The **Strange Spoon** is a Shop Relic. When playing a card that Exhausts itself, it will instead be sent to the discard pile as normal 50% of the time.

## Mechanics

- Cards Exhausted through effects other than their own will never be saved. Likewise, Ethereal cards will not be saved at the end of a turn when they Exhaust themselves. Deus Ex Machina is Unplayable, and its effect to Exhaust itself when drawn does not count as playing it, so it will not be saved.

- Cards played by Havoc and Omniscience temporarily gain the "Exhaust" effect, so the Strange Spoon can save these cards. However, if the card to be played is Unplayable (e.g. Wound, Tactician), it will Exhaust without being played, preventing the Strange Spoon from triggering.

- As of version 2.0, Strange Spoon interacts oddly with Omniscience. If the card played by Omniscience is saved by Strange Spoon, it will have the Exhaust effect for the rest of the combat, and will try to Exhaust every time it is played.Havoc does not have this issue.

- Although the in-game description claims that saved cards will discard, this is not entirely true. Instead, the card is simply placed in the discard pile as though it did not have the effect to Exhaust itself. This means that discard-related effects (e.g. Hovering Kite) will *not* trigger when the Strange Spoon prevents a card from Exhausting.

- Works with Corruption, allowing cards that cost 0 to be preserved, and played multiple times for free.

## Tips

- Remember that taking this relic isn't always advantageous.
    - Some effects (e.g. Dark Embrace, Dead Branch) *reward* you for Exhausting cards, and won't trigger if the Strange Spoon saves them.
    - Other cards (e.g. Shiv, Pride) you'll want to Exhaust, rather than having them remain to clutter your deck.
    - Statuses played with Medical Kit and Curses played with Blue Candle may be discarded instead of Exhausted.
- Because Apparition Exhausts when played and is incredibly powerful, it may be worthwhile to invest in buying a Strange Spoon if you have Apparitions, or in taking the Apparitions if you have Strange Spoon already. 

## Trivia
- This relic's flavor text references a popular stage magic trick known as spoon bending.
    - The practice itself was popularized by the magician Uri Geller, and since been associated with psychokinetic or paranormal abilities. It has been referenced in popular culture many time, such as a scene in The Matrix when a young boy bends a spoon to demonstrate the unreality of a computer simulation, and the evolutionary line of the Psychic-type [https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) Pokémon Abra, Kadabra, and Alakazam, who utilize spoons to amplify their psychokinetic capabilities.

# Strength

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Strength

**Infobox:**
- Name: Strength
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/8/8b/Strength.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202023757
- Description: Increases attack damage by X (per hit).
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: Intensity

Strength is a buff that increases damage dealt by Attacks. Each point of Strength gives +1 damage per hit. The strength resets at the end of combat (and doesn't change between turns by itself).

Bonus damage from Strength is added to the calculation first before other modifiers such as Vulnerable, Weak, Wrath, or Divinity.

Both the player characters and many enemy types are capable of gaining Strength.

It is possible to have negative stacks of Strength. For every negative stack, damage dealt is reduced by one per hit.

Strength is capped at 999 and -999.

## Sources
### Cards
#### Ironclad Cards
- Flex - 2 (4) Strength. At the end of your turn, lose 2(4) Strength.
- Inflame - 2 (3) Strength.
- Rupture - 1 (2) Strength whenever you lose HP from a card.
- Spot Weakness - 3 (4) Strength if target enemy intends to attack.
- Demon Form - 2 (3) Strength at the start of your turn.
- Limit Break - Doubles your Strength.
- Disarm - Enemy loses 2 (3) Strength.
#### Silent Cards
- Piercing Wail - All enemies lose 6 (8) Strength temporarily.
- Malaise - Enemy loses X (X+1) Strength.

#### Defect Cards
- Reprogram - 1 (2) Strength at the cost of 1 (2) Focus.
#### Watcher Cards
- Fasting - 3 (4) Strength, but reduces your  gain by 1.
- Wish - 3 (4) Strength, among two other options.
#### Colorless Cards
- J.A.X. - 2 (3) Strength at the cost of 3 HP.

### Relics
- Vajra - 1 Strength.
- Girya - Adds the  **Lift** option to Rest Site. Use to gain a permanent 1 Strength, up to 3 times per run.
- Shuriken - 1 Strength for every 3 Attack cards played in a single turn.
- Du-Vu Doll - 1 Strength for each Curse in your deck.
- Sling of Courage - 2 Strength at the start of each Elite combat.
- Mutagenic Strength - 3 Strength at the start each combat that is lost at the end of your turn.
- Brimstone - 2 Strength to the player and 1 Strength to all enemies at the start of your turn.
- Red Skull  - 3 Strength while your HP is below 50%.

### Potions
- Flex Potion - 5 (10) Strength. At the end of your turn, lose 5 (10) Strength.
- Strength Potion - 2 (4) Strength.
- Cultist Potion - 1 Strength at the end of each turn, from Ritual.

### Enemies

- Lagavulin - Reduces Dexterity and Strength by 1 (2) when using its Siphon Soul.
- Spire Shield - Reduces Strength by 1 when using its Bash (50% chance if player has at least 1 orb slot).

### Other

- Lethality modifier in Custom Mode: You and ALL enemies start each combat with 3 Strength.

## Enemies with Strength

### Monsters

- Cultist - From its Ritual power: Gains 3 (4) (5) Strength at the end of every turn.
- Jaw Worm - Gains Block and 3 (4) (5) Strength when using its Bellow. In act 3, all Jaw Worms gain the benefits of Bellow before the player's turn 1 begins.
- Red Louse - Gains 3 (4) Strength when using its Grow.
- Fungi Beast - Gains 3 (4) (5) Strength when using its Grow.
- Mad Gremlin - From its Angry power: Gains 1 (2) Strength when taking attack damage.
- Byrd - Gains 1 Strength when using its Caw.
- Chosen - Applies Weak and gains 3 Strength when using its Drain.
- Centurion & Mystic - ALL enemies gain 2 (3) (4) Strength when Mystic uses its Buff.
- Darkling - Gains 2 Strength when using its Harden on 17 and above. Loses all Strength when its HP reaches 0, relevant for when it revives with its Reincarnate.
- Orb Walker - From its Strength Up power: Gains 3 (5) Strength at the end of every turn. (Gets no additional Strength at 2.)
- The Maw - Gains 3 (5) Strength when using its Drool. (Gets no additional Strength at 2.)
- Transient - From its Shifting power: Upon losing HP, loses that much Strength until the end of the turn.

### Elites

- From the Elite Buffs given by the Emerald Key: 25% chance for a Super Elite to have additional Strength, equal to the current Act number + 1.
- Gremlin Nob - From its Enrage power: Gains 2 (3) Strength whenever you play a Skill.
- Gremlin Leader - Gains Block and 3 (4) (5) Strength when using its Encourage.
- Taskmaster - Deals damage, shuffles Wounds, and gains 1 Strength when using its Scouring Whip on 18 and above (has no other moves, so applies every turn).
- Spire Spear - ALL enemies gain 2 Strength when using its Piercer.

### Bosses

- Hexaghost - Gains Block and 2 (3) Strength when using its Inflame.
- Bronze Automaton - Gains Block and 3 (4) Strength when using its Boost.
- The Champ - Gains 2 (3) (4) Strength when using its Gloat. Clears all debuffs and gains 6 (9) (12) Strength when using its Anger (the turn after Champ drops below 50% HP).
- The Collector and Torch Head - ALL enemies gain Block and 3 (4) (5) Strength when Collector uses its Buff.
- Awakened One - Starts combat with 1 Strength at 4 and 2 Strength at 19. From its Curiosity power: Gains 1 (2) Strength whenever you play a Power card. Keeps all current Strength after reviving with its Rebirth.
- Time Eater - From its Time Warp power: Ends your turn and gains 2 Strength every 12 cards you play this combat.
- Donu and Deca - ALL enemies gain 3 Strength when Donu uses its Circle of Power.
- Corrupt Heart - Removes all negative Strength from itself, then gains 2 Strength plus an additional buff when using its Buff. This additional buff is 10 Strength at turn 13, and 50 Strength at turn 16 and every 3rd turn after.

### Other

- Philosopher's Stone: ALL enemies start each combat with 1 Strength.
- Lethality modifier in Custom Mode: You and ALL enemies start each combat with 3 Strength.

**Sunder** is an Uncommon Attack for The Defect.  It deals a lot of damage for a pricey Energy cost, but if this attack kills the target enemy, the energy is refunded.  When Upgraded, it deals an additional 8 damage.

## Usage
**Sunder** revolves around elimination. It can be recognised as a lesser Bludgeon, but is less rare, and killing an enemy with it regains its full cost. Generally, it's a good card for normal encounters with multiple enemies, and thus it's never too late to get your hands on one. Sunder should be upgraded as soon as possible, because upgrading heightens the “finishing line” to 32, thus allowing higher chances to regain its cost. Trip or Beam Cell can further increase it to 48, which is enough to defeat many monsters in one shot, even in The Beyond.

# Sundial

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Sundial

**Infobox:**
- Name: Sundial
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/1/15/Sundial.png/revision/latest?cb=20200203151421
- Description: Every 3 times you shuffle your draw pile, gain 2 Energy.
- Flavor: "Early man's foolish obsession with time caused them to look to the sky for guidance, hoping for something permanent." - Zoroth
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Class: Any

The Sundial is an Uncommon Relic. Every 3 times you shuffle your draw pile, you immediately gain 2 Energy.

Every time your discard pile is shuffled into your draw pile, including by effects such as Deep Breath and Reboot, the Sundial gains 1 charge. Charges persist between combats. 

The Sundial is arguably one of the stronger uncommon relics; it's very powerful in many infinite damage combos. In addition, it is activated more often in thinner decks, similarly to The Abacus.

The general requirement for an infinite using the Sundial is:

- Have a deck with few enough cards that the entire deck can be held in hand at once
- Be able to do the following repeatedly using 2 or less Energy:
    - Draw 1+ cards, 3 times (example: Pommel Strike+ or Shrug It Off). Essentially, the player needs 2 cards, with a total energy cost of 2 or less, that draw 3 cards between themselves. 
    -     - Deal any amount of damage

This works because the Sundial has a weird property when combined with cards that draw multiple cards at once. If the player has an empty draw pile, a single card in their discard pile, and they play an effect that draws 2 cards, the draw pile will be shuffled *twice*. This is what allows Pommel Strike+, Shrug It Off and Sundial to go infinite, for example.

- Cost: 2
- Effect: Gain 8 Block. The next Attack you play costs 0.
- [Swivel+]
- Cost+: 2
- Effect+: Gain 11 Block. The next Attack you play costs 0.
- Name: Free Attack Power
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/b/b4/Icon_Swivel.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202164051
- Description: The next X Attacks you play costs 0.
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: Counter

CardAutobox
**Swivel** is a Skill for the Watcher. It gives 8 Block (11 if Upgraded), as well as 1 stack of the Free Attack Power buff, which makes the next Attack played cost 0 Energy.

## Mechanics

- Free Attack Power buff is a stackable buff that makes all Attacks cost 0, and 1 stack is removed each time an Attack is played. Multiple stacks can be gained by playing Swivel multiple times without playing any Attacks. 
    - Even if the Attack played already costs 0 (e.g. Flurry of Blows), a stack of Free Attack Power is still used up.
- Free Attack Power does not expire at the end of the turn.
- When using an Attack that costs X with Free Attack Power, X is still equal to current Energy. However, no Energy is spent after playing the card. 

## Tips

- Swivel is already quite Energy-efficient when using it with an Attack that costs 1, since it gains Block and also attacks for a total of 2 Energy. It becomes much more powerful when used with high-cost Attacks, such as Ragnarok.
    - As a result, Swivel can also fit well into a deck using the Snecko Eye.
Watcher Card Navbox

**Sword Boomerang** is an Attack card for the Ironclad. It deals 3 damage to random enemy 3 times.  Each target is picked randomly from live targets for each attack.  As a Common card, it can be found as a reward after combats.

Upon upgrade, it attacks one more time.

## Interactions

- As a multi-hit attack, it benefits three times from Strength bonuses (four times when upgraded).

## Trivia
- This card is possibly a reference to Disney's Hercules. During the training montage with Philoctetes, Hercules bends his sword into a boomerang, cutting off the heads of many training dummies.

# Talk to the Hand

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Talk_to_the_Hand

**Infobox:**
- Name: Talk to the Hand
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/f/f8/TalktotheHand.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20190918180936
- Class: Watcher
- Type: Attack
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Cost: 1
- Effect: Deal 5 damage. Whenever you attack this enemy, gain 2 Block. Exhaust.
- [Talk to the Hand+]
- Cost+: 1
- Effect+: Deal 7 damage. Whenever you attack this enemy, gain 3 Block. Exhaust.
- Name: Block Return
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/a/ac/Icon_TalktotheHand.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202164052
- Description: Whenever you attack this enemy, gain X Block.
- Type: Debuff
- Stacking; Behavior: Intensity

CardAutobox 
**Talk to the Hand** is an Uncommon Watcher Attack card. It is a single target hit dealing a modest 5(7) damage which exhausts itself afterwards. However, it applies a debuff to the attacked enemy which returns 2(3) Block to the player on future attacks against that enemy. Since the block return debuff is based on each hit on the debuffed enemy, attacks which hit the debuffed enemy more than once or hit multiple debuffed enemies will give multiple instances of Block. This makes Talk to the Hand an unusual attack which usually serves to defend the player on the played turn and after, more than to deal any meaningful damage. 

Talk to the Hand works well with multi-hitting cards like Flying Sleeves, Bowling Bash, Tantrum, Ragnarok, or Conjure Blade, as well as hand-returning cards such as Flurry of Blows or Weave. It also allows Wave of the Hand to apply its Weak debuff multiple times for extra defensive power. 

The block effect, like all debuffs, is blocked by Artifact, and can be removed by bosses, such as The Champ and Time Eater, with debuff clearing actions.

# Taskmaster

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Taskmaster

**Infobox:**
- Name: Taskmaster
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/2/26/Slaver-leader-pretty.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20180110054116
- HP: 54-60; 57-64 (Ascension 8+)
- In Party With: Blue Slaver + Red Slaver; Gremlin Nob (The Colosseum event)
- Debut Act: Act 2
- Powers: None

The Taskmaster is an enemy encountered in Act 2, either as an Elite encounter, or in the second fight of the Colosseum event. In the Elite encounter, he is accompanied by a Blue Slaver and a Red Slaver. In the Colosseum encounter, he is accompanied by a Gremlin Nob.

## Pattern
| Name | Intent | Effect | Asc 3+ | Asc 18+ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Scouring Whip |  | Deal 7 damage, shuffle 1 Wound into the discard pile. | Deal 7 damage, shuffle 2 Wounds into the discard pile. | Deal 7 damage, gain 1 Strength, and shuffle 3 Wounds into the discard pile. |

## Tips
- The large number of Wounds he shuffles in your deck can be very troublesome, especially on higher Ascension levels. If playing as the Ironclad, this can be countered by Evolve and/or Fire Breathing. Other characters can counter the Wounds by exhausting them or using the Medical Kit relic.
- If playing as the Silent, Piercing Wail is extremely useful, as all enemies will attack most turns. For other characters, Dark Shackles has a similar effect.
- It may be best to kill the Red Slaver in the back first, so that he can't use his Entangle ability to prevent you from attacking. In addition, the Vulnerable he applies is very dangerous when 3 enemies are attacking.
    - An exception is when your deck is already close to going infinite (e.g. Watcher with Rushdown, Silent with Acrobatics) , it may be wise to kill Taskmaster directly, as in decks that rely on going infinite, dealing with Wounds becomes much more important.
- After killing the Red Slaver, it may be a good idea to kill the Blue Slaver next, as it applies Weak, which will actively make your attacks less effective. However, on Ascension 18 and higher, it may be preferable to kill the Taskmaster earlier due to his Strength gain.
- A powerful card that damages all enemies such as Whirlwind, Immolate and Electrodynamics is extremely useful in this fight.
