# Technical Issues and Troubleshooting

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Technical_Issues_and_Troubleshooting

## Technical Issues

### In-Game Letters/Numbers Disappearing.
This indicates that the computer is low on memory/out of memory (**RAM** or **video memory**).
- Restart the game.
- Close other programs.
- Lower in-game settings.

### Game Saves Are Weird (No/Old Ascension Levels. Run Is Not Saved)
This might be because **Steam Cloud save file** is **interfering** with your local save file. 
- Run **SlayTheSpire.exe** as **administrator**:
    - Right-click on **SlayTheSpire.exe **.
    - Choose **Properties**.
    - Choose **Compatibility tab**.
    - Choose **Settings**.
    - Check **Run this program as an administrator** 
    - Now **SlayTheSpire.exe** should be run with **administrator** rights every time.

- To disable **Steam Cloud**, do the following:
    - Open **Steam**.
    - Browse your **Library**.
    - Right-click on **Slay the Spire**.
    - Choose **Properties**.
    - Select **Update** tab
    - Choose **Verify Integrity of Game Files**.
    - Under **Steam Cloud**, uncheck **Enable Steam Cloud synchronization for Slay the Spire**.
      - Your **Steam Cloud save files** can be found in *(...)\Steam\userdata\\646570\remote*.

### The Game Launches and the MegaCrit logo appears, But Nothing Else
- Disable **overlays**, like Discord, NVidia ShadowPlay/Geforce Experience/GSync, Duet (screen display program).

### The Game Does Not Load At All
The following are basic methods that should be attempted first in case Slay the Spire does not load at all.

#### Verify the integrity of game files.
- Open **Steam**.
- Browse your **Library**.
- Right-click on **Slay the Spire**.
- Choose **Properties**.
- Select **Local Files** tab.
- Choose **Verify Integrity of Game Files**.

#### Update audio/video drivers.
- Open **Device Manager** in Windows:
    - **Updating audio device:**
      - Choose **Sound, Video and Game controllers**.
      - Right-click on **your audio device**.
      - Choose **Update driver**.
      - Choose **Search automatically for updated driver software**.
        - Alternatively, if you have found a more up-to-date driver yourself, you can select **Browse my computer for driver software**.
    - **Updating video card:**
      - Choose **Sound, Video and Game controllers**.
      - Right-click on **your video card**.
      - Choose **Search automatically for updated driver software**.
        - Alternatively, if you have found a more up-to-date driver yourself, you can select **Browse my computer for driver software**.

If both failed to fix the problem, please continue to Troubleshooting Slay the Spire.

### Troubleshooting Slay the Spire

- Go to the **install folder of Slay the Spire**.
    - It should be at *...\Steam\steamapps\common\SlayTheSpire*
      - If you are not sure, you can browse the folder following these steps:
        - Open **Steam**.
        - Browse your **Library**.
        - Right-click on **Slay the Spire**.
        - Choose **Properties**.
        - Select **Local Files** tab.
        - Choose **Browse Local Files**.
        - This should open File Explorer window for *...\Steam\steamapps\common\SlayTheSpire*
- Run **SlayTheSpireTroubleshoot.bat**.

| macOS |
| --- |
| Instead of in installation package, **SlayTheSpireTroubleshoot.bat** can be found in *~/Library/Application Support/Steam/steamapps/common/SlayTheSpire/SlayTheSpire.app/Contents/MacOS* |

Running **SlayTheSpireTroubleshoot.bat** should produce one of the two results:

#### SlayTheSpireTroubleshoot.bat Launches The Game And It Works.
This often means you have to run **SlayTheSpire.exe** as an **administrator**.
- Right-click on **SlayTheSpire.exe**.
- Choose **Properties**.
- Choose **Compatibility tab**.
- Choose **Settings**.
- Check **Run this program as an administrator**. 
Now **SlayTheSpire.exe** should be run with **administrator** rights every time.

#### SlayTheSpireTroubleshoot.bat Produces An Error And The Game Does Not Launch
Continue to Slay the Spire Troubleshoot Errors.

### Slay the Spire Troubleshoot Errors

Observe your **troubleshoot.log** to pinpoint the problem. You can find the log in *(...)\SlayTheSpire\sendToDevs\troubleshoot.log*. See what is in  '''**troubleshoot.log** and follow the solution accordingly.

| macOS |
| --- |
| The install files for SlayTheSpire can be found as follows: - Open **Steam**. - Browse your **Library**. - Right-click on **Slay the Spire**. - Choose **Properties**. - Select **Local Files** tab. - Choose **Browse Local Files**. - Right-click on **SlayTheSpire app**. - Choose **Show Package Contents**. - Choose **Contents**. - Choose **Resources**. Apart from the lack of **SlayTheSpireTroubleshoot.bat**, there should be folders and files identical to the Windows version. |

#### System Locale Error
If the following is displayed in **troubleshoot.log**:

| ERROR Unable to invoke factory method in class org.apache.logging.log4j.core.appender.rolling.action.IfFileName for element IfFileName: ... Caused by: java.nio.charset.UnsupportedCharsetException: Cp65001 |
| --- |

This means you should change your **System Locale** to **English (United States). Do the following:
- Open Windows **Settings**.
- Choose **Time & Language**. 
- Choose **Language** tab.
- Choose **Administrative language settings. It should be by the top right side.
- New window called **Region** should appear, and is on the **Administrative** tab by default.
- Choose **Change system locale...**
- Choose **English (United States)**.
- Click **OK** on all windows to confirm changes.
You might need to **restart** before the effect takes place.

#### java.lang.UnsatisfiedLinkError
If the following is displayed in **troubleshoot.log**:

| java.lang.UnsatisfiedLinkError |
| --- |

See what follows, and follow the instruction accordingly.

If java.lang.UnsatisfiedLinkError is followed by a file path with weird characters, **for example:**

| C:\Users\??????\AppData\Local\Temp\libgdx??????\dc0f0009\lwjgl64.dll: Can't find dependent libraries |
| --- |

Notably, it ends with "Can't find dependent libraries". The "??????" in the file path may come in the form of boxes, or a name with a question mark in it, which is **not exactly the same to your Windows username**. It means that **your Windows account username contains special, non-ASCII characters**.

| Instruction for "Can't find dependent libraries" |
| --- |
|  |
| **ASCII characters** consist of the standard English alphabets and numbers (A-Z, a-z, 0-9). |
| What Should I Be Aware Of When Creating A Username? |
| --- |
| This error is usually caused by a username that uses a different character set (e.g. Chinese, Korean, Arabic) that are not **ASCII characters**, or a username that contains special accented letters (e.g. é, ç, ñ, ö, etc.). To avoid this error, you should avoid putting those characters in your username and use only **ASCII characters**. It is also strongly advised to avoid special characters (space, symbols such as !@#$%^&*()_-, etc.), since they might cause the same error as well. |

The main concern with this error is that you need an account with an appropriate name, containing only **ASCII characters**.

- Username Fix Mod
    - You can subscribe to Username Fix Mod by Alchyr.
    - Remember that, as per all mod, you need to subscribe to ModTheSpire first.
    - As of now, this method only works on Windows.
    - Be sure to read the detailed instructions on how to use this mod here.

- New User Profile
    - Make a new Windows user profile with the username only containing **ASCII characters**. Then use this user profile to play Slay the Spire.
      - Open Windows **Settings**.
      - Choose **Accounts**.
      - Choose **Family & other users** tab.
      - Choose **Add someone else to this PC**.
      - Choose '''I don't have this person's sign-in information**.
      - Choose **Add a user without a Microsoft account**.
      - Enter name, password and password hints.
        - Make sure that this name contains only **ASCII characters**.
      - Click **Next**. This should successfully create a new account on your computer.
      - **Log out** of your current account and **log into** the new account.

- Change Windows Account Username**
    - Change the name of your user profile to use **ASCII characters** only:
      - First, check if your Windows account username contains **special, non-ASCII characters** or not.
        - Press **Windows + R** to bring up the **Run** window.
        - Type in **cmd** and press **Enter** or click **OK**. This should launch Windows **Command Prompt**, a small black window.
        - * Alternatively, you can also search for **Command Prompt** in your taskbar **Search** bar.
        - In **Command Prompt**, type **echo %username%** and see what it returns.
        - This is your username used by the system. If this name contains **special, non-ASCII characters** characters (see above), you need to change it.
      - To change your user profile name, do the following.
        - Press **Windows + R** to bring up the **Run** window.
        - Type in **netplwiz** and press **Enter** or click **OK**. This should launch Windows **User Accounts** window.
        - Look for your account in the **Users** tab.
        - * It should be the one with the same name you got from checking your username with **echo %username%**.
        - Click on the account to select it.
        - Click **Properties.
        - Change the **Username** to something using only **ASCII characters**.
        - Click **Apply** and **OK**.
        - **Log out** of your account and then **log back in**.
        - * You can check whether the username has been changed correctly by doing **echo %username%** in the **Command Prompt** again.
        - Launch **Slay the Spire'*. Hopefully, it will create a correct folder and can access it.
    - If the *Users\* folder still shows the **old username**, and Slay the Spire **does not start** and **produces the same error message in the log**, we need to perform some additional steps (see also). Continue to Change Windows Account Username - Advanced below.

| WARNING |
| --- |
| The steps below are advanced as it requires **a change in the Registry**. Make a **backup** of your **Registry** and be *very careful* when changing something inside of it. **Perform these steps at your own risk!** |

- Change Windows Account Username - Advanced
    - **Log into** a **different administrator account**, as you cannot do the following changes when logged in on the same account. Create a new administrator account if necessary. This account can be deleted once you are done (see also).

| Creating A New Administrator Account |

This should successfully create a new account on your computer. - In **Settings** > **Accounts** > **Family & other users** you should now see the new account. - Select the account you want to make an administrator. - Under **Account type**, select **Administrator**. - Click **OK**. - **Log out** of your current account and **log into'* the new administrator account. |

:* Rename the *C:\Users\''** folder to the **new username**.

If java.lang.UnsatisfiedLinkError is followed by a **correct file path**, but with "Access is denied" at the end, **for example:**
| C:\Users\\dc0f0009\lwjgl64.dll: Access is denied |
| --- |

It means that **permissions for the files that are necessary to run the game might be restricted**.

| Instruction for "Access is denied" |
| --- |
| - Go to the mentioned path: *C:\Users\\AppData\Local\Temp\libgdx\dc0f0009\* - Check the **file permissions** of the **DLL files** in that folder (*lwjgl64.dll* and *OpenAL64.dll*): - **Right-click** the file. - Go to **Properties**. - Click on **Security tab**. - Click your **Windows username**. - Check in the **Permissions box** whether it has **check marks** on **Allow** for all entries (except for Special permissions, this one can be empty) - If you have checked and see that there are **check marks** that are **missing**: - Click **Edit... - select your **Windows username. - tick the **Allow** boxes for **all entries** (except for Special permissions). **—When Playing With Mods—** After the above, if you get the message "Could not connect to Steam": - Go to *C:\Users\\AppData\Local\Temp\steamworks4j\96ad60e5* - **Check the permissions** for *steam_api64.dll* and *steamworks4j64.dll*. - Adjust them if needed in the same way as described above for lwjgl64.dll and OpenAL64.dll. |
| Instruction for "rosetta error: /var/db/oah/.../libsteamworks4j.dylib.aot: attachment of code signature supplement failed: 1" |

# The Boot

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/The_Boot

**Infobox:**
- Name: The Boot
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/5/5c/Boot.png/revision/latest?cb=20200203150529
- Description: Whenever you would deal 4 or less unblocked Attack damage, increase it to 5.
- Flavor: When wound up, the boot grows larger in size.
- Rarity: Common
- Class: Any

**The Boot** is a Common Relic. Anytime an Attack would deal 4 or less unblocked damage, it deals 5 damage instead. 

The effect applies only to damage dealt by Attacks. It will *not* increase damage from other relics (Mercury Hourglass, Charon's Ashes), non-Attack cards that deal damage (Fire Breathing, Poison), or the Defect's Lightning and Dark Orbs.

## Interactions
- Positive
    - Riddle with Holes and Pummel deal much more damage, since they are many small hits. 
    - The Boot bypasses enemies' innate damage reduction, such as Byrd's Flight and Nemesis's Intangible.
    - Decks which utilize multiple low-damage 0 Energy Attacks (Shiv, Go for the Eyes) can especially benefit.
- Negative
    - Gaining Strength will quickly make The Boot obsolete.
    - Inflicting Vulnerable also makes The Boot obsolete. 
    - If an Attack would deal 0 damage due to negative Strength, The Boot will *not* increase the damage to 5.
    - Using Body Slam while having 0 Block will also occur in The Boot not increasing damage to 5.

## Trivia
The artwork for The Boot is a reference to Goomba's Shoe from the Mario Bros. franchise.

# The Champ

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/The_Champ

**Infobox:**
- Name: The Champ
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/9/9f/Champ.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20180910010541
- HP: 420; 440 9+
- In Party With: None
- Debut Act: Act 2
- Powers: None
- Name: Metallicize
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/3/35/Icon_Metallicize.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202163413
- Description: At the end of its turn, gain X block.
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: Intensity

-**The Champ** is one of the three bosses encountered at the end of Act 2.
## Pattern
### Phase 1
Always uses Taunt every 4 turns. On all other turns, has:
- 15% chance to Defensive Stance
- 15% chance to Gloat
- 25% chance to Face Slap
- 45% chance to Heavy Slash
Moves cannot be used twice in a row: If the previous move would be repeated, the move that comes after it in the list above is selected instead. For example, if the previous move was Gloat, there is now a 0% chance of Gloat and a 40% chance of Face Slap with all the other probabilities unchanged.

If Heavy Slash is used, its probability chance is added to Face Slap instead of Defensive Stance.

On Ascension, he will use Defensive Stance instead of Gloat. Defensive Stance can be cast at most twice per battle and subsequent casts are instead Gloats, regardless of ascension.

When HP drops below 50%, he will use Anger next turn and enter Phase 2.

### Phase 2
After using Anger, will use Execute immediately.

For the next two turns, selects random moves (same exact behavior as in Phase 1), then Executes again. Repeats this pattern (2 random moves, then Execute).

| Name | Intent | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Defensive Stance |  | Gains 15 Block and 5 Metallicize. |
| Gains 18 Block and 6 Metallicize. |  |  |
| Gains 20 Block and 7 Metallicize. |  |  |
| Face Slap |  | Deals 12 damage, applying 2 Frail and 2 Vulnerable. |
| Deals 14 damage, applying 2 Frail and 2 Vulnerable. |  |  |
| Taunt |  | Applies 2 Weak and 2 Vulnerable. |
| Heavy Slash |  | Deals 16 damage. |
| Deals 18 damage. |  |  |
| Gloat |  | Gains 2 Strength. |
| Gains 3 Strength. |  |  |
| Gains 4 Strength. |  |  |
| Execute |  | Deals 10 x 2 damage. |
| Anger |  | Removes all debuffs, gains 6 Strength. |
| Removes all debuffs, gains 9 Strength. |  |  |
| Removes all debuffs, gains 12 Strength. |  |  |
## Tips
Once the Champ uses his Phase 2 attacks, his strength will be very high, making his attacks do significantly more damage. Combined with the Frail and Vulnerable debuffs, the fight can quickly become very dangerous. Execute is a deadly attack; it can end up dealing damage in the twenties 2 times.

Generally, you want to spend the first half of the fight setting up, and then you want to very quickly kill the Champ once his HP drops below half.

Taunt is used on turn 4. Both Anger and Execute (from Phase 2) will override Taunt, letting you avoid the Weak debuff if you get his health below half of his max HP on turns 3 or 4. If you cannot burst this quickly (most decks cannot), avoid getting him angry on turns 5 and 6, as the weak effect makes it difficult for you burst properly through Phase 2, and likely means you will eat another Execute.

## Trivia

- The Champ is the owner of the Champion Belt, a Rare Relic for the Ironclad, and will recognize if you have it. He will say, "THATS MY BELT!!"
- A Slay the Spire 2 event called "The Round Tea Party" features The Champ, and reveals his name to be Sir Wygore.

## Gallery

File:WheelKick.png|The Champ as seen in the Wheel Kick card art.
File:PressurePoints.png|The Champ as seen in the Pressure Points card art.

# The Colosseum

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/The_Colosseum

**The Colosseum** is an event found exclusively in Act 2, but only appears in the top half of the act. You are abducted and forced to participate in an arena battle.

## Options

At the start of the event, there is only one option
- **[Fight]** Begins a battle with Blue Slaver and Red Slaver.

Once the battle is over, the following 2 options are given:
- **[COWARDICE]** Escape.
- **[VICTORY]** Begins a fight with a Taskmaster and a Gremlin Nob. 
    - The reward is 100 gold, 1 rare and 1 uncommon relics, and a standard card selection. 
    - Relics that triggers on Elites combat - Preserved Insect, Sling of Courage, and Slaver's Collar - also works on this part of this event. The only exception is Black Star, which has no effect whatsoever in this fight.

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| Thwack!!! |
| *You were knocked unconscious.* |
| *Groggy and with a* throbbing *head, you awaken to find yourself thrown in the center of a massive stadium with an overflowing audience of Slavers, Cultists, and other denizens of the City! * |
| *An armored giant with a golden crown bellows at you from atop,* |
| **Armored Giant:** "WE NOW BEGIN THE 4200TH COMBAT!!!!" |
| *A gate on the opposite side opens...* |
| After a battle with Blue Slaver and Red Slaver |
| **Armored Giant:** "WELL DONE, WEAKLING!" |
| *The giant mock claps whilst he riles up the crowd with exaggerated gestures.* |
| *Gold and confetti shower you!* |
| **Armored Giant:** "TIME FOR THE REAL CHALLENGE!!" |
| *The last battle left a small opening in the Colosseum’s wall, you can easily escape through there while everyone is distracted.* |
| *Do you stay and fight? * |

## Tips
- While the fight with the slavers is not optional, the second fight is completely optional. You can choose to opt out with **[COWARDICE]** if you are uncertain with facing powerful foes.
- Smoke Bomb may be used to avoid the confrontation with the slavers. It will be considered that you have finished the first battle, and the event will continue to the second part with **[COWARDICE]** and **[VICTORY]**.
- Gremlin Nob is powerful and gains Strength from skill cards played; it should be dispatched quickly. Taskmaster, on the other hand, can fill your discard pile with Wounds, but does less damage overall.

## Trivia
- The "armored giant with a golden crown" is possibly the Champ, one of the bosses of Act 2.

# The Divine Fountain

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/The_Divine_Fountain

**The Divine Fountain** is an event that can appear in Act 1, Act 2, and Act 3. You encounter a fountain of sacred water with a power to cleanse you of all Curses.
CategorY:Event
## Options
- **[Drink]** Remove all Curses from your deck.

- **[Leave]** Nothing happens.

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| *You come across shimmering water flowing endlessly from a fountain on a nearby wall.* |
| Drink |
| *As you drink the water, you feel a dark grasp loosen.* |
| Leave |
| *Unsure of the nature of this water, you continue on your way, parched.* |

## Strategy
- It may be advantageous to choose **[Leave]** instead of removing your curses if you have Du-Vu Doll, or have some other synergy (e.g. Pain and Rupture).
- Darkstone Periapt increases your max HP the moment you obtain a Curse, but provides no benefit for keeping them in your deck. You can remove all of them and retain your increased max HP.

## Notes
- This event will appear only if you have one or more Curse that can be removed from your deck.
- Necronomicurse, Curse of the Bell, and Ascender's Bane cannot be removed from your deck.

# The Guardian

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/The_Guardian

**Infobox:**
- Name: The Guardian
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/b/b0/The-guardian-atk-pretty.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20180110072016
- HP: 240; 250 9+
- In Party With: None
- Debut Act: Act 1
- Powers: Mode Shift 30; Mode Shift 35 9+ Mode Shift 40 19+

-**The Guardian** is one of the three bosses encountered at the end of Act 1.

## Pattern

### Offensive Mode
Will always perform the pattern Charging Up, Fierce Bash, Vent Steam, and then Whirlwind. When returning from Defensive Mode, the next attack will be Whirlwind, and then continues the pattern as normal. 

Its Mode Shift status reduces in number equal to health it has lost. Once it reaches 0, it will shift into Defensive Mode, interrupting any previous intentions and instantly changing its intent to Defensive Mode. 

In addition, shifting back to Offensive Mode will add 10 to Mode Shift.
| Name | Intent | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Charging Up |  | Gains 9 Block. |
| Fierce Bash |  | Deals 32 damage. |
| Deals 36 damage. |  |  |
| Vent Steam |  | Inflicts 2 Weak and 2 Vulnerable (in that order). |
| Whirlwind |  | Deals 5 x 4 damage. |
### Defensive Mode
Immediately gains 20 Block when shifting to Defensive Mode. Will perform the pattern Defensive Mode, Roll Attack, and Twin Slam. Will lose Sharp Hide when switching to Offensive Mode. Also note that the damage done by Sharp Hide can be blocked, so don't be too afraid to attack.

Sharp Hide works similarly to Thorns, except it activates when you play attack cards, not when you hit the enemy. For example, using a Twin Strike will activate it only once, and using a Skewer at 0 energy will also activate it once.
| Name | Intent | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Defensive Mode |  | Gain 3 Sharp Hide. |
| Gain 4  Sharp Hide. |  |  |
| Roll Attack |  | Deals 9 damage. |
| Deals 10 damage. |  |  |
| Twin Slam |  | Deals 8 x 2 damage, removes Sharp Hide and shifts back to Offensive mode. |

## Tips
Compared to the other Act 1 bosses, The Guardian is often considered the easiest of them, due to its mechanic that it will always interrupt its intent and change into gaining block upon receiving enough damage. Most decks will have an easy time simply focusing on doing as much direct damage as possible, so it will be interrupted just before it would release a Fierce Bash or Whirlwind. Manage your cards so you will have lots of damage during Offensive Mode and some Block during Defensive Mode so you don't get damaged as much if you want to attack while it has Thorns.

Poison will proc mode shift and avoid thorns, and as such is very effective against this boss.

SpotWeakness.png|The Guardian as seen in the Spot Weakness card art.

# The Joust

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/The_Joust

**The Joust** is an event found exclusively in Act 2. A knight settles the score with the murderer of his pet. He tells you to bet on who you think will emerge victorious.

## Options

There is no option to avoid betting.

- **[Murderer]** Bet 50 Gold - 70%: win 100 Gold. 

- **[Owner] **Bet 50 Gold - 30%: win 250 Gold.

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| *As you make your way through the large buildings you come across a long narrow bridge and spot knights on either side, facing one another. You approach…* |
| **Knight:** "HALT!" |
| *A knight forcefully gestures you to stop with its giant lance.* |
| **Knight:** *"Today is the day I must settle the score with the murderer of my beloved pet, Noodles. Until then, you may not pass."* |
| **Knight:** ''"Fellow witness, why don't you bet on who you think will emerge victorious?"* |
| Murderer |
| **Knight:** *"I can't believe you're betting against Noodles!"* |
| *Furious, he clamps down his helmet and rushes towards his nemesis.* |
| Owner |
| **Knight:** *"Give me strength, Noodles!"* |
| *Clamping down his helmet, the knight charges forward.* |
| Watch |
| *CRASH!!!* *KLAAAANG!* |
| *POW!* |
| The outcome |
| The murderer wins |
| The bet |
| Losing the bet |

## Strategy
By looking into the expected value of both outcomes, it's not hard to calculate that choosing the murderer will yield an EV of 20 Gold (100*0.7-50=20), while choosing owner will yield an EV of 25 Gold (250*0.3-50=25). Statistically, choosing owner will be more beneficial in the long run. HOWEVER, EV does not apply in singular events. In each run, choosing the murderer is generally a safer choice, as it's much more likely to give you Gold instead of just losing 50 Gold. If you are short on Gold (e.g. a little higher than 50), it may be an option to bet on the 250 Gold gain, as losing the Gold just changes your strategy to avoiding shops altogether.

## Notes
- Ectoplasm means you can't win, but you still have to bet, making it a guaranteed loss of 50 gold.

# The Library

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/The_Library

**The Library** is an event found exclusively in Act 2. Weary from the travel, you enter a peaceful library with books and cozy chairs.

## Options
*Numbers in parentheses are for Ascension 15 or higher.*

- **[Read]** Choose 1 of 20 cards to add to your deck.
- **[Sleep]** Heal 33% (20%)  of your max HP.

All card choices are the same color as your character's class and are non-upgraded (unless you have Toxic Egg, Molten Egg, or Frozen Egg}.

After choosing **[Read]**, you cannot go back and choose **[Sleep]**. However, you can access a cancel button by bringing up the Map, Deck, or Settings screen and then exiting that screen; clicking the cancel button allows you to progress without adding any card to your deck.

The cards for **[Read]** are affected by the current rarity rate, but do not affect it: If you haven't seen a rare card for a while, each of the cards will have a high chance of being rare, but the event won't reset your rare chance.

Unlike resting at the campfire, the **[Sleep]** effect is unaffected by Regal Pillow, does not trigger Dream Catcher, and can be chosen even with Coffee Dripper.

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| *You come across an ornate building which appears abandoned.* |
| *A plaque that has been torn free from a wall is on the floor. It reads, "THE LIBRARY".* |
| *Inside, you find countless rows of scrolls, manuscripts, and books.* |
| *You pick one and cozy yourself into a chair for some quiet time.* |
| Sleep |
| *Reading is for chumps.* |
| *You doze off in a comfy chair instead.* |
| *Zzz... zzz... ..Zz....* |
| *You wake up feeling refreshed.* |
| Read |
| Possible story #1 |
| *Satisfying.* |
| Possible story #2 |
| *Fascinating.* |
| Possible story #3 |
| *Unsettling.* |
## Trivia
- When choosing **[Read]**, the event will reference one out of 3 written works:
    - Story #1 references Worm by John C. McCrae.
    - Story #2 references The Martian by Andy Weir.
    - Story #3 references Wool by Hugh Howey.

# The Maw

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/The_Maw

**Infobox:**
- Name: The Maw
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/f/fa/The-maw-pretty.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20180110054128
- HP: 300
- In Party With: None
- Debut Act: 3
- Powers: None

**The Maw** is an Act 3 encounter. Its scaling over time both through buffing and its attacks increasing in intensity combined with its big health pool can make it a threat for decks with poor offense. Its scaling takes a particularly long time to ramp up to dangerous levels, however.

## Pattern
Always starts with Roar. 

After using Roar or Drool, the Maw has a 50/50 chance of using Slam or Nom its next turn.

After using Slam, the Maw has an 50/50 chance of using Drool or Nom its next turn.

After using Nom, the Maw will always use Drool.
| Name | Intent | Effect | Asc 2+ | Asc 17+ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Roar |  | Applies 3 Weak and 3 Frail. | Applies 3 Weak and 3 Frail. | Applies 5 Weak and 5 Frail. |
| Drool |  | Gains 3 Strength. | Gains 3 Strength. | Gains 5 Strength. |
| Slam |  | Deals 25 damage. | Deals 30 damage. | Deals 30 damage. |
| Nom |  | Deals 5 x T* damage. | Deals 5 x T* damage. | Deals 5 x T* damage. |
*T is equal to the total number of turns the combat has lasted, divided by 2 and rounded up.

## Tips
- While large damage cards such as Bludgeon may seem useful for whittling on its large health pool, forms of scaling like Demon Form or Creative AI work just as well, if not better than, large amounts of damage.
- Poison decks supported by Catalyst or that dish out high amounts of Poison quickly are also effective. However, Noxious Fumes alone is probably not enough to overcome the Maw's scaling attacks.

## Trivia
- Based on its appearance, it is highly probable that the Maw is, in some way, related to Jaw Worm.

# The Nest

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/The_Nest

**The Nest** is an event found exclusively in Act 2. You join a line of several robed characters entering a cathedral, seemingly performing a ritual of some sorts.

## Options

*Numbers in parentheses are for Ascension 15 or higher.*

- **[Smash and Grab]** Obtain 99 (50) Gold.

- **[Stay in Line]** Obtain Ritual Dagger. Lose 6 HP.

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| *A long line of hooded figures can be seen entering an unassuming cathedral.* |
| *Naturally, you join the line and are quickly surrounded by Cultists!* |
| *They ignore you as they gleefully* chant *and wave their weapons around.* |
| **Cultists:** "MURDER!! MURDER MURDER!!" |
| **Cultists:** *"CAW CAW CAAAAAWWW!"* |
| **Cultists:** "MURDER! MURDER MUURDER!!" |
| **Cultists:** *"CAAW CAW CAAAAAAWW!!"* |
| *You eye a Donation Box... |
| Smash and Grab |
| *They didn't even notice.* |
| Stay in Line |
| *You decide to stay in line (out of fear) to see what will happen.* |
| *Eventually, you are face-to-face with the leader. A well-dressed cultist hands you an Ornate Dagger. Like the others before you, you slash your forearm and let the blood drip into a misshapen bowl.* |
| *The cultists* chant *and* holler *for you!* |
| **Cultists:** *"CAAW CAW CAAAAAAWW!!"* |
| *You chant, too. Why not?'' |

## Strategy
This is one of the few events with no heavy downside. Both options are beneficial in some way.

- **[Smash and Grab]** grants a considerable amount of gold. Unless you have Ectoplasm, more gold obtained is always useful.

- **[Stay in Line]**, at a negligible cost of 6 HP, grants you Ritual Dagger, an infinite-scaling card with low cost and good base damage.
    - The card is particularly useful on the Watcher, as Wrath and Divinity allows her to multiply the card's damage, allowing an easy killing blow with the card. Meditate can also help bring the card back for a guaranteed Fatal turn.

# The Ssssserpent

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/The_Ssssserpent

**The Ssssserpent** is an Event found exclusively in Act 1. You come across a grinning serpent that tempts you to give in to your greed.

## Options

*Numbers in parentheses are for Ascension 15 or higher.*

- **[Agree]** Receive 175 (150) Gold. Become Cursed - Doubt.

- **[Disagree]** Nothing happens.

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| *You walk into a room to find a large hole in the ground. As you approach the hole, an enormous serpent creature appears from within.* |
| **Serpent:** *"Ho hooo! Hello hello! what have we got here? Hello adventurer, I ask a simple question."* |
| **Serpent:** *"The most fulfilling of lives is that in which you can buy anything!"* |
| **Serpent:** *"Do you agree?"* |
| Agree |
| **Serpent:** *"Yeeeeeeessssssssssessss"* |
| **Serpent:** *"Thisss will all be worthhh it."* |
| **Serpent:** *"..ssSSs..... ss... sssss....!"* |
| *The serpent rears its head and blasts a stream of gold upwards!* |
| *It is amazing and terrifying simultaneously.* |
| *You gather all the gold, thank the snake, and get going.* |
| Disagree |
| *The serpent stares at you with a look of extreme disappointment.* |

## Strategy
- While the question of whether the increase in card removal cost is worth it cannot be answered simply, it is generally not a good choice to take the Curse unless you have some form of ensured card removal in the near future (Peace Pipe, shop) or a relic which negates or lessens the impact (Ginger, Blue Candle, Omamori, Du-Vu Doll, Darkstone Periapt). This is especially true in Ascension 15+, where less gold is granted and the cost of removing a card via some events increases.
    - The gold obtained from this event, especially in Ascension 15+ tends to underweigh the risk. Without relics in synergy with Curses, removing Doubt in itself will cost at least 75 gold, with 75 remaining gold covering the increase in card removal cost. That means in 3 removals (which isn't uncommon), the gain from this event will be completely negated. Considering the risk of carrying Doubt even in short distances, it is not a good option to take the Curse.
- This event can occur very early in the game, meaning with a small deck, you'll end up weakened every 2-3 turns. Since overcoming the Act 1 elites tends to mean defeating them quickly before their buffs or negative effects overwhelm you, if you are unable to remove or negate the weakened card before the next Elite or Boss, it is wise to avoid it.
    - Strikes suffer significantly from weakened status. 6 damage being lowered to 4 is in fact a 33% decrease in damage output, and since Strike tends to be an important part of damage output in Act 1,  getting weakened in Act 1 combats are extremely dangerous in common and Elite combats alike.

## Trivia
- The Ssserpent Head, obtained from Face Trader event, is a reference to him.
- This event's internal name is "Liars Game", possibly why the Curse obtained from this event is Doubt.
    - The event name is a reference to the manga *Liar Game.*

## Reference

# The Woman in Blue

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/The_Woman_in_Blue

**The Woman in Blue** is an event that can appear in Act 1, Act 2, and Act 3. You encounter a pale, mysterious woman who forces you to buy her potions.

This event will appear only if you have at least 50 gold.

## Options

*Condition in parentheses are for Ascension 15 or higher.*

- **[Buy 1 Potion]** 20 Gold.

- **[Buy 2 Potions]** 30 Gold.

- **[Buy 3 Potions]** 40 Gold.

- **[Leave]** Nothing happens (Lose HP equal to 5% of Max HP).

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| *From the darkness, an arm pulls you into a small shop. As your eyes adjust, you see a pale woman in sharp clothes gesturing towards a wall of potions.* |
| **Pale Woman:** *"Buy a potion. Now!"* *she states.* |
| Buy any number of Potions |
| **Pale Woman:** *"Good. Now leave."* |
| *You exit the shop cautiously.* |
| Leave |
| WHAM |
| * Her gloved fist collides with your face, nearly knocking you off your feet.* |
| **Pale Woman:** *"Get out before I litter the floor with your guts."* |
| *You take her word and exit with your guts still safely in your body.* |

## Strategy
- Potions are generally useful, and this event costs less money compared to the Merchant to obtain the same number of potions. The only risks are its random nature and the possibility of taking damage at Ascension 15 and higher.
    - If this event is encountered at Ascension 15+ and you do not want any potions, always pick the cheapest option. As this event never occurs if you have less than 20 gold, there is no risk of being forced to take damage.

## Notes

- You do not get to choose what potion to buy. Once you choose a number of potions you would like to buy from her, a random selections of potions will be offered to you. You may choose to pick them or skip them.

# Thorns

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Thorns

**Infobox:**
- Name: Thorns
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/3/39/Icon_Thorns.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202234707
- Description: When attacked, deals X damage back.
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: Intensity

**Thorns** is a buff that deals damage to a character's attacker when attacked, for each hit in the attack.

For enemies, Thorns only applies for hits dealt by Attacks. Thus, damage from Powers (eg. Fire Breathing and A Thousand Cuts), Orbs, and relics such as Letter Opener do not trigger Thorns.

Thorns is particularly effective against enemies that hit many times in a single attack, such as Byrds, Book of Stabbing, or Corrupt Heart.

## Sources of Thorns
- Bronze Scales: Relic that grants the player 3 Thorns at the start of combat.
- Liquid Bronze: Potion that grants the player 3 Thorns when consumed.
- Caltrops(+): Power card for the Silent that grants 3(5) Thorns for that combat.
- Flame Barrier(+): Skill card for the Ironclad that grants 12(16) block and adds 4(6) Flame Barrier for that turn. The Flame Barrier buff is functionally identical to Thorns, the only difference being that it only lasts one turn.

## Enemies with Thorns
- Spiker (Act 3 Monster): Starts with 3 Thorns, capable of buffing Thorns to a large number

## Notes
- The Guardian (Act 1 Boss), gains a Thorns-like buff in Defensive Mode. Its buff triggers when an attack card is played rather than whenever it takes damage. In other words, playing a multi-hit attack only does the thorns damage once, but playing an X-cost card with 0 energy will still activate the buff.

# Time Eater

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Time_Eater

**Infobox:**
- Name: Time Eater
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/1/1a/Time-eater-pretty.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20180110054301
- HP: 456; 480 (Ascension 9+)
- In Party With: None
- Debut Act: Act 3
- Powers: Time Warp
- Name: Time Warp
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/7/7a/Icon_TimeWarp.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202234710
- Description: Whenever you play 12 cards, ends your turn and gains 2 Strength. (Carries over between turns.)
- Type: Buff
- Stacking; Behavior: Counter
- Name: Draw Reduction
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/a/a3/Icon_DrawReduction.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202162042
- Description: Draw 1 less card for the next X turns.
- Type: Debuff
- Stacking; Behavior: Duration

The **Time Eater** is one of the three bosses encountered at the end of Act 3.

## Pattern
If its HP falls below 50% health, will use Haste next turn. Can use Haste only once per battle.

Has a 20% chance of using Ripple, 45% chance of using Reverberate and a 35% chance of using Head Slam.

Ripple cannot be used twice in a row, Head Slam cannot be used twice in a row and Reverberate cannot be used three times in a row.
| Name | Intent | Effect | Asc 4+ | Asc 19+ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reverberate |  | Deal 7 x 3 damage. | Deal 8 x 3 damage. | Deal 8 x 3 damage. |
| Head Slam |  | Deal 26 damage, apply 1 Draw Reduction. | Deal 32 damage, apply 1 Draw Reduction. | Deal 32 damage, apply 1 Draw Reduction, and shuffle 2 Slimed into the discard pile. |
| Ripple |  | Gain 20 Block, inflict 1 Vulnerable and  1 Weak in that order. | Gain 20 Block, inflict 1 Vulnerable and  1 Weak in that order. | Gain 20 Block, inflict 1 Vulnerable,  1 Weak, and 1 Frail in that order. |
| Haste |  | Heal back to 50% HP and remove all debuffs. | Heal back to 50% HP and remove all debuffs. | Heal back to 50% HP, gain 32 Block, and remove all debuffs. |

## Tips
- Unique among enemies, Time Eater is capable of ending the player's turn immediately. The player should take special care to ensure that they can play an appropriate number of cards each turn.
    - The Time Eater punishes decks that play many cards per turn, such as infinite or Shiv decks, especially hard. If you are relying heavily on this deck type in Act 3, it may be worth reconsidering your strategy.
    - Playing a consistent number of cards per turn may be useful so that Time Warp does not limit you to a one-card turn. For example, it's usually preferable to play 4 cards, then 5, then 3, rather than 7 cards, then 4, then 1.
- Try to avoid using low-cost, spammable cards when you can. These cards will quickly increment the Time Warp ability and Time Eater will gain too much strength to be dealt with.
    - As an example, if you were to play Acrobatics, draw 1 Strike+ and 1 Defend+, and play them both, it would cost 3 Time Warp charges. A single Dash+ would give roughly the same block and damage for the same amount of energy, but only 1 Time Warp charge.

- Time Eater can only use Haste once and will *always* use Haste the turn after falling below half HP. Since Haste erases all debuffs and heals the Time Eater back to half HP, there is no reason to take offensive action once the Time Eater is below half HP unless you can kill the Time Eater in one turn. It is better to play Powers and buff yourself for the remaining battle when possible. 
    - Due to the fact that the heal can be reliably activated, it may be worth ending the turn with Time Warp close to 12 if it lets you get the Time Eater below half HP, as you can safely play only one or two cards next turn while he heals, resetting the timer.
    - The heal action will remove the debuffs from Piercing Wail and Dark Shackles and their "buffs" (regaining Strength), causing Time Eater to permanently lose any Strength it had before.
    - The debuff cleanse from Haste can be challenging for certain decks, such as slow-ramping Poison decks. Plan accordingly.
- The Watcher can nullify Time Warp by playing Vault as the twelfth card. The result is the same as if you had normally played a Vault card and the Time Warp counter is reset.
- Playing Omniscience as the 12th card (from hand or during an Omniscience chain) can bypass the card limit. However, it must be played as the 12th card, playing Omniscience as the 11th card cannot bypass the card limit unless another Omniscience is selected to be the 12th card play, see Omniscience wiki page for more information.
- If the 12th card play triggers a card select menu, and the player uses Distilled Chaos before closing the menu, then Distilled Chaos can bypass the card limit before being forced to end the turn (this is especially powerful with Scrying cards since they can manipulate which cards are being played by Distilled Chaos). Note that if the card draws, then the card draw happens before Distilled Chaos; The "Disabled confirmation when choosing 1 card" preference setting could stop this from working when there is only 1 card available to choose from. The list of all cards that triggers a card select menu is: Headbutt, Armaments (not upgraded), True Grit (upgraded), Warcry, Burning Pact, Dual Wield, Exhume, Survivor, Dagger Throw, Acrobatics, Prepared, Concentrate, Setup, Nightmare, Hologram, Recycle, Seek, Cut Through Fate, Just Lucky, Third Eye, Foreign Influence, Meditate, Omniscience, Wish, Discovery, Forethought, Purity, Secret Technique, Secret Weapon, Thinking Ahead.

## Trivia
- It is possible that the Time Eater is related to the Watcher in some way. Their attires are different shades of purple and adorned with a similar motif. It also says *"Never... Liked... You..."* on its first turn when facing the Watcher, instead of the usual *"Ah... company."*
    - The Watcher's Sensory Stone text implies that her peer went missing and stopped reporting back to their sect about the Spire. Time Eater might be that missing peer of hers.
- The Time Eater is the only enemy in the game to block and debuff simultaneously on its turn.

# Toolbox

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Toolbox

**Infobox:**
- Name: Toolbox
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/4/46/Toolbox.png/revision/latest?cb=20200203154340
- Description: At the start of each combat, choose 1 of 3 random Colorless cards and add the chosen card into your hand.
- Flavor: A tool for every job.
- Rarity: Shop
- Class: Any

The card added does NOT subtract from your normal starting hand, since it adds a colorless card after you have drawn your cards.

If your starting hand is full, the card Toolbox attempted to add will go to your Discard Pile.

It can only generate a card that is available through shop and rewards. It cannot generate a healing card.

# Transform

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Transform

**Transforming** is an act that permanently turns a card into a random different card. It is usually done through certain Relics and Events.

## Rules and mechanics

- Every eligible card has the same chance to be picked. A card is just as likely to become a Demon Form as it is a Disarm.
- A Curse will only transform into another Curse.
- A card cannot transform into the same card.
- Cannot transform a card into a Basic card.
- A colored (i.e. character-specific) card will only turn into another card of the same color. This means that, under normal circumstances, the player would only receive a card of their current character.
    - Prismatic Shard does *not* affect transforms, as it only affects combat rewards.
    - Diverse and similar modifiers *do* allow a card to transform into another color.
- Colorless Cards will only transform into another colorless card.
    - They cannot transform into Special cards.
- Mechanically, the old card is removed and the new card is added to your Deck. Because of this, the rules and effects for card removal/add are applied:
    - Cards that cannot be removed, such as Bottled cards, Necronomicurse, and Curse of the Bell, cannot be transformed.
    - An Upgraded card will not (normally) transform into an Upgraded card, since the original was removed and replaced.
    - Molten Egg, Toxic Egg, and Frozen Egg will upgrade the new card, since it is added to your deck.
    - Omamori and Darkstone Periapt will trigger if you Transform a Curse, since a new Curse is added.
    - Hoarder modifier will add 3 copies instead of 1.

## Sources of Transform
### Relics
- Astrolabe
- Pandora's Box

### Events
#### Common Events
- Designer In-Spire
- Transmogrifier
#### Act 1
- Neow
- Living Wall
#### Act 2
- Augmenter
Category:Game Mechanics

# Treasure Room

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Treasure_Room

Treasure Room is a map location. They are marked on the map with a chest icon. 

You are guaranteed a Treasure Room at the halfway points of Acts 1-3. The character also has a chance to go to this type of room from Unknown Locations.

## Structure
A single non-boss chest stands on where the enemy would be in combat rooms. Clicking the chest will open a reward window. Normally, the reward consists of 1 relic, although certain relics can change this. There was also a chance that gold may be offered alongside as well.

If Act 4 is unlocked and the player has not already picked up the Sapphire Key, the chest in the Treasure room will contain the key along with the relic. The key is linked with the relic, meaning the player can only pick one. If the key is not picked, it will show up again in later chests.

## Related Relics

- Tiny Chest: Every 4th ? room is a Treasure room.

## See Also
- Chest

Category:Map Location

**True Grit** is a Skill card for the Ironclad. It grants 7 Block (9 if Upgraded), and Exhausts a random other card in hand. If True Grit is Upgraded, the player chooses the card in hand to Exhaust. 

## Tips
- While True Grit only grants 2 more Block than a basic Defend, its real strength lies in the ability to Exhaust cards. Exhausting cards can trigger many strong effects, including Feel No Pain, Sentinel, Dark Embrace, Charon's Ashes, and the Dead Branch. It also disposes of Curse and Status cards.

- Even without dedicated combos, this card can still temporarily remove cards that are undesired in the current combat (e.g. having Pummel when fighting a Spiker).

- Upgrading True Grit is highly recommended. Without the ability to select the card, combos are die rolls, and the player runs the risk of Exhausting useful cards.

# Tungsten Rod

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Tungsten_Rod

**Infobox:**
- Name: Tungsten Rod
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/a/a3/TungstenRod.png/revision/latest?cb=20200203152420
- Description: Whenever you would lose HP, lose 1 less.
- Flavor: It's very very heavy.
- Rarity: Rare
- Class: Any

The **Tungsten Rod** is a rare Relic that reduces all health loss by 1. This includes health loss inflicted by damage, cards, and events.

## Interactions
- Torii: Torii activates before Tungsten Rod:
    - Incoming damage > 5: Torii does not activate; Tungsten Rod reduces damage by 1.
    - Incoming damage ≤ 5: Torii reduces damage to 1; Tungsten Rod activates and further reduces it to 0.

- Intangible: This buff reduce all damage and HP loss taken to 1 and then Tungsten Rod reduce it to 0, effectively give you immunity to all damage and HP loss.

- Buffer: Prevents HP loss before Tungsten Rod is applied, even if HP loss would be only 1 and prevented by Tungsten Rod.

- Plated Armor: If Tungsten Rod prevents the last point of damage, the Plated Armor will not be reduced.

If the amount of health lost is reduced to 0, the following effects still trigger: 

- Static Discharge

Conversely, the following effects will *not* trigger:  

- Rupture
- Emotion Chip
- Centennial Puzzle
- Runic Cube
- Self-Forming Clay

# Unknown Location

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Unknown_Location

**Unknown Locations**, also known as **? rooms**, are a type of Map Location. When the player visits one of them, they may encounter an Event, a Monster, a Shop or a Treasure Room.

## Chances
Upon entering the first ? room in an act, the chances of finding each type of encounter are:
- **Monster:** 10%, increased by 10% each time a ? room does not contain Monster.
- **Treasure:** 2%, increased by 2% each time a ? room does not contain Treasure.
    - With Deadly Events modifier, the chance is increased by 4% each time instead.
- **Shop:** 3%, increased by 3% each time a ? room does not contain Shop.
- **Elite:** 20%, increased by 20% each time a ? room does not contain Elite.
    - This only applies if using the Deadly Events modifier, starting at floor 6 and above.
- **Event:** if no other encounter is found.

The chance of finding each type of encounter increases whenever a ? room is visited and does not contain that type of encounter. For example, after visiting four ? rooms which do not contain shops, the chance of finding a shop in the next ? room will be 15%. If a shop is found, the shop chance will be reset back to 3%.

## Related Relics
- Tiny Chest Every 4th ? room is a Treasure room. (This resets the increasing treasure room chance.)
- Juzu Bracelet Regular enemy combats are no longer encountered in ? rooms.
- Ssserpent Head Whenever you enter a ? room, gain 50 Gold.

# Upgrade

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Upgrade

Every card in the game, aside from Curses and Statuses (with the exception of Burn), can be upgraded to a better version.

Cards can only be upgraded once, with the exception of Searing Blow.

Ordinarily, this is done by the "Smith" command in Rest sites.

Multiple Relics can upgrade cards.

This can also be done in a multitude of Events.
Category:Game MechanicsCategory:Cards
## Upgrade-based Cards
- Armaments: Directly upgrade 1 card in your hand for this combat. Armaments+ upgrades all cards in your hand for that combat.
- Searing Blow: Can be upgraded an infinite number of times. The first upgrade gives 4 extra damage. Each further upgrade gives 1 more damage than the previous upgrade.
- Lesson Learned: If this kills a non-minion enemy, upgrades 1 random card in your deck (permanently).  Does not upgrade the card for the current combat--you cannot use the upgraded version until next combat.
- Master Reality: Whenever a card is created during combat, upgrade it.
- Apotheosis: Upgrade ALL cards in your deck for this combat.
## Relics that Upgrade Cards
- Frozen Egg: All Power cards gained will be automatically upgraded.
- Molten Egg: All Attack cards gained will be automatically upgraded.
- Toxic Egg: All Skill cards gained will be automatically upgraded.
- War Paint: On pickup, upgrades 2 random Skills.
- Whetstone: On pickup, upgrades 2 random Attacks.
- Tiny House: On pickup, upgrades 1 random card.
- Warped Tongs: At the start of every turn, upgrades a random card in your hand for that combat.
- Astrolabe: upon pickup transform 3 cards, then upgrade them.

## Events that offers Cards upgrade
- **All acts**
    - Designer In-Spire
    - Ominous Forge
    - Upgrade Shrine
- **Act 1**
    - Living Wall
    - Shining Light
- **Act 2**
    - Ancient Writing
      - Only upgrades all of your Strikes and Defends
- **Act 3**
    - Mind Bloom
      - Upgrades all of your cards, but gives you Mark of the Bloom, which prevents future healing.
## Notes

| If you are playing the Silent or the Watcher |
| If you are playing the Defect |
| Offer: Blood Vial |

| *You are alone once more.'' |

## Strategy
- You are given 5 Bites regardless of how many Strikes were removed.
    - Bite is slightly stronger than Strike (though an upgraded Bite deals less damage than an upgraded Strike). Still, it is not a particularly damaging card, and its healing is not very powerful. If you are removing Strike already for a thinner deck, obtaining 5 Bites is not unlike re-adding Strikes, clogging your deck with rather mediocre cards.
    - If you are running a Perfected Strike deck, consider avoiding removing all Strikes with this event as it will reduce the damage of Perfected Strike.
- Feed card can be used to offset the reduction to max HP, albeit very slowly.
- Molten Egg upgrades all of the Bites.
- Unless you have already started to remove Strikes from your deck, offering the Blood Vial is worth considering. Receiving multiple Bites can be a quick way to replace and improve un-upgraded Strikes, and the healing effect can occur multiple times during a fight instead of the one-time effect of the Blood Vial. 
- This event can also be used to remove the Blood Vial if you’re aiming to get the “Who Needs Relics?” achievement.
- Bites are not upgraded by the Ancient Writing event, as Bites are not strikes.

# Vault

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Vault

**Infobox:**
- Name: Vault
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/c/c9/Vault.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20200918125353
- Class: Watcher
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Rare
- Cost: 3
- Effect: Take an extra turn after this one. ; End your turn. Exhaust.
- [Vault+]
- Cost+: 2
- Effect+: Take an extra turn after this one. ; End your turn. Exhaust.

CardAutobox
**Vault** is a Skill card for the Watcher. When played, it immediately ends the player's turn and the player starts a new turn (more precisely, skips the enemies' turn), the interaction of Vault with various buffs/debuffs does not follow a general rule and requires detailed explanations. 

Without Vault, the order after the player clicks the end turn button is: player's turn ends->enemy's turn starts->enemy's turn->enemy's turn ends->round ends->player's turn starts, the part where Vault skipped is: enemy's turn starts->enemy's turn->enemy's turn ends->round ends, below is an exhaustive explanation of Vault interaction. 

When the enemies' turn starts, enemies remove their Block, Byrd resets Flying, and Corrupt Heart resets Invincible, which are all prevented by Vault. 

"End of Turn Trigger" buffs/debuffs trigger at the end of the player's or enemies' turn, when playing Vault, if the buff/debuff belongs to the player, then it triggers, if it belongs to the enemy, then it does not (for example, Regeneration does trigger, but Regenerate does not): Combust, Constricted, Equilibrium, Establishment, Shackled, Dexterity Down, Strength Down, Omega, Regenerate, Regeneration, Ritual (player version), Study, The Bomb, Well-Laid Plans, Wraith Form. 

"End of Turn Decrease/Wear off" buffs/debuffs decrease/wear off at the end of the player's or enemies' turn, when playing Vault, if the buff/debuff belongs to the player, then it decreases/wears off, if it belongs to the enemy, then it does not: Amplify, Burst, Double Tap, Entangled, Shackled, Intangible (enemy version), Dexterity Down, Strength Down, No Draw, Rage, Rebound, Regeneration, The Bomb. 

"End of Round" buffs/debuffs decrease/wear off/reset at the end of the enemies' turn, all are prevented by Vault, whether it belongs to the player or the enemies: Blur, Double Damage, Draw Reduction, Duplication, Equilibrium, Frail, Strength Up, Intangible (player version), Lock-On, Malleable, No Block, Ritual (enemy version), Slow, Vulnerable, Wave of the Hand, Weak. 

## Interactions
 
- Synergizes with powers that trigger at the start of your turn, such as Deva Form, Devotion, and Establishment.
- Scry will trigger for '''Vault's''' extra turn if Foresight has been played.
- Triggers the effects of Perseverance, Sands of Time, or Windmill Strike if any of those cards are in the player's hand when **Vault** is played.
- If Simmering Fury is played before using Vault, Wrath will be entered on Vault's extra turn.
- Wave of the Hand's effects carry over to Vault's extra turn.
- Can be used to deal additional damage against Giant Head since Slow is not reset at the start of the extra turn.
- If played as the 12th card against Time Eater, Time Eater still gains strength but the player gets another turn with the Time Warp clock reset to 0.
- When played whilst having Velvet Choker, it gives you a new turn, thus resetting the number of cards you have played back to 0.

 
- Temporary buffs from Potions such as Flex Potion will be lost at the start of Vault's extra turn. 
- Constricted from the Spire Growth will damage you after playing Vault.
- Playing Vault after playing Blasphemy will instantly kill you unless you have an active form of damage prevention.
- The Corrupt Heart's Invincible buff counter does not reset for Vault's extra turn.
- Draw Reduction debuff from Time Eater does not wear off for Vault's extra turn, causing the extra turn and the turn after that to draw 1 less.

**Infobox:**

CardAutobox
**Void** is an Unplayable, Ethereal Status card.

When **Void** is drawn into your hand, you lose 1 Energy. Due to its Ethereal keyword, **Void** is Exhausted if in your hand at the end of your turn.

## Sources of Void
- Enemies
    - Awakened One (Stage 2)
    - Corrupt Heart (Debilitate)
- Cards
    - TURBO
- Blights
    - Twisting Mind

## Interactions
- Evolve: Draw 1 more card for each Void you draw. Stacking Evolves can allow you to draw 2 more cards when you draw a Void.
- Exhaust synergies can use Void as exhaust fuel. In addition, any effects you may gain from exhausting a card are fulfilled at the end of the turn, since Void is Ethereal.
- Medical Kit allows Void to be played and exhausted for no penalty, though they already exhaust at the end of your turn, and their effect is applied on draw. One of the only scenarios in which such an interaction would be relevant, though, is with Dark Embrace.
- Energy is only lost when the card is drawn. If the card is added to your hand by other means, you don't lose energy. This means that by selecting Void via effects like Seek, Hologram, or Liquid Memories, the energy reduction can be evaded.

# Vulnerable

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Vulnerable

**Infobox:**
- Name: Vulnerable
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/a/ae/Icon_Vulnerable.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202234658
- Description: Target takes 50% more damage from attacks.
- Type: Debuff
- Stacking; Behavior: Duration

Vulnerable creatures take 50% more damage from Attacks.

When an enemy is Vulnerable, they will receive 50% more damage from your Attacks (75% with the Paper Phrog relic).

When the player is Vulnerable, they will receive 50% more damage from enemy Attacks (25% with the Odd Mushroom relic).

Does not affect non-attack damage such as Poison, Orbs, or Thorns. Only cards of the Attack type receive the bonus damage.

Stacks of Vulnerable only increase the duration, not the intensity. For example, 2 Vulnerable will last for 2 turns, and 5 Vulnerable will last for 5 turns, but in both cases they will take 50% more damage.

Vulnerable damage is rounded down. For example, Headbutt deals 9 damage. To a Vulnerable enemy it deals 13 instead of 13.5 or 14.

CardAutobox

## Tips
Wallop is useful for protecting oneself while in Wrath, as the block gained will scale to the increased damage. This makes it much better than playing regular Defend cards as well.

Using Wreath of Flame to increase the damage of this card also increases the Block gained from it. Remember that the effect of Vigor is doubled/tripled when in Wrath/Divinity. It also works well for this reason against Vulnerable enemies.

This is an excellent card for tackling enemies with Thorns, as the Block is received before the retaliation damage.

Avoid using this card against enemies with large amounts of Block, as you must deal unblocked damage to receive block in return.

It does not scale with Dexterity, as the block gained is always equal to the damage dealt. Instead, it scales twice with Strength, as each point increases the damage *and* block by one.

# Watcher

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Watcher

*"A blind ascetic who has come to "Evaluate" the Spire. Master of the divine Stances."*

The Watcher is one of four playable characters in Slay the Spire. She is a monk that utilizes the effects of her different stances to her advantage, boasts an arsenal oriented around deck control via scrying, retain, and Energy generation, as well as a unique focus on mid-combat card generation. She starts with 72 HP. 

The Watcher's starting Relic is Pure Water, which adds a Miracle to your hand at the start of each combat.

The Watcher was first added to the beta build in the Testing the Fourth Character update and released to the public on January 15th, 2020.

## Cards
### Starting Deck
- 4 Strike
- 4 Defend
- 1 Eruption
- 1 Vigilance
Watcher Card Navbox

## Relics
The Watcher has fewer class-specific relics than the other classes, having only two class-specific rare relics (rather than three like the Ironclad and Silent), and only two class-specific boss relics (rather than three, like those two and the Defect). The Defect has equally few overall, but is short two Rare relics instead of one Rare relic and one Boss relic.

Starting Relic: Pure Water

Common Relic: Damaru

Uncommon Relics: Duality, Teardrop Locket

Rare Relics: Cloak Clasp, Golden Eye

Boss Relics: Holy Water (replaces Pure Water), Violet Lotus

Shop Relic: Melange

## Strategy
The Watcher's gameplay centers nearly entirely around stances. She is, on average, much more powerful than the original 3 classes, owing primarily to the Wrath stance that allows her to double damage output and thus kill every enemy before they can retaliate. However, not every fight will present an immediate kill opportunity, and thus care needs to be taken so that the Watcher does not get stuck in Wrath on a bad turn and take large amounts of unnecessary damage in return. To this end, mechanics such as Scry and several cards that have Retain allow her to carefully choose turn actions, including even a turn or two ahead, to make sure she has a way to change stances at will to either escape danger or generate energy.

Most Watcher strategies will center around a small selection of key cards that she will want to play over and over again. Also notably, the Watcher's starter deck has significantly more power than other characters', allowing players to be much more picky with card selection even at higher Ascension levels. Because of this, consistent Watcher decks tend to be much smaller than average. However, it is not impossible (albeit more difficult) to succeed with a larger deck full of value cards.

### Build types
Listed below are the standard synergies that Watcher decks build towards, which may give you an idea of direction for your own runs. Unlike other characters, because Watcher's starter Deck is so powerful, you can get away with "forcing" a build more often, even at higher difficulties. However, you should still be open to taking cards that solve your immediate problems if they arise, as well as have the awareness to switch gears should key cards not be offered to you.

Stance Dance (Standard)
Stance Dance (Infinite)
Mantra / Divinity
Retain Build
Ragnarok Build
Scry Build
Pressure Points
Creation
Alpha

## Unlocks
The Watcher is unlocked by completing an unseeded run (defeating Act 3 boss) with any base-game character, if the Defect is already unlocked. Completing a run with a modded character will not unlock the Watcher.

| Unlock Number | Prizes Unlocked |
| --- | --- |
| 1st | Prostrate, Blasphemy, Devotion |
| 2nd | Foreign Influence, Alpha, Mental Fortress |
| 3rd | Spirit Shield, Wish, Foresight |
| 4th | Akabeko, Duality, Ceramic Fish |
| 5th | Strike Dummy, Teardrop Locket, Cloak Clasp |

# We Meet Again!

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/We_Meet_Again%21

**We Meet Again!** is an event that can appear in Act 1, Act 2, and Act 3. You encounter an eccentric man named Ranwid, who seemed to have met you before, though you have no recollection of such thing.
## Options

- **[Give Potion] **Lose a potion. Receive a Relic.
    - Requires at least 1 potion in your possession.
- **[Give Gold] **Lose a varying amount of gold. Receive a Relic.
    - Requires at least 50 gold in your possession.
      - The amount of gold he requests is between 50 (minimum value) and your current amount of gold, up to 150 gold.
- **[Give Card] **Lose a card. Receive a Relic.
    - Requires a valid card in your possession.
      - Not a Curse card.
      - Not a Basic card.
      - Not a Bottled card.
- **[Attack]** Nothing happens.

The Potion, Gold, and Card are chosen randomly, and are displayed to you when you make your choice.

The Relic rewarded will be a randomly-selected Common, Uncommon or Rare Relic. Which relic it is will not be displayed.

## Dialogue

| Encounter |
| --- |
| *"We meet again!"* |
| *A cheery disheveled fellow approaches you gleefully. You do not know this man.* |
| ''"It's me, Ranwid! Have any goods for me today? The usual? A fella like me can't make it alone, you know?* |
| *You eye him suspiciously and consider your options...* |
| Give... |
| ...Potion |
| **Ranwid:** *"Exquisite! Was feeling parched."* |
| *Glup glup glup* |
| *He downs the potion in one go and lets out a satisfied* burp*.* |
| ...Gold |
| **Ranwid:** *"Magnificent! This will be quite handy if I run into those mask wearing hoodlums again."* |
| ...Card |
| **Ranwid:** *"Exemplary! I shall study this further in my chambers."* |
| *He rummages around his various pockets...* |
| **Ranwid:** *"Here, look what I've got for you today! Take it take it!"* |
| Attack |
| **Ranwid:** *"*Aaaaagghh!! *What a jerk you are sometimes!"* |
| *He runs away.'' |

## Trivia
- The name Ranwid is an anagram for Darwin.
- Ranwid expresses knowledge and thoughts of certain items and creatures in the Spire as observed by his quotes in the relics Strawberry, Gold-Plated Cables, Gremlin Horn, Self-Forming Clay, Toxic Egg, The Specimen, Empty Cage, and Odd Mushroom. They also support Ranwid's tendency to research and examine some collectibles in his chambers.
- The starting dialogue of the event and its name imply that the player has met Ranwid before, referencing the constant revival of the player by Neow and hence, the repeating meetings. The first meeting between Ranwid and the player, however, is never made clear or explained in the game.
- Ranwid's mentioning of the *"mask wearing hoodlums"* refers to the Red Mask gang found in the Masked Bandits event.
- Giving Ranwid an Explosive Potion, Fire Potion, or Poison Potion does not affect him at all, ironically. The implications of him drinking a Fairy in a Bottle is likewise never addressed.
    - It is theorized that Ranwid may have the Sozu which is described to disable all potion effects. Ranwid drinking the potion like water seems to support this idea.

# Weak

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Weak

**Infobox:**
- Name: Weak
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/b/b9/Icon_Weak.png/revision/latest?cb=20200202234702
- Description: Target deals 25% less attack damage.
- Type: Debuff
- Stacking; Behavior: Duration

Weak creatures deal 25% less damage with Attacks.

When an enemy is Weakened, they deal 25% less damage with Attacks (40% less with Paper Crane).

When the player is Weakened, they deal 25% less damage with Attacks.  If they have Ginger, they cannot become Weakened by any means.

Weak does not affect Poison or Thorns damage; it only applies to Attack cards.

Stacks of Weak only increase the duration. For example, 2 Weak will last 2 turns, and 5 Weak will last 5 turns, but in both cases they will deal 25% less damage.

Weak damage is rounded down. For example, Byrd deals 1 damage at a time. While Weak it deals 0 damage instead of .75 damage or 1 damage.

## Interactions

### Any Character
- Doubt: Unplayable. At the end of your turn, gain 1 Weak.
- Blind: Apply 2 weak (to all enemies).
- Ginger: You can no longer become Weakened.
- Gremlin Visage: Start each combat with 1 Weak.
- Red Mask: At the start of combat, apply 1 Weak to ALL enemies.
- Weak Potion: Apply 3 Weak.

### Ironclad
- Champion Belt: Whenever you apply Vulnerable, also apply 1 Weak.
- Clothesline: Deal 12(14) damage. Apply 2(3) Weak.
- Intimidate: Apply 1(2) Weak to ALL enemies. Exhaust.
- Shockwave: Apply 3(5) Weak and Vulnerable to ALL enemies. Exhaust.
- Uppercut: Deal 12 damage. Apply 1(2) Weak. Apply 1(2) Vulnerable.

### Silent
- Paper Crane: Enemies with Weak deal 40% less damage rather than 25%.
- Crippling Cloud: Apply 4(7) Poison and 2 Weak to ALL enemies. Exhaust.
- Heel Hook: Deal 5 damage. If the enemy has Weak, gain  and draw 1 card.
- Leg Sweep: Applies 2(3) Weak. Gain 11(14) Block.
- Malaise: Enemy loses X(+1) Strength. Apply X(+1) Weak. Exhaust.
- Neutralize: Deal 3(4) damage. Apply 1(2) Weak.
- Sucker Punch: Deal 7(9) damage. Apply 1(2) Weak.

### Defect
- Go for the Eyes: Deal 3(4) damage. If the enemy intends to attack, apply 1(2) Weak.

### Watcher
- Sash Whip: Deal 8(10) damage. If the last card played this combat was an Attack, apply 1(2) Weak.
- Wave of the Hand: Whenever you gain Block this turn, apply 1(2) Weak to ALL enemies.
Category:Debuffs

**Wheel of Change** is an event that can appear in Act 1, Act 2, and Act 3. A small gremlin appears and forces you to play a wheel of fortune game.

*Condition in parentheses are for Ascension 15 or higher. HP percentages are rounded down.*

There is no option to avoid playing.
- **[Play]** Spin the wheel and get a prize.

|  | **[Prize!]** Obtain a random Relic - The Relic is a randomly-selected Common, Uncommon or Rare Relic. - The Relic cannot be Bottled Flame, Bottled Lightning, Bottled Tornado, or Whetstone. |
|  | **[Prize!]** Heal to full HP. |
|  | **[Prize?]** Become Cursed - Decay. |
|  | **[Prize!]** Remove a card from your deck. |
|  | **[Prize?]** Take 10% (15%) of your max HP as damage. |

| **Gremlin:** *"Enjoy!"* |

# Whirlwind

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Whirlwind

**Infobox:**
- Name: Whirlwind
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/e/e0/Whirlwind.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016211122
- Class: Ironclad
- Type: Attack
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Effect: Deal 5 damage to ALL enemies X times.
- [Whirlwind+]
- Effect+: Deal 8 damage to ALL enemies X times.

**Whirlwind** is an Attack card for the Ironclad. It spends all remaining Energy points and attacks each enemy for 5 damage for every Energy point spent. As an Uncommon card, it appears as a reward for combat, although less often than Commons.

Upon upgrade, each hit deals 3 more damage.

## Interactions

- As a multi-hit attack, it benefits highly from Strength so long as more than 1 Energy is used.
- Although using it with 0 Energy will have no immediate effect, it still counts as an Attack card played.
- If duplicated with Duplication Potion, Double Tap, Echo Form, or Necronomicon (If X is 2 or greater), the value of X will be preserved for the copied card.
- Chemical X allows for Whirlwind to deal damage 2 more times, even if no Energy is used to play it.
- When unupgraded against single enemies, it is better to use Strikes than burn all your energy on 5 damage instead of 6. This can make Whirlwind a card you might want to upgrade sooner.

- Effect+: Add a random Power card into your hand.; It costs 0 this turn.Exhaust.

CardAutobox 
White Noise is an Uncommon Skill for the Defect that generates a random Power and reduces its cost to 0 for the turn, then Exhausts.

If you use White Noise as other character that is not the Defect, it will grant a random Power card of the respective color of that character. For example, if you obtained this card as the Watcher, it will grant you a purple Power card. Prismatic Shard does not affect the variety of colors of the card it generates. However, it is affected by Run Modifiers, which could potentially allow it to generate an Power from more than one color of card pools. 

Upgrading White Noise reduces its cost to 0.

It can only generate a card that is available through shop and rewards. It cannot generate a healing card.

### Excluded Cards
- Self Repair *(Healing)*
- Omega *(Card effect only)*

# Wing Boots

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Wing_Boots

**Infobox:**
- Name: Wing Boots
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/7/70/WingedGreaves.png/revision/latest?cb=20200203152443
- Description: You may ignore paths when choosing the next room to travel to 3 times.
- Flavor: Stylish.
- Rarity: Rare
- Class: Any

**Wing Boots** is a Rare Relic.  It allows the player to choose any room on the next floor when going to the next floor, without being restricted by the paths.  The player may not choose a room on the same floor they are currently at, skip floors, or go back a floor.  The relic allows the paths to be ignored 3 times across a run before it is used up.

This relic does not spawn beyond floor 40, excluding Endless mode.  This relic is removed from the pool of available relics if the current run uses the Flight (ignore paths when choosing the next room) or Certain Future (map contains only one path) run modifiers, as either one would make the effect of this relic pointless.

# Worship

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Worship

**Infobox:**
- Name: Worship
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/d/d4/Worship.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20191216175551
- Class: Watcher
- Type: Skill
- Rarity: Uncommon
- Cost: 2
- Effect: Gain 5 Mantra.
- [Worship+]
- Cost+: 2
- Effect+: Retain. Gain 5 Mantra.

CardAutobox

Worship costs 2 energy, and generates 5 Mantra without doing anything else. Unlike Prostrate and Pray+, Worship is energy negative. However, it can allow you to enter Divinity through just two cycles of your deck, meaning Worship can be great as your only mantra-generating card. However, having this card be upgraded (which gives it Retain) is critical, as it means that it can be cast on turns where you have the energy, while also allowing you to enter Divinity at the perfect moment. Finally, if you're running Omniscience, choosing Worship allows you to instantly enter Divinity, and costs 0 energy if Omniscience is upgraded, which is an incredibly powerful combo.

Ultimately, one of the best ways to consider Divinity cards is to consider how many cycles through your deck it takes to achieve Divinity. For example, a card that gives 3 mantra takes 4 deck cycles to reach Divinity, while a card that gives 4 mantra would take 3 deck cycles. Thus, you should ultimately achieve to have your mantra cards give a total of either 5 or 10 mantra each deck cycle. Devotion and Damaru can also help with this. As an example of a great Divinity deck, a deck with an upgraded Prostrate, a Worship, and a Damaru can easily achieve 10 Mantra in just 2-3 turns.

# Wound

https://slay-the-spire.fandom.com/wiki/Wound

**Infobox:**
- Name: Wound
- Image: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/slay-the-spire/images/a/a4/Wound.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/268?cb=20181016212742
- Class: Neutral
- Type: Status
- Rarity: Common
- Cost: Unplayable
- Effect: Unplayable.

CardAutobox
**Wound** is an unplayable Status card.  It has no secondary effect, except for clogging up the deck.

## Sources of Wound
- Enemies
    - Book of Stabbing
    - Taskmaster
    - Dagger
    - Corrupt Heart
- Cards
    - Power Through
    - Wild Strike
- Relics
    - Mark of Pain
- Blights
    - Twisting Mind

## Interactions
- Positive
    - You can use the Evolve power card to draw another card from your deck, effectively negating the penalty. Multiple Evolves will allow you to draw more per wound, but you are still limited to 10 cards in your hand, which can lead to a hand full of wounds.
    - Exhaust synergies (such as Second Wind) can make use out of Wounds.
      - Medical Kit allows Wounds to be played and exhausted for no penalty.
- Negative
    - Clash builds are stopped dead by Wounds.
